gsbpm_description: This sub-process includes the initial investigation and identification of what statistics are needed and what is needed of the statistics. It may be triggered by a new information request from users, an environmental change such as a reduced budget, a periodic review, or respondent feedback. Action plans[11] from evaluations of previous iterations of the production cycle (including from respondent feedback) or from other programmes might provide an input to this sub-process. It also includes consideration of practice amongst other (national and international) statistical organisations producing similar data and the methods used by those organisations.

Decrease of approximately 900 full-time equivalents by 2028-29 reduces capacity to sustain all existing statistical activities, forcing sharper prioritization
Artificial intelligence, automation, machine learning, and new tools and methods create alternative lower-cost ways to meet some needs, influencing which needs are considered feasible

implicated_work_descriptions.title: International Relations Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This is the strongest relationship because the position explicitly analyzes user requirements from other national statistical offices and multilateral organizations in order to determine the most appropriate research, comparative analysis studies, sources of information, methods and approaches. It also interprets requests for statistical information and translates them into concrete, timely and affordable information requests. These are core need-identification activities, and they are more central to the work than downstream production tasks because the role acts as a focal point between external users and Statistics Canada expert communities. Future drivers such as Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment and Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline are likely to intensify prioritization of which international requests and cooperation opportunities should be pursued, requiring sharper triage, clearer trade-offs and stronger alignment to enterprise priorities under constrained expert capacity.

1. Decision Making: Analyzes the user requirements for data users of other national statistical offices (NSOs) in order to determine the most appropriate research and comparative analysis studies to do, as well as which sources of information, methods and approaches should be used. Modifies existing techniques or develops new methods such as for the dissemination and communication of statistical information.

As the focal point or project leader, defines project objectives and priorities, prepares work plans and summaries outlining approaches, time-frames and resources. Each project is unique in nature and decisions impact on the timing and scope of product and service delivery to multinational organizations and other national statistical offices. Decisions also affect capacity of Statistics Canada expert communities to continue to perform their regular duties. Recommendations lead to effective and efficient distribution of effort towards international cooperation objectives.

In order to provide advice and consultative services to internal subject matter experts participating in international cooperation projects in statistics, gathers relevant information from various sources (for example different NSOs, multilateral organizations, different ministries participating in the national statistical system of a particular country), performs appropriate analysis and interpretation, considers all possible options, impacts and outcomes, and makes decisions about recommending strategic improvements, involvement of subject matter experts, or impacts on planning and scheduling.

In order to effectively coordinate the preparation of briefing notes for the Chief Statistician attending international meetings, decisions need to be made about which expert community is doing work that best corresponds to each topic on the agenda, which in turn requires up-to-date knowledge of the research and development work going on at Statistics Canada, as well as its regular statistical programs. The position is also responsible for reviewing the briefing notes and seeking clarifications or revisions from the authors if they are deemed to be of insufficient quality.
Scope of decisions relates to coordination with multinational organizations, other National Statistical Offices, and departmental senior management.
2. Leadership And Operational Management: Plans and coordinates the work in support of technical assistance projects for national statistical offices and multilateral (international) organizations. Human resources responsibilities include selecting, coaching and training personnel; planning and assigning work; monitoring and follow-up; developing and implementing work plans and priorities; conducting performance reviews and taking disciplinary action when appropriate; managing through subordinate staff.

Operational management includes recommending resource needs; preparing cost estimates and projections; keeping projects on schedule and within budget; managing an operating budget; monitoring material and financial resources; reallocating resources within a set budget; providing input into financial planning exercises; supervision of staff.

Assists in the allocation of human and financial resources and monitors their usage relative to forecasts. This has a direct positive impact on the statistical processes of the NSO receiving the technical assistance, and ultimately a positive impact on the quality of official statistics globally.
Leads project teams involved in the conduct of technical assistance projects with other National Statistical offices or Statistical Agencies.
3. Communication: Gathers, compiles, analyzes and interprets information and data requests from multilateral (international) organizations, assesses the relevance and impact for Statistics Canada, and determines which expert community or communities should respond. Coordinates the delivery of data and information. Negotiates for deadline extensions or staggered delivery where appropriate. Ensures that all necessary approvals are secured prior to delivery. All correspondence both internal and external is professional, polite, grammatically and factually correct, timely and archived using information management current best practices.

Prepares analytical reports and work plans in the context of international cooperation, to be shared with international stakeholders. Interacts with participating countries and regional stakeholders, providing mutually acceptable solutions to the challenge of simultaneously meeting the needs of multiple stakeholders.

Prepare written reports or supervise staff in the preparation of written reports for internal and international stakeholders, to ensure that they are informed of the progress of statistical capacity building activities being conducted in the course of a large technical assistance project with foreign countries (where capacity building means showing senior managers at other NSOs better ways of planning, managing and executing their statistical programs so that they will bring positive changes to their own organizations).
Makes formal presentations of recommendations, supported by original research, to senior management at Statistics Canada and senior management of other NSOs and international organizations.

Meets with senior management upon their return from multinational events, to gather feedback, status and direction on topics and issues in which Statistics Canada expert communities are involved. Analyzes and interprets this information, and presents it to the expert communities, soliciting their continued contribution and involvement. Researches and provides more background and supporting information for new or emerging topics. Answers questions from the expert communities and ensures that they are in contact with the appropriate parties from other NSOs or multilateral (international) organizations.

The Chief Statistician of Canada attends several international meetings per year at which he actively participates in discussions about emerging issues of global concern (for example global warming or population censuses based solely on administrative data) or international partnerships on the development of new technology (for example how to exploit Big Data). In order to actively participate in these discussions, the Chief Statistician needs detailed and accurate briefing notes from Statistics Canada’s expert communities. Each meeting has approximately 20 different discussion topics. These topics are very briefly described on the meeting agenda, which is made available typically a couple of weeks prior to the meeting. The position analyses the agenda items and recruits the appropriate expert communities to prepare briefing notes. The position supports the expert communities by searching the internet (sites of multilateral organizations such as the UNECE, UNSD, OECD, IMF) for background documentation, coordinating correspondence between Statistics Canada and experts from other NSOs working on similar topics, and providing other relevant information to the experts such as the governance structure of multilateral organizations or briefing notes from other meetings attended by senior managers.

Communicates orally with senior managers of other NSOs and multilateral organizations in a professional manner. Gathers and shares information relevant to the successful participation of Statistics Canada experts in capacity building activities, international working groups or senior manager level steering meetings. Provides written documentation to both Statistics Canada and external stakeholders of recommendations or results of studies or analysis, and progress on on-going activities.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of economic/sociologic principles and practices as they relate to a specialized area as well as specific knowledge of other regions (for example the Caribbean or South America) to initiate and conduct projects to improve existing concepts in other countries or develop new approaches to extend the application of official statistics internationally.
Knowledge of project management concepts, methods and techniques to determine the scope and depth of research and analysis projects for international clients.

Knowledge is required of computer software applications to conduct analysis and document project results, including specialized software such as statistical sampling, computer assisted techniques, automated working papers, and flowcharting.

Knowledge of social science research methods, techniques and practices, including multi-disciplinary analysis methods, to carry out analysis on a variety of approaches regarding the coordination of a national statistical system or improving relations between an NSO and other federal ministries.

Skill in synthesizing information from diverse disciplines (management science, economics, and public policy administration, etc.) to propose solutions that are feasible, reflect current best practices, and are multifaceted, addressing several challenges simultaneously.

Knowledge of theories, principles and techniques of consultation, management, small group process, interviewing and counselling to lead project teams, to negotiate contracts for services and agreements with other institutions.
Operational management requires management skills and knowledge of the theories and principles of general and project management to lead a multi-disciplinary project team.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge is required of the strategic direction, culture, structure and organization, mandate, objectives and relevant policies, procedures and practices of the International Cooperation programs and initiatives. This knowledge is required to achieve operational objectives and results in an effective and efficient manner, and to incorporate them into the conduct and management of studies and projects.

Knowledge of the mandate, objectives and organization of Statistics Canada to manage subject matter studies and projects. Knowledge of other statistical programs (concepts, methods, and databases) related to the area of expertise to plan and implement statistical activities, to integrate conceptually different data from other programs, to explain variances and to recommend improvements to other statistical programs.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements to other departments, agencies and international organizations.

Knowledge of current and emerging socio-economic issues in Canada and internationally such as the changing social context and the globalization of markets, particularly as they relate to the area of expertise in a statistical program (e.g. System of National Accounts, Education, Health, Labour, Prices, Demography, International Trade, Balance of Payments, Environment, etc.). This knowledge is required to provide subject-matter advice, consultative services and to analyze and interpret data requests and assess their impact on the area of specialization.

Knowledge of other countries’ national statistical offices, multilateral (international) organizations (International Statistical Agencies) and non-government organizations in order to effectively communicate on approaches, methods, data and analysis for the purpose of strengthening statistical reporting.
6. Research and analysis: Analysis is required to understand and interpret requests for statistical information and to translate them into a concrete, timely and affordable information request.
Research gaps and overlaps in Statistics Canada’s involvement in international activities, and propose to senior management a strategic approach to achieving effective and efficient collaboration.
Conducts research and comparative analysis on statistical products of different national statistical offices in order to recommend areas of improvement.

Conducts research and comparative analysis of international contexts and statistical processes in order to recommend how Statistics Canada will respond and prepares and edits analytical reports, including recommendations for improving efficiency or effectiveness.

Analysis is required to understand and interpret user requirements for statistical information and to translate them into concrete and timely research studies. Conducts research and comparative analysis on topics such as but not limited to: statistical products of different national statistical offices; data and information requests from multilateral (international) organizations; the scope and depth of involvement of internal subject matter experts in international activities. From this research and comparative analysis, prepares and edits analytical reports, including recommendations for improving efficiency or effectiveness, and shares these reports with both internal and international stakeholders. At the outset clients are often uncertain of their data needs and are unfamiliar with options, methods and techniques available.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Unit Head, Subject Matter
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This is the strongest relationship because the role explicitly 'determines changes in the statistical needs of clients,' 'assesses the policies and programs of key client departments to determine their requirements for statistical information,' and translates user needs into recommended studies and program changes. That is direct responsibility for identifying needs and shifts in demand. It is stronger than output-objective setting because the evidence focuses first on understanding needs, impacts on programs, and emerging client requirements. Future drivers such as operational efficiency, prioritization, and changing socio-economic conditions will materially affect this work by increasing the need to triage needs, identify high-value demands, and align programs with constrained resources and evolving user expectations.

key_activities: Plans, develops and directs the analysis, review and presentation of program results; coordinates and reviews the development, processing, analysis, marketing and dissemination of statistical data; prepares, edits and evaluates analytical material for publication purposes.
Plans, manages and coordinates economic, financial and/or socio-economic studies and develops new methods to produce, evaluate, analyze, present and extend the application of divisional statistics.
Determines changes in the statistical needs of clients; assesses the impact on divisional programs; develops options and strategies to manage complex issues and multi-stakeholder relations.

Provides expert advisory and consultative services to data users (e.g. academics, policy makers, international bodies, etc.) on the results of surveys and studies, survey concepts and methods, and economic / social science theories and principles.
Represents subject-matter divisions on development projects, task forces or committees in various roles such as Project Manager, Task Manager and Task Force Leader.

Supervises a unit and multi-disciplinary project teams responsible for significant multi-sectoral and inter-departmental files/issues; manages the financial resources attached to each statistical program.

1. DECISION MAKING: Assesses the policies and programs of key client departments to determine their requirements for statistical information and recommends, for approval, those studies that should be conducted.
Recommends plans to improve and expand the content and direction of existing studies as well as the development of policies, strategies and program proposals of concern to the sector.

Defines the objectives and content of the studies and the overall approach to be followed; determines the standards, data concepts, definitions and techniques to be applied in the development and conduct of studies and in the reporting, analysis and presentation of findings.

Interprets study findings and conclusions and prepares recommendations and advice to senior management on current trends affecting the Sector policies and programs and on the significant factors related to the changing environment.

Develops enhancements and recommends modifications to be made to the program content, coverage and operational procedures, such as new or modified data sources, concepts, methods and definitions to be applied.
Investigates client requirements for statistical information and determines the capacity and ability of existing or modified program activities to meet these requirements.

Provides input to management decisions and recommendations designed to develop or improve departmental policies and develops new program initiatives covering areas such as recruitment, official languages, employment equity, dissemination and confidentiality of information.
2. LEADERSHIP AND OPERATIONAL MANAGEMENT: Manages a unit involved in the conduct of economic, financial and/or socio-economic studies and research and leads project teams for special projects. Determines program objectives and priorities and assesses the requirements of the program. Plans and schedules the work, resolves conflicting priorities, ascertains human resource needs, determines the appropriate selection methods (internal and external resources / contractors) to meet program and project objectives, recruits staff, evaluates employee performance or reviews performance evaluations prepared by subordinates and approves training plans.

Plans, develops and manages a budget for the unit in accordance with departmental policy and procedures. Exercises direct authority and accountability for allocated funds to meet planned objectives. Authorises, commits and approves expenditures in accordance with approved budgets with the authority to reallocate funds among line objects.

Negotiates and arranges contracts with consulting firms and for the acquisition of services. Selects contractors for specific projects, assigns, directs, manages and evaluates the work according to contract specifications. Negotiates with suppliers for cost reductions/discounts.
3. COMMUNICATION: Provides expert advisory and consultative services to policy makers at all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academics and presents rationale on the practical application and interpretation of statistical data and information. This information is used as input to decision making for a vast array of economic and social policies, programs and other activities.

Writes and presents analytical material to be disseminated to a target audience ranging from the general public to a specialized audience (e.g. academics). When media representatives and others challenge or misinterpret findings, it is necessary to present logical arguments to justify the results and to defend the validity of statistical methods and approaches used in order to maintain the department’s reputation for producing high quality data.
Provides expert advice to STC and other professionals from the private sector or from other statistical agencies on statistical program findings and their application to the area of specialization.

Provides guidance to subordinate staff, other professionals and management on study results, on methods of socio-economic analysis, dissemination, or on statistical techniques and systems; comments on written material to be published by STC.
Negotiates agreements and arranges contracts with consulting firms and suppliers for the acquisition of services.
Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and groups to develop understanding, consensus and share knowledge of the program area.
4. KNOWLEDGE OF SPECIALIZED FIELDS: Knowledge of economic or sociology principles and theory to provide expert advisory and consultative services to clients on program results and on the concepts and methods used in the collection, compilation, analysis, presentation and interpretation of findings.

Extensive knowledge of current and emerging socio-economic issues in Canada and internationally such as the changing social context and the globalization of markets, particularly as they relate to all aspects of a statistical program. This knowledge is required to analyze program outputs, anticipate and understand needs for new data, and assess the impact on the area of specialization.

Knowledge of advanced statistical theories, methods (including data gathering and analysis techniques), concepts and practices used in the development, collection, compilation, analysis and interpretation of statistical data.

Management and coordination skills and knowledge of general and project management methods, techniques and practices to manage and coordinate the activities of a multi-disciplinary sub-division/operational area and supporting project teams.
5. CONTEXTUAL KNOWLEDGE: Knowledge of the divisional mandate, activities, priorities, practices, standards and procedures applicable to the work to incorporate them into the management of a statistical program to recommend changes to management.
Knowledge of the mandate, objectives, organization, practices, policies, culture and priorities of Statistics Canada to define the objectives and content of studies.
Knowledge of other statistical programs related to the area of expertise within the department, especially the concepts, methods, and databases used in other divisions.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies (e.g. confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations, data quality), practices and classification systems to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of studies.
Knowledge of the policies and programs of key client departments in order to determine their information requirements.

Knowledge of data users from governments and from the private sector to identify potential new markets, to understand client needs for statistical data or studies, to negotiate contracts and to provide expert advice on study results.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements to other departments, agencies, industry, members of the public and the media. Knowledge of the Statitstics and Privacy Acts is particulary important with respect to the security and confidentiality of information and data provided and to ensure that they and their subordinates do not release any information which may identify an individual or group without prior consent.
6. RESEARCH AND ANALYSIS: Reviews the conceptual framework of existing statistical programs and determines the need for development, modification and adaption. Programs involve a combination of statistical techniques and methods and the integration of data from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses). Source data have often been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts and must be translated into common concepts, taking into consideration the impact of the results on other statistical programs as well as departmental priorities.

Assesses and reviews statistical techniques, methods and approaches used in the collection, processing, analysis and dissemination of data within a program area (e.g. System of National Accounts, Demography, Health, Justice, Education, Labour, Prices, International Trade, Balance of Payments, Environment, etc.). Program areas are often unique in nature and involve different collection, processing, analysis and dissemination activities conducted concurrently.
Analyzes the results and findings of studies conducted by in-house analysts and consultants and provides senior management with interpretation and recommendations affecting social policy issues.

Researches gaps and inconsistencies in the collection, processing, analysis and dissemination methods and procedures used; reviews the conceptual framework used and the compatibility with other statistical programs. Problems to be resolved usually impact on other statistical programs.

Analysis is required to understand and interpret user needs for statistical information and to translate them into a timely and affordable information request. Clients are often uncertain of their data needs and are unfamiliar with statistical options, methods and techniques available.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Assistant Director
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: The role is strongly connected to identifying needs because it analyzes socio-economic trends and developments, analyzes user needs, defends proposals for new surveys, and recommends development of new statistical information or expansion of existing programs. It also mediates with governments, associations, corporations, and other stakeholders to understand needs and maintain relations with users and data suppliers. This is evidence of upstream need identification and program opportunity assessment. It ranks below 1.3 because the role not only identifies needs but more directly approves and shapes resulting objectives and program content. Future drivers such as fiscal restraint, prioritization, and changing user demand will likely require sharper triage of needs, stronger evidence-based scanning, and more explicit decisions on what needs can still be met.

key_activities: Directs, through subordinates, the work of a sub-division involved in statistical program operations, analysis, interpretation, marketing and dissemination.

1. Decision making: Reviews strategic directions for the management of significant surveys and recommends innovative solutions to address departmental goals and objectives. Approves survey content and design; sample estimation and imputation methods; data integration from different sources; sample sizes and allocations to maximize efficiency within resource constraints.

Provides expert recommendations and advice to senior officials and policy makers at all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academics on the socio-economic implications of surveys and studies and the effect of their results on policies, programs and regulations, on the practical application and interpretation of statistical data and information, on advanced analytical methods and techniques and the relevancy of their use in order to develop research or analytical projects.

Directs the conduct of in-depth and unique surveys in an area of specialization or wide-ranging and extensive reviews extending across a number of subject matter areas and determines the broad objectives and content of projects and develops solutions to complex methodology issues.
Defends proposals for the development of new surveys and negotiates the allocation of funding for the conduct of projects.

Directs the review and assessment of the overall quality and completeness of statistical program results. Develops recommendations for senior management on the objectives, content, and approaches of survey programs in order to develop new statistical information or programs or expand existing programs, and data concepts and definitions to be included in the programs.
2. Leadership and operational management: Directs, through subordinates, the work of a sub-division involved in high profile surveys and projects. Reviews strategic directions for the management of significant surveys and determines the parameters, priorities, broad objectives and extent of such surveys.

Develops long term plans and objectives and allocates human resources requirements to ensure that these goals are met. Directs recruitment activities for both, permanent and project team staff, and approves training and development plans. Prepares performance appraisals for subordinate staff, reviews performance appraisals prepared by subordinate supervisors, and resolves performance and disciplinary matters.

Plans, develops and manages budgets for projects, including estimates for salaries, professional fees and implementation costs, with authority to allocate/reallocate funds as needed. Submits cost estimates and projections to senior management and authorises expenditures in accordance with approved budgets.

Negotiates and approves contracts with consulting firms and for the acquisition of services. Selects contractors for specific projects, assigns, directs, manages and evaluates the work according to contract specifications.
3. Communication: Mediates with senior executives of major Canadian corporations, representatives of private sector associations, federal, provincial and municipal government departments, unions and universities to establish joint survey agreements, to maintain good relations and cooperation with the user community and data suppliers, to promote an understanding of programs, to market statistical products and services, and to monitor relevant concepts and practices related to the use and application of program results.

As a departmental representative, explains the results and statistical methods and approaches used in the conduct of studies and surveys to all levels of government, international organizations, the media and public. At this level, there is a particular requirement to deal with sensitive and political issues that could embarrass the department.

Defends proposals for the development of new surveys to address current socio-economic trends and developments at the national and international levels, and negotiates the allocation of funding for the conduct of such surveys and projects. Presents arguments and options and negotiates resources and timeframes for large-scale projects requiring the participation of data suppliers. It is not unusual to encounter resistance on the part of data suppliers. Major difficulties can be encountered as the projects involve the negotiation of significant resources and services with multiple milestones.

Writes analytical papers and articles on the interpretation of statistical surveys or projects and their application to the area of specialization and presents analytical material to media representatives to maintain the department’s reputation where there is a particular requirement to deal with sensitive and political issues that could embarrass the department.
Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and groups to develop consensus or share knowledge in a particular field.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Expert knowledge of advanced economic or sociology theories and principles relating to a specialized subject area to provide authoritative and expert advice to senior officials and policy advisors within and outside Statistics Canada on the results of unique economic and socio-economic studies and their impact on major program, policy or regulatory issues and to define the objectives, content and approaches of unique and complex analytical projects covering a broad area of specialization or a range of departmental statistical programs, to improve existing concepts or develop new concepts, to extend the application of statistics and to analyze data.

A deep understanding of the underlying theoretical concepts of economics, sociology and statistics as they relate to a group of specialized areas to develop and implement programs to produce statistics covering a wide range of issues.

A comprehensive knowledge of economic and social information to develop and implement programs to produce statistics depicting Canada’s population, labour force, economic life, education, housing, transportation and social and cultural life.

Knowledge of writing and editing skills and techniques to write and review papers, articles and reports and to determine and assess the design and content of studies, articles and reports that will be disseminated widely or published.

Knowledge of the principles and practices of management with regards to human and financial resources in order to direct the work of a sub-division through subordinate section chiefs, and/or multi-disciplinary departmental and interdepartmental project teams, working groups and committees.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of current and emerging socio-economic and political issues in Canada in relation to that of other industrialized countries such as the changed social context and the globalization of markets, particularly as they relate to all the aspects of a variety of statistical programs. This knowledge is necessary to defend proposals for the development of new surveys.

Knowledge of governmental policies, programs and regulatory issues in order to provide expert advice to senior officials and policy advisors, within and outside Statistics Canada, on the results and impact of unique economic and socio-economic studies.
Knowledge of the division mandate and priorities as well as subject-matter expertise is required to review strategic directions in the management of significant surveys.

Knowledge of the policies and programs of key client departments in order to mediate with their representatives to reach a consensus on the major issues affecting departments, industries and special interest groups, and to recommend priorities for new surveys and studies.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act is needed to explain the legislative requirements to other departments, agencies, industry, members of the public and the media. This knowledge, along with knowledge of the Privacy Act is also required to ensure that the organization meets its commitment to ensuring the confidentiality of all information provided to them and does not release any information that identifies an individual or group without prior consent.
Knowledge of a variety of Acts related to the area of expertise such as the Income Tax Act, the Excise Sales Tax Act, the Employment Insurance Act, and the Corporate Returns Act.
6. Research and analysis: Analyses current socio-economic trends and developments at the national and international levels and determines the implications of proposed areas of study. Analyses user needs in relation to current socio-economic trends and developments at the national and international levels, translates them into a concrete, timely and affordable information request, determines the implications of proposed areas of study and defends proposals for the development of new surveys.
Provides expert analysis and interpretation of program results, develops the overall conclusions and recommendations, reviews and approves analytical material and research papers for publication.
Directs the development of new methods and techniques for unique studies, assesses the implications of new approaches and develops solutions to complex issues.

Analyses the impact of study results on major program, policy and regulatory issues and provides authoritative and expert advice to senior officials and policy advisors within and outside Statistics Canada.

implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This subprocess is meaningfully related because the role gathers and analyzes international user needs and emerging issues to shape comparative studies and internal mobilization. Evidence includes: 'gathers, compiles, analyzes and interprets information and data requests from multilateral organizations,' 'researches and provides more background and supporting information for new or emerging topics,' and 'conducts research and comparative analysis on statistical products of different national statistical offices in order to recommend areas of improvement.' This fits identifying needs, especially from external users and environmental changes. It is ranked below 1.5 and 7.3 because the job appears to respond to and coordinate needs rather than formally set corporate output objectives. Future drivers such as governance, prioritization and modern methods may increase demand for more disciplined triage of international requests and sharper assessment of which emerging global topics warrant Statistics Canada engagement.

gsbpm_description: This sub-process identifies the statistical output objectives that are required to meet the user needs confirmed in sub-process 1.2 (Consult and confirm needs). It includes agreeing the suitability of the proposed outputs and their quality measures with users. Legal or normative frameworks (e.g. relating to confidentiality, methodologies), and available resources are important to consider when establishing output objectives.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: International Relations Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This subprocess is strongly relevant because the role does not merely identify needs; it also defines project objectives and priorities, prepares work plans, time frames and resource summaries, and determines the timing and scope of product and service delivery to multinational organizations and other NSOs. It assesses relevance and impact for Statistics Canada, determines which expert communities should respond, and coordinates delivery. That aligns with establishing output objectives by shaping what will be delivered, to whom, on what timeline and with what resources. This is slightly weaker than 1.1 because user need identification is more explicit and foundational in the work description, but stronger than most other subprocesses because the analyst materially influences scope, priorities and deliverables. Future drivers around governance, prioritization and efficiency are likely to change this work by forcing clearer enterprise decisions about international commitments, service levels, and trade-offs among scope, timeliness and internal capacity.

position_information.branch_division: International Cooperation and Corporate Statistical Methods Division
key_activities: HR A to Z index
HR service standards
Wellness at Statistics Canada

HR contact list
Corporate service providers

1. Decision Making: Analyzes the user requirements for data users of other national statistical offices (NSOs) in order to determine the most appropriate research and comparative analysis studies to do, as well as which sources of information, methods and approaches should be used. Modifies existing techniques or develops new methods such as for the dissemination and communication of statistical information.

As the focal point or project leader, defines project objectives and priorities, prepares work plans and summaries outlining approaches, time-frames and resources. Each project is unique in nature and decisions impact on the timing and scope of product and service delivery to multinational organizations and other national statistical offices. Decisions also affect capacity of Statistics Canada expert communities to continue to perform their regular duties. Recommendations lead to effective and efficient distribution of effort towards international cooperation objectives.

In order to provide advice and consultative services to internal subject matter experts participating in international cooperation projects in statistics, gathers relevant information from various sources (for example different NSOs, multilateral organizations, different ministries participating in the national statistical system of a particular country), performs appropriate analysis and interpretation, considers all possible options, impacts and outcomes, and makes decisions about recommending strategic improvements, involvement of subject matter experts, or impacts on planning and scheduling.

In order to effectively coordinate the preparation of briefing notes for the Chief Statistician attending international meetings, decisions need to be made about which expert community is doing work that best corresponds to each topic on the agenda, which in turn requires up-to-date knowledge of the research and development work going on at Statistics Canada, as well as its regular statistical programs. The position is also responsible for reviewing the briefing notes and seeking clarifications or revisions from the authors if they are deemed to be of insufficient quality.
Scope of decisions relates to coordination with multinational organizations, other National Statistical Offices, and departmental senior management.
2. Leadership And Operational Management: Plans and coordinates the work in support of technical assistance projects for national statistical offices and multilateral (international) organizations. Human resources responsibilities include selecting, coaching and training personnel; planning and assigning work; monitoring and follow-up; developing and implementing work plans and priorities; conducting performance reviews and taking disciplinary action when appropriate; managing through subordinate staff.

Operational management includes recommending resource needs; preparing cost estimates and projections; keeping projects on schedule and within budget; managing an operating budget; monitoring material and financial resources; reallocating resources within a set budget; providing input into financial planning exercises; supervision of staff.

Assists in the allocation of human and financial resources and monitors their usage relative to forecasts. This has a direct positive impact on the statistical processes of the NSO receiving the technical assistance, and ultimately a positive impact on the quality of official statistics globally.
Leads project teams involved in the conduct of technical assistance projects with other National Statistical offices or Statistical Agencies.
3. Communication: Gathers, compiles, analyzes and interprets information and data requests from multilateral (international) organizations, assesses the relevance and impact for Statistics Canada, and determines which expert community or communities should respond. Coordinates the delivery of data and information. Negotiates for deadline extensions or staggered delivery where appropriate. Ensures that all necessary approvals are secured prior to delivery. All correspondence both internal and external is professional, polite, grammatically and factually correct, timely and archived using information management current best practices.

Prepares analytical reports and work plans in the context of international cooperation, to be shared with international stakeholders. Interacts with participating countries and regional stakeholders, providing mutually acceptable solutions to the challenge of simultaneously meeting the needs of multiple stakeholders.

Prepare written reports or supervise staff in the preparation of written reports for internal and international stakeholders, to ensure that they are informed of the progress of statistical capacity building activities being conducted in the course of a large technical assistance project with foreign countries (where capacity building means showing senior managers at other NSOs better ways of planning, managing and executing their statistical programs so that they will bring positive changes to their own organizations).
Makes formal presentations of recommendations, supported by original research, to senior management at Statistics Canada and senior management of other NSOs and international organizations.

Meets with senior management upon their return from multinational events, to gather feedback, status and direction on topics and issues in which Statistics Canada expert communities are involved. Analyzes and interprets this information, and presents it to the expert communities, soliciting their continued contribution and involvement. Researches and provides more background and supporting information for new or emerging topics. Answers questions from the expert communities and ensures that they are in contact with the appropriate parties from other NSOs or multilateral (international) organizations.

The Chief Statistician of Canada attends several international meetings per year at which he actively participates in discussions about emerging issues of global concern (for example global warming or population censuses based solely on administrative data) or international partnerships on the development of new technology (for example how to exploit Big Data). In order to actively participate in these discussions, the Chief Statistician needs detailed and accurate briefing notes from Statistics Canada’s expert communities. Each meeting has approximately 20 different discussion topics. These topics are very briefly described on the meeting agenda, which is made available typically a couple of weeks prior to the meeting. The position analyses the agenda items and recruits the appropriate expert communities to prepare briefing notes. The position supports the expert communities by searching the internet (sites of multilateral organizations such as the UNECE, UNSD, OECD, IMF) for background documentation, coordinating correspondence between Statistics Canada and experts from other NSOs working on similar topics, and providing other relevant information to the experts such as the governance structure of multilateral organizations or briefing notes from other meetings attended by senior managers.

Communicates orally with senior managers of other NSOs and multilateral organizations in a professional manner. Gathers and shares information relevant to the successful participation of Statistics Canada experts in capacity building activities, international working groups or senior manager level steering meetings. Provides written documentation to both Statistics Canada and external stakeholders of recommendations or results of studies or analysis, and progress on on-going activities.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of economic/sociologic principles and practices as they relate to a specialized area as well as specific knowledge of other regions (for example the Caribbean or South America) to initiate and conduct projects to improve existing concepts in other countries or develop new approaches to extend the application of official statistics internationally.
Knowledge of project management concepts, methods and techniques to determine the scope and depth of research and analysis projects for international clients.

Knowledge is required of computer software applications to conduct analysis and document project results, including specialized software such as statistical sampling, computer assisted techniques, automated working papers, and flowcharting.

Knowledge of social science research methods, techniques and practices, including multi-disciplinary analysis methods, to carry out analysis on a variety of approaches regarding the coordination of a national statistical system or improving relations between an NSO and other federal ministries.

Skill in synthesizing information from diverse disciplines (management science, economics, and public policy administration, etc.) to propose solutions that are feasible, reflect current best practices, and are multifaceted, addressing several challenges simultaneously.

Knowledge of theories, principles and techniques of consultation, management, small group process, interviewing and counselling to lead project teams, to negotiate contracts for services and agreements with other institutions.
Operational management requires management skills and knowledge of the theories and principles of general and project management to lead a multi-disciplinary project team.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge is required of the strategic direction, culture, structure and organization, mandate, objectives and relevant policies, procedures and practices of the International Cooperation programs and initiatives. This knowledge is required to achieve operational objectives and results in an effective and efficient manner, and to incorporate them into the conduct and management of studies and projects.

Knowledge of the mandate, objectives and organization of Statistics Canada to manage subject matter studies and projects. Knowledge of other statistical programs (concepts, methods, and databases) related to the area of expertise to plan and implement statistical activities, to integrate conceptually different data from other programs, to explain variances and to recommend improvements to other statistical programs.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements to other departments, agencies and international organizations.

Knowledge of current and emerging socio-economic issues in Canada and internationally such as the changing social context and the globalization of markets, particularly as they relate to the area of expertise in a statistical program (e.g. System of National Accounts, Education, Health, Labour, Prices, Demography, International Trade, Balance of Payments, Environment, etc.). This knowledge is required to provide subject-matter advice, consultative services and to analyze and interpret data requests and assess their impact on the area of specialization.

Knowledge of other countries’ national statistical offices, multilateral (international) organizations (International Statistical Agencies) and non-government organizations in order to effectively communicate on approaches, methods, data and analysis for the purpose of strengthening statistical reporting.
6. Research and analysis: Analysis is required to understand and interpret requests for statistical information and to translate them into a concrete, timely and affordable information request.
Research gaps and overlaps in Statistics Canada’s involvement in international activities, and propose to senior management a strategic approach to achieving effective and efficient collaboration.
Conducts research and comparative analysis on statistical products of different national statistical offices in order to recommend areas of improvement.

Conducts research and comparative analysis of international contexts and statistical processes in order to recommend how Statistics Canada will respond and prepares and edits analytical reports, including recommendations for improving efficiency or effectiveness.

Analysis is required to understand and interpret user requirements for statistical information and to translate them into concrete and timely research studies. Conducts research and comparative analysis on topics such as but not limited to: statistical products of different national statistical offices; data and information requests from multilateral (international) organizations; the scope and depth of involvement of internal subject matter experts in international activities. From this research and comparative analysis, prepares and edits analytical reports, including recommendations for improving efficiency or effectiveness, and shares these reports with both internal and international stakeholders. At the outset clients are often uncertain of their data needs and are unfamiliar with options, methods and techniques available.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Head of Operations
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: The role materially connects to establish output objectives because it assesses client department policies and requirements for statistical information, defines the objectives, content and approaches of statistical programs, and presents recommendations to senior management to improve and expand program direction and elaborate new options. That is direct involvement in determining what outputs the program should deliver. This relationship is stronger than identify-needs because the evidence goes beyond recognizing needs to setting program objectives, scope and direction. Drivers such as governance and prioritization, cost realignment, and evolving client needs will likely make objective-setting more constrained, requiring sharper trade-offs among scope, quality, timeliness and affordability.

key_activities: Plans and leads the development of statistical operations to produce, evaluate, analyze, present and extend the application of statistics.
Reviews the survey collection framework for existing statistical programs and determines the need for development, modification and adaptation.
Coordinates and reviews collection, coding, processing and client-relation activities to determine changes in data needs and assesses their impact on divisional programs.
Provides expert advisory and consultative services to users on the collection, capture, coding and processing of statistical data.
Participates in or leads task forces or committees as an expert in data collection operations.
Manages a unit and project teams responsible for statistical program operations. Manages the financial resources attached to the statistical program.

1. Decision making: Assesses the policies and programs of key client departments to determine their requirements for statistical information, to identify the most appropriate sources of data, and to modify existing techniques, methods and approaches or develop new ones to meet specific needs.

Develops enhancements and recommends modifications to be made to the program content, coverage and operational procedures, such as new or modified data sources, concepts, methods and definitions to be applied.

Defines the objectives, content and approaches of statistical programs and presents recommendations to senior management to improve and expand the content and direction of existing programs and elaborate new program options.

Determines program priorities and milestones, and allocates and manages the human and financial resources of the program. Many program activities are conducted concurrently and occur within tight deadlines and involve a multi-disciplinary team approach where consensus must be maintained. Problems to be resolved can impact on other statistical programs and operations within the department.
Determines the concepts, definitions, standards and techniques to be applied in the development and conduct of statistical programs and in the reporting, analysis and presentation of findings.

Recommends survey content and design, sample estimation and imputation methods, data integration from different sources, sample sizes and allocations to maximize efficiency within resource constraints.

Provides input to management decisions and recommendations designed to develop or improve departmental policies and develop new program initiatives covering areas such as recruitment, official languages, employment equity, dissemination and confidentiality of information.
2. Leadership and operational management: Manages a unit involved in statistical operations and leads project teams for special projects. Determines program objectives and priorities and assesses the requirements of operational programs. Plans and schedules the work, resolves conflicting priorities, ascertains human resource needs, determines the appropriate selection methods (internal and external resources / contractors) to meet program and project objectives, recruits staff, evaluates employee performance or reviews performance evaluations prepared by subordinates and approves training plans.

Plans, develops and manages a budget for the unit in accordance with departmental policy and procedures. Exercises direct authority and accountability for allocated funds to meet planned objectives. Authorises, commits and approves expenditures in accordance with approved budgets with the authority to reallocate funds among line objects.

Negotiates cost reductions and arranges contracts with consulting firms and for the acquisition of services. Selects contractors for specific projects, assigns, directs, manages and evaluates the work according to contract specifications.
3. Communication: Provides expert advisory and consultative services to policy makers at all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academia. Explains and elaborates on statistical program findings and their practical application and interpretation of statistical data and information. This information is used as input to decision making for a vast array of economic and social policies, programs and other activities.

Writes and presents analytical material to be disseminated to a target audience ranging from the general public to a specialized audience (e.g. academia). When media representatives and others challenge or misinterpret findings, it is necessary to present logical arguments to justify the results and to defend the validity of statistical methods and approaches used in order to maintain the department’s reputation for producing high quality data.
Provides guidance on survey results, methods of socio-economic analysis and statistical techniques and systems.
Prepares, edits and evaluates analytical material to be published by Statistics Canada.
Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and groups to develop understanding, consensus and share knowledge of the program area.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of economic or sociology principles and theory to provide expert advisory and consultative services to clients on program results and on the concepts and methods used in the collection, capture, coding, processing and interpretation of findings.

Extensive knowledge of current and emerging socio-economic issues in Canada and internationally, such as the changing social context and the globalization of markets, particularly as they relate to all the aspects of a statistical program. This knowledge is required to analyze program outputs, anticipate and understand needs for new data, and assess the impact on the area of specialization.

Knowledge of advanced statistical theories, methods (including data gathering and analysis techniques), concepts and practices used in the collection, capture, coding, processing and interpretation of statistical data.

Management and coordination skills and knowledge of general and project management methods, techniques and practices to manage and coordinate the activities of a multi-disciplinary sub-division/operational area and supporting project teams.
Knowledge of the principles and practices of human and financial resource management is required to manage the work of a multi-disciplinary unit and project teams.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of the departmental and divisional mandate, activities, priorities, practices, standards and procedures applicable to the work to incorporate them into the management of a statistical program and to recommend changes to management.

Knowledge of other statistical programs (concepts, methods, and databases) related to the area of expertise to plan and implement statistical activities, to integrate conceptually different data from other programs, to explain variances and to recommend changes to other statistical programs.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies, (e.g. confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations, and data quality), practices and classification systems is required to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of operations.
Knowledge of the policies and programs of key client departments is needed to determine their information requirements.

Knowledge of data users from governments and from the private sector to identify potential new markets, to understand client needs for statistical data or studies, to negotiate contracts and to provide expert advice on survey results.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act is needed to explain the legislative requirements to data suppliers/users, and to negotiate special agreements. This knowledge, along with knowledge of the Privacy Act is also required to ensure that the organization meets its commitment to ensuring the confidentiality of all information provided to them and does not release any information that identifies an individual or group without prior consent.
Knowledge of a variety of Acts related to the area of expertise such as the Income Tax Act, the Excise Sales Tax Act, the Employment Insurance Act, and the Corporate Returns Act.
6. Research and analysis: Reviews the conceptual framework of existing statistical programs and determines the need for development, modification and adaption. Programs involve a combination of statistical techniques and methods and the integration of data from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses). Source data have often been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts and must be translated into common concepts, taking into consideration the impact of the result on other statistical programs as well as departmental priorities.

Assesses and reviews techniques and methods used to integrate and interpret massive volumes of data and resolves analytical and operational problems. Data can come from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses) and have often been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts. There is a requirement to integrate data into a common conceptual framework, and to identify and measure relationships among variables to produce statistical information.

Analyses the relative quality of data produced by statistical programs, determines reasons for variances; reviews the comparability of data over time and relevance in light of trends, developments, changing requirements, policy issues and socio-economic conditions.

Researches gaps and inconsistencies in the collection, capture, coding and processing methods and procedures used, reviews the conceptual framework used and the compatibility with other statistical programs. Problems to be resolved usually impact on other statistical operations.
Investigates client requirements for statistical information and determines the capacity and ability of existing or modified program activities to meet these requirements.

gsbpm_description: This sub-process checks whether current sources of data could meet user requirements and the conditions under which they would be available, including any restrictions on their use. An assessment of possible alternatives would normally include research into potential administrative or other non-statistical sources of data (e.g. privately-held data or “Big Data”), to: Determine whether they would be suitable for use for statistical purposes (e.g. the extent to which administrative concepts match data requirements, and whether the timeliness and quality of the data, security, and continuity of data supply are suitable); Assess the division of responsibilities between data suppliers and the statistical organisation; Check necessary ICT resources (e.g. data storage, technology required to handle incoming data and data processing) as well as any provision agreements with data suppliers (which could be legal or other agreements such as memoranda of understanding) for accessing and sharing the data (e.g. formats, delivery, accompanying metadata and quality check). When existing sources have been assessed, a strategy for filling any remaining gaps in the data requirement is prepared. This may include identifying possible partnerships with data holders or conducting a new survey to collect data if necessary. This sub-process also includes a more general assessment of the legal framework in which data would be collected and used, and may therefore identify proposals for changes to existing legislation or the introduction of a new legal framework.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 4
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This is the strongest relationship because the role "reviews data collection and information systems to determine the usefulness of the existing data sources," identifies and selects sources of information for development and operations, assesses feasibility and impact of new or modified programs, and interprets user needs while assessing the suitability of existing data products and services. That is direct evidence of checking source availability and suitability. This is stronger than adjacent collection or processing subprocesses because the description explicitly centers source usefulness, source selection, and suitability assessment. Future drivers such as administrative and alternative data expansion, metadata-driven discovery, privacy constraints, and cost pressure will likely shift this work further toward evaluating reusable non-survey data sources and their operational feasibility.

key_activities: Undertakes the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes.
Participates in the analysis of socio-economic trends and developments to assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs.

Suggests feedback on collection processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures following data analysis and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.
Provides assistance and subject matter advice to data users within and outside STC.
Undertakes subject matter studies/reviews in support of project teams or senior officers.
Leads project teams involved in special studies.

1. DECISION MAKING: Identifies and assesses changes and developments in the subject area, determines the impact on program subject-matter content and recommends alternative statistical methods and approaches.

Modifies existing techniques and approaches to improve program coverage or to meet specific needs and develops subject-matter concepts and definitions. Develops operational plans and project priorities and identifies areas necessitating study at the local, regional or national levels.

Reviews data collection and information systems to determine the usefulness of the existing data sources, to propose changes to the system and to assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs.

Identifies and evaluates problems in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical information to provide solutions or recommendations to management and to resolve subject-matter, conceptual and technical problems referred by staff.
2. LEADERSHIP AND OPERATIONAL MANAGEMENT: Leads project teams, determines goals, priorities and milestones, sets objectives, and plans and schedules the work, resolves conflicting priorities; assesses human resources needs, recommends the appropriate selection methods (internal and external resources / contractors) to meet program objectives, recruits staff, provides feedback on employee performance, develops training plans, motivates and maintains morale of employees.

Plans and budgets for special projects, including estimates for salaries, professional fees and implementation costs, with authority to allocate funds within budget. Provides input to budgets based on operational needs and by obtaining/providing cost estimates for personnel, supplies, equipment purchases and travel for use in developing section or division budgets. Procures goods and services according to approved budget allocations.
3. COMMUNICATION: Provides information and advice to managers, data users and clients on matters relating to subject-matter concepts used in the development and operation of a statistical database and to the data processing environment in general.

Discusses program subject-matter content requirements with operations managers, other subject matter and systems specialists, clients, service providers and others to comprehend and elaborate the framework and conditions within which statistical development and operations will occur. There is a requirement to understand the issues and resolve differences that can affect the efficiency of the division's operations and quality of outputs.

Liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development, to suggest improvements to ongoing programs, to negotiate procedural modifications and to establish project plans, priorities and target dates.
Writes and presents detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify divisional program content and applications.

Writes program information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports for use by colleagues, operational staff and management in the development, implementation and assessment of statistical programs.
4. KNOWLEDGE OF SPECIALIZED FIELDS: A thorough knowledge of the theories and principles of economics, econometric methods and techniques and of sampling theory are required, along with a working knowledge of survey design, time series and special analysis and forecasting.
Knowledge of current or emerging economic and social issues relating to the program area in order to identify and resolve existing and potential subject-matter conflicts, duplication and gaps.

Knowledge of the concepts, methods and techniques used in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical data in order to coordinate and advise on subject-matter development and resolve subject-matter concept and definition issues.

Knowledge of system analysis and design, computer processing, generalized survey software packages to manage the design, development, testing, maintenance and implementation of processing systems; to design specifications for the testing of data, and to maintain and develop databases.
Knowledge of high level programming languages, utility programs or statistical packages to retrieve and manipulate data.
Knowledge of management techniques and principles to manage financial and human resources, either directly or within a matrix management environment.
5. CONTEXTUAL KNOWLEDGE: Knowledge of statistical programs within Statistics Canada related to the area of expertise in order to identify and select sources of information for development and operations and/or special studies and to identify and evaluate data conflicts.

Knowledge of contacts within key client departments to establish a liaison; to understand need for statistical data, and to provide advice and guidance on subject-matter concepts, methods, techniques and results.
Knowledge of the divisional mandate, objectives, priorities, practices, standards, processes and procedures in order to coordinate and manage on-going operational activities and/or special projects.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements to data suppliers, users and others with respect to the manipulation, storage and retrieval of data. Knowledge of the Statistics and Privacy Acts is particulary important with respect to the security and confidentiality of information and data provided and to ensure that they and their subordinates do not release any information which may identify an individual or group without prior consent.
6. RESEARCH AND ANALYSIS: Analyzes and synthesizes geographic, demographic, social, economic and/or labour market characteristics and prepares profiles and forecasts.
Reviews the development of new subject-matter methods, concepts and definitions and conducts studies and analytical projects to improve existing surveys and data.

Analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to determine the need for modification or replacement with alternative systems, methods and procedures.
Interprets program and user needs for statistical information, assesses the suitability of existing data products and services and translates them into a concrete, timely and affordable product.
Reviews the results of projects and surveys in order to provide interpretation and analysis on subject-matter concepts and definitions, survey methods, statistical applications and techniques used.
7. PHYSICAL Effort: Frequent, extended periods of sitting at a work station while keyboarding, proofreading, telephoning, reviewing data, or writing text.
Occasional periods of physical exertion, such as bending and stretching to retrieve, organize and distribute publications, printouts, documents or files.
There may be an occasional requirement to carry equipment, presentation material and document cases to meetings or during travel.
8. SENSORY Effort: There is an occasional requirement for sensory observation when comparing old and new versions of data.
9. WORKING CONDITIONS: The work is performed in an open office environment with constant exposure to glare from a computer screen, noise from conversations, telephones, traffic and equipment in the immediate area.
Work is performed while facing multiple and sometimes competing demands from clients, frequent changes in methods, systems and approaches and competing priorities and changing deadlines.
There is a requirement to travel nationally and/or internationally, several times a year for several days at a time.

Encounters resistance from external clients or respondents who may be impatient, irritated or uncooperative, as well as program criticism from clients, the media, and members of the public and special interest groups.
