implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Development Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This is the strongest relationship because the role explicitly develops and coordinates the implementation and maintenance of manual and automated operations for collection, capture, coding and processing, and evaluates trends and developments in data collection, capture, coding and processing. It also reviews respondent relations issues and recommends new approaches, which aligns directly with collection design choices around instruments, methods, and operational procedures. This is stronger than setup or run collection because the wording emphasizes development, new approaches, and operational redesign rather than only day-to-day execution. Future drivers such as online-first collection, AI-enabled respondent interaction, administrative and alternative data intake, and adaptive collection will materially change this role toward redesigning collection methods and hybrid acquisition strategies.

key_activities: Develops and coordinates the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, capture, coding and processing of data.
Reviews data inconsistency and integrity problems, recommends new approaches and resolves reporting and respondent relations issues.
Evaluates changes in statistical needs of clients, as well as trends and developments in data collection, capture, coding and processing.
Provides advisory and consultative services to users regarding collection and production efficiency and/or quality.
Participates as a statistical operations representative on teams and working groups throughout the department.
Leads project teams involved in the collection, capture, coding and processing of statistical data.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This is the strongest match because the role explicitly "reviews and designs questionnaires for the collection of data" and develops procedures for the collection of data. Those are direct collection-design responsibilities involving instrument content and collection procedures. This is stronger than adjacent design or processing subprocesses because questionnaire design is explicit evidence for 2.3. Future drivers such as online-first collection, adaptive collection, administrative and alternative data substitution, and digital collection tooling are likely to change this work materially by shifting design away from traditional questionnaires toward mixed-source and digital collection methods.

key_activities: Under guidance, participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes.
Identifies statistical trends and developments.

Under guidance, participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.
Provides data and assistance to users, within and outside Statistics Canada.
Under guidance, participates in subject matter studies and reviews to support the work of project teams or senior officers.

1. Decision making: Evaluates problems in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical information to provide solutions or recommendations to management and to resolve subject-matter, conceptual and technical problems.

Prepares special data releases, reviews and verifies data sources and methods of data compilation; develops and implements procedures for the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of data.
Develops and outlines new statistical methods, concepts and procedures or modifies existing techniques and approaches to incorporate changes in subject-matter content and definitions.
Reviews and designs questionnaires for the collection of data and assesses the timeliness, completeness, accuracy and validity of data compiled for publication.
Implements enhancements or modifications to processing systems and applications used to collect, process, edit, compile and present statistical data.
Develops or modifies statistical methods, concepts, definitions and approaches to improve existing surveys or to meet specific needs.
2. Leadership and operational management: Participates in project teams, work groups, meetings and conferences in order to develop and improve work methods and practices, share knowledge and contribute to skill development.

Monitors and tracks time spent on activities for the purposes of recording and recovering such costs from the client. Incurs and accounts for petty cash, credit card, taxi voucher, bus pass, and other expenditures.
3. Communiction: Writes and presents detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify divisional systems and applications.

Writes program information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports for use by colleagues, operational staff and management in the development, implementation and assessment of statistical programs.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of statistical or economic theory and principles and the relevance of their application in a computerized environment, and the methods and techniques of data gathering, statistical estimation and economic modeling.
Knowledge of current and emerging economic and social issues relating to the program area in order to identify and assess trends and issues represented by statistical data series.
Knowledge of methods, techniques, practices and procedures to conduct studies and to develop/assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs.

Knowledge of the socio-economic concepts and methods to assess the validity of collected and processed data, the output from computer applications, the validity of database contents and results from alternative manipulations of data.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of the subject and universe of the survey is required in order to propose suitable changes to statistical or reporting methods and techniques.
Knowledge of program context, program sponsors, participants and respondents to plan and organize the retrieval and processing of data for research or development projects.

Knowledge of the divisional mandate, objectives, programs, policies and activities to adhere to the various statistical and administrative practices and procedures involved in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical data.
Knowledge of data sources within Statistics Canada in order to locate, analyze and compare related statistical output to ensure consistency and reliability

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to ensure understanding and application in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of data. The position must have a particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data to ensure their own actions are in compliance.
6. Research and analysis: Analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services.
Assesses and determines the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored.
Analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: The strongest relationship is with Design collection because the role evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results; prepares operational specifications and training for manual and automated collection; recommends procedures, software and hardware for collection; and works with data suppliers or respondents to explain data formatting and statistical concepts. The key activities also explicitly state participation in implementation, conduct and maintenance of collection operations. This is stronger than adjacent subprocesses because the evidence points to determining and refining collection methods and operational specifications, not merely running existing collection. Future drivers such as administrative and alternative data expansion, online-first collection, secure digital collection, and enterprise platforms will materially change this work toward digital acquisition, supplier coordination, API-based collection and more adaptive collection design, increasing skill needs in digital collection architecture and secure source integration.

key_activities: Participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data.
Evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives.
Provides assistance and advice to users on methods and practices of collection and coding.
Participates on data collection and operations teams.
Provides input to training materials concerning data collection operations and assists in training delivery.

1. Decision making: Evaluates methods, procedures and results of statistical collection, coding and processing operations and recommends alternatives. The surveys worked on can vary in size, complexity and methods.
Prepares and distributes procedures, operational specifications and training for the manual and automated collection, coding and processing of statistical data.
Develops and outlines system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems.
Evaluates and recommends appropriate procedures, software and hardware for the collection, coding and processing of data.
Develops test cases and data from functional specifications and specifies testing approaches for own use and use by other program staff to ensure that computer applications meet requirements.
2. Leadership and operational management: Participates in project teams, work groups, meetings and conferences in order to develop and improve work methods and practices, share knowledge and contribute to skill development.

Monitors and tracks time spent on activities for the purposes of recording and recovering such costs from the client. Incurs and accounts for petty cash, credit card, taxi voucher, bus pass, and other expenditures.
3. Communication: Responds orally and in writing to enquiries from managers, employees and the general public to provide information on the operation of divisional systems and processes and the use of program results.
Writes survey information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports.
Designs and prepares statistical tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text for use in regular and ad-hoc publications.
Prepares reports and recommendations outlining options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection and processing systems.

Meets with subject matter and systems specialists, clients, service providers and others, in order to comprehend and elaborate on the conditions within which statistical operations will occur. There is a requirement to understand the issues and resolve differences that can affect the efficiency of the division's operations and quality of outputs.

Contacts data suppliers or respondents to obtain their collaboration in responding to surveys, to clarify problems or irregularities. This may necessitate having to explain technical procedures for obtaining the data in the appropriate format, or to clarify and explain statistical concepts.
Participates in departmental meetings and working groups in order to share knowledge within an area of operational expertise.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of the underlying statistical and economic principles and concepts required for the collection, coding and processing of data.
Knowledge of the concepts, methods and techniques used in the management and control of statistical collection, coding and processing activities.
Knowledge of methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications.

Knowledge of methods and practices of operating personal computers in a network environment and of using databases and software packages (word processing, statistical analysis, graphics, spreadsheets, etc.) to prepare correspondence, reports and presentations.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows, general software packages and computer languages, for designing the specifications for testing of applications, the application and conversion of databases, and the maintenance and use of databases both for regular production of statistical data and for ad hoc manipulations and retrievals.

Knowledge of developments and changes in the subject area that may affect the efficiency and validity of data collection, coding and processing in order to devise and modify operational systems and processes.

Knowledge of divisional mandates, objectives, programs, policies and activities to adhere to the various statistical and administrative practices and procedures involved in the collection, coding and processing of statistical data.

Knowledge of data sources and contacts within Statistics Canada in order to locate, analyze and compare statistical output to ensure consistency and reliability; and external to Statistics Canada to obtain collaboration in the provision of statistical information and to verify the accuracy of data.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to ensure understanding and application in the collection, coding and processing of data. The position must have a particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data to ensure their own actions are in compliance.
6. Research and analysis: Analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results.
Assesses and reviews system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems.

Analyses reported data and work results and prepares reports for program managers or subject matter specialists, presenting findings on how the survey was conducted, problems encountered in implementing concepts, definitions, classifications and other instructions, and recommending alternatives.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Head of Operations
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This is the strongest relationship because the position owns collection framework and operational design decisions. Evidence includes 'reviews the survey collection framework for existing statistical programs and determines the need for development, modification and adaptation,' coordinates 'collection, coding, processing and client-relation activities,' and recommends 'survey content and design.' This is stronger than workflow design because the work description explicitly foregrounds collection framework ownership and redesign. Future drivers such as online-first collection, administrative and alternative data expansion, AI-assisted collection, secure digital channels, and operational efficiency will materially reshape the role and required skills.

key_activities: Plans and leads the development of statistical operations to produce, evaluate, analyze, present and extend the application of statistics.
Reviews the survey collection framework for existing statistical programs and determines the need for development, modification and adaptation.
Coordinates and reviews collection, coding, processing and client-relation activities to determine changes in data needs and assesses their impact on divisional programs.
Provides expert advisory and consultative services to users on the collection, capture, coding and processing of statistical data.
Participates in or leads task forces or committees as an expert in data collection operations.
Manages a unit and project teams responsible for statistical program operations. Manages the financial resources attached to the statistical program.

1. Decision making: Assesses the policies and programs of key client departments to determine their requirements for statistical information, to identify the most appropriate sources of data, and to modify existing techniques, methods and approaches or develop new ones to meet specific needs.

Develops enhancements and recommends modifications to be made to the program content, coverage and operational procedures, such as new or modified data sources, concepts, methods and definitions to be applied.

Defines the objectives, content and approaches of statistical programs and presents recommendations to senior management to improve and expand the content and direction of existing programs and elaborate new program options.

Determines program priorities and milestones, and allocates and manages the human and financial resources of the program. Many program activities are conducted concurrently and occur within tight deadlines and involve a multi-disciplinary team approach where consensus must be maintained. Problems to be resolved can impact on other statistical programs and operations within the department.
Determines the concepts, definitions, standards and techniques to be applied in the development and conduct of statistical programs and in the reporting, analysis and presentation of findings.

Recommends survey content and design, sample estimation and imputation methods, data integration from different sources, sample sizes and allocations to maximize efficiency within resource constraints.

Provides input to management decisions and recommendations designed to develop or improve departmental policies and develop new program initiatives covering areas such as recruitment, official languages, employment equity, dissemination and confidentiality of information.
2. Leadership and operational management: Manages a unit involved in statistical operations and leads project teams for special projects. Determines program objectives and priorities and assesses the requirements of operational programs. Plans and schedules the work, resolves conflicting priorities, ascertains human resource needs, determines the appropriate selection methods (internal and external resources / contractors) to meet program and project objectives, recruits staff, evaluates employee performance or reviews performance evaluations prepared by subordinates and approves training plans.

Plans, develops and manages a budget for the unit in accordance with departmental policy and procedures. Exercises direct authority and accountability for allocated funds to meet planned objectives. Authorises, commits and approves expenditures in accordance with approved budgets with the authority to reallocate funds among line objects.

Negotiates cost reductions and arranges contracts with consulting firms and for the acquisition of services. Selects contractors for specific projects, assigns, directs, manages and evaluates the work according to contract specifications.
3. Communication: Provides expert advisory and consultative services to policy makers at all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academia. Explains and elaborates on statistical program findings and their practical application and interpretation of statistical data and information. This information is used as input to decision making for a vast array of economic and social policies, programs and other activities.

Writes and presents analytical material to be disseminated to a target audience ranging from the general public to a specialized audience (e.g. academia). When media representatives and others challenge or misinterpret findings, it is necessary to present logical arguments to justify the results and to defend the validity of statistical methods and approaches used in order to maintain the department’s reputation for producing high quality data.
Provides guidance on survey results, methods of socio-economic analysis and statistical techniques and systems.
Prepares, edits and evaluates analytical material to be published by Statistics Canada.
Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and groups to develop understanding, consensus and share knowledge of the program area.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of economic or sociology principles and theory to provide expert advisory and consultative services to clients on program results and on the concepts and methods used in the collection, capture, coding, processing and interpretation of findings.

Extensive knowledge of current and emerging socio-economic issues in Canada and internationally, such as the changing social context and the globalization of markets, particularly as they relate to all the aspects of a statistical program. This knowledge is required to analyze program outputs, anticipate and understand needs for new data, and assess the impact on the area of specialization.

Knowledge of advanced statistical theories, methods (including data gathering and analysis techniques), concepts and practices used in the collection, capture, coding, processing and interpretation of statistical data.

Management and coordination skills and knowledge of general and project management methods, techniques and practices to manage and coordinate the activities of a multi-disciplinary sub-division/operational area and supporting project teams.
Knowledge of the principles and practices of human and financial resource management is required to manage the work of a multi-disciplinary unit and project teams.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of the departmental and divisional mandate, activities, priorities, practices, standards and procedures applicable to the work to incorporate them into the management of a statistical program and to recommend changes to management.

Knowledge of other statistical programs (concepts, methods, and databases) related to the area of expertise to plan and implement statistical activities, to integrate conceptually different data from other programs, to explain variances and to recommend changes to other statistical programs.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies, (e.g. confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations, and data quality), practices and classification systems is required to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of operations.
Knowledge of the policies and programs of key client departments is needed to determine their information requirements.

Knowledge of data users from governments and from the private sector to identify potential new markets, to understand client needs for statistical data or studies, to negotiate contracts and to provide expert advice on survey results.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act is needed to explain the legislative requirements to data suppliers/users, and to negotiate special agreements. This knowledge, along with knowledge of the Privacy Act is also required to ensure that the organization meets its commitment to ensuring the confidentiality of all information provided to them and does not release any information that identifies an individual or group without prior consent.
Knowledge of a variety of Acts related to the area of expertise such as the Income Tax Act, the Excise Sales Tax Act, the Employment Insurance Act, and the Corporate Returns Act.
6. Research and analysis: Reviews the conceptual framework of existing statistical programs and determines the need for development, modification and adaption. Programs involve a combination of statistical techniques and methods and the integration of data from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses). Source data have often been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts and must be translated into common concepts, taking into consideration the impact of the result on other statistical programs as well as departmental priorities.

Assesses and reviews techniques and methods used to integrate and interpret massive volumes of data and resolves analytical and operational problems. Data can come from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses) and have often been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts. There is a requirement to integrate data into a common conceptual framework, and to identify and measure relationships among variables to produce statistical information.

Analyses the relative quality of data produced by statistical programs, determines reasons for variances; reviews the comparability of data over time and relevance in light of trends, developments, changing requirements, policy issues and socio-economic conditions.

Researches gaps and inconsistencies in the collection, capture, coding and processing methods and procedures used, reviews the conceptual framework used and the compatibility with other statistical programs. Problems to be resolved usually impact on other statistical operations.
Investigates client requirements for statistical information and determines the capacity and ability of existing or modified program activities to meet these requirements.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Supervisor
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: Strongest fit because the position develops collection procedures and determines methods for 'collection, capture, coding and processing of data.' Evidence includes supervising a unit involved in 'development of collection procedures,' investigating client requirements to determine methods and approaches for collection, and recommending changes to questionnaire design, survey content and operational procedures. This is stronger than processing design because collection procedure development is the clearest direct responsibility. Future drivers such as online-first collection, administrative and alternative data intake, secure digital channels and automation will materially reshape the job and required skills.

key_activities: Integrates and analyzes statistical outputs and reviews/certifies the quality and completeness of the individual program results.
Develops statistical systems and processes, evaluates the quality of collections’ outputs and prepares analytical reviews.
Evaluates changes in the statistical needs of clients and develops new methods of collecting, coding and processing data.
Provides advice and guidance to users on the development, operation and use of collection systems and processes.
Acts as a divisional data collection and operations representative on projects, task forces or committees in various roles.
Supervises a unit or project team involved in the development of collection procedures and the capture, coding and processing of statistical data.

1. Decision making: Investigates client requirements for statistical information, determines the sources of information, methods and approaches to be used for the collection, capture, coding and processing of data. Modifies existing techniques, methods and approaches or develops new ones to meet specific needs. Each statistical project is unique in nature and decisions impact on other statistical programs.

Defines project objectives and priorities and assesses the requirements to conduct developmental projects; prepares work plans and summaries outlining approaches, time-frames and resources involved in the operation of statistical systems and processes.
Proposes modifications to program content and coverage and operational procedures, such as new or modified data sources, concepts, methods and definitions.

Evaluates the effectiveness of existing and new statistical systems and processes, the quality and completeness of outputs and pepares studies and reports for use by senior management of the division in assessing the attainment of divisional program objectives and the cost, efficiency and utilization of divisional resources.

Develops and distributes guidelines, instructions and procedures for the development, use and evaluation of statistical systems and processes for use by operational and systems staff when planning and performing their work.
Establishes and implements specifications, guidelines and procedures for the maintenance and safeguarding of computer systems, equipment, databases and files.

Develops proposals and recommends changes and improvements on questionnaire design, enhancements or modifications to survey content and coverage, revisions to collection or production systems and processes, and the implementation of new hardware and software to be used in data collection or statistical production activities.
2. Leadership and operational management: Supervises a unit involved in statistical operations and/or leads project teams for special projects. Determines goals, priorities and milestones, sets objectives, and plans and schedules the work, resolves conflicting priorities; identifies human resources needs, determines the appropriate selection methods (internal and external resources / contractors) to meet program or project objectives, recruits staff, evaluates employee performance, develops training plans, motivates and maintains morale of employees.

Plans and budgets for on-going operations and/or special projects, including estimates for salaries, professional fees and implementation costs, with authority to allocate/reallocate funds within the budget. Provides input to budgets based on operational needs and by obtaining/providing cost estimates for personnel, supplies, equipment purchases and travel for use in developing section or division budgets. Establishes and negotiates contracts for projects. Responsible for the acquisition of goods and services, according to the budget allocated.
3. Communication: Provides advice and interpretation to various data users at all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academics, on the practical use and application of statistical data and information. This often requires the adaptation and presentation of complex information in basic, understandable formats. When media representatives and others challenge or misinterpret findings, it is necessary to further explain the results and statistical methods and approaches used in order to maintain the department’s reputation for producing high quality data.
Writes and presents subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify operational systems and processes or explain program results.
Prepares and explains specifications and guidelines to be used by others in developing and operating systems and processes.
Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and groups to develop consensus or share knowledge within the area of operational expertise.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of economic/sociology principles and practices as they relate to a specialized area as well as specific knowledge of the area to initiate and conduct projects to improve existing concepts or to develop new approaches to extend processing systems applications for the collection, capture, coding and processing of statistical data. This knowledge is also required to provide expert advice and guidance to users within and outside Statistics Canada.
Knowledge of statistical theories, methods (including data gathering and analysis techniques), concepts and practices used in the collection, capture, coding and processing of statistical data.
Knowledge of the principles and practices of human and financial resource management is required to manage the work of a multi-disciplinary unit and/or a project team.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of the departmental and divisional mandate, objectives and organization is required in the management of statistical operations.
Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies, practices and classification systems is needed to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of statistical projects and activities.
Knowledge of other statistical programs related to the area of expertise within the department, especially the concepts, methods, and databases used in other divisions.

Knowledge of departmental publication, marketing and dissemination policies and practices in order to establish common divisional policies and practices in the preparation of statistical tables, charts, explanatory notes etc. for dissemination to user and/or subject matter clients.

Knowledge of data suppliers is required to discuss data reporting agreements, as well as knowledge of data users from governments and the private sector to identify potential new markets, to understand client needs for complex statistical data or studies, to negotiate contracts and to provide advice on survey results.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements to data suppliers, users and others with respect to the collection, capture, coding and processing of data. Knowledge of the Statitstics and Privacy Acts is particulary important with respect to the security and confidentiality of information and data provided and to ensure that they and their subordinates do not release any information which may identify an individual or group without prior consent.
6. Research and analysis: Interprets the relative quality of data produced, determines reasons for variances, its comparability over time and its relevancy in light of changing requirements, trends, developments, policy issues and socio-economic conditions.

Reviews and modifies existing operational techniques, methods and approaches or develops new ones to meet specific needs. Operational programs may involve a combination of statistical techniques and methods and the integration of data from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses). Often, the data have often been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts and must be translated into common concepts.

Reviews and resolves gaps and inconsistencies in the collection, capture, coding and processing methods and procedures used, reviews the conceptual framework used and the compatibility with other statistical programs, reviews and resolves technical and conceptual problems referred by staff or project teams.

Analysis is required to understand and interpret user requirements for statistical information and translate them into a concrete, timely and affordable information request. Clients are often uncertain of their data needs and are unfamiliar with statistical options, methods and techniques available.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Supervisor
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: The role has a strong connection to design collection because it investigates client requirements, determines sources of information and methods for collection, proposes questionnaire design changes, and develops improvements to survey content and coverage and collection procedures. It also advises users on development and operation of collection systems and processes. This is stronger than specify-needs subprocesses because the evidence points to translating requirements into concrete collection approaches and procedures. Future drivers including online-first strategy, alternative and administrative data expansion, secure collection channels, and operational efficiency pressures will materially affect the collection methods and systems this role designs.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Head of Operations
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: The role strongly relates to design collection because it reviews the survey collection framework, recommends survey content and design, develops new or modified data sources and operational procedures, and assesses client requirements to identify the most appropriate sources of data. These are direct strategic collection-design responsibilities with program-level authority. This is stronger than source-availability checking because the evidence is not just source assessment but determining collection content, design and operational approaches. Future-state drivers such as online-first collection, administrative and alternative data substitution, adaptive methods, and cyber/privacy constraints will significantly change collection strategy and the skills needed to redesign collection models.

key_activities: Plans and leads the development of statistical operations to produce, evaluate, analyze, present and extend the application of statistics.
Reviews the survey collection framework for existing statistical programs and determines the need for development, modification and adaptation.
Coordinates and reviews collection, coding, processing and client-relation activities to determine changes in data needs and assesses their impact on divisional programs.
Provides expert advisory and consultative services to users on the collection, capture, coding and processing of statistical data.
Participates in or leads task forces or committees as an expert in data collection operations.
Manages a unit and project teams responsible for statistical program operations. Manages the financial resources attached to the statistical program.

1. Decision making: Assesses the policies and programs of key client departments to determine their requirements for statistical information, to identify the most appropriate sources of data, and to modify existing techniques, methods and approaches or develop new ones to meet specific needs.

Develops enhancements and recommends modifications to be made to the program content, coverage and operational procedures, such as new or modified data sources, concepts, methods and definitions to be applied.

Defines the objectives, content and approaches of statistical programs and presents recommendations to senior management to improve and expand the content and direction of existing programs and elaborate new program options.

Determines program priorities and milestones, and allocates and manages the human and financial resources of the program. Many program activities are conducted concurrently and occur within tight deadlines and involve a multi-disciplinary team approach where consensus must be maintained. Problems to be resolved can impact on other statistical programs and operations within the department.
Determines the concepts, definitions, standards and techniques to be applied in the development and conduct of statistical programs and in the reporting, analysis and presentation of findings.

Recommends survey content and design, sample estimation and imputation methods, data integration from different sources, sample sizes and allocations to maximize efficiency within resource constraints.

Provides input to management decisions and recommendations designed to develop or improve departmental policies and develop new program initiatives covering areas such as recruitment, official languages, employment equity, dissemination and confidentiality of information.
2. Leadership and operational management: Manages a unit involved in statistical operations and leads project teams for special projects. Determines program objectives and priorities and assesses the requirements of operational programs. Plans and schedules the work, resolves conflicting priorities, ascertains human resource needs, determines the appropriate selection methods (internal and external resources / contractors) to meet program and project objectives, recruits staff, evaluates employee performance or reviews performance evaluations prepared by subordinates and approves training plans.

Plans, develops and manages a budget for the unit in accordance with departmental policy and procedures. Exercises direct authority and accountability for allocated funds to meet planned objectives. Authorises, commits and approves expenditures in accordance with approved budgets with the authority to reallocate funds among line objects.

Negotiates cost reductions and arranges contracts with consulting firms and for the acquisition of services. Selects contractors for specific projects, assigns, directs, manages and evaluates the work according to contract specifications.
3. Communication: Provides expert advisory and consultative services to policy makers at all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academia. Explains and elaborates on statistical program findings and their practical application and interpretation of statistical data and information. This information is used as input to decision making for a vast array of economic and social policies, programs and other activities.

Writes and presents analytical material to be disseminated to a target audience ranging from the general public to a specialized audience (e.g. academia). When media representatives and others challenge or misinterpret findings, it is necessary to present logical arguments to justify the results and to defend the validity of statistical methods and approaches used in order to maintain the department’s reputation for producing high quality data.
Provides guidance on survey results, methods of socio-economic analysis and statistical techniques and systems.
Prepares, edits and evaluates analytical material to be published by Statistics Canada.
Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and groups to develop understanding, consensus and share knowledge of the program area.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of economic or sociology principles and theory to provide expert advisory and consultative services to clients on program results and on the concepts and methods used in the collection, capture, coding, processing and interpretation of findings.

Extensive knowledge of current and emerging socio-economic issues in Canada and internationally, such as the changing social context and the globalization of markets, particularly as they relate to all the aspects of a statistical program. This knowledge is required to analyze program outputs, anticipate and understand needs for new data, and assess the impact on the area of specialization.

Knowledge of advanced statistical theories, methods (including data gathering and analysis techniques), concepts and practices used in the collection, capture, coding, processing and interpretation of statistical data.

Management and coordination skills and knowledge of general and project management methods, techniques and practices to manage and coordinate the activities of a multi-disciplinary sub-division/operational area and supporting project teams.
Knowledge of the principles and practices of human and financial resource management is required to manage the work of a multi-disciplinary unit and project teams.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of the departmental and divisional mandate, activities, priorities, practices, standards and procedures applicable to the work to incorporate them into the management of a statistical program and to recommend changes to management.

Knowledge of other statistical programs (concepts, methods, and databases) related to the area of expertise to plan and implement statistical activities, to integrate conceptually different data from other programs, to explain variances and to recommend changes to other statistical programs.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies, (e.g. confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations, and data quality), practices and classification systems is required to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of operations.
Knowledge of the policies and programs of key client departments is needed to determine their information requirements.

Knowledge of data users from governments and from the private sector to identify potential new markets, to understand client needs for statistical data or studies, to negotiate contracts and to provide expert advice on survey results.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act is needed to explain the legislative requirements to data suppliers/users, and to negotiate special agreements. This knowledge, along with knowledge of the Privacy Act is also required to ensure that the organization meets its commitment to ensuring the confidentiality of all information provided to them and does not release any information that identifies an individual or group without prior consent.
Knowledge of a variety of Acts related to the area of expertise such as the Income Tax Act, the Excise Sales Tax Act, the Employment Insurance Act, and the Corporate Returns Act.
6. Research and analysis: Reviews the conceptual framework of existing statistical programs and determines the need for development, modification and adaption. Programs involve a combination of statistical techniques and methods and the integration of data from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses). Source data have often been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts and must be translated into common concepts, taking into consideration the impact of the result on other statistical programs as well as departmental priorities.

Assesses and reviews techniques and methods used to integrate and interpret massive volumes of data and resolves analytical and operational problems. Data can come from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses) and have often been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts. There is a requirement to integrate data into a common conceptual framework, and to identify and measure relationships among variables to produce statistical information.

Analyses the relative quality of data produced by statistical programs, determines reasons for variances; reviews the comparability of data over time and relevance in light of trends, developments, changing requirements, policy issues and socio-economic conditions.

Researches gaps and inconsistencies in the collection, capture, coding and processing methods and procedures used, reviews the conceptual framework used and the compatibility with other statistical programs. Problems to be resolved usually impact on other statistical operations.
Investigates client requirements for statistical information and determines the capacity and ability of existing or modified program activities to meet these requirements.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: The role has a strong connection to design collection because it 'reviews and designs questionnaires for the collection of data,' develops procedures for collection, and suggests feedback on collection methods and activities. This is stronger than source assessment because the evidence is about instrument and procedure design rather than strategic source choice. Future drivers like online-first collection, APIs, digital tools, and alternative data will materially change required skills toward digital collection design, metadata-aware instruments, and mixed-source collection procedures.

key_activities: Under guidance, participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes.
Identifies statistical trends and developments.

Under guidance, participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.
Provides data and assistance to users, within and outside Statistics Canada.
Under guidance, participates in subject matter studies and reviews to support the work of project teams or senior officers.

1. Decision making: Evaluates problems in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical information to provide solutions or recommendations to management and to resolve subject-matter, conceptual and technical problems.

Prepares special data releases, reviews and verifies data sources and methods of data compilation; develops and implements procedures for the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of data.
Develops and outlines new statistical methods, concepts and procedures or modifies existing techniques and approaches to incorporate changes in subject-matter content and definitions.
Reviews and designs questionnaires for the collection of data and assesses the timeliness, completeness, accuracy and validity of data compiled for publication.
Implements enhancements or modifications to processing systems and applications used to collect, process, edit, compile and present statistical data.
Develops or modifies statistical methods, concepts, definitions and approaches to improve existing surveys or to meet specific needs.
2. Leadership and operational management: Participates in project teams, work groups, meetings and conferences in order to develop and improve work methods and practices, share knowledge and contribute to skill development.

Monitors and tracks time spent on activities for the purposes of recording and recovering such costs from the client. Incurs and accounts for petty cash, credit card, taxi voucher, bus pass, and other expenditures.
3. Communiction: Writes and presents detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify divisional systems and applications.

Writes program information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports for use by colleagues, operational staff and management in the development, implementation and assessment of statistical programs.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of statistical or economic theory and principles and the relevance of their application in a computerized environment, and the methods and techniques of data gathering, statistical estimation and economic modeling.
Knowledge of current and emerging economic and social issues relating to the program area in order to identify and assess trends and issues represented by statistical data series.
Knowledge of methods, techniques, practices and procedures to conduct studies and to develop/assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs.

Knowledge of the socio-economic concepts and methods to assess the validity of collected and processed data, the output from computer applications, the validity of database contents and results from alternative manipulations of data.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of the subject and universe of the survey is required in order to propose suitable changes to statistical or reporting methods and techniques.
Knowledge of program context, program sponsors, participants and respondents to plan and organize the retrieval and processing of data for research or development projects.

Knowledge of the divisional mandate, objectives, programs, policies and activities to adhere to the various statistical and administrative practices and procedures involved in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical data.
Knowledge of data sources within Statistics Canada in order to locate, analyze and compare related statistical output to ensure consistency and reliability

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to ensure understanding and application in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of data. The position must have a particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data to ensure their own actions are in compliance.
6. Research and analysis: Analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services.
Assesses and determines the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored.
Analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 4
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: A strong second fit is design collection. Evidence includes 'reviews data collection and information systems to determine the usefulness of existing data sources,' proposes changes to systems, and suggests recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities. This is stronger than frame/sample because there is explicit evidence on collection systems, procedures and survey methods, but not much on sampling design. Future drivers such as online-first collection, digital instruments, APIs, adaptive collection and alternative sources will reshape this work and create skill gaps in digital collection design and secure mixed-mode collection.

key_activities: Undertakes the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes.
Participates in the analysis of socio-economic trends and developments to assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs.

Suggests feedback on collection processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures following data analysis and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.
Provides assistance and subject matter advice to data users within and outside STC.
Undertakes subject matter studies/reviews in support of project teams or senior officers.
Leads project teams involved in special studies.

1. DECISION MAKING: Identifies and assesses changes and developments in the subject area, determines the impact on program subject-matter content and recommends alternative statistical methods and approaches.

Modifies existing techniques and approaches to improve program coverage or to meet specific needs and develops subject-matter concepts and definitions. Develops operational plans and project priorities and identifies areas necessitating study at the local, regional or national levels.

Reviews data collection and information systems to determine the usefulness of the existing data sources, to propose changes to the system and to assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs.

Identifies and evaluates problems in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical information to provide solutions or recommendations to management and to resolve subject-matter, conceptual and technical problems referred by staff.
2. LEADERSHIP AND OPERATIONAL MANAGEMENT: Leads project teams, determines goals, priorities and milestones, sets objectives, and plans and schedules the work, resolves conflicting priorities; assesses human resources needs, recommends the appropriate selection methods (internal and external resources / contractors) to meet program objectives, recruits staff, provides feedback on employee performance, develops training plans, motivates and maintains morale of employees.

Plans and budgets for special projects, including estimates for salaries, professional fees and implementation costs, with authority to allocate funds within budget. Provides input to budgets based on operational needs and by obtaining/providing cost estimates for personnel, supplies, equipment purchases and travel for use in developing section or division budgets. Procures goods and services according to approved budget allocations.
3. COMMUNICATION: Provides information and advice to managers, data users and clients on matters relating to subject-matter concepts used in the development and operation of a statistical database and to the data processing environment in general.

Discusses program subject-matter content requirements with operations managers, other subject matter and systems specialists, clients, service providers and others to comprehend and elaborate the framework and conditions within which statistical development and operations will occur. There is a requirement to understand the issues and resolve differences that can affect the efficiency of the division's operations and quality of outputs.

Liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development, to suggest improvements to ongoing programs, to negotiate procedural modifications and to establish project plans, priorities and target dates.
Writes and presents detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify divisional program content and applications.

Writes program information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports for use by colleagues, operational staff and management in the development, implementation and assessment of statistical programs.
4. KNOWLEDGE OF SPECIALIZED FIELDS: A thorough knowledge of the theories and principles of economics, econometric methods and techniques and of sampling theory are required, along with a working knowledge of survey design, time series and special analysis and forecasting.
Knowledge of current or emerging economic and social issues relating to the program area in order to identify and resolve existing and potential subject-matter conflicts, duplication and gaps.

Knowledge of the concepts, methods and techniques used in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical data in order to coordinate and advise on subject-matter development and resolve subject-matter concept and definition issues.

Knowledge of system analysis and design, computer processing, generalized survey software packages to manage the design, development, testing, maintenance and implementation of processing systems; to design specifications for the testing of data, and to maintain and develop databases.
Knowledge of high level programming languages, utility programs or statistical packages to retrieve and manipulate data.
Knowledge of management techniques and principles to manage financial and human resources, either directly or within a matrix management environment.
5. CONTEXTUAL KNOWLEDGE: Knowledge of statistical programs within Statistics Canada related to the area of expertise in order to identify and select sources of information for development and operations and/or special studies and to identify and evaluate data conflicts.

Knowledge of contacts within key client departments to establish a liaison; to understand need for statistical data, and to provide advice and guidance on subject-matter concepts, methods, techniques and results.
Knowledge of the divisional mandate, objectives, priorities, practices, standards, processes and procedures in order to coordinate and manage on-going operational activities and/or special projects.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements to data suppliers, users and others with respect to the manipulation, storage and retrieval of data. Knowledge of the Statistics and Privacy Acts is particulary important with respect to the security and confidentiality of information and data provided and to ensure that they and their subordinates do not release any information which may identify an individual or group without prior consent.
6. RESEARCH AND ANALYSIS: Analyzes and synthesizes geographic, demographic, social, economic and/or labour market characteristics and prepares profiles and forecasts.
Reviews the development of new subject-matter methods, concepts and definitions and conducts studies and analytical projects to improve existing surveys and data.

Analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to determine the need for modification or replacement with alternative systems, methods and procedures.
Interprets program and user needs for statistical information, assesses the suitability of existing data products and services and translates them into a concrete, timely and affordable product.
Reviews the results of projects and surveys in order to provide interpretation and analysis on subject-matter concepts and definitions, survey methods, statistical applications and techniques used.
7. PHYSICAL Effort: Frequent, extended periods of sitting at a work station while keyboarding, proofreading, telephoning, reviewing data, or writing text.
Occasional periods of physical exertion, such as bending and stretching to retrieve, organize and distribute publications, printouts, documents or files.
There may be an occasional requirement to carry equipment, presentation material and document cases to meetings or during travel.
8. SENSORY Effort: There is an occasional requirement for sensory observation when comparing old and new versions of data.
9. WORKING CONDITIONS: The work is performed in an open office environment with constant exposure to glare from a computer screen, noise from conversations, telephones, traffic and equipment in the immediate area.
Work is performed while facing multiple and sometimes competing demands from clients, frequent changes in methods, systems and approaches and competing priorities and changing deadlines.
There is a requirement to travel nationally and/or internationally, several times a year for several days at a time.

Encounters resistance from external clients or respondents who may be impatient, irritated or uncooperative, as well as program criticism from clients, the media, and members of the public and special interest groups.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Regional Program Manager (Data Collection)
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This subprocess is relevant because the position "participates in the development of strategies and business solutions for data collection and transmission requirements," provides advice on proposed questionnaire design and survey content and coverage, evaluates response patterns and respondent behaviour, and recommends revisions to collection systems and processes. These are direct collection-design contributions, especially around instruments, modes, operational methods, and respondent interaction. It is ranked below 4.3 and 4.2 because the role participates in and advises on design rather than owning enterprise-level design authority. Future drivers such as adaptive collection, online-first strategy, AI-enabled respondent support, administrative and alternative data use, and modular/reusable collection tooling are likely to shift this work toward more digital mode design, source substitution, and redesign of questionnaires and collection workflows.

key_activities: Leads and coordinates the 7-day statistical data collection activities for either telephone interviewing (CATI) or personal interviewing (CAPI or PAPI) programs; including the management of the Statistical Survey Operations (SSO) Interviewers and Senior Interviewers as well as the supervision of subordinates and interdisciplinary teams.
Assesses the cost, quality, efficiency, productivity and security of the functions and activities associated with the data collection, processing, editing, and compilation of statistical outputs.
Evaluates trends and developments in data collection concepts, methods and techniques including response patterns and respondent behaviour.
Participates in the development of strategies and business solutions for data collection and transmission requirements.
Sollicits participation from non-respondents and resolves complaints.
Acts as a regional representative on departmental projects, task forces and committees and provides advice on proposed questionnaire design and survey content and coverage.

1. Decision making: Prepares and reviews correspondence, manuals and data to ensure completeness, accuracy, integrity and compliance with job requirements. Develops and implements alternate work methods and models and proposes changes and improvements to questionnaire design, enhancements or modifications to survey content and coverage, revisions to collection systems and processes, and the implementation of new hardware and software for use in data collection activities.
Develops operational plans and schedules to manage, organize and control the 7-day data collection activities.

Develops guidelines, instructions and procedures for the use and evaluation of statistical systems and processes and for the maintenance and safeguarding of computer systems, equipment, databases and files.

Identifies and assesses new statistical methods, techniques and practices and the associated costs and limitations to identify the availability of respondents and to ensure quality control of data, to evaluate the suitability of new hardware and software, and to identify and determine the short and long term program impact and benefits.
2. Leadership and operational management: Leads and coordinates multi-disciplinary project teams, committees or work groups comprising professional, technical, administrative and interviewers engaged in initiating, developing and implementing programs. Identifies and recommends human resources needs and levels to meet program and project goals and objectives within branch mandate. Approves work plans and priorities. In collaboration with Regional Management, establishes organizational structures, recommends classification levels, assigns responsibilities to team or group members, monitors progress and performance, provides guidance and direction on career development and approves individual training plans.
Establishes and monitors program budgets, including both main estimate and cost recovery funding, to ensure that funds are spent appropriately, with authority to reallocate funds among line objects.

Plans and budgets for the management and operation of the regional CATI or CAPI program in accordance with departmental policy and procedures. Responsibilities include identifying content and cost of development and operational requirements, estimating salary and travel costs, professional fees and equipment costs.
3. Communication: Discusses and negotiates with subject matter and systems specialists, clients, service providers and other stakeholders to come to an agreement on the development of questionnaires, collection applications, and the framework and conditions within which statistical programs will occur. There is a requirement to understand issues and to resolve differences that can affect the efficiency and quality of program operations and outputs.
Responds orally or in writing to inquiries from managers, employees and the general public to provide information and advice, to solicit participation from non-respondents and to resolve complaints.

Prepares schedules, work plans and summaries outlining approaches, time-frames and resources involved in the operation of statistical collection systems and processes. The information is used by senior management to prepare program plans and has an impact on the nature, scope and cost of divisional statistical activities.

Prepares evaluation reports outlining the effectiveness of existing and new statistical systems and processes and the quality and completeness of data. Senior management uses this information to assess the attainment of program objectives and the cost, efficiency and utilization of regional resources.

Provides advice to senior management and subject matter experts regarding proposed changes to questionnaire design, modifications to survey content and coverage, revisions to collection systems and processes, and the implementation of new hardware and software used in data collection activities.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Practical knowledge of socio-economic concepts, methods and techniques applied in the development and operation of statistical programs.

Knowledge of financial and human resources management, and of project management methods, techniques and practices to develop proposals and work plans, to establish and monitor resource requirements, schedules and progress, to establish and manage project teams, and to resolve problems related to the development and operation of the division's systems and processes.
Knowledge of questionnaire development to outline specifications and requirements for the collection and processing of statistical information and to provide feedback to subject matter experts.
Knowledge of communication principles and techniques in order to negotiate program requirements, present and explain options and recommendations and resolve operational disputes.
Knowledge of training methods, techniques and practices to develop and present operational training modules.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of trends and developments in data collection processes to select and integrate new computer hardware and software technology and applications in mass statistical data capture and conversion systems and processes.
Knowledge of the trends and developments in data collection concepts, methods and techniques to evaluate response patterns and respondent behavior and to provide feedback to subject matter experts.

Knowledge and understanding of Statistics Canada’s mandate, programs, objectives, policies and procedures in areas such as survey methodology, operations integration, data confidentiality and security, dissemination and marketing to coordinate and ensure the development and operation of divisional programs consistent with departmental requirements.

Knowledge of the content and operation of the Agency’s household and business survey programs and their impact upon systems and processes to determine and devise procedures and standards to be applied in operational activities.
Knowledge of the Statistical Survey Operations organization, its collective agreements, grievance procedures, policies and directives to ensure equitable treatment of all staff.
Knowledge of the Regional Operations Branch mandate, objectives, standards and procedures to coordinate and manage on-going development and operational activities and/or special projects.
Knowledge of the structure and operation of internal client organizations to establish and maintain a framework for the collection, exchange and dissemination of information.

Knowledge and understanding of the structure, operation and practices of Statistics Canada and Regional Operations Branch service areas, such as human resources and finance, in order to access the services of such areas.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act pertaining to data security and confidentiality to ensure adherence in all development and operational activities. Knowledge of the Canada Labor Code to ensure safe working conditions exist for all employees. Knowledge of the Financial Administration Act, the Public Service Employment Act and related policies and directives.
6. Research and analysis: Evaluates trends and developments in data collection concepts, methods and techniques, including response patterns and respondent behaviour. Prepares assessments of questionnaire design, concepts, change in technology, respondent reaction and understanding for feedback to senior management and survey clients.

Interprets the relative quality of data produced, determines reasons for variances, its comparability over time and its relevancy in light of changing requirements, trends, developments, policy issues and socio-economic conditions.

Reviews and modifies existing operational techniques, methods and approaches or develops new ones to meet specific needs. Operational programs may involve a combination of statistical techniques and methods and the integration of data from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses).

Reviews and resolves gaps and inconsistencies in the collection methods and procedures, reviews the conceptual framework used and the compatibility with other statistical programs, reviews and resolves technical and conceptual problems referred by staff or project teams. Reviews the development of new subject-matter methods, concepts and definitions and conducts studies and analytical projects to improve existing surveys and data.

Analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to determine the need for modification or replacement with alternative systems, methods and procedures.
Interprets program and user needs for statistical information, assesses the suitability of existing data products and services and translates them into a concrete, timely and affordable product.
Reviews the results of projects and surveys in order to provide interpretation and analysis on subject-matter concepts and definitions, survey methods, statistical applications and techniques used.
7. PHYSICAL Effort: Frequent, extended periods of sitting at a work station while keyboarding, proofreading, telephoning, reviewing data, or writing text.
Occasional periods of physical exertion, such as bending and stretching to retrieve, organize and distribute publications, printouts, documents or files.
There may be an occasional requirement to carry equipment, presentation material and document cases to meetings or during travel.
8. SENSORY Effort: There is an occasional requirement for sensory observation when comparing old and new versions of data.
9. WORKING CONDITIONS: The work is performed in an open office environment with constant exposure to glare from a computer screen, noise from conversations, telephones, traffic and equipment in the immediate area.
Work is performed while facing multiple and sometimes competing demands from clients, frequent changes in methods, systems and approaches and competing priorities and changing deadlines.
There is a requirement to travel nationally and/or internationally, several times a year for several days at a time.

Encounters resistance from external clients or respondents who may be impatient, irritated or uncooperative, as well as program criticism from clients, the media, and members of the public and special interest groups.

Decrease of approximately 900 full-time equivalents by 2028-29 increases the need for methods that are sustainable with fewer operational staff
New tools and methods enable redesigned estimation and integration approaches that improve throughput and lower unit costs

safe, respectful, and supportive work environments

a decrease of approximately 900 full-time equivalents by 2028-29
cultural change associated with modernization and evolving ways of working
embed accessibility and inclusive design principles into its digital platforms
enhancing employee development so employees feel confident in leveraging new programming and analytical tools and methods
equipping managers to effectively guide and support employees as they advance their work and navigate change
invest in employee well-being through training, engagement and awareness initiatives

supporting employees and equipping managers to lead teams effectively through transitions
supporting employees and leaders through workforce adjustment pressures
