impact_mechanisms: AI, new programming and analytical tools, and modern open-source technologies directly change the methods available for coding, validation, imputation, estimation, and integration
Analytical expertise and training are required to design robust processing and analysis methodologies using new tools and methods
Leadership capacity, management competencies, and disciplined decision-making are needed to approve methodological changes and manage associated risks
Supporting employees through transitions and mentorship are necessary where staff must adopt unfamiliar methods while maintaining production
Reduced workforce capacity and realistic sequencing of work constrain how quickly advanced methods can be introduced into production design

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Principal Consumer Prices Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: The strongest relationship is with Design processing and analysis because the role is fundamentally about developing, reviewing, and implementing statistical methods, concepts, techniques and processes for the temporal and spatial consumer price index program. Evidence includes 'develops new methods and techniques', 'oversees and coordinates the review of established statistical methods and processes', 'implements new systems or methodologies and processes', and 'determines the objectives, content and methodology' of studies. This is stronger than needs specification because the job owns methodological and process design decisions with high program impact. Future drivers such as modern statistical methods, big data, AI/automation, integrated pipelines, and operational efficiency will most directly reshape this work through redesign of coding, integration, estimation, validation and production methods for CPI and related index programs.

key_activities: Plans and implements long term strategies for the development, enhancement and operation of the highly specialized temporal and spatial consumer price index program. Develops new methods and techniques based on leading edge international developments, to meet the needs of the highly specialized temporal and spatial consumer price index program. Assesses the implications of new approaches and makes recommendations for their adoption.

Performs detailed analysis, evaluation and review of statistical methods and concepts to improve existing data and determines changes in the statistical needs of clients, assessing the impact on the critical programs and developing options and strategies to manage complex issues and multi-stakeholder relations.

Provides expert recommendations, analysis and advice to senior managers in government (from various divisions within Statistics Canada and in key client departments such as Finance Canada and the Bank of Canada) and officials in industry (data providers and users), academia, other national and international statistical institutions and special interest groups.

Oversees and coordinates the review of established statistical methods and processes within the highly specialized realm of temporal and spatial consumer prices indexes. Determines departmental and government-wide impacts and implications and makes recommendations for change.
Implements new systems or methodologies and processes to meet client demands, identifies new statistical methods, techniques and practices and evaluates their cost, efficiency and productivity
Supervision of project teams responsible for statistical outputs, research projects or studies and management of the financial resources attached to each project.

Work is done within the context of temporal and spatial indexes which are used throughout Statistics Canada (i.e., Producer Prices program and the Canadian System of Macroeconomic Accounts), throughout government and industry to index payments worth billions of dollars, and by the Bank of Canada, as the basis for the country’s inflation targeting and monetary policy. Impact of errors is extremely high and cuts across Statistics Canada, other departments and throughout the economy. These factors add to the priority, complexity and scrutiny of the work of this position.

Decision Making: Reviews and evaluates statistical program methods and concepts to improve existing data, to develop new techniques and methods of producing, evaluating and analyzing data and to extend the use and application of departmental statistical programs. Recommendations based on this work have the ability to influence the direction of major corporate initiatives, programs and policies, including those related to big data (e.g., scanner data, web-scraped data).

Initiates changes and implements new systems or methodologies and processes, identifies and assesses new statistical methods, techniques and practices and the associated costs and limitations, identifies the availability and reliability of new data sources, evaluates the suitability of new hardware and software, and identifies and determines the short and long term program impact and benefits. Recommendations lead to changes in approach for the program and take into consideration risks and impacts related to the changes and the use of the resulting program data for indexing and monetary policy purposes.

Manages complex studies related to the temporal and spatial consumer prices program, determines the objectives, content and methodology of such work, defines and sets priorities and milestones, selects and evaluates analytical techniques and methods to be used to integrate and interpret massive volumes of data and organizes the review and presentation of findings. Problems to be resolved usually impact other statistical programs such as Producer Prices and the Canadian System of Macroeconomic Accounts.

Determines objectives and priorities for specific studies and provides expert advice and innovative solutions and recommendations to senior management on course of action and outcomes, or on significant issues affecting temporal and spatial price index programs.
Leadership And Operational Management: Provides advanced subject matter expertise within a multi-disciplinary departmental and interdepartmental project team environment to facilitate big data or temporal and spatial consumer price index research and development activities and establishes objectives and priorities to achieve long term program goals.

Assesses and recommends human and financial resource needs to achieve research and project objectives. Monitors the scope, schedule and cost of the work against approved baselines. Provides input into ongoing and strategic financial planning exercises.

Manages multi-disciplinary intradepartmental and/or interdepartmental project teams involved in research and development activities and establishes objectives and priorities to achieve long term project goals.
For project team members, establishes work objectives and training related to project requirements, monitors achievements and provides input into performance evaluations.
Communication: Provides expert advice and consultative services to senior officials and policy makers at all levels of government, business and national agencies and academics on the results of research and analytical studies, economic and socio-economic theories and principles and statistical concepts and methods as they relate to temporal and spatial consumer price indices.

Attends divisional and intradepartmental meetings and represents the division in interdepartmental and international meetings, conferences and groups to develop consensus or share knowledge in the field of temporal and spatial consumer price indices or big data. Represents, expresses and defends the viewpoint, priorities, conceptual integrity and the validity of methods of the program in venues where decisions are made in order to promote the organization’s interests and influence conceptual directions.

When addressing the general public, explains in clear terms the interpretation of complex data and conceptual frameworks, reasons for variances in the results and the trends derived. When addressing a specialized public, it is also necessary to provide more detailed explanations of the concepts, statistical and analytical approaches used. When media representatives challenge or misinterpret the results of surveys or projects, it is necessary to further explain the results and statistical methods and approaches used in layman’s terms in order to maintain the department's reputation for producing high quality data.
Knowledge of specialized fields: Expert knowledge of economic and sociological principles, concepts and theories, especially as they relate to price index number theory, and specific knowledge of temporal and spatial consumer price indexes. This knowledge is required to provide expert advice on the results of surveys and studies to data users, to STC senior management and to other professionals within and outside STC. It is also required to provide expert evaluation of impacts and risks associated with proposed program changes on the use of the resulting program data for other Statistics Canada programs such as the Producer Prices program and the Canadian System of Macroeconomic Accounts, as well as for government-wide and economy-wide uses such as indexation and monetary policy uses.

Expert knowledge of systems, systems design and practices relevant for the maintenance and development of the temporal and spatial price index statistical programs. *related to the development environment only

Expert knowledge of statistical theories, methods, concepts and practices used in the development, collection, compilation, analysis and interpretation of temporal and spatial price index data in order to develop new methods and techniques and provide expert advice to internal and external stakeholders.
Advanced knowledge of resource and project management practices and principles in order to manage project teams and deliver on high priority projects related to temporal and spatial price indexes.

Advanced knowledge of the methodologies related to the highly specialized fields, such as big data in order to performed detailed analysis and assess new methods relevant to temporal and spatial price indexes.

Knowledge of quantitative analytical methods is required to integrate and interpret massive volumes of data within the context of temporal and spatial price index programs and to provide technical advice to other professionals.
Writing and editing skills to write papers, articles and reports and to determine and assess the design and content of studies, articles and reports that will be disseminated widely or published.
Contextual knowledge: Advanced knowledge of international frameworks (Canadian System of Macroeconomic Accounts, Prices, etc.), their conceptual building blocks and their interdependencies to contribute in a meaningful way to the evaluation and impact assessment of concepts and compilation methods within the realm of temporal and spatial price indexes.

Knowledge of divisional mandate, policies, priorities, practices, standards and procedures as well as existing databases and conceptual frameworks applicable to the work to incorporate them into the conduct and management of analytical and development projects and to determine or recommend changes.

Knowledge of STC mandate, policies, priorities, practices and classification systems as well as existing data bases, conceptual frameworks, and the statistical methods and procedures applicable to the work, to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of statistical projects and activities, and in the elaboration of recommendations for change to the program.

Knowledge of current and emerging economic issues in Canada and internationally as they relate to temporal and spatial price indexes, to understand needs for new data, analyze the data and assess their impact on the work of Consumer Prices Division and share expertise internally and/or with international organizations.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent legislation such as the Foreign Service Directives, and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements to other departments (e.g., Bank of Canada, Finance Canada, Treasury Board Secretariat), agencies, industry, members of the public and the media. Knowledge of the Statistics Act and Privacy Acts is particularly important with respect to the security and confidentiality of information and data provided and to ensure that they and their subordinates do not release any information which may identify an individual or group without prior consent, and to apply within the context of establishing big data applications for use in the temporal and spatial price index programs.

Knowledge of the uses of temporal and spatial indexes within the mandates and legislation of other federal organizations such as the Bank of Canada, Finance Canada and Treasury Board Secretariat. This knowledge is important so that proposed changes to the temporal and spatial index programs can be assessed to ensure that outputs continue to meet the legislated requirements and mandates of stakeholders without negative impacts on those uses.
Research and analysis: Investigates and assesses changes in the statistical needs of clients, determines the extent and approaches of surveys or studies such as the sources of information, statistical techniques, methods and approaches to be used for the collection, processing, analysis and dissemination of price index data. Modifies existing techniques, methods and approaches or develops new ones to meet specific needs.

Investigates and challenges existing conceptual frameworks from multiple disciplines and examines multiple variables from distinct sources within the realm of temporal and spatial price indexes to reach new conclusions or generate new solutions. Researches cutting-edge applications of new data sources, including those related to big data to make recommendations on changes to the program. Recommendations made result from work which is evaluated through the lenses of conceptual integrity, operational viability and a deep understanding of the needs of key users for applying the data for indexing and monetary policy purposes.

Evaluates various data sources for relevance and accuracy when integrating them into the statistical program data. Continuously researches and evaluates new data sources in order to maintain the program's relevance and accuracy.

Interprets the relative quality of data produced, determines reasons for variances, its comparability over time and its relevance in light of changing requirements, trends, developments, policy issues and economic conditions. It is necessary to understand and interpret present policy issues and the economic conditions of Canadians.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Supervisor
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This is the strongest relationship because the role directly develops statistical systems and processes, develops new methods of collecting, coding and processing data, modifies existing techniques and approaches, and establishes guidelines and procedures for operational and systems staff. It also evaluates effectiveness of systems and output quality, and reviews conceptual and technical problems across collection, capture, coding and processing. Those are core responsibilities for designing processing and analysis methods rather than simply operating them. Future-state drivers such as AI and automation, administrative and linked data, modern methods, and modular reusable components will likely reshape this work toward automated coding, rule-based validation, integrated multi-source processing, and stronger methodological governance.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Head of Operations
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This is the strongest relationship because the role determines concepts, definitions, standards and techniques to be applied in development and conduct of statistical programs, recommends sample estimation and imputation methods, data integration from different sources, and reviews techniques and methods used to integrate and interpret large volumes of data. These are core design decisions for processing and analysis methodology, with clear decision-making authority and governance responsibility. This is stronger than operational subprocesses because the role is setting methodological direction for programs. Future drivers such as AI and automation, alternative and linked data expansion, modern statistical methods, and pipeline orchestration will materially reshape this work toward enterprise-scale method modernization and stronger governance of automated processing methods.

key_activities: Plans and leads the development of statistical operations to produce, evaluate, analyze, present and extend the application of statistics.
Reviews the survey collection framework for existing statistical programs and determines the need for development, modification and adaptation.
Coordinates and reviews collection, coding, processing and client-relation activities to determine changes in data needs and assesses their impact on divisional programs.
Provides expert advisory and consultative services to users on the collection, capture, coding and processing of statistical data.
Participates in or leads task forces or committees as an expert in data collection operations.
Manages a unit and project teams responsible for statistical program operations. Manages the financial resources attached to the statistical program.

1. Decision making: Assesses the policies and programs of key client departments to determine their requirements for statistical information, to identify the most appropriate sources of data, and to modify existing techniques, methods and approaches or develop new ones to meet specific needs.

Develops enhancements and recommends modifications to be made to the program content, coverage and operational procedures, such as new or modified data sources, concepts, methods and definitions to be applied.

Defines the objectives, content and approaches of statistical programs and presents recommendations to senior management to improve and expand the content and direction of existing programs and elaborate new program options.

Determines program priorities and milestones, and allocates and manages the human and financial resources of the program. Many program activities are conducted concurrently and occur within tight deadlines and involve a multi-disciplinary team approach where consensus must be maintained. Problems to be resolved can impact on other statistical programs and operations within the department.
Determines the concepts, definitions, standards and techniques to be applied in the development and conduct of statistical programs and in the reporting, analysis and presentation of findings.

Recommends survey content and design, sample estimation and imputation methods, data integration from different sources, sample sizes and allocations to maximize efficiency within resource constraints.

Provides input to management decisions and recommendations designed to develop or improve departmental policies and develop new program initiatives covering areas such as recruitment, official languages, employment equity, dissemination and confidentiality of information.
2. Leadership and operational management: Manages a unit involved in statistical operations and leads project teams for special projects. Determines program objectives and priorities and assesses the requirements of operational programs. Plans and schedules the work, resolves conflicting priorities, ascertains human resource needs, determines the appropriate selection methods (internal and external resources / contractors) to meet program and project objectives, recruits staff, evaluates employee performance or reviews performance evaluations prepared by subordinates and approves training plans.

Plans, develops and manages a budget for the unit in accordance with departmental policy and procedures. Exercises direct authority and accountability for allocated funds to meet planned objectives. Authorises, commits and approves expenditures in accordance with approved budgets with the authority to reallocate funds among line objects.

Negotiates cost reductions and arranges contracts with consulting firms and for the acquisition of services. Selects contractors for specific projects, assigns, directs, manages and evaluates the work according to contract specifications.
3. Communication: Provides expert advisory and consultative services to policy makers at all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academia. Explains and elaborates on statistical program findings and their practical application and interpretation of statistical data and information. This information is used as input to decision making for a vast array of economic and social policies, programs and other activities.

Writes and presents analytical material to be disseminated to a target audience ranging from the general public to a specialized audience (e.g. academia). When media representatives and others challenge or misinterpret findings, it is necessary to present logical arguments to justify the results and to defend the validity of statistical methods and approaches used in order to maintain the department’s reputation for producing high quality data.
Provides guidance on survey results, methods of socio-economic analysis and statistical techniques and systems.
Prepares, edits and evaluates analytical material to be published by Statistics Canada.
Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and groups to develop understanding, consensus and share knowledge of the program area.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of economic or sociology principles and theory to provide expert advisory and consultative services to clients on program results and on the concepts and methods used in the collection, capture, coding, processing and interpretation of findings.

Extensive knowledge of current and emerging socio-economic issues in Canada and internationally, such as the changing social context and the globalization of markets, particularly as they relate to all the aspects of a statistical program. This knowledge is required to analyze program outputs, anticipate and understand needs for new data, and assess the impact on the area of specialization.

Knowledge of advanced statistical theories, methods (including data gathering and analysis techniques), concepts and practices used in the collection, capture, coding, processing and interpretation of statistical data.

Management and coordination skills and knowledge of general and project management methods, techniques and practices to manage and coordinate the activities of a multi-disciplinary sub-division/operational area and supporting project teams.
Knowledge of the principles and practices of human and financial resource management is required to manage the work of a multi-disciplinary unit and project teams.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of the departmental and divisional mandate, activities, priorities, practices, standards and procedures applicable to the work to incorporate them into the management of a statistical program and to recommend changes to management.

Knowledge of other statistical programs (concepts, methods, and databases) related to the area of expertise to plan and implement statistical activities, to integrate conceptually different data from other programs, to explain variances and to recommend changes to other statistical programs.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies, (e.g. confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations, and data quality), practices and classification systems is required to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of operations.
Knowledge of the policies and programs of key client departments is needed to determine their information requirements.

Knowledge of data users from governments and from the private sector to identify potential new markets, to understand client needs for statistical data or studies, to negotiate contracts and to provide expert advice on survey results.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act is needed to explain the legislative requirements to data suppliers/users, and to negotiate special agreements. This knowledge, along with knowledge of the Privacy Act is also required to ensure that the organization meets its commitment to ensuring the confidentiality of all information provided to them and does not release any information that identifies an individual or group without prior consent.
Knowledge of a variety of Acts related to the area of expertise such as the Income Tax Act, the Excise Sales Tax Act, the Employment Insurance Act, and the Corporate Returns Act.
6. Research and analysis: Reviews the conceptual framework of existing statistical programs and determines the need for development, modification and adaption. Programs involve a combination of statistical techniques and methods and the integration of data from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses). Source data have often been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts and must be translated into common concepts, taking into consideration the impact of the result on other statistical programs as well as departmental priorities.

Assesses and reviews techniques and methods used to integrate and interpret massive volumes of data and resolves analytical and operational problems. Data can come from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses) and have often been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts. There is a requirement to integrate data into a common conceptual framework, and to identify and measure relationships among variables to produce statistical information.

Analyses the relative quality of data produced by statistical programs, determines reasons for variances; reviews the comparability of data over time and relevance in light of trends, developments, changing requirements, policy issues and socio-economic conditions.

Researches gaps and inconsistencies in the collection, capture, coding and processing methods and procedures used, reviews the conceptual framework used and the compatibility with other statistical programs. Problems to be resolved usually impact on other statistical operations.
Investigates client requirements for statistical information and determines the capacity and ability of existing or modified program activities to meet these requirements.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 3
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This is the strongest relationship because the role develops new statistical methods, concepts and procedures; determines and implements modifications to systems used to collect, capture, process, edit, compile and present data; and examines processing specifications to determine effects on integration and coordination of capture and processing functions. This is direct evidence of designing processing and analysis methods and specifications. It is stronger than adjacent subprocesses because the emphasis is on method, system, and specification development rather than solely operational use. Future drivers such as AI-enabled methods, integrated pipelines, metadata-driven processing, and reusable processing components are likely to materially reshape this work and create skill gaps in automated, modular, and multi-source method design.

key_activities: Participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes.
Identifies statistical trends and developments and reviews statistical survey and production results.

Assists in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.
Provides data, assistance and advice to users within and outside Statistics Canada.
Assists in subject matter studies and reviews to support the work of project teams or senior officers.

1. DECISION MAKING: Develops new statistical methods, concepts and procedures or modifies existing techniques and approaches to incorporate changes in subject-matter content and definitions.
Determines the need for and implements enhancements or modifications to processing systems and applications used to collect, capture, process, edit, compile and present statistical data.

Specifies sources of data to be used in the preparation of subject-matter statistics and forecasts, verifies the consistency and comparability of the various sets of data obtained and modifies the data to permit comparison.

Identifies and assesses trends and developments in the subject area; reviews the potential impact on program subject-matter content and determines the implications for statistical methods and procedures.

Identifies and evaluates problems in the collection, capture, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical information to provide solutions or recommendations to management and to resolve subject-matter, conceptual and technical problems.
2. LEADERSHIP AND OPERATIONAL MANAGEMENT: Coordinates the activities of work groups established to implement program activities: assigns work; provides feedback on performance of working group members; monitors progress against objectives and provides guidance and direction to working group members; identifies financial and human resource needs.

Monitors and tracks time spent on activities for the purposes of recording and recovering such costs from the client. Responsible for identifying costs and fees associated with cost recovery activities and preparing estimates for special requests and tabulations based upon established fee schedules. Arranges for the acquisition of goods and services according to approved budget allocations. Incurs and accounts for petty cash, credit card, taxi voucher, bus pass, and other expenditures.
3. COMMUNICATION: Liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development, to suggest improvements to ongoing programs, to negotiate procedural modifications and to establish project plans, priorities and target dates. Writes and presents detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify divisional systems and applications.

Provides advice to data users and clients on matters relating to subject-matter concepts used in the development and operation of a statistical database and to the data processing environment in general. Writes program information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports for use by colleagues, operational staff and management in the development, implementation and assessment of statistical programs.
4. KNOWLEDGE OF SPECIALIZED FIELDS: The conduct of special economic, demographic and technological studies requires a thorough knowledge of statistical theories and principles, a good understanding of econometrics and the application of such techniques as linear regression, mathematical programming and modeling.
Knowledge of current or emerging economic and social issues relating to the program area in order to identify and resolve subject-matter concept and definition requirements.

Knowledge of the concepts, methods and techniques used in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical data in order to advise on subject-matter development and resolve subject-matter concept and definition issues.

Knowledge of system analysis and design, computer processing, generalized survey software packages to design, develop, test, maintain and implement processing systems; to design specifications for the testing of data, and to maintain and use databases.
Knowledge of high level programming languages, utility programs or statistical packages to retrieve and manipulate data.
5. CONTEXTUAL KNOWLEDGE: Knowledge of statistical programs within Statistics Canada related to the area of expertise in order to identify potential sources of information for development and operations and/or special studies and to identify and evaluate data conflicts.

Knowledge of contacts within key client departments to establish a liaison; to understand need for statistical data, and to provide advice and guidance on subject-matter concepts, methods, techniques and results.
Knowledge of the divisional mandate, objectives, priorities, practices, standards, processes and procedures in order to coordinate on-going operational activities and/or special projects.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to ensure understanding and application in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of data. The position must have a particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data to ensure their own actions are in compliance.
6. RESEARCH AND ANALYSIS: Reviews current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.

Researches and compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output. Adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats, depending on the complexity of the subject matter or the number of different sources.
Assesses and determines the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored.

Examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Principal Researcher
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: Strongest relationship because the role explicitly 'develops new methods and techniques,' 'assesses the implications of new approaches,' and 'oversees and coordinates the review of established statistical methods.' It also 'selects and evaluates analytical techniques and methods' and organizes review of findings. These are direct method design and methodological governance responsibilities, which align most closely to designing processing and analysis methods. Future-state drivers such as AI and automation, modern statistical methods, integrated pipelines, and workforce skills transition are likely to reshape this work by requiring new expertise in automated, reusable, and metadata-driven analytical methods, with stronger governance, transparency, and quality controls than adjacent subprocesses.

key_activities: Plans and directs major economic, financial and/or socio-economic studies and research and writes/presents analytical material and research papers to be disseminated to a target audience ranging from the general public to a specialized audience.
Provides expert analysis and advice to senior officials at all levels of government, industry, academia, other national and international institutions and special interest groups.
Develops new methods and techniques to meet the needs of the most unique studies and assesses the implications of new approaches.
Oversees and coordinates the review of established statistical methods and determines departmental impact and implications.
Manages the work of multi-disciplinary departmental and interdepartmental project teams involved in research and analytical activities.
Represents the federal government and broad Canadian interests while presenting options and strategies to develop research studies on complex policy issues of interest to a variety of stakeholders.

1. Decision making: Plans and directs major economic, financial and/or socio-economic studies and research covering a range of departmental statistical programs; proposes new approaches and develops solutions or enhancements to methodology; selects and evaluates analytical techniques and methods to be used to integrate and interpret massive volumes of data and organizes the review and presentation of findings. Problems to be resolved usually impact on other statistical programs. Coordinates non-recurring research studies covering issues impacting on major departmental entities across government.
Recommends new research initiatives to address current socio-economic trends and developments at the national and international levels.

Reviews and evaluates statistical program methods and concepts to improve existing data, to develop new techniques and methods of producing, evaluating and analyzing data and to extend the use and application of departmental statistical programs.
2. Leadership and operational management: Manages multi-disciplinary departmental and interdepartmental project teams involved in research and development activities and establishes objectives and priorities to achieve long term project goals. Allocates human and financial resource needs to achieve project objectives. Prepares performance appraisals for subordinate staff.

Plans and manages budgets for projects, including estimates for salaries, professional fees and implementation costs, with authority to allocate/reallocate funds as needed. Submits cost estimates and projections to senior management and authorises expenditures in accordance with approved budgets.

Negotiates and arranges contracts with consulting firms and for the acquisition of services. Selects contractors for specific projects, assigns, directs, manages and evaluates the work according to contract specifications.
3. Communication: As a subject matter expert, provides advisory and consultative services to senior officials within and outside Statistics Canada on the results of major economic and socio-economic studies and research and their impact on complex issues.
Writes and presents analytical material and research papers to be disseminated to a target audience ranging from the general public to a specialized audience (e.g. academics).

When addressing the general public, explains in clear terms the interpretation of complex research results and the trends derived. When addressing a specialized public, it is also necessary to provide more detailed explanations of research findings. When media representatives challenge or misinterpret the results of research and analysis, it is necessary to further explain the results, methods and approaches used in order to maintain the department’s reputation for producing high quality data.

Provides expert advice and consultative services to policy makers at all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academics on the results of research and analytical studies, economic / social science theories and principles and statistical concepts and methods.

Consults with officials of other government departments, industries and special interest groups, to ensure that their priorities and interests, and those of the department, are considered in the departmental decision making process. Broader government wide objectives must also be considered.
Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and groups to develop consensus or share knowledge in a particular field.
Represents the federal government and broad Canadian interests while presenting options and strategies to develop research studies on complex policy issues of interest to a variety of stakeholders.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of economic or sociological theories and principles especially as they relate to a specialized area as well as specific knowledge of the specialized area. This is necessary to initiate and conduct research and analytical projects to improve upon existing or develop new concepts, and to assess the content of articles and reports that will be distributed widely or published.
Knowledge of advanced statistical theories, methods, concepts and practices used in the development, collection, compilation, analysis and interpretation of statistical data.

Knowledge of writing and editing skills and techniques to write papers, articles and reports and to determine and assess the design and content of studies, articles and reports that will be disseminated widely or published.
Knowledge of resource and project management practices and principles in order to manage project teams.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of current and emerging socio-economic issues in Canada and internationally such as the changed social context and the globalization of markets, particularly as they relate to all the aspects of a statistical program.

Knowledge of divisional mandate, policies, priorities, practices, standards and procedures as well as existing databases and conceptual frameworks applicable to the work to incorporate them into the conduct and management of analytical projects and to determine or recommend changes.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada mandate, objectives, organization, culture and priorities to define the objectives and content of analytical and research projects, as well as other statistical programs related to the area of expertise within the department, especially the concepts, methods, and databases used in other divisions.

Knowledge of the policies and programs of key client departments in order to determine their information requirements, analysis opportunities and to initiate the development of special projects to meet client needs.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements to other departments, agencies, industry, members of the public and the media. Knowledge of the Statitstics and Privacy Acts is particulary important with respect to the security and confidentiality of information and data provided and to ensure that they and their subordinates do not release any information which may identify an individual or group without prior consent.
Knowledge of a variety of Acts related to the area of expertise such as the Income Tax Act, the Excise Sales Tax Act, the Employment Insurance Act, and the Corporate Returns Act.
6. Research and analysis: Manages and coordinates economic, financial and/or socio-economic research and studies on complex policy issues impacting on major departmental entities across government, industry, academia and other national and international organizations. This includes determining the objectives, content and methodology of the research and development work and organizing the review and presentation of findings.

Presents options and strategies to develop research studies on complex policy issues of interest to a variety of stakeholders, directs major cross-sectoral and inter-departmental studies and provides expert analysis and advice to senior officials at all levels of government, industry, and academia, other national and international institutions and special interest groups.

key_activities: Participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes.
Identifies statistical trends and developments and reviews statistical survey and production results.

Assists in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.
Provides data, assistance and advice to users within and outside Statistics Canada.
Assists in subject matter studies and reviews to support the work of project teams or senior officers.

1. DECISION MAKING: Develops new statistical methods, concepts and procedures or modifies existing techniques and approaches to incorporate changes in subject-matter content and definitions.
Determines the need for and implements enhancements or modifications to processing systems and applications used to collect, capture, process, edit, compile and present statistical data.

Specifies sources of data to be used in the preparation of subject-matter statistics and forecasts, verifies the consistency and comparability of the various sets of data obtained and modifies the data to permit comparison.

Identifies and assesses trends and developments in the subject area; reviews the potential impact on program subject-matter content and determines the implications for statistical methods and procedures.

Identifies and evaluates problems in the collection, capture, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical information to provide solutions or recommendations to management and to resolve subject-matter, conceptual and technical problems.
2. LEADERSHIP AND OPERATIONAL MANAGEMENT: Coordinates the activities of work groups established to implement program activities: assigns work; provides feedback on performance of working group members; monitors progress against objectives and provides guidance and direction to working group members; identifies financial and human resource needs.

Monitors and tracks time spent on activities for the purposes of recording and recovering such costs from the client. Responsible for identifying costs and fees associated with cost recovery activities and preparing estimates for special requests and tabulations based upon established fee schedules. Arranges for the acquisition of goods and services according to approved budget allocations. Incurs and accounts for petty cash, credit card, taxi voucher, bus pass, and other expenditures.
3. COMMUNICATION: Liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development, to suggest improvements to ongoing programs, to negotiate procedural modifications and to establish project plans, priorities and target dates. Writes and presents detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify divisional systems and applications.

Provides advice to data users and clients on matters relating to subject-matter concepts used in the development and operation of a statistical database and to the data processing environment in general. Writes program information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports for use by colleagues, operational staff and management in the development, implementation and assessment of statistical programs.
4. KNOWLEDGE OF SPECIALIZED FIELDS: The conduct of special economic, demographic and technological studies requires a thorough knowledge of statistical theories and principles, a good understanding of econometrics and the application of such techniques as linear regression, mathematical programming and modeling.
Knowledge of current or emerging economic and social issues relating to the program area in order to identify and resolve subject-matter concept and definition requirements.

Knowledge of the concepts, methods and techniques used in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical data in order to advise on subject-matter development and resolve subject-matter concept and definition issues.

Knowledge of system analysis and design, computer processing, generalized survey software packages to design, develop, test, maintain and implement processing systems; to design specifications for the testing of data, and to maintain and use databases.
Knowledge of high level programming languages, utility programs or statistical packages to retrieve and manipulate data.
5. CONTEXTUAL KNOWLEDGE: Knowledge of statistical programs within Statistics Canada related to the area of expertise in order to identify potential sources of information for development and operations and/or special studies and to identify and evaluate data conflicts.

Knowledge of contacts within key client departments to establish a liaison; to understand need for statistical data, and to provide advice and guidance on subject-matter concepts, methods, techniques and results.
Knowledge of the divisional mandate, objectives, priorities, practices, standards, processes and procedures in order to coordinate on-going operational activities and/or special projects.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to ensure understanding and application in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of data. The position must have a particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data to ensure their own actions are in compliance.
6. RESEARCH AND ANALYSIS: Reviews current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.

Researches and compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output. Adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats, depending on the complexity of the subject matter or the number of different sources.
Assesses and determines the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored.

Examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems.

This is stronger than collection-design subprocesses because the evidence spans multiple downstream statistical methods rather than instrument design specifically. Drivers like AI and automation, metadata-driven processing, and next-generation production will materially shift the work toward designing more automated, integrated, and reusable analytical processes.

key_activities: Plans and conducts the analysis of statistical program data; writes and edits analytical material for internal use and publication purposes.
Conducts analysis of socio-economic trends and developments to assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs.

Provides feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures following data analysis and makes recommendations for improvements to established survey methods and activities.
Provides advisory and consultative services as well as subject matter advice to data users within and outside STC.
Represents subject-matter divisions on development projects, task forces or committees in various roles such as Project Manager, Task manager and Task Force Leader.
Leads project teams involved in the conduct of subject matter studies/reviews.

1. DECISION MAKING: Investigates client requirements for statistical information, determines the nature and scope of studies, as well as the sources of information, methods and approaches to be used. Modifies existing techniques or develops new methods of collecting, processing, editing, compiling and presenting statistical data.

Assesses the requirement to conduct research into socio-economic trends and developments, evaluates feasibility studies and project proposals submitted by stakeholders and makes recommendations to senior management.

Defines project objectives and priorities, prepares work plans and summaries outlining approaches, time-frames and resources. Each project is unique in nature and decisions impact on other ongoing studies.
Interprets preliminary results, reviews study format and modifies approaches and techniques as necessary.

Develops proposals for futher study and recommends changes and improvements on questionnaire design, enhancements or modifications to survey content and coverage, revisions to collection or production systems and processes, and the implementation of new hardware and software to be used in data collection or statistical production activities.
Determines the need for and prepares specifications and guidelines for the contracting of work to internal service areas, outside agencies and contractors.
2. LEADERSHIP AND OPERATIONAL MANAGEMENT: Supervises project teams involved in the conduct of unique, complex and/or non-recurring subject matter studies/reviews and/or leads project teams for special projects/studies. Determines goals, priorities and milestones, sets objectives, and plans and schedules the work, resolves conflicting priorities; identifies human resources needs, determines the appropriate selection methods (internal and external resources / contractors) to meet program or project objectives, participates in the recruitment of staff, provides input to employee performance, develops training plans, motivates and maintains morale of employees.

Plans and budgets for on-going studies and/or special projects, including estimates for salaries, professional fees and implementation costs, with authority to allocate/reallocate funds within the budget. Provides input to budgets based on operational needs and by obtaining/providing cost estimates for personnel, supplies, equipment purchases and travel for use in developing section or division budgets. Establishes and negotiates contracts for projects. Responsible for the acquisition of goods and services, according to the budget allocated.
3. COMMUNICATION: Provides subject-matter expertise and advice to all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academics, regarding potential development areas or to identify and resolve processing and marketing issues. As Subject Matter Specialist, the studies, analyses, forecasts and advice are usually accepted by senior management without substantial changes, and are the first stage in formulating departmental policy or action on opportunities or problems in this sector.

Presents arguments and options and negotiates resources, timeframes and costs with service providers (e.g. system specialists, regional office staff, survey methodologists, contractors, etc.) and clients within and outside the department.

Attends meetings with senior officials to interpret or explain study results and recommendations. There is a requirement to understand the issues and resolve differences that can affect the efficiency of the collection and compilation of data and the quality of outputs.
Writes and presents subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify current developments or to explain the results of studies.
Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and groups to develop consensus or share knowledge within the area of expertise.
4. KNOWLEDGE OF SPECIALIZED FIELDS: Knowledge of economic/ sociology principles and practices as they relate to a specialized area as well as specific knowledge of the area. This is necessary to initiate and conduct studies/projects to improve existing concepts or develop new approaches to extend the application of divisional statistics, and to analyze, review and present survey findings. This knowledge is also required to provide subject-matter expertise, advice and consultative services to users, within and outside STC, as well as to provide related advice to other professionals.

Knowledge of statistical theories, methods (including data gathering and analysis techniques), concepts and practices used in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical data.
Management skills and knowledge of the theories and principles of general and project management to lead a multi-disciplinary project team.
5. CONTEXTUAL KNOWLEDGE: Knowledge of the divisional mandate, activities, priorities, practices, standards and procedures applicable to the work to incorporate them into the conduct and management of studies/reviews.

Knowledge of the mandate, objectives and organization of Statistics Canada to manage subject matter studies/reviews. Knowledge of other statistical programs (concepts, methods, and databases) related to the area of expertise to plan and implement statistical activities, to integrate conceptually different data from other programs, to explain variances and to recommend changes to other statistical programs.

Knowledge of departmental publication, marketing and dissemination policies and practices in order to establish common divisional policies and practices in the preparation of statistical tables, charts, explanatory notes etc. for dissemination to user and/or subject matter clients.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies (confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations, data quality), practices and classification systems to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of statistical projects and activities.

Knowledge of data suppliers to discuss data reporting agreements. Knowledge of data users from governments and from the private sector to identify potential new markets, to understand client needs for complex statistical data or studies, to negotiate contracts and to provide advice on survey results.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements to other departments, agencies, industry, members of the public and the media. Knowledge of the Statitstics and Privacy Acts is particulary important with respect to the security and confidentiality of information and data provided and to ensure that they and their subordinates do not release any information which may identify an individual or group without prior consent.
6. RESEARCH AND ANALYSIS: Interprets study results, determines reasons for variances, its comparability over time and its relevancy in light of changing requirements, trends, developments, policy issues and socio-economic conditions.

Reviews and modifies existing techniques, methods and approaches or develops new ones to meet specific needs. Some studies may involve a combination of statistical techniques and methods and the integration of data from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses). Often, the data have been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts and must be translated into common concepts.

Reviews and resolves gaps and inconsistencies in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures used, reviews the conceptual framework used and the compatibility with other statistical programs, reviews and resolves technical and conceptual problems referred by staff or project team members.

Analysis is required to understand and interpret user requirements for statistical information and to translate them into a concrete, timely and affordable information request. Clients are often uncertain of their data needs and are unfamiliar with statistical options, methods and techniques available.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Unit Head, Subject Matter
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: The role strongly affects design of processing and analysis because it 'develops new methods to produce, evaluate, analyze, present and extend the application of divisional statistics,' determines 'standards, data concepts, definitions and techniques,' and reviews techniques used in collection, processing, analysis and dissemination. This is a direct methodological design and stewardship function. It is stronger than broader workflow design because the work description emphasizes statistical methods, concepts, and analytical approaches. Drivers such as modern methods, AI and automation, and integrated pipelines will reshape the work toward more automated, linked, and reusable analytical methods with stronger governance and staff upskilling needs.

key_activities: Plans, develops and directs the analysis, review and presentation of program results; coordinates and reviews the development, processing, analysis, marketing and dissemination of statistical data; prepares, edits and evaluates analytical material for publication purposes.

Represents subject-matter divisions on development projects, task forces or committees in various roles such as Project Manager, Task Manager and Task Force Leader.

Develops enhancements and recommends modifications to be made to the program content, coverage and operational procedures, such as new or modified data sources, concepts, methods and definitions to be applied.
Investigates client requirements for statistical information and determines the capacity and ability of existing or modified program activities to meet these requirements.

Negotiates and arranges contracts with consulting firms and for the acquisition of services. Selects contractors for specific projects, assigns, directs, manages and evaluates the work according to contract specifications. Negotiates with suppliers for cost reductions/discounts.
3. COMMUNICATION: Provides expert advisory and consultative services to policy makers at all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academics and presents rationale on the practical application and interpretation of statistical data and information. Provides guidance to subordinate staff, other professionals and management on study results, on methods of socio-economic analysis, dissemination, or on statistical techniques and systems; comments on written material to be published by STC.

Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and groups to develop understanding, consensus and share knowledge of the program area.

KNOWLEDGE OF SPECIALIZED FIELDS: Knowledge of economic or sociology principles and theory to provide expert advisory and consultative services to clients on program results and on the concepts and methods used in the collection, compilation, analysis, presentation and interpretation of findings.

Management and coordination skills and knowledge of general and project management methods, techniques and practices to manage and coordinate the activities of a multi-disciplinary sub-division/operational area and supporting project teams.

Researches gaps and inconsistencies in the collection, processing, analysis and dissemination methods and procedures used; reviews the conceptual framework used and the compatibility with other statistical programs. Problems to be resolved usually impact on other statistical programs.

Analysis is required to understand and interpret user needs for statistical information and to translate them into a timely and affordable information request. Clients are often uncertain of their data needs and are unfamiliar with statistical options, methods and techniques available.

Directs recruitment activities for both, permanent and project team staff, and approves training and development plans. Prepares performance appraisals for subordinate staff, reviews performance appraisals prepared by subordinate supervisors, and resolves performance and disciplinary matters.

Plans, develops and manages budgets for projects, including estimates for salaries, professional fees and implementation costs, with authority to allocate/reallocate funds as needed. Submits cost estimates and projections to senior management and authorises expenditures in accordance with approved budgets.

Negotiates and approves contracts with consulting firms and for the acquisition of services. Selects contractors for specific projects, assigns, directs, manages and evaluates the work according to contract specifications.
3. Communication: Mediates with senior executives of major Canadian corporations, representatives of private sector associations, federal, provincial and municipal government departments, unions and universities to establish joint survey agreements, to maintain good relations and cooperation with the user community and data suppliers, to promote an understanding of programs, to market statistical products and services, and to monitor relevant concepts and practices related to the use and application of program results.

As a departmental representative, explains the results and statistical methods and approaches used in the conduct of studies and surveys to all levels of government, international organizations, the media and public. At this level, there is a particular requirement to deal with sensitive and political issues that could embarrass the department.

Defends proposals for the development of new surveys to address current socio-economic trends and developments at the national and international levels, and negotiates the allocation of funding for the conduct of such surveys and projects. Presents arguments and options and negotiates resources and timeframes for large-scale projects requiring the participation of data suppliers. It is not unusual to encounter resistance on the part of data suppliers. Major difficulties can be encountered as the projects involve the negotiation of significant resources and services with multiple milestones.

Writes analytical papers and articles on the interpretation of statistical surveys or projects and their application to the area of specialization and presents analytical material to media representatives to maintain the department’s reputation where there is a particular requirement to deal with sensitive and political issues that could embarrass the department.

Knowledge of specialized fields: Expert knowledge of advanced economic or sociology theories and principles relating to a specialized subject area to provide authoritative and expert advice to senior officials and policy advisors within and outside Statistics Canada on the results of unique economic and socio-economic studies and their impact on major program, policy or regulatory issues and to define the objectives, content and approaches of unique and complex analytical projects covering a broad area of specialization or a range of departmental statistical programs, to improve existing concepts or develop new concepts, to extend the application of statistics and to analyze data.

A deep understanding of the underlying theoretical concepts of economics, sociology and statistics as they relate to a group of specialized areas to develop and implement programs to produce statistics covering a wide range of issues.

A comprehensive knowledge of economic and social information to develop and implement programs to produce statistics depicting Canada’s population, labour force, economic life, education, housing, transportation and social and cultural life.

Knowledge of writing and editing skills and techniques to write and review papers, articles and reports and to determine and assess the design and content of studies, articles and reports that will be disseminated widely or published.

Knowledge of the principles and practices of management with regards to human and financial resources in order to direct the work of a sub-division through subordinate section chiefs, and/or multi-disciplinary departmental and interdepartmental project teams, working groups and committees.
5. This knowledge is necessary to defend proposals for the development of new surveys.

Knowledge of governmental policies, programs and regulatory issues in order to provide expert advice to senior officials and policy advisors, within and outside Statistics Canada, on the results and impact of unique economic and socio-economic studies.
Knowledge of the division mandate and priorities as well as subject-matter expertise is required to review strategic directions in the management of significant surveys.

Knowledge of the policies and programs of key client departments in order to mediate with their representatives to reach a consensus on the major issues affecting departments, industries and special interest groups, and to recommend priorities for new surveys and studies.

Directs the development of new methods and techniques for unique studies, assesses the implications of new approaches and develops solutions to complex issues.

Analyses the impact of study results on major program, policy and regulatory issues and provides authoritative and expert advice to senior officials and policy advisors within and outside Statistics Canada.

key_activities: Manages a section and/or multidisciplinary project teams involved in statistical program operations, analysis, interpretation, marketing and dissemination.
Plans and implements long term strategies for the development, enhancement and operation of statistical programs.

1. Decision making: Establishes and maintains a framework for the development and on-going operation of statistical systems and processes and evaluates and incorporates all the functions and activities associated with the data collection, processing, editing, compilation, analysis and dissemination of the division's statistical outputs and assesses the impact of changes in both technology and the subject area.

Establishes strategic directions for the management of significant studies, proposes innovative solutions and recommends to senior officials of Statistics Canada new or modified statistical programs to address departmental goals and objectives.

Manages complex studies covering a range of departmental statistical programs, determines the objectives, content and methodology of the research and development work, defines and sets priorities and milestones, selects and evaluates analytical techniques and methods to be used to integrate and interpret massive volumes of data and organizes the review and presentation of findings. Problems to be resolved usually impact on other statistical programs.

Initiates changes and implements new systems and processes to meet client demands, identifies and assesses new statistical methods, techniques and practices and the associated costs and limitations, identifies the availability and reliability of new data sources, evaluates the suitability of new hardware and software and identifies and determines the short and long term program impact and benefits.

Plans and manages the review and evaluation of statistical program methods and concepts to certify the overall quality and completeness of program results, to improve existing data, to develop new techniques and methods of producing, evaluating and analyzing data, to ensure the continued relevancy of data in light of changing requirements, trends, developments, policy issues and socio-economic conditions and to extend the use of statistical programs

Leadership and operational management: Manages, through subordinates, the work of a section and/or multidisciplinary project teams involved in statistical program operations, analysis, interpretation, marketing and dissemination. Evaluates the cost, efficiency and productivity of statistical systems and processes. Manages budgets including estimates for salaries, professional fees and implementation costs, with authority to allocate/reallocate funds as needed. Negotiates and arranges contracts with consulting firms and for the acquisition of services. Selects contractors for specific projects, assigns, directs, manages and evaluates the work according to contract specifications.

Negotiates significant resources and services, timeframes and costs for large scale projects with service providers(e.g. system specialists, regional office staff, survey methodologists, contractors, etc.) and clients within and outside the department.

Knowledge of advanced statistical theories, methods, concepts and practices used in the development, collection, compilation, analysis and interpretation of statistical data.

Knowledge of writing and editing skills and techniques to write papers, articles and reports and to determine and assess the design and content of studies, articles and reports that will be disseminated widely or published.
Knowledge of management practices and the theories and principles of project management in order to manage staff, either directly or within a matrix management environment.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge and understanding of current and emerging socio-economic trends and issues in Canada and internationally such as the changed social context and the globalization of markets, particularly as they relate to a broad area of expertise including all aspects of a statistical program.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada mandate, objectives, organization, culture and priorities to define the objectives and content of analytical and research projects, as well as other statistical programs related to the area of expertise within the department, especially the concepts, methods, and databases used in other divisions.

Knowledge of the policies and programs of key client departments in order to determine their information requirements, analysis opportunities and to initiate the development of special projects to meet client needs.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act is needed to explain the legislative requirements to other departments, agencies, industry, members of the public and the media. This knowledge, along with knowledge of the Privacy Act is also required to ensure that the organization meets its commitment to ensuring the confidentiality of all information provided to them and does not release any information that identifies an individual or group without prior consent.
Knowledge of a variety of Acts related to the area of expertise such as the Income Tax Act, the Excise Sales Tax Act, the Employment Insurance Act, and the Corporate Returns Act.

Research and analysis: Undertakes analytical studies evaluating the effectiveness of divisional statistical programs and the resulting products and services in order to determine the attainment of divisional program objectives and the cost, efficiency and utilization of divisional resources. Prepares reports outlining program results, developments and changes in the subject area in order to explain the nature, content and use of divisional statistical programs.

Identifies gaps and inconsistencies in the collection, processing, analysis and dissemination methods and procedures used, reviews the conceptual framework used and the compatibility with other statistical programs. Conceptualizes enhancements and determines modifications to be made to the program content, coverage and operational procedures, such as new or modified data sources, concepts, methods and definitions to be applied.

Investigates and assesses changes in the statistical needs of clients, determines the extent and approaches of surveys or studies such as the sources of information, statistical techniques, methods and approaches to be used for the collection, processing, analysis and dissemination of the data in an area of specialty modifies existing techniques, methods and approaches or develops new ones to meet specific needs.

Researches and reports on trends and developments in data processing concepts, methods and techniques in order to present options and recommendations on the use and application of new computer hardware and software technology to mass data capture, conversion and dissemination applications; recommends strategies for the introduction or enhancement of statistical programs, the acquisition of new equipment and services and/or the adoption of new collection, production and dissemination strategies.
Writes and presents analytical material and research papers to be disseminated to a target audience ranging from the general public to a specialized audience (e.g. academics).
