implicated_work_descriptions.title: Unit Head, Subject Matter
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: A strong second fit is design processing and analysis. Evidence includes determining 'the standards, data concepts, definitions and techniques to be applied,' developing new methods, reviewing program methods across collection, processing, analysis and dissemination, and researching gaps and inconsistencies in methods and procedures. This is stronger than design outputs/dissemination because the role owns substantive methodological choices that shape production. Future drivers such as AI, alternative data, integrated pipelines and modern methods will materially affect this work by increasing methodological complexity and need for reusable, governed approaches.

key_activities: Plans, develops and directs the analysis, review and presentation of program results; coordinates and reviews the development, processing, analysis, marketing and dissemination of statistical data; prepares, edits and evaluates analytical material for publication purposes.
Plans, manages and coordinates economic, financial and/or socio-economic studies and develops new methods to produce, evaluate, analyze, present and extend the application of divisional statistics.
Determines changes in the statistical needs of clients; assesses the impact on divisional programs; develops options and strategies to manage complex issues and multi-stakeholder relations.

Provides expert advisory and consultative services to data users (e.g. academics, policy makers, international bodies, etc.) on the results of surveys and studies, survey concepts and methods, and economic / social science theories and principles.
Represents subject-matter divisions on development projects, task forces or committees in various roles such as Project Manager, Task Manager and Task Force Leader.

Supervises a unit and multi-disciplinary project teams responsible for significant multi-sectoral and inter-departmental files/issues; manages the financial resources attached to each statistical program.

1. DECISION MAKING: Assesses the policies and programs of key client departments to determine their requirements for statistical information and recommends, for approval, those studies that should be conducted.
Recommends plans to improve and expand the content and direction of existing studies as well as the development of policies, strategies and program proposals of concern to the sector.

Defines the objectives and content of the studies and the overall approach to be followed; determines the standards, data concepts, definitions and techniques to be applied in the development and conduct of studies and in the reporting, analysis and presentation of findings.

Interprets study findings and conclusions and prepares recommendations and advice to senior management on current trends affecting the Sector policies and programs and on the significant factors related to the changing environment.

Develops enhancements and recommends modifications to be made to the program content, coverage and operational procedures, such as new or modified data sources, concepts, methods and definitions to be applied.
Investigates client requirements for statistical information and determines the capacity and ability of existing or modified program activities to meet these requirements.

Provides input to management decisions and recommendations designed to develop or improve departmental policies and develops new program initiatives covering areas such as recruitment, official languages, employment equity, dissemination and confidentiality of information.
2. LEADERSHIP AND OPERATIONAL MANAGEMENT: Manages a unit involved in the conduct of economic, financial and/or socio-economic studies and research and leads project teams for special projects. Determines program objectives and priorities and assesses the requirements of the program. Plans and schedules the work, resolves conflicting priorities, ascertains human resource needs, determines the appropriate selection methods (internal and external resources / contractors) to meet program and project objectives, recruits staff, evaluates employee performance or reviews performance evaluations prepared by subordinates and approves training plans.

Plans, develops and manages a budget for the unit in accordance with departmental policy and procedures. Exercises direct authority and accountability for allocated funds to meet planned objectives. Authorises, commits and approves expenditures in accordance with approved budgets with the authority to reallocate funds among line objects.

Negotiates and arranges contracts with consulting firms and for the acquisition of services. Selects contractors for specific projects, assigns, directs, manages and evaluates the work according to contract specifications. Negotiates with suppliers for cost reductions/discounts.
3. COMMUNICATION: Provides expert advisory and consultative services to policy makers at all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academics and presents rationale on the practical application and interpretation of statistical data and information. This information is used as input to decision making for a vast array of economic and social policies, programs and other activities.

Writes and presents analytical material to be disseminated to a target audience ranging from the general public to a specialized audience (e.g. academics). When media representatives and others challenge or misinterpret findings, it is necessary to present logical arguments to justify the results and to defend the validity of statistical methods and approaches used in order to maintain the department’s reputation for producing high quality data.
Provides expert advice to STC and other professionals from the private sector or from other statistical agencies on statistical program findings and their application to the area of specialization.

Provides guidance to subordinate staff, other professionals and management on study results, on methods of socio-economic analysis, dissemination, or on statistical techniques and systems; comments on written material to be published by STC.
Negotiates agreements and arranges contracts with consulting firms and suppliers for the acquisition of services.
Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and groups to develop understanding, consensus and share knowledge of the program area.
4. KNOWLEDGE OF SPECIALIZED FIELDS: Knowledge of economic or sociology principles and theory to provide expert advisory and consultative services to clients on program results and on the concepts and methods used in the collection, compilation, analysis, presentation and interpretation of findings.

Extensive knowledge of current and emerging socio-economic issues in Canada and internationally such as the changing social context and the globalization of markets, particularly as they relate to all aspects of a statistical program. This knowledge is required to analyze program outputs, anticipate and understand needs for new data, and assess the impact on the area of specialization.

Knowledge of advanced statistical theories, methods (including data gathering and analysis techniques), concepts and practices used in the development, collection, compilation, analysis and interpretation of statistical data.

Management and coordination skills and knowledge of general and project management methods, techniques and practices to manage and coordinate the activities of a multi-disciplinary sub-division/operational area and supporting project teams.
5. CONTEXTUAL KNOWLEDGE: Knowledge of the divisional mandate, activities, priorities, practices, standards and procedures applicable to the work to incorporate them into the management of a statistical program to recommend changes to management.
Knowledge of the mandate, objectives, organization, practices, policies, culture and priorities of Statistics Canada to define the objectives and content of studies.
Knowledge of other statistical programs related to the area of expertise within the department, especially the concepts, methods, and databases used in other divisions.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies (e.g. confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations, data quality), practices and classification systems to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of studies.
Knowledge of the policies and programs of key client departments in order to determine their information requirements.

Knowledge of data users from governments and from the private sector to identify potential new markets, to understand client needs for statistical data or studies, to negotiate contracts and to provide expert advice on study results.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements to other departments, agencies, industry, members of the public and the media. Knowledge of the Statitstics and Privacy Acts is particulary important with respect to the security and confidentiality of information and data provided and to ensure that they and their subordinates do not release any information which may identify an individual or group without prior consent.
6. RESEARCH AND ANALYSIS: Reviews the conceptual framework of existing statistical programs and determines the need for development, modification and adaption. Programs involve a combination of statistical techniques and methods and the integration of data from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses). Source data have often been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts and must be translated into common concepts, taking into consideration the impact of the results on other statistical programs as well as departmental priorities.

Assesses and reviews statistical techniques, methods and approaches used in the collection, processing, analysis and dissemination of data within a program area (e.g. System of National Accounts, Demography, Health, Justice, Education, Labour, Prices, International Trade, Balance of Payments, Environment, etc.). Program areas are often unique in nature and involve different collection, processing, analysis and dissemination activities conducted concurrently.
Analyzes the results and findings of studies conducted by in-house analysts and consultants and provides senior management with interpretation and recommendations affecting social policy issues.

Researches gaps and inconsistencies in the collection, processing, analysis and dissemination methods and procedures used; reviews the conceptual framework used and the compatibility with other statistical programs. Problems to be resolved usually impact on other statistical programs.

Analysis is required to understand and interpret user needs for statistical information and to translate them into a timely and affordable information request. Clients are often uncertain of their data needs and are unfamiliar with statistical options, methods and techniques available.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Specialist, Data Analytics and Integration
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: Design processing and analysis is materially affected because the role 'manages activities related to ... data analytics, processing, analysis,' leads 'program development, research or analysis,' and oversees 'implementation of various tools or software' while ensuring 'overall quality and completeness of program results.' This indicates substantive ownership of how processing and analytical work is designed and operationalized. It is ranked behind 5.1 and 1.5 because the clearest evidence is about integration and source acquisition, but it is still stronger than pure dissemination subprocesses since the job directly manages processing/analytics methods and tools. Future drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Modern Statistical Methods and Next-Generation Production, Modular Architecture and Reusable Components, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment are likely to change this work toward more automated, metadata-driven, modular and AI-assisted processing and analytical designs, increasing demand for advanced methodological and platform skills.

key_activities: Manages activities related to: data integration, data manipulation, data analytics, processing, analysis and the preparation of dissemination and data visualization products. This involves setting objectives; leading program development, research or analysis; implementation of various tools or software, and ensuring overall quality and completeness of program results.

Responsible for outreach and collaboration with a variety of stakeholders (within the Agency, the federal, provincial-territorial or municipal governments and agencies, academia and international institutions and private organizations) in order to establish relationships to leverage new methods and data sources, understand user needs and keep abreast of economic trends and developments, and providing expert advice and analysis.

Leads complex projects involving data acquisition, integration, linkage and use of alternative data sources to respond to user needs; develops mitigation strategies to address delays and briefs senior management when cost or scope changes are necessary.
Authors analytical papers and other types of material supporting data development and dissemination.
Participates in or leads data acquisition negotiations.
Supervises directly or in a matrix environment to plan and coordinate teams responsible for statistical outputs or projects.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: A meaningful third fit is design processing and analysis. Evidence includes 'develops and implements procedures for the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of data,' 'implements enhancements or modifications to processing systems and applications,' and analyzes impacts of methodology and technology changes on outputs. This is stronger than final output interpretation because the work is closer to processing design than high-level analysis. Future drivers will increase demands for skills in automated workflows, integrated data pipelines, modern tools, and more complex processing rules for diverse sources.

key_activities: Under guidance, participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes.
Identifies statistical trends and developments.

Under guidance, participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.
Provides data and assistance to users, within and outside Statistics Canada.
Under guidance, participates in subject matter studies and reviews to support the work of project teams or senior officers.

1. Decision making: Evaluates problems in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical information to provide solutions or recommendations to management and to resolve subject-matter, conceptual and technical problems.

Prepares special data releases, reviews and verifies data sources and methods of data compilation; develops and implements procedures for the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of data.
Develops and outlines new statistical methods, concepts and procedures or modifies existing techniques and approaches to incorporate changes in subject-matter content and definitions.
Reviews and designs questionnaires for the collection of data and assesses the timeliness, completeness, accuracy and validity of data compiled for publication.
Implements enhancements or modifications to processing systems and applications used to collect, process, edit, compile and present statistical data.
Develops or modifies statistical methods, concepts, definitions and approaches to improve existing surveys or to meet specific needs.
2. Leadership and operational management: Participates in project teams, work groups, meetings and conferences in order to develop and improve work methods and practices, share knowledge and contribute to skill development.

Monitors and tracks time spent on activities for the purposes of recording and recovering such costs from the client. Incurs and accounts for petty cash, credit card, taxi voucher, bus pass, and other expenditures.
3. Communiction: Writes and presents detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify divisional systems and applications.

Writes program information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports for use by colleagues, operational staff and management in the development, implementation and assessment of statistical programs.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of statistical or economic theory and principles and the relevance of their application in a computerized environment, and the methods and techniques of data gathering, statistical estimation and economic modeling.
Knowledge of current and emerging economic and social issues relating to the program area in order to identify and assess trends and issues represented by statistical data series.
Knowledge of methods, techniques, practices and procedures to conduct studies and to develop/assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs.

Knowledge of the socio-economic concepts and methods to assess the validity of collected and processed data, the output from computer applications, the validity of database contents and results from alternative manipulations of data.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of the subject and universe of the survey is required in order to propose suitable changes to statistical or reporting methods and techniques.
Knowledge of program context, program sponsors, participants and respondents to plan and organize the retrieval and processing of data for research or development projects.

Knowledge of the divisional mandate, objectives, programs, policies and activities to adhere to the various statistical and administrative practices and procedures involved in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical data.
Knowledge of data sources within Statistics Canada in order to locate, analyze and compare related statistical output to ensure consistency and reliability

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to ensure understanding and application in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of data. The position must have a particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data to ensure their own actions are in compliance.
6. Research and analysis: Analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services.
Assesses and determines the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored.
Analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Head of Operations
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: A meaningful third fit is design processing and analysis. Evidence includes recommending 'sample estimation and imputation methods, data integration from different sources,' determining concepts, definitions and techniques for program conduct, and reviewing techniques used to integrate and interpret large volumes of data. This is stronger than integration in Process phase because the role sets methods and standards rather than performing day-to-day processing. Future drivers such as modern statistical methods, automation, linked data and metadata-driven processing will increase the need for advanced methodological and governance skills.

key_activities: Plans and leads the development of statistical operations to produce, evaluate, analyze, present and extend the application of statistics.
Reviews the survey collection framework for existing statistical programs and determines the need for development, modification and adaptation.
Coordinates and reviews collection, coding, processing and client-relation activities to determine changes in data needs and assesses their impact on divisional programs.
Provides expert advisory and consultative services to users on the collection, capture, coding and processing of statistical data.
Participates in or leads task forces or committees as an expert in data collection operations.
Manages a unit and project teams responsible for statistical program operations. Manages the financial resources attached to the statistical program.

Develops enhancements and recommends modifications to be made to the program content, coverage and operational procedures, such as new or modified data sources, concepts, methods and definitions to be applied.

Defines the objectives, content and approaches of statistical programs and presents recommendations to senior management to improve and expand the content and direction of existing programs and elaborate new program options.

Authorises, commits and approves expenditures in accordance with approved budgets with the authority to reallocate funds among line objects.

Negotiates cost reductions and arranges contracts with consulting firms and for the acquisition of services. Selects contractors for specific projects, assigns, directs, manages and evaluates the work according to contract specifications.
3. Communication: Provides expert advisory and consultative services to policy makers at all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academia. Explains and elaborates on statistical program findings and their practical application and interpretation of statistical data and information. This information is used as input to decision making for a vast array of economic and social policies, programs and other activities.

Prepares, edits and evaluates analytical material to be published by Statistics Canada.

Knowledge of advanced statistical theories, methods (including data gathering and analysis techniques), concepts and practices used in the collection, capture, coding, processing and interpretation of statistical data.

Management and coordination skills and knowledge of general and project management methods, techniques and practices to manage and coordinate the activities of a multi-disciplinary sub-division/operational area and supporting project teams.
Knowledge of the principles and practices of human and financial resource management is required to manage the work of a multi-disciplinary unit and project teams.

Knowledge of other statistical programs (concepts, methods, and databases) related to the area of expertise to plan and implement statistical activities, to integrate conceptually different data from other programs, to explain variances and to recommend changes to other statistical programs.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies, (e.g. confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations, and data quality), practices and classification systems is required to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of operations.
Knowledge of the policies and programs of key client departments is needed to determine their information requirements.

Knowledge of data users from governments and from the private sector to identify potential new markets, to understand client needs for statistical data or studies, to negotiate contracts and to provide expert advice on survey results.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act is needed to explain the legislative requirements to data suppliers/users, and to negotiate special agreements. This knowledge, along with knowledge of the Privacy Act is also required to ensure that the organization meets its commitment to ensuring the confidentiality of all information provided to them and does not release any information that identifies an individual or group without prior consent.
Knowledge of a variety of Acts related to the area of expertise such as the Income Tax Act, the Excise Sales Tax Act, the Employment Insurance Act, and the Corporate Returns Act.

There is a requirement to integrate data into a common conceptual framework, and to identify and measure relationships among variables to produce statistical information.

Analyses the relative quality of data produced by statistical programs, determines reasons for variances; reviews the comparability of data over time and relevance in light of trends, developments, changing requirements, policy issues and socio-economic conditions.

Researches gaps and inconsistencies in the collection, capture, coding and processing methods and procedures used, reviews the conceptual framework used and the compatibility with other statistical programs. Problems to be resolved usually impact on other statistical operations.
Investigates client requirements for statistical information and determines the capacity and ability of existing or modified program activities to meet these requirements.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Supervisor
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: A meaningful third fit is design processing and analysis. Evidence includes developing statistical systems and processes, modifying techniques and methods for coding and processing, and developing guidelines and procedures for systems and processes. This is stronger than configure workflows because the work description emphasizes determining methods and procedures more than technical workflow assembly. Future drivers such as AI-enabled coding, modular reusable components, integrated pipelines and modern processing platforms will materially change this work.

key_activities: Integrates and analyzes statistical outputs and reviews/certifies the quality and completeness of the individual program results.
Develops statistical systems and processes, evaluates the quality of collections’ outputs and prepares analytical reviews.
Evaluates changes in the statistical needs of clients and develops new methods of collecting, coding and processing data.
Provides advice and guidance to users on the development, operation and use of collection systems and processes.
Acts as a divisional data collection and operations representative on projects, task forces or committees in various roles.

Proposes modifications to program content and coverage and operational procedures, such as new or modified data sources, concepts, methods and definitions.

Establishes and implements specifications, guidelines and procedures for the maintenance and safeguarding of computer systems, equipment, databases and files.

Develops proposals and recommends changes and improvements on questionnaire design, enhancements or modifications to survey content and coverage, revisions to collection or production systems and processes, and the implementation of new hardware and software to be used in data collection or statistical production activities.

Plans and budgets for on-going operations and/or special projects, including estimates for salaries, professional fees and implementation costs, with authority to allocate/reallocate funds within the budget. Provides input to budgets based on operational needs and by obtaining/providing cost estimates for personnel, supplies, equipment purchases and travel for use in developing section or division budgets. Establishes and negotiates contracts for projects. Responsible for the acquisition of goods and services, according to the budget allocated.

Communication: Provides advice and interpretation to various data users at all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academics, on the practical use and application of statistical data and information. Prepares and explains specifications and guidelines to be used by others in developing and operating systems and processes.
Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and groups to develop consensus or share knowledge within the area of operational expertise.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies, practices and classification systems is needed to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of statistical projects and activities.
Knowledge of other statistical programs related to the area of expertise within the department, especially the concepts, methods, and databases used in other divisions.

Knowledge of departmental publication, marketing and dissemination policies and practices in order to establish common divisional policies and practices in the preparation of statistical tables, charts, explanatory notes etc. for dissemination to user and/or subject matter clients.

Knowledge of the Statitstics and Privacy Acts is particulary important with respect to the security and confidentiality of information and data provided and to ensure that they and their subordinates do not release any information which may identify an individual or group without prior consent.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Data Analytics and Integration Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This subprocess is material because the role recommends and implements new methods of processing, modeling, analyzing and disseminating data. Evidence includes: 'implements initiatives pertaining to new methods of acquiring, processing, modeling, analyzing or disseminating data' and 'provides specialized technical, advisory and consultative services.' That aligns with designing processing and analysis methodologies, especially for integrated, linked and alternative data environments. It is stronger than dissemination-only subprocesses because the emphasis is on methods and technical initiatives rather than product assembly. Future drivers such as AI and automation, modern statistical methods and integrated pipelines will shift the role toward more advanced model-based processing, automated validation/integration logic, and stronger method governance and reproducibility skills.

key_activities: Performs data integration, data manipulation, data analytics and in-depth analysis, towards producing dissemination and data visualization products using a variety of techniques and tools.
Develops recommendations, provides advice to management and implements initiatives pertaining to new methods of acquiring, processing, modeling, analyzing or disseminating data to meet user needs.
Provides specialized technical, advisory and consultative services. Undertakes technical projects requiring data integration, data linkage and use of alternative data sources.
Participates in data acquisition negotiations.
May supervise employees directly or in a matrix environment to perform statistical processes, outputs or projects.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Specialist, Data Analytics and Integration
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This subprocess is materially related because the role manages processing, analysis and quality/completeness of program results and implements tools/software supporting those activities. Evidence includes: 'manages activities related to... processing, analysis,' 'setting objectives; leading program development, research or analysis; implementation of various tools or software, and ensuring overall quality and completeness of program results.' This fits designing processing and analysis methods and specifications. It is stronger than dissemination-only subprocesses because the work is framed around analytical and processing methods, not just product packaging. Future drivers around AI and automation, modern statistical methods, open-source environments and pipeline orchestration are likely to increase the role's need to design scalable processing approaches, model-based methods, automated quality controls and reusable analysis workflows.

key_activities: Manages activities related to: data integration, data manipulation, data analytics, processing, analysis and the preparation of dissemination and data visualization products. This involves setting objectives; leading program development, research or analysis; implementation of various tools or software, and ensuring overall quality and completeness of program results.

Responsible for outreach and collaboration with a variety of stakeholders (within the Agency, the federal, provincial-territorial or municipal governments and agencies, academia and international institutions and private organizations) in order to establish relationships to leverage new methods and data sources, understand user needs and keep abreast of economic trends and developments, and providing expert advice and analysis.

Leads complex projects involving data acquisition, integration, linkage and use of alternative data sources to respond to user needs; develops mitigation strategies to address delays and briefs senior management when cost or scope changes are necessary.
Authors analytical papers and other types of material supporting data development and dissemination.
Participates in or leads data acquisition negotiations.
Supervises directly or in a matrix environment to plan and coordinate teams responsible for statistical outputs or projects.

gsbpm_description: This sub-process determines the workflow from data collection to dissemination, taking an overview of all the processes required within the whole production process and ensuring that they fit together efficiently with no gaps or redundancies. Various systems and databases may be needed throughout the process. The GSBPM can be used to design a statistical organisation’s business architecture layer when a statistical organisation has an existing enterprise architecture in place. The design might be adjusted to fit the organisation. A general principle is to reuse processes and technology across many statistical business processes, so existing production solutions (e.g. services, systems and databases) should be examined first, to determine whether they are fit for purpose for this specific production process, then, if any gaps are identified, new solutions can be designed. This sub-process also considers how staff will interact with systems and who will be responsible for what and when.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Production and Database Expert
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: The strongest relationship is with Design production systems and workflows because the role explicitly designs, evaluates, improves and operationalizes production, validation and dissemination systems, processes and databases for ongoing statistical program delivery. Evidence includes 'innovates and implements the design, evaluation, and applications for the manipulation, storage, and retrieval of high-impact statistical data', 'develops and maintains production and dissemination processes and outputs', and 'provides specialized expertise and consultative services regarding production systems and processes'. This is stronger than narrower processing subprocesses because the work spans the end-to-end production architecture, partner coordination, schedules, and system specifications. Future drivers such as enterprise digital platforms, integrated data pipelines, modular architecture, AI/automation, and workforce transition would most directly change this role by shifting it toward reusable enterprise workflows, orchestration, cloud/platform-based production, and redesigned staff-system interactions.

key_activities: Innovates and implements the design, evaluation, and applications for the manipulation, storage, and retrieval of high-impact statistical data.

Develops and maintains production and dissemination processes and outputs for analytical databases and provides support for tools and systems for the delivery of high-impact statistical programs, new products, special studies, and ad hoc requests.
Coordinates activities of multiple Statistic Canada divisional partners and other external partners to process, validate, and disseminate statistical data.
Provides specialized expertise and consultative services regarding production systems and processes for ongoing statistical program delivery.
Represents economic subject matter divisions on statistical development projects.
Occasionally leads project teams and undertakes complex technical projects in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems.

Decision Making: Integrates input from multiple economic subject matter areas to develop and maintain complex systems and frameworks for the ongoing production, validation and dissemination of a range of specialized, high-impact statistical outputs.
Operationalizes specialized conceptual and measurement frameworks in the development of production, validation and dissemination systems, processes and databases.

Evaluates alternatives and develops and applies new strategies to maintain and improve operational systems, processes and databases in the production and dissemination of official statistics. Decisions and recommendations regarding data production and dissemination practices impact multiple projects and high-impact statistical programs.
Develops and implements quality-assurance processes for high-impact statistical outputs.

Investigates requirements for statistical information and analysis, defines the nature and scope of special studies, data requirements, and decides the methods and approaches to be used to satisfy complex data requirements. Modifies existing techniques or develops new approaches to meet specific needs.

Defines project objectives and priorities, prepares work plans and summaries outlining approaches, time-frames and resources. Each project is unique in nature and decisions impact on other ongoing studies.
Develops guidelines for the design, evaluation, and testing of processing systems and applications and recommends and implements modifications and improvements to existing procedures.
Recommends and executes solutions to resolve complex technical issues pertaining to data production and dissemination that may lack precedents.
Develops data bases for the provision of time-series information, interprets preliminary results, reviews, and modifies approaches and techniques as necessary.
Reviews and approves detailed processing parameters, devises criteria and methods to rectify inconsistencies, and recommends modifications to ensure the continuity and compatibility of data.
Leadership And Operational Management: Occasionally plans, organizes and functionally coordinates the work of multiple partners within Statistic Canada divisions and units, as well as clients from other federal government departments involved in the conduct of statistical processing, validation and dissemination of specialized statistical outputs. Determines goals, priorities and milestones, sets objectives, plans and schedules the work and resolves conflicting priorities.
Establishes and coordinates schedules for the production, validation and dissemination of regular statistical outputs across multiple production teams.
Coordinates input and specifications from multiple partners to implement specialized solutions according to established production schedules in the context of complex statistical frameworks.
Communication: Provides expert advice and guidance to internal partners on statistical program results, dissemination methods, concepts, and techniques applied and on trends and developments in economic or related data programs. This information is used as input to decision making for a vast array of economic programs and other activities.
Interprets specialized information pertaining to a range of specialized subject matter areas to present arguments and options to clients within and outside the department.

Communicates subject matter concepts and technical definitions to internal contacts and other subject matter experts to explain and clarify current developments, to explain the results of studies, and to resolve differences that can affect the efficiency of the manipulation, storage, and retrieval of data and the quality of outputs.
Specialized knowledge: Advanced knowledge of economic statistical frameworks, principles, and practices as they relate to a specialized subject matter area.

Advanced knowledge of theories, concepts, and principles in statistical measurement, and how they interrelate with at least one specialized economic subject matter area or discipline, is required to design, evaluate, and innovate systems and applications for the production, validation, and dissemination of high-impact statistical outputs. This knowledge is also required to provide subject-matter expertise, advice, and consultative services to Statistic Canada partners, as well as to work with other professionals, in the ongoing production and validation of high-impact statistical data.
In-depth knowledge and mastery in the application of specialized software, such as SAS, for the compilation, validation, and quality assurance of key statistical outputs.
Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of the divisional mandate, activities, priorities, practices, standards and procedures applicable to the work is required to incorporate them into the conduct and management of surveys and complex and technical studies and projects.

Knowledge of the mandate, objectives and organization of Statistics Canada is required to manage subject matter studies, surveys and projects across economic-based divisions. Knowledge of other statistical programs (concepts, methods, and databases) related to the area of expertise is also required to plan and implement statistical activities, to integrate conceptually different data from other programs, to explain variances, and to recommend changes to other statistical programs if necessary.

In-depth knowledge of economics-related subject matter area(s) is required to understand complex data needs from internal and external data users and to deliver expert technical solutions in response to analytical requirements for statistical projects and programs.

Knowledge of departmental publication, marketing and dissemination policies and practices in order to establish common divisional policies and practices in the preparation of statistical tables, charts, explanatory notes etc. for dissemination to user and/or subject matter clients.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies (confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations, data quality), practices and classification systems to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of complex and technical statistical projects and activities.

Knowledge of data suppliers to discuss data reporting agreements. Knowledge of data users from governments and from the private sector is required to identify potential new markets and to understand client needs for complex statistical data or studies.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements to others. Knowledge of the Statistic and Privacy Acts is particularly important with respect to the security and confidentiality of information and data provided and to ensure that they do not release any information which may identify an individual or group without prior consent.
Research and analysis: Interprets the results of tests, procedural investigations, and feasibility studies to produce data bases and data retrieval packages used for the production of integrated statistical information.

Reviews and approves detailed processing parameters, classification, coding systems and report formats or develops new ones to meet specific needs. Some studies may involve a combination of statistical techniques and methods and the integration of data from a wide variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses). Often, the data has been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts and must be translated into common concepts.

Reviews new and revised processing systems and procedures to ensure compatibility with other statistical programs. Assesses technical and conceptual problems and inconsistencies in the manipulation, storage and retrieval of statistical data and develops specifications for new and existing data compilation programs.
Evaluates the impact of technological developments on operation and production procedures and prepares reports recommending appropriate approaches and guidelines.

Research and validation is required to evaluate the effectiveness of the processing systems, to formulate computer systems specifications, to design and create test procedures and acceptance criteria, and to ensure that processing systems yield desired statistical outputs.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Chief
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This is the strongest relationship because the role 'establishes and maintains a framework for the development and on-going operation of statistical systems and processes' and 'evaluates and incorporates all the functions and activities associated with the data collection, processing, editing, compilation, analysis and dissemination of the division's statistical outputs.' That is direct ownership of end-to-end production systems and workflow design. It is stronger than any single method or dissemination subprocess because the responsibility is enterprise-like across the full production chain. Future-state drivers such as integrated data pipelines, enterprise platforms, modular architecture, AI and automation, and workforce skills transition will materially change the work by shifting it toward orchestrated, reusable, secure, and lower-touch production workflows.

key_activities: Manages a section and/or multidisciplinary project teams involved in statistical program operations, analysis, interpretation, marketing and dissemination.
Plans and implements long term strategies for the development, enhancement and operation of statistical programs.

Plans, develops and manages a comprehensive program of detailed analysis and evaluation across sectors and departments to improve existing data, develop new methods of producing, evaluating and analyzing data and to extend the application of divisional statistics.

Implements new systems and processes to meet client demands, identifies new statistical methods, techniques and practices and evaluates the cost, efficiency and productivity of divisional statistical systems and processes.

1. Decision making: Establishes and maintains a framework for the development and on-going operation of statistical systems and processes and evaluates and incorporates all the functions and activities associated with the data collection, processing, editing, compilation, analysis and dissemination of the division's statistical outputs and assesses the impact of changes in both technology and the subject area.

Establishes strategic directions for the management of significant studies, proposes innovative solutions and recommends to senior officials of Statistics Canada new or modified statistical programs to address departmental goals and objectives.

Manages complex studies covering a range of departmental statistical programs, determines the objectives, content and methodology of the research and development work, defines and sets priorities and milestones, selects and evaluates analytical techniques and methods to be used to integrate and interpret massive volumes of data and organizes the review and presentation of findings. Problems to be resolved usually impact on other statistical programs.

Initiates changes and implements new systems and processes to meet client demands, identifies and assesses new statistical methods, techniques and practices and the associated costs and limitations, identifies the availability and reliability of new data sources, evaluates the suitability of new hardware and software and identifies and determines the short and long term program impact and benefits.

Plans and manages the review and evaluation of statistical program methods and concepts to certify the overall quality and completeness of program results, to improve existing data, to develop new techniques and methods of producing, evaluating and analyzing data, to ensure the continued relevancy of data in light of changing requirements, trends, developments, policy issues and socio-economic conditions and to extend the use of statistical programs

Establishes policies and procedures for the security and confidentiality of data and the maintenance and protection of divisional computer systems, equipment, databases and files. The data, systems and equipment are used by staff for the collection, compilation, distribution and analysis of a broad range of statistical and administrative information.
2. Leadership and operational management: Manages, through subordinates, the work of a section and/or multidisciplinary project teams involved in statistical program operations, analysis, interpretation, marketing and dissemination. Establishes objectives and priorities to achieve long term program goals. Participates in the recruitment of staff and approves training and development plans. Allocates human and financial resource needs to achieve objectives. Prepares performance appraisals for subordinate staff, reviews performance appraisals prepared by subordinate supervisors.

Evaluates the cost, efficiency and productivity of statistical systems and processes. Manages budgets including estimates for salaries, professional fees and implementation costs, with authority to allocate/reallocate funds as needed. Submits cost estimates and projections to senior management and authorises expenditures in accordance with approved budgets.

Negotiates and arranges contracts with consulting firms and for the acquisition of services. Selects contractors for specific projects, assigns, directs, manages and evaluates the work according to contract specifications.
3. Communication: Provides expert advisory and consultative services to senior officials and policy makers at all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academics on the results of economic and socio-economic studies and their impact on complex policy issues, on the practical application and interpretation of statistical data, on advanced analytical methods, concepts and techniques, and on economic and social science theories and principles.
Writes reports outlining program results, developments and changes in the subject area in order to explain the nature, content and use of divisional statistical programs.

When addressing the general public, explains in clear terms the interpretation of complex data, reasons for variances in the results and the trends derived. When addressing a specialized public, it is also necessary to provide more detailed explanations of statistical and analytical methods and approaches used. When media representatives challenge or misinterpret the results of surveys or projects, it is necessary to further explain the results and statistical methods and approaches used in order to maintain the department’s reputation for producing high quality data.
Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and groups to develop consensus or share knowledge in a particular field.

Negotiates significant resources and services, timeframes and costs for large scale projects with service providers(e.g. system specialists, regional office staff, survey methodologists, contractors, etc.) and clients within and outside the department.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of economic and sociological principles and theories, especially as they relate to a specialized area, and specific knowledge of the specialized area. This knowledge is required to provide expert advice on the results of surveys and studies to data users, to STC senior management and to other professionals within and outside STC.
Knowledge of advanced statistical theories, methods, concepts and practices used in the development, collection, compilation, analysis and interpretation of statistical data.

Knowledge of writing and editing skills and techniques to write papers, articles and reports and to determine and assess the design and content of studies, articles and reports that will be disseminated widely or published.
Knowledge of management practices and the theories and principles of project management in order to manage staff, either directly or within a matrix management environment.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge and understanding of current and emerging socio-economic trends and issues in Canada and internationally such as the changed social context and the globalization of markets, particularly as they relate to a broad area of expertise including all aspects of a statistical program.

Knowledge of STC policies, practices and classification systems as well as existing data bases, conceptual frameworks, and the statistical methods and procedures applicable to the work, to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of statistical projects and activities, and to recommend changes.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada mandate, objectives, organization, culture and priorities to define the objectives and content of analytical and research projects, as well as other statistical programs related to the area of expertise within the department, especially the concepts, methods, and databases used in other divisions.

Knowledge of the policies and programs of key client departments in order to determine their information requirements, analysis opportunities and to initiate the development of special projects to meet client needs.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act is needed to explain the legislative requirements to other departments, agencies, industry, members of the public and the media. This knowledge, along with knowledge of the Privacy Act is also required to ensure that the organization meets its commitment to ensuring the confidentiality of all information provided to them and does not release any information that identifies an individual or group without prior consent.
Knowledge of a variety of Acts related to the area of expertise such as the Income Tax Act, the Excise Sales Tax Act, the Employment Insurance Act, and the Corporate Returns Act.
6. Research and analysis: Undertakes analytical studies evaluating the effectiveness of divisional statistical programs and the resulting products and services in order to determine the attainment of divisional program objectives and the cost, efficiency and utilization of divisional resources. Prepares reports outlining program results, developments and changes in the subject area in order to explain the nature, content and use of divisional statistical programs.

Identifies gaps and inconsistencies in the collection, processing, analysis and dissemination methods and procedures used, reviews the conceptual framework used and the compatibility with other statistical programs. Conceptualizes enhancements and determines modifications to be made to the program content, coverage and operational procedures, such as new or modified data sources, concepts, methods and definitions to be applied.

Investigates and assesses changes in the statistical needs of clients, determines the extent and approaches of surveys or studies such as the sources of information, statistical techniques, methods and approaches to be used for the collection, processing, analysis and dissemination of the data in an area of specialty modifies existing techniques, methods and approaches or develops new ones to meet specific needs.

Researches and reports on trends and developments in data processing concepts, methods and techniques in order to present options and recommendations on the use and application of new computer hardware and software technology to mass data capture, conversion and dissemination applications; recommends strategies for the introduction or enhancement of statistical programs, the acquisition of new equipment and services and/or the adoption of new collection, production and dissemination strategies.
Writes and presents analytical material and research papers to be disseminated to a target audience ranging from the general public to a specialized audience (e.g. academics).

1. Decision making: Prepares program proposals outlining options and recommendations on the statistical framework, strategies, resource implications and impact of new or modified statistical programs.

Determines the methods, concepts, techniques and practices to be applied in the development and operation of statistical programs regarding the acquisition, production and dissemination of data.

Reviews trends and developments in data processing concepts, methods and techniques in order to present options and recommendations to management on the use and application of new technology to mass data capture, conversion and dissemination applications.
2. Leadership and operational management: Manages a unit and leads project teams for special projects. Assesses program requirements and determines objectives and priorities. Plans and schedules the work, resolves conflicting priorities, ascertains human resource needs, determines the appropriate selection methods (internal and external resources / contractors) to meet program and project objectives, recruits staff, evaluates employee performance or reviews performance evaluations prepared by subordinates and approves training plans.

Plans, develops and manages a budget for the unit in accordance with departmental policy and procedures. Exercises direct authority and accountability for allocated funds to meet planned objectives. Authorises, commits and approves expenditures in accordance with approved budgets with the authority to reallocate funds among line objects.

Negotiates cost reductions and arranges contracts with consulting firms and for the acquisition of services. Selects contractors for specific projects, assigns, directs, manages and evaluates the work according to contract specifications.
3. Communication: Provides expert advisory and consultative services to policy makers at all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academia. Explains and elaborates on statistical program findings and their practical application and interpretation of statistical data and information. This information is used as input to decision making for a vast array of economic and social policies, programs and other activities.

Writes and presents subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify developmental projects and operational systems and processes or program results. When findings are challenged or misinterpreted, it is necessary to present logical arguments to justify the results and to defend the validity of statistical methods and approaches used in order to maintain the department’s reputation for producing high quality data.
Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and groups to develop understanding, consensus and share knowledge of the program area.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of economic or sociology principles and theory to provide expert advisory and consultative services to clients on program results and on the concepts and methods used in mass data processing.

Extensive knowledge of current and emerging socio-economic issues in Canada and internationally, such as the changing social context and the globalization of markets, particularly as they relate to all the aspects of a statistical program. This knowledge is required to analyze program outputs, anticipate and understand needs for new data, and assess the impact on the area of specialization.

Advanced knowledge of systems analysis and design and of new and emerging computer technology and applications in order to establish and manage mass statistical data collection, production and dissemination environments.
Knowledge of the principles and practices of project management including the management of human and financial resources.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of the departmental and divisional mandate, activities, priorities, practices, standards and procedures applicable to the work to incorporate them into the management of a statistical program and to recommend changes to management.

Knowledge of other statistical programs (concepts, methods, and databases) related to the area of expertise to plan and implement statistical activities, to integrate conceptually different data from other programs, to explain variances and to recommend changes to other statistical programs.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies, (e.g. confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations, and data quality), practices and classification systems is required to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of production and dissemination activities.
Knowledge of the policies and programs of key client departments is needed to determine their information requirements.

Knowledge of data users from governments and from the private sector to identify potential new markets, to understand client needs for statistical data or studies, to negotiate contracts and to provide expert advice on program results.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act is needed to explain the legislative requirements to data suppliers/users, and to negotiate special agreements. Knowledge of a variety of Acts related to the area of expertise such as the Income Tax Act, the Excise Sales Tax Act, the Employment Insurance Act, and the Corporate Returns Act.

Source data have often been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts and must be translated into common concepts, taking into consideration the impact of the result on other statistical programs as well as departmental priorities.

Assesses new statistical methods, techniques and practices and the associated costs and limitations and identifies the availability and reliability of new data sources to evaluate the suitability of new hardware and software and to determine the short and long term program impact and benefits.

Analyses the relative quality of data produced by statistical programs, determines reasons for variances; reviews the comparability of data over time and relevance in light of trends, developments, changing requirements, policy issues and socio-economic conditions.

Researches gaps and inconsistencies in the production and dissemination methods and procedures, reviews the conceptual framework used and the compatibility with other statistical programs. Problems to be resolved usually impact on other statistical programs.
Investigates client requirements for statistical information and determines the capacity and ability of existing or modified systems to meet these requirements.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Coordinator
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: The strongest relationship is with Design production systems and workflows because the work description centers on coordinating and improving end-to-end operational systems for collection, coding and processing. Evidence includes: 'Coordinates and organizes the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data'; 'Develops operational plans and procedures'; 'Develops and outlines system requirements'; and 'Writes specifications and guidelines to be used by others in developing or operating systems and processes.' This is stronger than narrower subprocesses such as 2.3 or 2.5 because the role spans multiple stages and explicitly addresses how systems, processes, testing, integrity, security, and work groups fit together. Future-state drivers such as Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Workforce Skills Transition will materially change this work by increasing the need to configure reusable enterprise workflows, standardize handoffs, embed monitoring and controls, and redesign staff roles from manual execution toward oversight, coordination, and exception handling.

key_activities: Coordinates and organizes the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data.
Reviews and documents operational processes and assesses the quality and application of data outputs in order to propose solutions or explain results.
Provides advice to users on the methods and procedures related to statistical operations services.
Participates as a statistical operations representative on various teams and working groups.
Leads the activities of work groups involved in different stages of data collection operations.

1. Decision making: Develops operational plans and procedures for the manual and automated collection, coding and processing of statistical data.

Outlines proposals for changes and improvements to survey content and coverage, questionnaire design, collection and processing of data, and the implementation and use of new hardware and software options to support survey development and assessment.

Determines the nature of the problem with respect to data inconsistency or integrity, reviews operational processes, and assesses the quality and application of data outputs in order to propose solutions or explain results.
Specifies testing approaches, plans and environments for use by other project staff to set up and carry out acceptance testing of new or modified computer applications.
Prepares and implements policies and guidelines to maintain the integrity, security and 'back-up' systems and processes.
Reviews test results from new or revised procedures to determine the impact on existing program operations. Documents the results and prepares recommendations for implementation.
2. Leadership and operational management: Leads work groups established to coordinate and implement statistical production activities: assigns work; provides feedback on performance of working group members; monitors progress against objectives and provides guidance and direction to working group members; identifies financial and human resource needs.

Monitors and tracks time spent on activities for the purposes of recording and recovering such costs from the client. Responsible for identifying costs and fees associated with cost recovery activities and preparing estimates for special requests and tabulations based upon established fee schedules. Responsible for the acquisition of goods and services, according to the budget allocated. Incurs and accounts for petty cash, credit card, taxi voucher, bus pass, and other expenditures.
3. Communication: Interprets and clarifies client requests and inquiries for statistical data and information; responds orally or in writing to enquiries from managers, employees and the general public to provide information on the operation of divisional systems and processes and the use of program results.

Meets with subject matter and systems specialists, clients, service providers and others to establish and elaborate the framework and conditions within which statistical operations will occur. There is a requirement to understand the issues and resolve differences that can affect the efficiency of the division's operations and quality of outputs.

Contacts data suppliers or respondents to obtain their collaboration in responding to surveys, to clarify problems or irregularities, to explain technical procedures for obtaining the data in the appropriate format, or to clarify and explain statistical concepts.
Designs and prepares statistical tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text for use in statistical analysis by clients both inside and outside Statistics Canada.
Writes specifications and guidelines to be used by others in developing or operating systems and processes.
Participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and working groups in order to share knowledge within an area of operational expertise.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of the statistical and economic concepts and principles used in the collection, coding and processing of statistical data in order to recommend and implement improvements to survey collection, coding and processing activities.

Knowledge of system analysis and design, computer processing, generalized survey software packages to oversee the design, testing, operation and maintenance of processing systems; to design specifications for the testing of data, and to maintain and use databases.
Knowledge of project and time management methods, practices and techniques to develop work plans, estimate resource requirements and to monitor and report on work progress.

Knowledge of methods and practices of operating personal computers in a network environment and of using databases and software packages (word processing, statistical analysis, graphics, spreadsheets, etc.) to prepare correspondence, reports and presentations.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of developments and changes in the subject area that may affect the efficiency and validity of data collection, coding and processing in order to devise and modify operational systems and processes.

Knowledge of the departmental and divisional mandate, objectives, priorities, practices, standards, processes and procedures in order to coordinate and manage on-going operational activities and/or special projects.

Knowledge of departmental publication, marketing and dissemination policies and practices in order to establish common divisional policies and practices in the preparation of statistical tables, charts, explanatory notes for dissemination to user and/or subject matter clients.

Knowledge of statistical programs within Statistics Canada in order to identify potential sources of information for operations and/or special studies and to identify and evaluate possible data conflicts.
Knowledge of contacts within key client departments to understand and explain the need for statistical data, and to provide advice and guidance on survey concepts, methods, techniques and results.
Knowledge of data sources and contacts within and external to Statistics Canada to obtain collaboration in the provision of statistical information and to verify the accuracy of data.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to ensure understanding and application in the collection, coding and processing of data. The position must have a particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data to ensure their own actions are in compliance.
6. Research and analysis: Researches options and requirements for the operation of divisional statistical systems and processes in order to assist in the establishment of divisional and program objectives and priorities.

Reviews and compares the concepts and definitions of data sources with those of the statistical program. Reconciles differences and develops special methods of adjusting source data. This requires interpreting or adapting practices.
Develops and outlines system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in revising existing systems or in developing new processing systems.
Assesses trends and developments in the program area by preparing tabulations and reviews outlining program results for use by program managers and general data users.

Knowledge of methods and practices of operating personal computers in a network environment and of using databases and software packages (word processing, statistical analysis, graphics, spreadsheets, etc.) to prepare correspondence, reports and presentations.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of developments and changes in the subject area that may affect the efficiency and validity of data collection, coding and processing in order to devise and modify operational systems and processes.

Knowledge of the departmental and divisional mandate, objectives, priorities, practices, standards, processes and procedures in order to coordinate and manage on-going operational activities and/or special projects.

Knowledge of departmental publication, marketing and dissemination policies and practices in order to establish common divisional policies and practices in the preparation of statistical tables, charts, explanatory notes for dissemination to user and/or subject matter clients.

Knowledge of statistical programs within Statistics Canada in order to identify potential sources of information for operations and/or special studies and to identify and evaluate possible data conflicts.
Knowledge of contacts within key client departments to understand and explain the need for statistical data, and to provide advice and guidance on survey concepts, methods, techniques and results.
Knowledge of data sources and contacts within and external to Statistics Canada to obtain collaboration in the provision of statistical information and to verify the accuracy of data.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to ensure understanding and application in the collection, coding and processing of data. The position must have a particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data to ensure their own actions are in compliance.
6. Research and analysis: Researches options and requirements for the operation of divisional statistical systems and processes in order to assist in the establishment of divisional and program objectives and priorities.

Reviews and compares the concepts and definitions of data sources with those of the statistical program. Reconciles differences and develops special methods of adjusting source data. This requires interpreting or adapting practices.
Develops and outlines system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in revising existing systems or in developing new processing systems.
Assesses trends and developments in the program area by preparing tabulations and reviews outlining program results for use by program managers and general data users.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Development Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: The strongest relationship is with Design production systems and workflows because the position explicitly 'develops and coordinates the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, capture, coding and processing of data.' It also 'recommends new approaches,' 'evaluates changes in statistical needs,' and provides advice on 'collection and production efficiency and/or quality.' This indicates responsibility for shaping and improving the overall operational workflow and production model, not only executing one step. This is stronger than 2.3 or 2.5 individually because the role spans collection, capture, coding and processing and participates department-wide on teams and working groups. Future drivers such as Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, AI and Automation in Statistical Production, and Governance/efficiency drivers will likely require more enterprise-standard workflow design, reusable services, clearer handoffs, and stronger role redesign around automated production.

key_activities: Develops and coordinates the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, capture, coding and processing of data.
Reviews data inconsistency and integrity problems, recommends new approaches and resolves reporting and respondent relations issues.
Evaluates changes in statistical needs of clients, as well as trends and developments in data collection, capture, coding and processing.
Provides advisory and consultative services to users regarding collection and production efficiency and/or quality.
Participates as a statistical operations representative on teams and working groups throughout the department.
Leads project teams involved in the collection, capture, coding and processing of statistical data.
