position_information.position_title: Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer
key_activities: Develops processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.
Designs specifications for the testing of data and for the maintenance and development of databases.
Assesses changes in the subject area and determines the need to modify or replace processing systems and applications for the manipulation, storage and retrieval of statistical data
Provides subject matter advice and direction to users, negotiates procedural modifications and establishes project plans, priorities and target dates.
Participates as a subject area representative on teams and working groups throughout the department.
Leads project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems.

1. Decision making: Identifies and assesses changes and developments in the subject area; determines the impact on program subject-matter content and the implication for statistical methods and procedures and the dissemination of program results.

Develops subject-matter concepts and definitions; proposes new statistical methods, techniques and approaches or the modification of existing techniques and approaches to improve program coverage or to meet specific needs.

Identifies and evaluates problems in the manipulation, storage and retrieval of statistical information to provide solutions or recommendations to management and to resolve subject-matter, conceptual and technical problems referred by staff.
Implements enhancements or modifications to processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.
2. Leadership and operational management: Leads project teams or work units. Determines goals, priorities and milestones, sets objectives, and plans and schedules the work, resolves conflicting priorities; assesses human resources needs, recommends the appropriate selection methods (internal and external resources / contractors) to meet program objectives, recruits staff, evaluates employee performance, develops training plans, motivates and maintains morale of employees.

Plans and budgets for special projects, including estimates for salaries, professional fees and implementation costs, with authority to allocate funds within budget. Provides input to budgets based on operational needs and by obtaining/providing cost estimates for personnel, supplies, equipment purchases and travel for use in developing section or division budgets. Procures goods and services within approved budget allocations.
3. Communication: Discusses program subject-matter content requirements with operations managers, other subject matter and systems specialists, clients, service providers and others to comprehend and elaborate the framework and conditions within which statistical development and operations will occur. There is a requirement to understand the issues and resolve differences that can affect the efficiency of the division's operations and quality of outputs.

Liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development, to suggest improvements to ongoing programs, to negotiate procedural modifications and to establish project plans, priorities and target dates. Writes and presents detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify divisional program content and applications.

Writes analytical reports and articles on the interpretation of surveys, statistical applications or project findings and the methodology used. These reports and articles are to be reviewed by program managers and included into publications. Exchanges information and provides advice to professionals from the private sector or from other statistical agencies abroad on subject-matter concepts and definitions, statistical survey methods and techniques. This information is used to develop similar surveys or analytical projects.

Provides guidance to other STC professionals on subject-matter concepts and definitions, survey methods, statistical applications and techniques used. This information is used to implement similar surveys or projects.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of current or emerging economic and social issues relating to the program area in order to identify and resolve existing and potential subject-matter conflicts, duplication and gaps.

Knowledge of the concepts, methods and techniques used in the manipulation, storage and retrieval of statistical data in order to coordinate and advise on subject-matter development and resolve subject-matter concept and definition issues.

Knowledge of system analysis and design, computer processing, generalized survey software packages to manage the design, development, testing, maintenance and implementation of processing systems; to design specifications for the testing of data, and to maintain and develop databases.
Knowledge of high level programming languages, utility programs or statistical packages to retrieve and manipulate data.
Knowledge of management techniques and principles to manage financial and human resources, either directly or within a matrix management environment.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of statistical programs within Statistics Canada related to the area of expertise in order to identify and select sources of information for development and operations and/or special studies and to identify and evaluate data conflicts.

Knowledge of contacts within key client departments to establish a liaison; to understand need for statistical data, and to provide advice and guidance on subject-matter concepts, methods, techniques and results.
Knowledge of the divisional mandate, objectives, priorities, practices, standards, processes and procedures in order to coordinate and manage on-going operational activities and/or special projects.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements to data suppliers, users and others with respect to the manipulation, storage and retrieval of data. Knowledge of the Statistics and Privacy Acts is particulary important with respect to the security and confidentiality of information and data provided and to ensure that they and their subordinates do not release any information which may identify an individual or group without prior consent.
6. Research and analysis: Plans and implements the review and development of new subject-matter methods, concepts and definitions and conducts studies and analytical projects to improve existing surveys and data.

Analyzes current manipulation, storage and retrieval methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to determine the need for modification or replacement with alternative systems, methods and procedures.

Conducts feasibility studies concerning new system and product requirements by examining existing, proposed or new software programs and systems to determine their feasibility and adaptability to the needs of the statistical program.

Provides subject-matter interpretation and analysis to media representatives on the results of surveys or projects, and the interpretation of statistical data. This information is disseminated to the Canadian population for information and decision making purposes.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Production and Database Expert
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This is highly relevant because the position develops, modifies, tests and maintains processing components and database capabilities used in production. Evidence includes: 'develops guidelines for the design, evaluation, and testing of processing systems and applications,' 'develops specifications for new and existing data compilation programs,' 'reviews new and revised processing systems and procedures,' and 'research and validation is required... to design and create test procedures and acceptance criteria.' This matches reusing or building processing and analysis components such as transformation, workflow, database and data services. It is ranked below 2.6 because the role appears to span architecture and operational production-system design more broadly than component build alone. Drivers such as AI and automation, modular reusable components, open-source and enterprise platforms will increase demand for reusable processing services, stronger testing/validation patterns, and skills in component-based modernization rather than custom program-by-program builds.

key_activities: Innovates and implements the design, evaluation, and applications for the manipulation, storage, and retrieval of high-impact statistical data.

Develops and maintains production and dissemination processes and outputs for analytical databases and provides support for tools and systems for the delivery of high-impact statistical programs, new products, special studies, and ad hoc requests.
Coordinates activities of multiple Statistic Canada divisional partners and other external partners to process, validate, and disseminate statistical data.
Provides specialized expertise and consultative services regarding production systems and processes for ongoing statistical program delivery.
Represents economic subject matter divisions on statistical development projects.
Occasionally leads project teams and undertakes complex technical projects in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems.

Decision Making: Integrates input from multiple economic subject matter areas to develop and maintain complex systems and frameworks for the ongoing production, validation and dissemination of a range of specialized, high-impact statistical outputs.
Operationalizes specialized conceptual and measurement frameworks in the development of production, validation and dissemination systems, processes and databases.

Evaluates alternatives and develops and applies new strategies to maintain and improve operational systems, processes and databases in the production and dissemination of official statistics. Decisions and recommendations regarding data production and dissemination practices impact multiple projects and high-impact statistical programs.
Develops and implements quality-assurance processes for high-impact statistical outputs.

Investigates requirements for statistical information and analysis, defines the nature and scope of special studies, data requirements, and decides the methods and approaches to be used to satisfy complex data requirements. Modifies existing techniques or develops new approaches to meet specific needs.

Defines project objectives and priorities, prepares work plans and summaries outlining approaches, time-frames and resources. Each project is unique in nature and decisions impact on other ongoing studies.
Develops guidelines for the design, evaluation, and testing of processing systems and applications and recommends and implements modifications and improvements to existing procedures.
Recommends and executes solutions to resolve complex technical issues pertaining to data production and dissemination that may lack precedents.
Develops data bases for the provision of time-series information, interprets preliminary results, reviews, and modifies approaches and techniques as necessary.
Reviews and approves detailed processing parameters, devises criteria and methods to rectify inconsistencies, and recommends modifications to ensure the continuity and compatibility of data.
Leadership And Operational Management: Occasionally plans, organizes and functionally coordinates the work of multiple partners within Statistic Canada divisions and units, as well as clients from other federal government departments involved in the conduct of statistical processing, validation and dissemination of specialized statistical outputs. Determines goals, priorities and milestones, sets objectives, plans and schedules the work and resolves conflicting priorities.
Establishes and coordinates schedules for the production, validation and dissemination of regular statistical outputs across multiple production teams.
Coordinates input and specifications from multiple partners to implement specialized solutions according to established production schedules in the context of complex statistical frameworks.
Communication: Provides expert advice and guidance to internal partners on statistical program results, dissemination methods, concepts, and techniques applied and on trends and developments in economic or related data programs. This information is used as input to decision making for a vast array of economic programs and other activities.
Interprets specialized information pertaining to a range of specialized subject matter areas to present arguments and options to clients within and outside the department.

Communicates subject matter concepts and technical definitions to internal contacts and other subject matter experts to explain and clarify current developments, to explain the results of studies, and to resolve differences that can affect the efficiency of the manipulation, storage, and retrieval of data and the quality of outputs.
Specialized knowledge: Advanced knowledge of economic statistical frameworks, principles, and practices as they relate to a specialized subject matter area.

Advanced knowledge of theories, concepts, and principles in statistical measurement, and how they interrelate with at least one specialized economic subject matter area or discipline, is required to design, evaluate, and innovate systems and applications for the production, validation, and dissemination of high-impact statistical outputs. This knowledge is also required to provide subject-matter expertise, advice, and consultative services to Statistic Canada partners, as well as to work with other professionals, in the ongoing production and validation of high-impact statistical data.
In-depth knowledge and mastery in the application of specialized software, such as SAS, for the compilation, validation, and quality assurance of key statistical outputs.
Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of the divisional mandate, activities, priorities, practices, standards and procedures applicable to the work is required to incorporate them into the conduct and management of surveys and complex and technical studies and projects.

Knowledge of the mandate, objectives and organization of Statistics Canada is required to manage subject matter studies, surveys and projects across economic-based divisions. Knowledge of other statistical programs (concepts, methods, and databases) related to the area of expertise is also required to plan and implement statistical activities, to integrate conceptually different data from other programs, to explain variances, and to recommend changes to other statistical programs if necessary.

In-depth knowledge of economics-related subject matter area(s) is required to understand complex data needs from internal and external data users and to deliver expert technical solutions in response to analytical requirements for statistical projects and programs.

Knowledge of departmental publication, marketing and dissemination policies and practices in order to establish common divisional policies and practices in the preparation of statistical tables, charts, explanatory notes etc. for dissemination to user and/or subject matter clients.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies (confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations, data quality), practices and classification systems to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of complex and technical statistical projects and activities.

Knowledge of data suppliers to discuss data reporting agreements. Knowledge of data users from governments and from the private sector is required to identify potential new markets and to understand client needs for complex statistical data or studies.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements to others. Knowledge of the Statistic and Privacy Acts is particularly important with respect to the security and confidentiality of information and data provided and to ensure that they do not release any information which may identify an individual or group without prior consent.
Research and analysis: Interprets the results of tests, procedural investigations, and feasibility studies to produce data bases and data retrieval packages used for the production of integrated statistical information.

Reviews and approves detailed processing parameters, classification, coding systems and report formats or develops new ones to meet specific needs. Some studies may involve a combination of statistical techniques and methods and the integration of data from a wide variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses). Often, the data has been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts and must be translated into common concepts.

Reviews new and revised processing systems and procedures to ensure compatibility with other statistical programs. Assesses technical and conceptual problems and inconsistencies in the manipulation, storage and retrieval of statistical data and develops specifications for new and existing data compilation programs.
Evaluates the impact of technological developments on operation and production procedures and prepares reports recommending appropriate approaches and guidelines.

Research and validation is required to evaluate the effectiveness of the processing systems, to formulate computer systems specifications, to design and create test procedures and acceptance criteria, and to ensure that processing systems yield desired statistical outputs.

gsbpm_description: This sub-process describes the activities to build new components or reuse existing components needed for the dissemination of statistical products as designed in sub-process 2.1 (Design outputs and dissemination). All types of dissemination components are included, from those that produce traditional paper publications to those that provide web services, (linked) open data outputs, geospatial statistics, maps, or access to microdata.

drivers.driver: AI and Automation in Statistical Production
workforce_implications: agency staff will integrate AI assistants into their daily work to increase efficiency
clarify handoffs across programs
developing skills to support the adoption of modern, open-source technologies and AI
enhancing executives' skills in all areas, from AI upskilling and strengthening leadership competencies, to promoting their change leadership capacity
extensive coordination across the agency's collection, communications, analysis and dissemination teams
involve the recruitment of thousands of employees—including enumerators who conduct in-person data collection
reduce manual effort
requires extensive preparation to ensure that Statistics Canada's infrastructure, systems and workforce ready to deliver Canada's largest statistical undertaking
work embedded directly into production workflows
drivers.impact: Dissemination component builds are materially affected by AI-enabled search and chatbot capabilities, along with reusable web and platform components that automate user access and support more scalable dissemination services.
impact_mechanisms: AI chatbots, chatbot, and website search drive new dissemination service components
enterprise platforms and shared solutions support reusable dissemination infrastructure
automation reduces manual handling in product assembly and user navigation
public trust, transparency, and governance require careful controls and documentation for AI-enabled dissemination tools
extensive coordination across communications and dissemination teams affects implementation of these components

drivers.driver: Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access
drivers.impact: Dissemination components are directly affected because secure publication channels, controlled microdata access and privacy-preserving delivery mechanisms must be built into dissemination services. The driver is especially material for web services, open data platforms and researcher access environments.
impact_mechanisms: secure access and authorizations are central to controlled access for confidential outputs and microdata
privacy requirements affect dissemination component design for suppression, filtering and controlled release
cyber security requirements shape protection of public and restricted dissemination services
platforms and tooling determine how securely dissemination services can be deployed, monitored and maintained
safer innovation supports new dissemination modes only where confidentiality and security risks are managed

drivers.driver: Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure
technology_themes: scalable, secure and sustainable digital infrastructure
workforce_implications: empower employees to access the IT systems and resources they need, when they need them
extensive coordination across the agency's collection, communications, analysis and dissemination teams
involve the recruitment of thousands of employees—including enumerators who conduct in-person data collection
make it easier for employees to locate, analyze and use the data and tools they need
make it easier for employees to locate, analyze and use the data and tools they need to deliver results efficiently
providing robust information technology (IT) infrastructure, advanced IT tools and strengthened cyber security
requires extensive preparation to ensure that Statistics Canada's infrastructure, systems and workforce ready to deliver Canada's largest statistical undertaking
self-serve platforms will also empower employees to access the IT systems and resources they need, when they need them
supports digital readiness and modern infrastructure for employees
drivers.impact: Dissemination component build is materially affected because enterprise digital platforms and cloud infrastructure enable scalable web services, open data delivery, controlled microdata access and reusable dissemination tooling. Security and authorization controls become embedded in dissemination components.
impact_mechanisms: Cloud, platforms and digital infrastructure support scalable dissemination services and online products
Self-serve platforms and tooling enable reusable dissemination components and user-facing services
Secure access, authorizations, privacy and data security directly shape controlled-access dissemination components
Target Enterprise Architecture promotes reuse of common dissemination services across programs
Capability themes of data accessibility and usability, faster delivery and operational efficiency drive platform-based dissemination builds
Workforce coordination across analysis, communications and dissemination teams increases the need for shared enterprise dissemination components

drivers.driver: Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability
drivers.impact: Dissemination components are strongly affected because the driver requires dissemination platforms to support searchable metadata, standardized asset descriptions, and stronger linkage between data products and their metadata for reuse and access.
impact_mechanisms: Searchable repositories require dissemination components with indexing and metadata-based discovery functions.
Standardized data assets require reusable dissemination services that consistently expose metadata.
Metadata-rich outputs improve interoperability for web services, linked open data and microdata access channels.
The driver increases the need for components that bind data products to descriptive, structural and quality metadata.

drivers.driver: Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development
capability_themes: capacity required to support solutions over time
workforce_implications: Teams will be supported as they continue to adopt open‑source tools while meeting ongoing production responsibilities
greater emphasis on validation, upskilling and governance
including through training and collaborative development practices
drivers.impact: Dissemination component build is materially affected because dissemination products are increasingly expected to run on shared, reusable services and modular publishing components. Self-service development can accelerate product assembly, but only within governance, interoperability, and secure production constraints.
impact_mechanisms: reusable solutions and shared components support standard dissemination services, templates, and publishing modules
interoperability enables dissemination through APIs, linked open data services, and shared metadata services
enterprise architecture and governance constrain dissemination builds to approved enterprise patterns
open-source tools may be used for dissemination components but require validation and production controls
secure and stable production environments are critical for public-facing dissemination services
upskilling and collaborative development practices support business-led assembly of dissemination products using approved components

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Development and Evaluation Specialist
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: Reuse or build dissemination components is the third strongest relationship because the role develops, enhances, implements and tests methods, procedures and systems used in the production and dissemination of statistical metadata. Evidence includes 'developing specifications for, implementing and testing modifications in methods and procedures' and directing documentation, procedures manuals and training materials related to metadata dissemination. This is stronger than broader design subprocesses because the role is operationally involved in modifying and testing dissemination-related metadata systems and methods. Future drivers such as modular reusable components, enterprise dissemination platforms, and metadata-rich product standards will likely move this work further toward reusable metadata services, interoperable dissemination components and governed self-service metadata tooling.

Wellness at Statistics Canada
HR committees

Corporate service providers

1. Decision Making: Plans, prioritizes, coordinates, directs, monitors and undertakes the development and preparation of statistical metadata for storage and dissemination, reviewing, editing and validating statistical metadata.

Evaluates and investigates corporate and client the metadata requirements, estimates the time required to complete tasks and assesses issues related to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata in order to provide direction to clients and management with respect to possible approaches, priorities, target dates and training plans; to resolve conceptual and technical problems; and to provide feedback on the capacity and ability of existing methods, procedures and systems to fulfill client requirements effectively and efficiently.

Reviews trends and developments in the area of statistical metadata management, liaising with internal and external clients within Canada, in order to determine the need for short-term projects and strategies relevant to the development, enhancement and implementation of methods and procedures used at Statistics Canada for managing statistical metadata; recommending plans to improve methods and procedures; developing specifications for, implementing and testing modifications in methods and procedures; and identifying the impacts and results of new or modified approaches to metadata management.

Directs the development of, evaluates, and approves reports, documentation, procedures manuals and training materials which are related to the production, storage dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata and which are distributed internally and externally within Canada.

Plans, directs and undertakes quality evaluations in accordance with documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines, reviews and certifies the results of quality evaluations undertaken by subordinates and colleagues, compiles results and writes reports for clients and management; and presents results to management.

Provides input to management decisions and recommendations designed to develop or improve departmental, divisional and program initiatives covering areas such as recruitment, training, official languages, wellness, employment equity and information management.
2. Leadership And Operational Management: Manages a unit involved in activities related to the development and evaluation of statistical metadata and/or leads multi-disciplinary project teams for special metadata projects. Determines goals, priorities and milestones, sets objectives, and plans and schedules the work, resolves conflicting priorities; identifies human resources needs, determines the appropriate selection methods (internal and external resources) to meet program or project objectives, recruits staff, evaluates employee performance, develops training plans, motivates and maintains morale of employees.

Plans and budgets for on-going and/or special projects, including estimates for salaries, professional fees and implementation costs, with authority to allocate/reallocate funds within the budget and in accordance with Statistics Canada’s policies and procedures. Provides input to budgets based on operational needs and by obtaining/providing cost estimates for personnel, supplies, equipment purchases and travel for use in developing section or division budgets. Establishes and negotiates contracts for projects. Responsible for the acquisition of goods and services, according to the budget allocated.
3. Communication: Provides expert advice and training with respect to the policies, directives, guidelines, methods, procedures and systems used in the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata to subordinates, other statistical metadata specialists, systems specialists, clients and managers who use the information as input to on-going operations and to decisions concerning the management of statistical metadata at Statistics Canada and within other national organizations and agencies.

Liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, systems specialists, clients and managers at Statistics Canada to plan statistical metadata projects and implement short-term strategies for the development and enhancement of policies, procedures and methods used in the management of statistical metadata; to develop and translate strategies and requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata; to establish project plans, priorities and target dates; to negotiate modifications to methods, procedures and timelines; to coordinate and deliver training, and to suggest improvements to methods, procedures and systems.

Writes detailed reports and prepares and delivers presentations which explain rationale, requirements and results relating to policies, directives, guidelines, methods and procedures used in the production, storage and dissemination of statistical metadata and which are used by other statistical metadata specialists, systems specialists, clients, and management in the operation and enhancement of statistical metadata management programs.

Writes reports which describe policy requirements related to the development, production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of high quality metadata, which describe the results of metadata quality evaluations and which make recommendations for procedures and tools that could be developed to evaluate the quality of statistical metadata. These reports are used by clients and management to ensure the quality and consistency of statistical metadata disseminated by Statistics Canada.
Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and workgroups to develop consensus or share knowledge within the area of expertise.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Advanced knowledge of statistical metadata concepts and frameworks used within Canada and internationally and knowledge of how those concepts and frameworks are used and reflected in policies, methods and procedures relating to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata in order to plan, prioritize, coordinate, direct, monitor and undertake the preparation, editing, validation and quality evaluation of statistical metadata and short-term strategies for the enhancement of statistical metadata management processes

Advanced knowledge of methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata and the potential impacts of new or modified methods, procedures and systems on project teams and clients in order to plan, prioritize, coordinate, direct, monitor and undertake statistical metadata projects and short-term strategies for the development, operation and enhancement of statistical metadata management processes; to recommend improvements to methods, procedures and training; to develop procedures and tools for evaluating the quality of statistical metadata; and to explain the results of metadata quality evaluations.

Knowledge of survey and statistical program subject matter concepts, methods and techniques relevant to the collection, processing, certification and dissemination of data in order to evaluate client requirements for metadata production, storage and dissemination; to determine when changes in the needs of clients will impact statistical metadata programs and projects; and to more accurately and efficiently evaluate the quality of statistical metadata across surveys and statistical programs.

Knowledge of management principles, techniques and practices in order to lead a multi-disciplinary project team and manage financial and human resources, either directly or within a matrix management environment. Knowledge of the principles and practices of project management used at Statistics Canada.
Knowledge of software, statistical packages and programming languages used in the production, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata
5. Contextual knowledge: Advanced knowledge of Statistics Canada and Government of Canada policies, directives and guidelines directly and specifically related to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata, as well as other Statistics Canada policies, in order to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of all program activities and in order to explain policy requirements to clients and partners within Canada.

Knowledge of other statistical metadata management programs within Statistics Canada in order to integrate conceptually and structurally the statistical metadata required for various activities and programs.

Advanced knowledge of contacts within key client Divisions in order to establish a liaison; to evaluate and understand program statistical metadata requirements; and to provide expert assistance, advice and direction with respect to policy requirements, methods, procedures, systems, training, priorities and timelines relevant to the production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation of statistical metadata.

Knowledge of surveys and statistical programs within Statistics Canada in order to establish short-term priorities for the processing, storage, dissemination and evaluation of metadata across program areas and to effectively and efficiently direct metadata quality assessment projects, certifying and reporting to management on the overall quality, completeness, coherence and consistency of statistical metadata.

Knowledge of the mandate, objectives, organization, practices, policies, culture and priorities of Statistics Canada in order to ensure that these are reflected in the objectives and management of all statistical metadata projects and short-term strategies for the development and enhancement of statistical metadata management processes and systems, and to explain the context of statistical metadata management at Statistics Canada to clients and partners across Canada.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and Privacy Act is required in order to ensure understanding and application of these Acts in the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata, particularly with respect to the security and confidentiality of statistical metadata and other information; to explain legislative requirements to other departments, agencies, industry, members of the public and the media; and to ensure that Statistics Canada meets its commitment to ensuring confidentiality and does not release any information that identifies an individual or group without prior consent.
6. Research and analysis: Analyses and synthesizes diverse sources of statistical metadata in order to ensure that the quantity and quality of statistical metadata disseminated is optimal for Statistics Canada’s surveys and statistical programs.

Provides expert assistance, advice and direction to internal clients and external clients within Canada with respect to statistical metadata, documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines, determining changes in the needs of clients, assessing the impacts of these changes on statistical metadata programs and projects, and establishing short-term plans and priorities.

Analyses client requirements in order to determine the feasibility, procedural options, priorities, and target dates relevant to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata in order to ensure that approaches and results are consistent within, and across, surveys and statistical programs, and in order to direct and monitor statistical metadata projects and short-term strategies for the development, operation and enhancement of statistical metadata management processes.

Analyzes current production, storage, dissemination and evaluation methods, procedures and systems in comparison to those used elsewhere at Statistics Canada and elsewhere in Canada in order to ascertain their relevancy and to determine the need for modifications or the use of alternative methods, procedures and systems which would result in operational efficiencies and/or improvements in the quality of statistical metadata at Statistics Canada.

Analyzes changes in methods, procedures and systems used to produce, store, disseminate and evaluate the quality of statistical metadata in order to determine the need to update statistical metadata or adapt it to new formats; to determine where updates are required to existing documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals and to prioritize those updates; and to determine and mitigate potential short-term and long-term impacts on clients.

Analyses the quality of statistical metadata produced by surveys and statistical programs at Statistics Canada; evaluates current and proposed methods, procedures and tools for evaluating the quality of statistical metadata in order to develop enhancements; analyses gaps and inconsistencies in metadata quality and suggests possible reasons for variances among program areas; reviews the comparability of metadata over time in light of changing policy requirements, systems functionality and changing methodologies used by statistical programs; provides management with reports of findings.

gsbpm_description: This sub-process configures the workflows, systems and transformations used within the business processes, from data collection through to dissemination. In this sub-process, the workflows are configured based on the design created in sub-process 2.6 (Design production systems and workflows). This could include modifying a standardised workflow for a specific purpose, assembling the workflows for the different phases together (possibly with a workflow/business process management system) and configuring systems accordingly.

Target Enterprise Architecture drives standard workflow patterns and system interoperability
Centralized data repository and data platforms affect workflow handoffs and data movement configuration
Cyber security, secure access, authorizations and privacy controls must be configured into workflows
Capability themes of faster delivery, operational efficiency and digital readiness support workflow automation and standardization
Workforce implications around employee access to systems and cross-team coordination make workflow usability and role configuration materially important

drivers.driver: Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline
workforce_implications: scarce resources are focused on the highest-value outcomes
drivers.impact: Workflow configuration is materially affected because stronger governance and decision discipline constrain how far teams can customize workflows, reinforce enterprise-standard configurations, and require clearer approval and accountability for deviations and resource use.
impact_mechanisms: Accountability capability clarifies who can approve workflow configurations and exceptions.
Prioritization capability determines which workflow changes are implemented when resources are limited.
Transparent trade-offs capability makes deviations from standard workflows more explicit and justifiable.
Cross-field decision-making capability is needed when workflow configuration affects shared services or multiple production areas.
Workforce implication of scarce resources being focused on highest-value outcomes encourages configuration choices that maximize reuse and minimize low-value customization.

drivers.driver: Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration
capability_themes: Automated monitoring and control of production flow
Coordinated execution across collection, processing, analysis and dissemination
workforce_implications: Shift from manual step execution to pipeline supervision
Greater need for workflow configuration and orchestration skills
Greater emphasis on exception handling rather than routine processing
Need for cross-functional coordination across production stages
Increased operational responsibility for monitoring automated end-to-end runs
drivers.impact: This is one of the most directly affected subprocesses because the driver centers on configuring orchestrated end-to-end workflows, automated triggers, dependencies, and handoffs across the production chain.
impact_mechanisms: Process orchestration directly changes how workflows are assembled and configured
Event-driven workflows require trigger-based execution and dependency management
Automated handoffs across production stages reduce manual transitions between phases
Workflow/business process management systems become core enabling technology
Staff need workflow configuration and operational monitoring skills rather than manual coordination of stage transitions

drivers.driver: Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability
drivers.impact: Workflow configuration is materially affected because metadata capture, propagation, linkage and publication must be configured across the end-to-end process. Metadata handling becomes part of operational workflow orchestration rather than a separate documentation activity.
impact_mechanisms: Metadata-driven workflows require configuration of metadata handoffs between collection, processing, analysis and dissemination.
Standardized workflows are needed to consistently manage metadata-rich assets across processes.
Discoverability depends on configured steps that publish or register metadata into searchable repositories.
System transformations must preserve metadata lineage and associations as data move through the workflow.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Production and Database Expert
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: Configure workflows is the second strongest fit because the role moves beyond design into implementation of new or modified processing systems and maintenance of operational production flows. Evidence includes 'occasionally leads project teams and undertakes complex technical projects in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems', 'establishes and coordinates schedules for the production, validation and dissemination of regular statistical outputs across multiple production teams', and 'coordinates input and specifications from multiple partners to implement specialized solutions according to established production schedules'. This is stronger than pure build of individual components because the work emphasizes operational configuration, parameters, schedules, handoffs and coordinated execution across teams. Future drivers around integrated process orchestration, execution discipline, secure workflow controls, and efficiency pressures will likely increase the need for workflow configuration, monitoring, exception handling and standardized reusable flows.

key_activities: Innovates and implements the design, evaluation, and applications for the manipulation, storage, and retrieval of high-impact statistical data.

Develops and maintains production and dissemination processes and outputs for analytical databases and provides support for tools and systems for the delivery of high-impact statistical programs, new products, special studies, and ad hoc requests.
Coordinates activities of multiple Statistic Canada divisional partners and other external partners to process, validate, and disseminate statistical data.
Provides specialized expertise and consultative services regarding production systems and processes for ongoing statistical program delivery.
Represents economic subject matter divisions on statistical development projects.
Occasionally leads project teams and undertakes complex technical projects in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems.

Decision Making: Integrates input from multiple economic subject matter areas to develop and maintain complex systems and frameworks for the ongoing production, validation and dissemination of a range of specialized, high-impact statistical outputs.
Operationalizes specialized conceptual and measurement frameworks in the development of production, validation and dissemination systems, processes and databases.

Evaluates alternatives and develops and applies new strategies to maintain and improve operational systems, processes and databases in the production and dissemination of official statistics. Decisions and recommendations regarding data production and dissemination practices impact multiple projects and high-impact statistical programs.
Develops and implements quality-assurance processes for high-impact statistical outputs.

Investigates requirements for statistical information and analysis, defines the nature and scope of special studies, data requirements, and decides the methods and approaches to be used to satisfy complex data requirements. Modifies existing techniques or develops new approaches to meet specific needs.

Defines project objectives and priorities, prepares work plans and summaries outlining approaches, time-frames and resources. Each project is unique in nature and decisions impact on other ongoing studies.
Develops guidelines for the design, evaluation, and testing of processing systems and applications and recommends and implements modifications and improvements to existing procedures.
Recommends and executes solutions to resolve complex technical issues pertaining to data production and dissemination that may lack precedents.
Develops data bases for the provision of time-series information, interprets preliminary results, reviews, and modifies approaches and techniques as necessary.
Reviews and approves detailed processing parameters, devises criteria and methods to rectify inconsistencies, and recommends modifications to ensure the continuity and compatibility of data.
Leadership And Operational Management: Occasionally plans, organizes and functionally coordinates the work of multiple partners within Statistic Canada divisions and units, as well as clients from other federal government departments involved in the conduct of statistical processing, validation and dissemination of specialized statistical outputs. Determines goals, priorities and milestones, sets objectives, plans and schedules the work and resolves conflicting priorities.
Establishes and coordinates schedules for the production, validation and dissemination of regular statistical outputs across multiple production teams.
Coordinates input and specifications from multiple partners to implement specialized solutions according to established production schedules in the context of complex statistical frameworks.
Communication: Provides expert advice and guidance to internal partners on statistical program results, dissemination methods, concepts, and techniques applied and on trends and developments in economic or related data programs. This information is used as input to decision making for a vast array of economic programs and other activities.
Interprets specialized information pertaining to a range of specialized subject matter areas to present arguments and options to clients within and outside the department.

Communicates subject matter concepts and technical definitions to internal contacts and other subject matter experts to explain and clarify current developments, to explain the results of studies, and to resolve differences that can affect the efficiency of the manipulation, storage, and retrieval of data and the quality of outputs.
Specialized knowledge: Advanced knowledge of economic statistical frameworks, principles, and practices as they relate to a specialized subject matter area.

Advanced knowledge of theories, concepts, and principles in statistical measurement, and how they interrelate with at least one specialized economic subject matter area or discipline, is required to design, evaluate, and innovate systems and applications for the production, validation, and dissemination of high-impact statistical outputs. This knowledge is also required to provide subject-matter expertise, advice, and consultative services to Statistic Canada partners, as well as to work with other professionals, in the ongoing production and validation of high-impact statistical data.
In-depth knowledge and mastery in the application of specialized software, such as SAS, for the compilation, validation, and quality assurance of key statistical outputs.
Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of the divisional mandate, activities, priorities, practices, standards and procedures applicable to the work is required to incorporate them into the conduct and management of surveys and complex and technical studies and projects.

Knowledge of the mandate, objectives and organization of Statistics Canada is required to manage subject matter studies, surveys and projects across economic-based divisions. Knowledge of other statistical programs (concepts, methods, and databases) related to the area of expertise is also required to plan and implement statistical activities, to integrate conceptually different data from other programs, to explain variances, and to recommend changes to other statistical programs if necessary.

In-depth knowledge of economics-related subject matter area(s) is required to understand complex data needs from internal and external data users and to deliver expert technical solutions in response to analytical requirements for statistical projects and programs.

Knowledge of departmental publication, marketing and dissemination policies and practices in order to establish common divisional policies and practices in the preparation of statistical tables, charts, explanatory notes etc. for dissemination to user and/or subject matter clients.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies (confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations, data quality), practices and classification systems to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of complex and technical statistical projects and activities.

Knowledge of data suppliers to discuss data reporting agreements. Knowledge of data users from governments and from the private sector is required to identify potential new markets and to understand client needs for complex statistical data or studies.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements to others. Knowledge of the Statistic and Privacy Acts is particularly important with respect to the security and confidentiality of information and data provided and to ensure that they do not release any information which may identify an individual or group without prior consent.
Research and analysis: Interprets the results of tests, procedural investigations, and feasibility studies to produce data bases and data retrieval packages used for the production of integrated statistical information.

Reviews and approves detailed processing parameters, classification, coding systems and report formats or develops new ones to meet specific needs. Some studies may involve a combination of statistical techniques and methods and the integration of data from a wide variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses). Often, the data has been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts and must be translated into common concepts.

Reviews new and revised processing systems and procedures to ensure compatibility with other statistical programs. Assesses technical and conceptual problems and inconsistencies in the manipulation, storage and retrieval of statistical data and develops specifications for new and existing data compilation programs.
Evaluates the impact of technological developments on operation and production procedures and prepares reports recommending appropriate approaches and guidelines.

Research and validation is required to evaluate the effectiveness of the processing systems, to formulate computer systems specifications, to design and create test procedures and acceptance criteria, and to ensure that processing systems yield desired statistical outputs.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Coordinator
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: Configure workflows is the second strongest relationship because the role is operationally involved in putting designed processes into use through implementation, testing approaches, and revised procedures. Evidence includes: 'Specifies testing approaches, plans and environments for use by other project staff to set up and carry out acceptance testing of new or modified computer applications'; 'Reviews test results from new or revised procedures to determine the impact on existing program operations'; and 'Coordinates and organizes the implementation, conduct and maintenance' of operations. This is stronger than build-component subprocesses because the position is not primarily a developer; it specifies, coordinates, and operationalizes workflows and procedures across business stages. Associated drivers such as Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration, Modular Architecture, and Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment will shift the job toward configuring standardized automated flows, embedding security and control points, and supporting workflow changes required by leaner staffing and more enterprise tooling.

key_activities: Coordinates and organizes the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data.
Reviews and documents operational processes and assesses the quality and application of data outputs in order to propose solutions or explain results.
Provides advice to users on the methods and procedures related to statistical operations services.
Participates as a statistical operations representative on various teams and working groups.
Leads the activities of work groups involved in different stages of data collection operations.

1. Decision making: Develops operational plans and procedures for the manual and automated collection, coding and processing of statistical data.

Outlines proposals for changes and improvements to survey content and coverage, questionnaire design, collection and processing of data, and the implementation and use of new hardware and software options to support survey development and assessment.

Determines the nature of the problem with respect to data inconsistency or integrity, reviews operational processes, and assesses the quality and application of data outputs in order to propose solutions or explain results.
Specifies testing approaches, plans and environments for use by other project staff to set up and carry out acceptance testing of new or modified computer applications.
Prepares and implements policies and guidelines to maintain the integrity, security and 'back-up' systems and processes.
Reviews test results from new or revised procedures to determine the impact on existing program operations. Documents the results and prepares recommendations for implementation.
2. Leadership and operational management: Leads work groups established to coordinate and implement statistical production activities: assigns work; provides feedback on performance of working group members; monitors progress against objectives and provides guidance and direction to working group members; identifies financial and human resource needs.

Monitors and tracks time spent on activities for the purposes of recording and recovering such costs from the client. Responsible for identifying costs and fees associated with cost recovery activities and preparing estimates for special requests and tabulations based upon established fee schedules. Responsible for the acquisition of goods and services, according to the budget allocated. Incurs and accounts for petty cash, credit card, taxi voucher, bus pass, and other expenditures.
3. Communication: Interprets and clarifies client requests and inquiries for statistical data and information; responds orally or in writing to enquiries from managers, employees and the general public to provide information on the operation of divisional systems and processes and the use of program results.

Meets with subject matter and systems specialists, clients, service providers and others to establish and elaborate the framework and conditions within which statistical operations will occur. There is a requirement to understand the issues and resolve differences that can affect the efficiency of the division's operations and quality of outputs.

Contacts data suppliers or respondents to obtain their collaboration in responding to surveys, to clarify problems or irregularities, to explain technical procedures for obtaining the data in the appropriate format, or to clarify and explain statistical concepts.
Designs and prepares statistical tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text for use in statistical analysis by clients both inside and outside Statistics Canada.
Writes specifications and guidelines to be used by others in developing or operating systems and processes.
Participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and working groups in order to share knowledge within an area of operational expertise.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of the statistical and economic concepts and principles used in the collection, coding and processing of statistical data in order to recommend and implement improvements to survey collection, coding and processing activities.

Knowledge of system analysis and design, computer processing, generalized survey software packages to oversee the design, testing, operation and maintenance of processing systems; to design specifications for the testing of data, and to maintain and use databases.
Knowledge of project and time management methods, practices and techniques to develop work plans, estimate resource requirements and to monitor and report on work progress.

Knowledge of methods and practices of operating personal computers in a network environment and of using databases and software packages (word processing, statistical analysis, graphics, spreadsheets, etc.) to prepare correspondence, reports and presentations.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of developments and changes in the subject area that may affect the efficiency and validity of data collection, coding and processing in order to devise and modify operational systems and processes.

Knowledge of the departmental and divisional mandate, objectives, priorities, practices, standards, processes and procedures in order to coordinate and manage on-going operational activities and/or special projects.

Knowledge of departmental publication, marketing and dissemination policies and practices in order to establish common divisional policies and practices in the preparation of statistical tables, charts, explanatory notes for dissemination to user and/or subject matter clients.

Knowledge of statistical programs within Statistics Canada in order to identify potential sources of information for operations and/or special studies and to identify and evaluate possible data conflicts.
Knowledge of contacts within key client departments to understand and explain the need for statistical data, and to provide advice and guidance on survey concepts, methods, techniques and results.
Knowledge of data sources and contacts within and external to Statistics Canada to obtain collaboration in the provision of statistical information and to verify the accuracy of data.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to ensure understanding and application in the collection, coding and processing of data. The position must have a particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data to ensure their own actions are in compliance.
6. Research and analysis: Researches options and requirements for the operation of divisional statistical systems and processes in order to assist in the establishment of divisional and program objectives and priorities.

Reviews and compares the concepts and definitions of data sources with those of the statistical program. Reconciles differences and develops special methods of adjusting source data. This requires interpreting or adapting practices.
Develops and outlines system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in revising existing systems or in developing new processing systems.
Assesses trends and developments in the program area by preparing tabulations and reviews outlining program results for use by program managers and general data users.

gsbpm_description: This sub-process is concerned with the testing of assembled and configured services and related workflows. It includes technical testing and sign-off of new programmes and routines, as well as confirmation that existing routines from other statistical business processes are suitable for use in this case. Whilst part of this activity concerning the testing of individual components and services could logically be linked with sub-processes 3.1 (Reuse or build collection instruments), 3.2 (Reuse or build processing and analysis components) and 3.3 (Reuse or build dissemination components), this sub-process also includes testing of interactions between assembled and configured services and ensuring that the whole production solution works in a coherent way. It can also include arranging secure channels for the transmission of the data, checking detailed information about files and metadata with a data supplier and receiving test files to assess if data are fit for use.
