Knowledge of system analysis and design, computer processing, generalized survey software packages to manage the design, development, testing, maintenance and implementation of processing systems; to design specifications for the testing of data, and to maintain and develop databases.
Knowledge of high level programming languages, utility programs or statistical packages to retrieve and manipulate data.
Knowledge of management techniques and principles to manage financial and human resources, either directly or within a matrix management environment.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of statistical programs within Statistics Canada related to the area of expertise in order to identify and select sources of information for development and operations and/or special studies and to identify and evaluate data conflicts.

Knowledge of contacts within key client departments to establish a liaison; to understand need for statistical data, and to provide advice and guidance on subject-matter concepts, methods, techniques and results.
Knowledge of the divisional mandate, objectives, priorities, practices, standards, processes and procedures in order to coordinate and manage on-going operational activities and/or special projects.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements to data suppliers, users and others with respect to the manipulation, storage and retrieval of data. Knowledge of the Statistics and Privacy Acts is particulary important with respect to the security and confidentiality of information and data provided and to ensure that they and their subordinates do not release any information which may identify an individual or group without prior consent.
6. Research and analysis: Plans and implements the review and development of new subject-matter methods, concepts and definitions and conducts studies and analytical projects to improve existing surveys and data.

Analyzes current manipulation, storage and retrieval methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to determine the need for modification or replacement with alternative systems, methods and procedures.

Conducts feasibility studies concerning new system and product requirements by examining existing, proposed or new software programs and systems to determine their feasibility and adaptability to the needs of the statistical program.

Provides subject-matter interpretation and analysis to media representatives on the results of surveys or projects, and the interpretation of statistical data. This information is disseminated to the Canadian population for information and decision making purposes.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Recruit
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: Test production systems is the second strongest relationship because the description explicitly states that the role creates test data, sets up testing processes, identifies and corrects errors and problems, documents inputs and presents results for review. It also mentions reviewing specifications, identifying inconsistencies, and supporting procedures manuals and training packages tied to applications and systems. This is stronger than broader workflow or design subprocesses because the role is operationally involved in system and application testing rather than only upstream planning. Future drivers such as enterprise platforms, cloud infrastructure, modular reusable components, and cyber/privacy controls will increase the complexity of integrated system testing, secure testing, and testing of reusable production components, changing the work toward more automated and cross-system test practices.

1. Decision making: Assesses the capabilities of data systems to meet user requests, maintains and updates a statistical database, manipulates and processes data to generate tables, charts and data files.
Creates test data, sets up testing processes, identifies and corrects errors and problems, documents the inputs and presents the results for review.

Applies existing techniques and approaches to incorporate changes in subject-matter content and definitions and selects the appropriate software to be used for the preparation of reports, tables and charts.

Reviews specifications, identifies inconsistencies, recommends improvements and incorporates changes into procedures manuals. Provides support in the development and review of information manuals and training packages.

Identifies options for improvements to processing systems and implements enhancements or modifications to systems and applications used in the editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of statistical data.
Assesses trends and developments in the subject area and identifies the potential impact on concepts, methods, techniques and procedures.
2. Leadership and operational management: Participates in project teams, work groups, meetings and conferences in order to develop and improve work methods and practices, share knowledge and contribute to skill development.

Monitors and tracks time spent on activities for the purposes of recording and recovering such costs from the client. Incurs and accounts for petty cash, credit card, taxi voucher, bus pass, and other expenditures.
3. Communication: Drafts reports on survey process, data quality and reliability for review by a project leader or supervisor.
Drafts reference and training material for data collection operations.

Responds to requests from subject matter specialists and clients for custom tabulations and liaises with survey officers, respondents and data users to understand and obtain clarifications on concepts, data collection and processing requirements.
Explains requirements and procedures for obtaining the information in the appropriate format.
Responds to inquiries from managers, employees and the general public on the availability, consistency and application of statistical data and on the methods and techniques used.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of the methods, techniques and practices required for the collection, capture, processing, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data.
Knowledge of statistical survey concepts and quantitative analytical techniques involved in the development, conduct and monitoring of statistical programs.

Knowledge of methods and practices of operating personal computers in a network environment and of using databases and software packages (word processing, statistical analysis, graphics, spreadsheets, etc.) to prepare correspondence, reports and presentations.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of a variety of commercial software tools and of customized production applications to regularly process data and/or to produce specified statistical outputs.
Knowledge of automated collection software and data capture applications to test applications and prepare reference material and training for the applications.

Knowledge of divisional mandates, objectives, programs, policies and activities to adhere to the various statistical and administrative practices and procedures involved in the collection, capture, processing, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of statistical data.
Knowledge of program context, program sponsors and participants to identify and resolve specific data production and dissemination issues.

Knowledge of data sources and contacts within STC in order to locate, analyze and compare statistical output to ensure consistency and reliability; and external to STC to obtain collaboration in the provision of statistical information and verify the accuracy of data.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to ensure understanding and application in the collection, capture, processing, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data. The position must have a particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data to ensure their own actions are in compliance.
6. Research and analysis: Reviews reported data and prepares reports outlining data quality and any problems encountered in the implementation of established guidelines and results.
Compiles data from a number of different but easily identifiable sources to produce statistical tables and charts.

Analyses outputs with other related data sources or by making calculations to ensure no errors exist due to programming and classification of the original data, that it is in an acceptable format, and that the data is reasonable in relation to similar data for other periods.
Reviews user requests to determine the nature, feasibility, and options for providing the information required.
Adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats, depending on the complexity of the subject matter or the number of different sources.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Production and Dissemination Specialist
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: A meaningful testing relationship exists because the role interprets results of tests, procedural investigations and feasibility studies, develops criteria and methods to rectify inconsistencies, and evaluates effectiveness of processing systems through test procedures and acceptance criteria. This is stronger than broader evaluation subprocesses because it is about testing production systems and ensuring desired outputs before or during implementation. Future drivers such as modular architecture, secure production environments, and cloud/platform modernization will increase the importance of validating reusable components and system compatibility.

key_activities: Develops data bases for the provision of time-series information as well as data for special studies and requests.
Coordinates and controls the activities of staff involved in manipulating, storing and retrieving statistical data.
Provides subject-matter expertise and consultative services to users within and outside STC.
Represents subject matter divisions on development projects, task forces or committees in various roles.
Leads project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems.

1. Decision making: Investigates client requirements for statistical information, defines the nature and scope of special studies, determines the sources of data for special requests as well as the methods and approaches to be used. Modifies existing techniques or develops new approaches to meet specific needs.

Defines project objectives and priorities, prepares work plans and summaries outlining approaches, time-frames and resources. Each project is unique in nature and decisions impact on other ongoing studies.
Develops guidelines for the design, evaluation and testing of processing systems and applications and recommends modifications and improvements to existing procedures.
Develops data bases for the provision of time-series information, interprets preliminary results, reviews and modifies approaches and techniques as necessary.
Reviews and approves detailed processing parameters, devises criteria and methods to rectify inconsistencies and recommends modifications to ensure the continuity and compatibility of data.
2. Leadership and operational management: Plans, organizes and coordinates the work of a unit or project team involved in the conduct of special studies, surveys and projects. Determines goals, priorities and milestones, sets objectives, plans and schedules the work, resolves conflicting priorities; identifies human resources needs, determines the appropriate selection methods (internal and external resources / contractors) to meet program or project objectives, participates in the recruitment of staff, provides input to employee performance, develops training plans, motivates and maintains morale of employees.

Plans and budgets for on-going studies and/or special projects, including estimates for salaries, professional fees and implementation costs, with authority to allocate/reallocate funds within the budget. Provides input to budgets based on operational needs and by obtaining/providing cost estimates for personnel, supplies, equipment purchases and travel for use in developing section or division budgets. Establishes and negotiates contracts for projects. Responsible for the acquisition of goods and services, according to the budget allocated.
3. Communication: Provides expert advice and guidance to all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academics, on statistical program results, methods, concepts and techniques applied and on trends and developments in economic, sociological or related data programs. This often requires the adaptation and presentation of complex information in basic, understandable formats. This information is used as input to decision making for a vast array of economic and social policies, programs and other activities.

Presents arguments and options and negotiates resources, timeframes and costs with service providers (e.g. system specialists, regional office staff, survey methodologists, contractors, etc.) and clients within and outside the department.

Writes and presents subject matter concepts and technical definitions in common terminology in order to explain and clarify current developments, to explain the results of studies and to resolve differences that can affect the efficiency of the manipulation, storage and retrieval of data and the quality of outputs.
Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and groups to develop consensus or share knowledge within the area of expertise.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of economic/sociologic principles and practices as they relate to a specialized area as well as specific knowledge of the area to initiate and conduct projects to improve existing concepts or develop new approaches to extend the application of divisional statistics, and to analyze, review and present survey findings. This knowledge is also required to provide subject-matter expertise, advice and consultative services to users, within and outside STC, as well as to provide related advice to other professionals.
Knowledge of statistical theories, methods, concepts and practices used in the manipulation, storage and retrieval of statistical data.
Knowledge of the principles and practices of human and financial resource management to plan and budget for on-going studies, surveys and/or special projects carried out by project teams.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of the divisional mandate, activities, priorities, practices, standards and procedures applicable to the work to incorporate them into the conduct and management of studies, surveys and projects.

Knowledge of the mandate, objectives and organization of Statistics Canada to manage subject matter studies, surveys and projects. Knowledge of other statistical programs (concepts, methods, and databases) related to the area of expertise to plan and implement statistical activities, to integrate conceptually different data from other programs, to explain variances and to recommend changes to other statistical programs.

Knowledge of departmental publication, marketing and dissemination policies and practices in order to establish common divisional policies and practices in the preparation of statistical tables, charts, explanatory notes etc. for dissemination to user and/or subject matter clients.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies (confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations, data quality), practices and classification systems to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of statistical projects and activities.

Knowledge of data suppliers to discuss data reporting agreements. Knowledge of data users from governments and from the private sector to identify potential new markets, to understand client needs for complex statistical data or studies, to negotiate contracts and to provide advice on program results.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements to other departments, agencies, industry, members of the public and the media. Knowledge of the Statitstics and Privacy Acts is particulary important with respect to the security and confidentiality of information and data provided and to ensure that they and their subordinates do not release any information which may identify an individual or group without prior consent.
6. Research and analysis: Interprets the results of tests, procedural investigations and feasibility studies to produce data bases and data retrieval packages used for the production of integrated statistical information.

Reviews and approves detailed processing parameters, classification, coding systems and report formats or develops new ones to meet specific needs. Some studies may involve a combination of statistical techniques and methods and the integration of data from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses). Often, the data have been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts and must be translated into common concepts.

Reviews new and revised processing systems and procedures to ensure compatibility with other statistical programs, assesses technical and conceptual problems and inconsistencies in the manipulation, storage and retrieval of statistical data and develops specifications for new and existing data compilation programs.
Evaluates the impact of technological developments on respondent operation and production procedures and prepares reports recommending appropriate approaches and guidelines.

Research and analysis are required to evaluate the effectiveness of processing systems, to formulate computer systems specifications, to design and create test procedures and acceptance criteria to ensure that processing systems yield the desired outputs.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Head, Production and Dissemination
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: There is meaningful evidence for testing production systems because the role 'reviews and certifies the overall quality and completeness of program results,' assesses system suitability, and defines specifications and guidelines for contracted development work and operational procedures. While not as central as system/workflow design, certification of output quality and system suitability implies strong involvement in production testing and readiness. Future drivers such as cloud infrastructure, secure access, modular components, and integrated orchestration will increase the need for robust production testing, secure readiness checks, and interoperability assurance.

key_activities: Plans and implements long term strategies for the development, enhancement and operation of divisional statistical programs.
Plans and controls the development, implementation and operation of new or modified statistical systems and processes.
Defines, coordinates and evaluates the cost of statistical system development work.
Reviews and certifies the overall quality and completeness of program results.
Identifies and researches trends and developments in mass data processing concepts, methods and techniques.
Provides expert advisory and consultative services to users within and outside Statistics Canada.
Participates in or leads task forces or committees as an expert in statistical production and dissemination systems.
Manages a unit and project teams involved in systems design. Manages the financial resources attached to the statistical program.

1. Decision making: Prepares program proposals outlining options and recommendations on the statistical framework, strategies, resource implications and impact of new or modified statistical programs.
Develops policies, guidelines, instructions and procedures for the development, use and evaluation of systems and processes.
Defines processing and production specifications and guidelines for the contracting of development work to internal service areas, outside agencies and contractors.
Determines the methods, concepts, techniques and practices to be applied in the development and operation of statistical programs regarding the acquisition, production and dissemination of data.
Establishes policies and procedures for the security and confidentiality of data and the maintenance and protection of computer systems, equipment, databases and files.

Reviews trends and developments in data processing concepts, methods and techniques in order to present options and recommendations to management on the use and application of new technology to mass data capture, conversion and dissemination applications.
2. Leadership and operational management: Manages a unit and leads project teams for special projects. Assesses program requirements and determines objectives and priorities. Plans and schedules the work, resolves conflicting priorities, ascertains human resource needs, determines the appropriate selection methods (internal and external resources / contractors) to meet program and project objectives, recruits staff, evaluates employee performance or reviews performance evaluations prepared by subordinates and approves training plans.

Plans, develops and manages a budget for the unit in accordance with departmental policy and procedures. Exercises direct authority and accountability for allocated funds to meet planned objectives. Authorises, commits and approves expenditures in accordance with approved budgets with the authority to reallocate funds among line objects.

Negotiates cost reductions and arranges contracts with consulting firms and for the acquisition of services. Selects contractors for specific projects, assigns, directs, manages and evaluates the work according to contract specifications.
3. Communication: Provides expert advisory and consultative services to policy makers at all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academia. Explains and elaborates on statistical program findings and their practical application and interpretation of statistical data and information. This information is used as input to decision making for a vast array of economic and social policies, programs and other activities.

Writes and presents subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify developmental projects and operational systems and processes or program results. When findings are challenged or misinterpreted, it is necessary to present logical arguments to justify the results and to defend the validity of statistical methods and approaches used in order to maintain the department’s reputation for producing high quality data.
Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and groups to develop understanding, consensus and share knowledge of the program area.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of economic or sociology principles and theory to provide expert advisory and consultative services to clients on program results and on the concepts and methods used in mass data processing.

Extensive knowledge of current and emerging socio-economic issues in Canada and internationally, such as the changing social context and the globalization of markets, particularly as they relate to all the aspects of a statistical program. This knowledge is required to analyze program outputs, anticipate and understand needs for new data, and assess the impact on the area of specialization.

Advanced knowledge of systems analysis and design and of new and emerging computer technology and applications in order to establish and manage mass statistical data collection, production and dissemination environments.
Knowledge of the principles and practices of project management including the management of human and financial resources.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of the departmental and divisional mandate, activities, priorities, practices, standards and procedures applicable to the work to incorporate them into the management of a statistical program and to recommend changes to management.

Knowledge of other statistical programs (concepts, methods, and databases) related to the area of expertise to plan and implement statistical activities, to integrate conceptually different data from other programs, to explain variances and to recommend changes to other statistical programs.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies, (e.g. confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations, and data quality), practices and classification systems is required to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of production and dissemination activities.
Knowledge of the policies and programs of key client departments is needed to determine their information requirements.

Knowledge of data users from governments and from the private sector to identify potential new markets, to understand client needs for statistical data or studies, to negotiate contracts and to provide expert advice on program results.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act is needed to explain the legislative requirements to data suppliers/users, and to negotiate special agreements. This knowledge, along with knowledge of the Privacy Act is also required to ensure that the organization meets its commitment to ensuring the confidentiality of all information provided to them and does not release any information that identifies an individual or group without prior consent.
Knowledge of a variety of Acts related to the area of expertise such as the Income Tax Act, the Excise Sales Tax Act, the Employment Insurance Act, and the Corporate Returns Act.
6. Research and analysis: Reviews the conceptual framework of existing statistical programs and determines the need for development, modification and adaption. Programs involve a combination of statistical techniques and methods and the integration of data from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses). Source data have often been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts and must be translated into common concepts, taking into consideration the impact of the result on other statistical programs as well as departmental priorities.

Assesses new statistical methods, techniques and practices and the associated costs and limitations and identifies the availability and reliability of new data sources to evaluate the suitability of new hardware and software and to determine the short and long term program impact and benefits.

Analyses the relative quality of data produced by statistical programs, determines reasons for variances; reviews the comparability of data over time and relevance in light of trends, developments, changing requirements, policy issues and socio-economic conditions.

Researches gaps and inconsistencies in the production and dissemination methods and procedures, reviews the conceptual framework used and the compatibility with other statistical programs. Problems to be resolved usually impact on other statistical programs.
Investigates client requirements for statistical information and determines the capacity and ability of existing or modified systems to meet these requirements.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: A meaningful third relationship is to testing production systems because the description includes designing specifications for the testing of data, managing system analysis and design for testing and maintenance, and conducting feasibility studies of software and systems to determine adaptability to statistical program needs. This indicates material involvement in testing and suitability assessment of assembled systems. It is stronger than collection or dissemination subprocesses because the role’s direct responsibilities focus on system readiness and data-processing infrastructure rather than operational collection or release. Future drivers such as cyber security, cloud platforms, integrated pipelines and modular architecture will likely expand testing requirements for interoperability, scalability, security, and production readiness of shared statistical processing systems.

position_information.position_title: Data Production and Dissemination Development Officer
key_activities: Develops processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.
Designs specifications for the testing of data and for the maintenance and development of databases.
Assesses changes in the subject area and determines the need to modify or replace processing systems and applications for the manipulation, storage and retrieval of statistical data
Provides subject matter advice and direction to users, negotiates procedural modifications and establishes project plans, priorities and target dates.
Participates as a subject area representative on teams and working groups throughout the department.
Leads project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems.

There is a requirement to understand the issues and resolve differences that can affect the efficiency of the division's operations and quality of outputs.

Liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development, to suggest improvements to ongoing programs, to negotiate procedural modifications and to establish project plans, priorities and target dates. Writes and presents detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify divisional program content and applications.

Writes analytical reports and articles on the interpretation of surveys, statistical applications or project findings and the methodology used. These reports and articles are to be reviewed by program managers and included into publications. Exchanges information and provides advice to professionals from the private sector or from other statistical agencies abroad on subject-matter concepts and definitions, statistical survey methods and techniques. This information is used to develop similar surveys or analytical projects.

Provides guidance to other STC professionals on subject-matter concepts and definitions, survey methods, statistical applications and techniques used. This information is used to implement similar surveys or projects.

gsbpm_description: This sub-process includes the activities to put the assembled and configured processes and services, including modified and newly-created services, into production ready for use. The activities include: Producing documentation about the process components, including technical documentation and user manuals; Training the users of the system on how to operate the process; Moving the process components into the production environment and ensuring they work as expected in that environment (this activity may also be part of sub-process 3.5 (Test production systems).

agency staff integrating AI assistants into daily work requires updated training and operating guidance

parallel census operations across the agency
provide employees with the tools and training they need
support a skilled and adaptable workforce

Coordinated execution across collection, processing, analysis and dissemination

1. Decision making: Judgment and initiative are required to provide technical subject matter expertise and coaching support to course participants. This involves continually studying changes to business practices of Statistics Canada survey, subject matter, and statistical learning programs to provide up-to-date and accurate information to staff. Judgment is required to identify and analyze coaching and training needs of course participants, to track and evaluate problems encountered, to ensure compliance to methodologies and to recommend solutions to resolve these issues. Each course participant has different levels of knowledge, and each learning session must be adapted to meet the individual performance requirements.

Apply judgment on the interpretation of various methodologies applied in “live” case scenarios undertaken by course participants; and conduct research and offer guidance to atypical issues that arise. This involves seeking out information from a variety of sources and providing advice and guidance based on the application of knowledge and a solid understanding of the Stats Can business practices.
2. Leadership and operational management: Contributes to new skill development by providing day-to-day technical guidance and direction to course participants; monitors and identifies performance gaps and develops and recommends coaching and training plans.

Ensures that training text, handouts, simulation exercises and testing tools reflect current business policies and practices. The incumbent is responsible for recording and following up on deficiencies, and in complex situations, working with subject matter resources in the design of new products to reflect changes to business practices.
3. Communication: Communication skills are required to mentor and coach course participants in the day-to-day classroom and group training activities and to provide technical guidance. Communication skills are required to adapt the style, tone and terminology to the course participant’s level of knowledge, which can vary considerably.

Communication skills are also required to participate in case studies; conduct interviews with external sources of information as part of the data gathering exercise; and respond to questions on methodologies accordingly.

Writing skills are required to develop, adapt and draft training materials and tools and to respond to concerns and information request from course participants. Writing skills are also required to prepare reports and correspondence.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of the theories and principles of Business and Economic development, Survey development is required in order to provide subject matter expertise to course participants on the interpretation and application of these business practices; mentor and coach throughout the duration of the course, and to provide subject matter expertise in the development and delivery training materials and tools to enhance competencies.

Knowledge of training delivery methods and practices in order to determine training needs of course participants and provide day-to-day coaching; assess the content of training case study materials and tools and recommend and initiate changes to deal with performance concerns.

Analytical and problem-solving methods, interviewing/information-gathering techniques and problem escalation practices, is required to provide support and troubleshooting services to course participants, to research, analyze and resolve interpretation problems, respond to questions and to provide coaching, training and ongoing technical guidance.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of Stats Can’s mandate, and business practices in order to ensure that the training programs accurately reflects Stats Can business practices; to provide advice subject matter expertise and guidance to course participants on the application of those practices; and to assess individual trainees knowledge and contribute to their training performance assessment.

Knowledge of TDL’s mandate, strategic objectives, business plans, organization, and accountability framework to work in close cooperation with Learning Specialist and transpose technical subject matter knowledge into adult learning methodologies.
6. Research and analysis: Conducts research and analysis of changes to Survey, Subject Matter and Statistical learning programs-related business practices in order to provide subject matter expertise to course participants, conduct monitoring and quality assurance exercises to ensure compliance and to case study methodologies.

gsbpm_description: This sub-process establishes the frame and selects the sample for this iteration of the collection, as specified in sub-process 2.4 (Design frame and sample). It also includes the coordination of samples between instances of the same business process (e.g. to manage overlap or rotation), and between different processes using a common frame or register (e.g. to manage overlap or to spread response burden). Quality assurance and approval of the frame and the selected sample are also undertaken in this sub-process, though maintenance of underlying registers, from which frames for several statistical business processes are drawn, is treated as a separate activity. The sampling aspect of this sub-process is often not relevant for processes based entirely on the use of preexisting sources (e.g. administrative sources and other non-survey sources) as such processes generally create frames from the available data and then follow a census approach. Variables from administrative and other non-statistical sources of data can be used as auxiliary variables in the construction of sampling design.

gsbpm_description: This sub-process ensures that the people, processes and technology (e.g. web-based applications, devices to be used in collection, communication channels) are ready to collect data and metadata, as designed. It takes place over a period of time, as it includes the strategy, planning and training activities in preparation for the specific instance of the statistical business process. Where the process is repeated regularly, some (or all) of these activities may not be explicitly required for each iteration. For one-off and new processes, these activities can be lengthy. For survey data, this sub-process includes: Training collection staff; Training system using supervised machine learning techniques; Ensuring collection resources are available (e.g. collection devices, apps, APIs); Agreeing on terms with any intermediate collection bodies, (e.g. sub-contractors for computer assisted telephone interviewing, web service providers); Configuring collection systems to request and receive the data, including location data; Ensuring the security of data to be collected; Preparing collection instruments (e.g. printing questionnaires, pre-filling them with existing data, loading questionnaires and data onto interviewers' devices/computers, APIs, web scraping tools); Providing information for respondents (e.g. drafting letters/emails to respondents, credentials, guidance or tailored information to address questions they may have, or notifying respondents when online reporting instruments will be made available); Translation of materials (e.g. into the different languages spoken or used in the country). For non-survey sources, this sub-process ensures that the necessary processes, systems and confidentiality procedures are in place, to receive or extract the necessary information from the source. This includes: Evaluating requests to obtain the data and logging the request in a centralised inventory; Initiating contacts with organisations providing the data, and sending an introductory package with details on the process of obtaining the data; Routine checks that the system is working as expected.

sustained attention to training, mentorship, and realistic sequencing of work alongside production demands
drivers.impact: This subprocess is strongly affected because it explicitly includes training staff, preparing people and technology, and setting up AI- and digital-enabled collection operations. Workforce transition and leadership support are central to collection readiness.
impact_mechanisms: Training collection staff is directly driven by skills transition in digital tools, data, methods, and new tools
Use of web applications, devices, APIs, and machine learning in collection setup requires employee development and technical reskilling
Managers guiding teams through transitions are essential to prepare staff and resolve setup issues within timelines
Accessibility and inclusive design principles affect digital collection platforms and respondent-facing materials
Safe, respectful, and supportive work environments and employee well-being matter during intensive setup periods under production pressure
Reduced staffing and realistic sequencing of work affect collection planning, staffing models, and readiness activities

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Coordinator
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This is the strongest relationship because the role directly coordinates and organizes implementation and maintenance of manual and automated operations for collection, coding and processing; develops operational plans and procedures; leads work groups implementing statistical production activities; and writes specifications and guidelines used by others in operating systems and processes. Those are core setup and readiness responsibilities for collection operations. This relationship is stronger than run collection because the evidence emphasizes preparation, planning, readiness, policies, testing setup, and staff coordination. Future-state drivers such as enterprise digital platforms, online-first collection, secure access requirements, and workforce transition will increase the need for digital operational setup, secure configuration, scalable staff preparation, and standardized collection readiness practices.

key_activities: Coordinates and organizes the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data.
Reviews and documents operational processes and assesses the quality and application of data outputs in order to propose solutions or explain results.
Provides advice to users on the methods and procedures related to statistical operations services.
Participates as a statistical operations representative on various teams and working groups.
Leads the activities of work groups involved in different stages of data collection operations.

1. Decision making: Develops operational plans and procedures for the manual and automated collection, coding and processing of statistical data.

Outlines proposals for changes and improvements to survey content and coverage, questionnaire design, collection and processing of data, and the implementation and use of new hardware and software options to support survey development and assessment.

Determines the nature of the problem with respect to data inconsistency or integrity, reviews operational processes, and assesses the quality and application of data outputs in order to propose solutions or explain results.
Specifies testing approaches, plans and environments for use by other project staff to set up and carry out acceptance testing of new or modified computer applications.
Prepares and implements policies and guidelines to maintain the integrity, security and 'back-up' systems and processes.
Reviews test results from new or revised procedures to determine the impact on existing program operations. Documents the results and prepares recommendations for implementation.
2. Leadership and operational management: Leads work groups established to coordinate and implement statistical production activities: assigns work; provides feedback on performance of working group members; monitors progress against objectives and provides guidance and direction to working group members; identifies financial and human resource needs.

Monitors and tracks time spent on activities for the purposes of recording and recovering such costs from the client. Responsible for identifying costs and fees associated with cost recovery activities and preparing estimates for special requests and tabulations based upon established fee schedules. Responsible for the acquisition of goods and services, according to the budget allocated. Incurs and accounts for petty cash, credit card, taxi voucher, bus pass, and other expenditures.
3. Communication: Interprets and clarifies client requests and inquiries for statistical data and information; responds orally or in writing to enquiries from managers, employees and the general public to provide information on the operation of divisional systems and processes and the use of program results.

Meets with subject matter and systems specialists, clients, service providers and others to establish and elaborate the framework and conditions within which statistical operations will occur. There is a requirement to understand the issues and resolve differences that can affect the efficiency of the division's operations and quality of outputs.

Contacts data suppliers or respondents to obtain their collaboration in responding to surveys, to clarify problems or irregularities, to explain technical procedures for obtaining the data in the appropriate format, or to clarify and explain statistical concepts.
Designs and prepares statistical tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text for use in statistical analysis by clients both inside and outside Statistics Canada.
Writes specifications and guidelines to be used by others in developing or operating systems and processes.
Participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and working groups in order to share knowledge within an area of operational expertise.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of the statistical and economic concepts and principles used in the collection, coding and processing of statistical data in order to recommend and implement improvements to survey collection, coding and processing activities.

Knowledge of system analysis and design, computer processing, generalized survey software packages to oversee the design, testing, operation and maintenance of processing systems; to design specifications for the testing of data, and to maintain and use databases.
Knowledge of project and time management methods, practices and techniques to develop work plans, estimate resource requirements and to monitor and report on work progress.

Knowledge of methods and practices of operating personal computers in a network environment and of using databases and software packages (word processing, statistical analysis, graphics, spreadsheets, etc.) to prepare correspondence, reports and presentations.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of developments and changes in the subject area that may affect the efficiency and validity of data collection, coding and processing in order to devise and modify operational systems and processes.

Knowledge of the departmental and divisional mandate, objectives, priorities, practices, standards, processes and procedures in order to coordinate and manage on-going operational activities and/or special projects.

Knowledge of departmental publication, marketing and dissemination policies and practices in order to establish common divisional policies and practices in the preparation of statistical tables, charts, explanatory notes for dissemination to user and/or subject matter clients.

Knowledge of statistical programs within Statistics Canada in order to identify potential sources of information for operations and/or special studies and to identify and evaluate possible data conflicts.
Knowledge of contacts within key client departments to understand and explain the need for statistical data, and to provide advice and guidance on survey concepts, methods, techniques and results.
Knowledge of data sources and contacts within and external to Statistics Canada to obtain collaboration in the provision of statistical information and to verify the accuracy of data.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to ensure understanding and application in the collection, coding and processing of data. The position must have a particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data to ensure their own actions are in compliance.
6. Research and analysis: Researches options and requirements for the operation of divisional statistical systems and processes in order to assist in the establishment of divisional and program objectives and priorities.

Reviews and compares the concepts and definitions of data sources with those of the statistical program. Reconciles differences and develops special methods of adjusting source data. This requires interpreting or adapting practices.
Develops and outlines system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in revising existing systems or in developing new processing systems.
Assesses trends and developments in the program area by preparing tabulations and reviews outlining program results for use by program managers and general data users.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Local Census Office Manager
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This is the strongest relationship because the role manages census field and office operations readiness for a Local Census Office, including recruitment for a large temporary workforce, development of collection strategies and contingency plans, office readiness, training of assistant managers, and provision of guidelines, instructions and procedures for staff. These are direct setup responsibilities covering people, processes, facilities and systems before and during launch. This is stronger than run collection because the evidence places major emphasis on readiness, resourcing, operational framework, and opening the office. Future drivers such as digital collection infrastructure, secure setup, workforce transition, and large-scale operational readiness demands will materially reshape this work.

key_activities: As part of the Area Management team, contributes to the development of operational plans for Census data collection activities; and manages census field and office operations for an LCO (7-day collection operation).

Manages the financial, human and material resources for the assigned LCO ; and manages the recruitment process for both Public Service Employment Act (PSEA) and Statistics Act employees required to meet the demands of a large temporary workforce.

Develops collections strategies and contingency plans; establishes and defines priorities; monitors and evaluates the cost, quality, efficiency, productivity and security of LCO data collection systems and processes; analyzes and produces reports on the progress of the LCO activities; and resolves problems including but not limited to the need for development, modification and adaptation of operational processes.

Monitors performance indicators; reports on the efficiency and effectiveness of LCO operations; and implements corrective action to resolve problems. Evaluates cost efficiencies, productivity and security of the Local Census Office.

Implements and provides expert interpretation of departmental legislation and the application of Statistics Canada policies and procedures; and leads the preparation and delivery of training to Assistant Manager, Field Operations, Assistant Manager Collection Unit, Assistant Manager Recruitment and Administration Officer.

Represents the department in consultations with the general public to solicit participation from non-respondents, responds to and resolves complaints; and contributes to public relations activities to promote Census Communications and respondent co-operation.
Represents the LCO in regional and/or department committees involved in the evaluation of the Census collection activities and provides advice on proposed modifications to operational procedures.
Disseminates and collects evaluation reports for the assigned LCO ; summarizes findings; and makes recommendations for program improvements.

Provides support to Regional administration with the opening of the office space such as visits during construction fit up, ensures office readiness for the beginning of field activities as well as closing down the LCO once operations have been completed.

Decision making: Effort is required to make decisions/recommendations on: the determination and definition of objectives, content and approaches for Census collection activities in the LCO and the operational framework and conditions within which the statistical program will occur; development and implementation of collection applications, alternate work methods and models to achieve desired outcomes; the development of strategies and business solutions to improve respondent relations, data collection and transmission processes; the resolution of complaints and problems related to survey participation and non-respondents; the development and distribution of guidelines, instructions and procedures for use by LCO Managers and staff; approval of appointments of all Statistics Act staff in the LCO region; the assurance that financial expenditures and resources are within allocated budgets; and the day-to-day management of financial, human and material resources of the LCO.
Decisions/recommendations taken affect the efficient and effective operations of the LCO and the LCO’s compliance to the Statistics Act and departmental policies and procedures.
Leadership and operational management: Manages the recruitment, development and retention of a fully trained and professional data collection workforce in the LCO. Establishes, coordinates and leads multi-disciplinary project teams and work groups comprising professional, technical, and administrative and Field Staff engaged in initiating, developing and implementing programs. Approves work plans and priorities. Establishes organizational structures, assigns responsibilities to team or group members, monitors progress and evaluates employee performance, provides training and guidance.
Monitors expenditures for staffing and material resources to ensure funds are spent appropriately and the LCO budget is respected.

Plans and budgets for the management and operation of the LCO in accordance with departmental policy and procedures, identifies content and cost of development and operational requirements, estimates salary, equipment and travel costs, as well as professional fees.

Oversees some of the aspects related to the LCO fit up with local contractors to ensure readiness at time of opening and coordinate the dismantlement of the facility at the end of Census collection operation
Communication: Communications skills are required to respond orally and in writing to inquiries from managers, employees to provide information and advice on the operation and use of systems and processes and briefings on LCO program results.
Communications skills are required to respond orally and in writing to inquiries from the general public on the requirements for response, purpose of the Census or issues with employees.

There is an occasional requirement to respond to inquiries from the media. These situations are difficult as dealing with the media requires "thinking on your feet", as well as ensuring that statements made are clear so as not to be misunderstood.

Communications skills are also required to intervene and deal with uncooperative and sometimes hostile respondents. There is a requirement to "take control" over these emotionally charged situations, and persuade the respondent to take a more rational approach to a situation.
Knowledge of specialized fields: Advanced knowledge of socio-economic concepts, methods and techniques applied in the development and operation of statistical programs to manage the LCO field operations, analyze program outputs, anticipate and understand the need for new data and to assess the impact on collection activities and programs.
In-depth knowledge of statistical data collection methods, concepts and practices and survey operations to manage the activities of the LCO and to provide expert advice on data collection issues.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies (e.g. confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations and data quality), practices and classifications systems is required to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of Census activities.

Knowledge of financial and human resources management and of project management methods, techniques and practices to manage the work of a Local Census Office and organize, plan, schedule and control the LCO operational activities.
Contextual knowledge: Knowledge and understanding of Statistics Canada’s mandate, programs, objectives, policies and procedures in areas such as survey methodology, operations integration, data confidentiality and security, dissemination and marketing to manage staff in the delivery of the program within a LCO and ensure that the work undertaken is standardized and consistent with departmental requirements.

Knowledge of the, regional and local operations’ mandate, activities, priorities, standards and procedures to the work to incorporate them into the management of the LCO and to recommend changes to management.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies (e.g. confidentiality of data, security, and respondent relations and data quality), practices and classification systems is required to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of Census activities.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act, Financial Administration Act, the Public Service Employment Act, Collective Agreementsand related policies and directives and supporting financial and human resources management methods, techniques and practices in order to manage the financial, human resource and material resources of assigned LCOs.
Research and analysis: Reviews and interprets the methods, concepts, techniques and practices applied in the operation of existing systems and processes and proposes modifications and enhancements or develops alternative approaches.
Analyses the relative quality of data, researches gaps and inconsistencies in the collection methods and procedures used, determines reasons for variances and initiates solutions.
Identifies and evaluates variations in survey responses and contributes to promotional activities to increase respondent participation rates.
Analyzes and produces reports on the progress of the LCO activites and resolves problems including but not limited to the need for development, modification and adaptation of operational processes.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: The role has a strong operational connection to setting up collection through preparing and distributing procedures, operational specifications and training for manual and automated collection, coding and processing, participating on data collection and operations teams, and providing input to training materials and training delivery. These are direct readiness and enablement activities for collection operations rather than only general support. This relationship is stronger than broader collection execution because the evidence centers on preparation, procedures, systems readiness and training. Drivers such as online-first collection, digital tools, AI-enabled collection supports, secure access requirements, and workforce skills transition will likely change this work toward more digital setup, tool configuration, and workforce enablement for automated and mixed-source collection environments.

key_activities: Participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data.
Evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives.
Provides assistance and advice to users on methods and practices of collection and coding.
Participates on data collection and operations teams.
Provides input to training materials concerning data collection operations and assists in training delivery.

1. Decision making: Evaluates methods, procedures and results of statistical collection, coding and processing operations and recommends alternatives. The surveys worked on can vary in size, complexity and methods.
Prepares and distributes procedures, operational specifications and training for the manual and automated collection, coding and processing of statistical data.
Develops and outlines system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems.
Evaluates and recommends appropriate procedures, software and hardware for the collection, coding and processing of data.
Develops test cases and data from functional specifications and specifies testing approaches for own use and use by other program staff to ensure that computer applications meet requirements.
2. Leadership and operational management: Participates in project teams, work groups, meetings and conferences in order to develop and improve work methods and practices, share knowledge and contribute to skill development.

Monitors and tracks time spent on activities for the purposes of recording and recovering such costs from the client. Incurs and accounts for petty cash, credit card, taxi voucher, bus pass, and other expenditures.
3. Communication: Responds orally and in writing to enquiries from managers, employees and the general public to provide information on the operation of divisional systems and processes and the use of program results.
Writes survey information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports.
Designs and prepares statistical tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text for use in regular and ad-hoc publications.
Prepares reports and recommendations outlining options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection and processing systems.

Meets with subject matter and systems specialists, clients, service providers and others, in order to comprehend and elaborate on the conditions within which statistical operations will occur. There is a requirement to understand the issues and resolve differences that can affect the efficiency of the division's operations and quality of outputs.

Contacts data suppliers or respondents to obtain their collaboration in responding to surveys, to clarify problems or irregularities. This may necessitate having to explain technical procedures for obtaining the data in the appropriate format, or to clarify and explain statistical concepts.
Participates in departmental meetings and working groups in order to share knowledge within an area of operational expertise.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of the underlying statistical and economic principles and concepts required for the collection, coding and processing of data.
Knowledge of the concepts, methods and techniques used in the management and control of statistical collection, coding and processing activities.
Knowledge of methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications.

Knowledge of methods and practices of operating personal computers in a network environment and of using databases and software packages (word processing, statistical analysis, graphics, spreadsheets, etc.) to prepare correspondence, reports and presentations.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows, general software packages and computer languages, for designing the specifications for testing of applications, the application and conversion of databases, and the maintenance and use of databases both for regular production of statistical data and for ad hoc manipulations and retrievals.

Knowledge of developments and changes in the subject area that may affect the efficiency and validity of data collection, coding and processing in order to devise and modify operational systems and processes.

Knowledge of divisional mandates, objectives, programs, policies and activities to adhere to the various statistical and administrative practices and procedures involved in the collection, coding and processing of statistical data.

Knowledge of data sources and contacts within Statistics Canada in order to locate, analyze and compare statistical output to ensure consistency and reliability; and external to Statistics Canada to obtain collaboration in the provision of statistical information and to verify the accuracy of data.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to ensure understanding and application in the collection, coding and processing of data. The position must have a particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data to ensure their own actions are in compliance.
6. Research and analysis: Analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results.
Assesses and reviews system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems.

Analyses reported data and work results and prepares reports for program managers or subject matter specialists, presenting findings on how the survey was conducted, problems encountered in implementing concepts, definitions, classifications and other instructions, and recommending alternatives.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: District Manager, Regional Operations (Data Collection)
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: The role strongly relates to set up collection because it defines objectives, content and approaches for district collection activities, develops and distributes guidelines and procedures, develops and implements collection applications and alternate work methods, and manages recruitment and training of a professional data collection workforce. It also establishes systems safeguarding procedures and operational frameworks for ongoing collection. This is stronger than design collection because the emphasis is on preparing people, processes and technologies for live operations in the district. Future drivers such as enterprise platforms, secure devices and channels, new digital tools, and workforce transition will increase the setup burden around provisioning, training, secure access and operational readiness.

key_activities: Manages the work of the district office and the organization, planning, scheduling and control of statistical data collection activities in the regional district office (7-day collection operation), including the management of the Statistical Survey Operations (SSO) Office Interviewers and Senior Interviewers.
Monitors and evaluates the cost, quality, efficiency, productivity and security of regional data collection systems and processes and determines the need for development, modification and adaptation.

Identifies and reviews trends and developments in data collection concepts, methods and techniques, including response patterns and respondent behaviour, to determine variances in response rates and to assess their impact on statistical programs and operations within the department.

Develops and implements long term strategies and business solutions to improve respondent relations, data collection and transmission processes, and the development, enhancement and operation of Statistics Canada’s data collection programs.
Leads or participates in task forces, committees or departmental multidisciplinary project teams as a data collection expert and provides advice on proposed modifications to operational procedures.

1. Decision making: Defines the objectives, content and approaches for data collection activities in the regional district office and the framework and conditions within which statistical programs will occur.

Assesses the impact of changes in both technology and the subject area, develops and implements collection applications, alternate work methods and models, and establishes a framework for the on-going operation of statistical systems and processes.

Develops strategies and business solutions to improve respondent relations, data collection and transmission processes and resolves complaints and problems related to survey participation and non-respondents. A poor response rate can impact statistical programs and operations within the department.

Identifies and assesses new statistical methods, techniques and practices and the associated costs and limitations to identify the availability of respondents and to ensure quality control of data, to evaluate the suitability of new hardware and software, and to identify and determine the short and long term program impact and benefits.

Develops and distributes guidelines, instructions and procedures for the use and evaluation of statistical systems and processes. The information is used and applied by program, operational and system staff, when planning and performing their work, and contributes to the overall efficiency operations and quality of the outputs.

Identifies trends and developments in data processing concepts, methods and processes in order to select and integrate new computer hardware and software technology and applications in mass statistical data capture, conversion and dissemination systems and processes.

Establishes and implements specifications, guidelines and procedures for the maintenance and safeguarding of computer systems, equipment, databases and files. The information is used by staff for the collection, compilation, distribution and analysis of a broad range of statistical and administrative information.

Evaluates the effectiveness of existing and new statistical systems and processes and the quality and completeness of data. Senior management uses the studies to assess the attainment of program objectives and the cost, efficiency and utilization of regional resources.
Plans and coordinates concurrent projects or production operations involving multi-disciplinary resources in order to meet program objectives.
2. Leadership and operational management: Manages the recruitment, development and retention, of a fully trained and professional data collection workforce in the regional district office. Establishes, coordinates and leads multi-disciplinary project teams and work groups comprising professional, technical, administrative and interviewers engaged in initiating, developing and implementing programs. Approves work plans and priorities. Establishes organizational structures, recommends classification levels, assigns responsibilities to team or group members, monitors progress and evaluates employee performance, provides guidance and direction on career development, and approves training plans.
Establishes and monitors district budgets, including main estimate and cost recovery funding, to ensure that funds are spent appropriately, with authority to reallocate funds among line objects.

Plans and budgets for the management and operation of the district office in accordance with departmental policy and procedures, identifies content and cost of development and operational requirements, estimates salary, equipment and travel costs, as well as professional fees.
3. Communication: Discusses and negotiates with subject matter and systems specialists to come to an agreement on the conditions within which statistical programs will occur. There is a requirement to understand the issues and to resolve differences that can affect the efficiency and quality of program operations and outputs.

Responds orally or in writing to inquiries from managers, employees and the general public to provide information and advice on the operation and use of systems and processes and the use of program results.

Prepares work plans and summaries outlining approaches, time-frames and resources involved in the operation of statistical collection systems and processes. The information is used by senior management of the region/branch and/or client divisions to prepare program plans, priorities, responsibilities, schedules and budget submissions and will influence the nature, scope and cost of divisional statistical activities.

Develops proposals and provides advice regarding changes and improvements on questionnaire design; enhancements or modifications to survey content and coverage; revisions to collection systems and processes, and the implementation of new hardware and software to be used in data collection activities. The information is used by program managers to define and modify operational procedures.

Negotiates agreements with program managers, subject matter or service divisions, departments/agencies and other outside organizations for the acquisition and dissemination of data and/or the procurement and use of services and equipment.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Advanced knowledge of socio-economic concepts, methods and techniques applied in the development and operation of statistical programs to analyze program outputs, to anticipate and understand the need for new data and to assess the impact on collection activities and programs.

In-depth knowledge of statistical data collection methods, concepts and practices and survey operations to manage the activities of a district office and to provide expert advice on data collection issues.

Extensive knowledge of current and emerging socio-economic issues in Canada and internationally, such as the changing social context and the globalization of markets, particularly as they relate to all aspects of a statistical program. This knowledge is required to understand the issues and to resolve differences that can affect the efficiency and quality of program operations and outputs.

Knowledge of financial and human resources management and of project management methods, techniques and practices to manage the work of a district office and the organization, planning, scheduling and control of statistical data collection activities.

Knowledge of questionnaire development to provide advice to subject matter experts and to recommend changes and improvements to questionnaire design as well as enhancements or modifications to survey content and coverage.
Knowledge of communication principles and techniques to negotiate agreements with subject matter and systems specialists and to defend the validity of collection methods and approaches.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of the departmental and regional operations branch mandate, activities, priorities, practices, standards and procedures applicable to the work to incorporate them into the management of a district office and to recommend changes to management.

Knowledge of broad subject matter areas and their interrelationship to other statistical programs in order to select and integrate new computer hardware and software technology and applications in mass statistical data capture and conversion systems and processes.
Knowledge of other departments and their business lines and legislative frameworks in order to seek cooperation in the conduct of surveys conducted on a cost recovery basis.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies (e.g. confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations and data quality), practices and classification systems is required to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of data collection activities.
Knowledge of the structure and operation of internal client organizations to establish and maintain a framework for the collection, exchange and dissemination of information.
Knowledge of the trends and developments in data collection concepts, methods and techniques to evaluate response patterns and respondent behavior and to provide feedback to subject matter experts.

Knowledge of the content and operation of the Agency’s household and business survey programs and their impact upon systems and processes to determine and devise procedures and standards to be applied in operational activities.
Knowledge of the Statistical Survey Operations organization, its collective agreements, grievance procedures, policies and directives to ensure equitable treatment of all staff.
