Identifies trends and developments in data processing concepts, methods and processes in order to select and integrate new computer hardware and software technology and applications in mass statistical data capture, conversion and dissemination systems and processes.

Analyses the relative quality of data, researches gaps and inconsistencies in the collection methods and procedures used, determines reasons for variances, reviews the comparability of data over time and its relevance in light of trends, developments, changing requirements, policy issues and socio-economic conditions.

Reviews and interprets the methods, concepts, techniques and practices applied in the operation of existing systems and processes; proposes modifications and enhancements or develops alternative approaches.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Area Manager
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: The role strongly relates to set up collection because it contributes to development of regional strategies and operational plans, manages financial, human and material resources for the assigned area, and contributes to planning and implementation of collection methodologies and techniques. It also provides expert direction and training to CFO managers and staff. This is stronger than design collection because the focus is on operational readiness, staffing, and implementation for a major collection. Future-state drivers such as digital readiness, secure collection environments, large-scale workforce mobilization, and new collection technologies will materially affect the setup and enablement aspects of the job.

key_activities: As part of the Regional Census Center Management team, contributes to the development of regional strategies and operational plans, and manages the organization, planning, scheduling and control of Census data collection activities (7-day, collection operation) for a large regional area comprised of a number of Census Field Offices (CFOs).

Manages the financial, human and material resources for the assigned area; and monitors, analyzes and resolves problems associated with resource allocations/expenditures and human resource recruitment strategies for the CFOs.
Directs statistical data collection activities for the assigned CFOs, and contributes to the planning and implementation of collection methodologies and techniques related to the Census Program.

Monitors response patterns and respondent behaviour, variances in response rates, assesses their impact on field collection operations within the area and provides advice and guidance on options to resolve problems identified.

As a subject matter expert, provides expert direction and guidance to CFO Managers and staff on the interpretation of departmental legislation and the application of Statistics Canada policies and procedures; and leads the preparation and delivery of training to CFO Managers.
Represents the department at area public relations venues intended to promote Census participation.

Represents the Region or Regional Census Center area in regional and/or departmental committees or departmental multidisciplinary project teams as a Census collection expert and provides advice on proposed modifications to operational procedures.

Oversees the dissemination and collection of evaluation reports for the assigned Region or Regional Census Center; and contributes, through briefings to discussions on enhancements to the overall Census Program.

Decision making: Effort is required to make decisions/recommendations on strategies and operational plans for multiple Census Field Offices; the organization, planning and scheduling of Census data collection activities (7-day, collection operation) for a large regional area; the resolution of problems associated with resource allocations/expenditures and human resource recruitment strategies for the CFOs; the provision of advice and expert guidance on collection methodologies and techniques related to the Census Program; action required to resolve unacceptable response patterns and strategies to promote Census participation; the analysis of evaluation reports for the assigned Region or Regional Census Center and recommendations for enhancements to the overall Census Program; the management of financial expenditures resources and ongoing analysis of CFO operations to ensure that they are within allocated budgets; and the day-to-day management of financial, human and material resources of the CFOs.
Decisions/recommendations made affect the efficient and effective operations of the CFOs and their compliance to the Statistics Act and departmental policies and procedures.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Regional Program Manager (Data Collection)

This aligns with preparing people, processes, technology, training, and operational readiness before collection starts. It ranks below 4.3 because the work description places slightly more emphasis on leading active collection than on one-time or recurring setup tasks. Future-state drivers around enterprise digital platforms, cyber security, modern collection tools, and workforce skills transition are likely to increase the setup burden for secure devices, applications, credentials, staff readiness, and digital collection infrastructure.

Assesses the cost, quality, efficiency, productivity and security of the functions and activities associated with the data collection, processing, editing, and compilation of statistical outputs.
Evaluates trends and developments in data collection concepts, methods and techniques including response patterns and respondent behaviour.
Participates in the development of strategies and business solutions for data collection and transmission requirements.
Sollicits participation from non-respondents and resolves complaints.
Acts as a regional representative on departmental projects, task forces and committees and provides advice on proposed questionnaire design and survey content and coverage.

1. Decision making: Prepares and reviews correspondence, manuals and data to ensure completeness, accuracy, integrity and compliance with job requirements. Develops operational plans and schedules to manage, organize and control the 7-day data collection activities.

Develops guidelines, instructions and procedures for the use and evaluation of statistical systems and processes and for the maintenance and safeguarding of computer systems, equipment, databases and files.

Identifies and assesses new statistical methods, techniques and practices and the associated costs and limitations to identify the availability of respondents and to ensure quality control of data, to evaluate the suitability of new hardware and software, and to identify and determine the short and long term program impact and benefits.
2. Leadership and operational management: Leads and coordinates multi-disciplinary project teams, committees or work groups comprising professional, technical, administrative and interviewers engaged in initiating, developing and implementing programs. In collaboration with Regional Management, establishes organizational structures, recommends classification levels, assigns responsibilities to team or group members, monitors progress and performance, provides guidance and direction on career development and approves individual training plans.
Establishes and monitors program budgets, including both main estimate and cost recovery funding, to ensure that funds are spent appropriately, with authority to reallocate funds among line objects.

Plans and budgets for the management and operation of the regional CATI or CAPI program in accordance with departmental policy and procedures. Responsibilities include identifying content and cost of development and operational requirements, estimating salary and travel costs, professional fees and equipment costs.
3. Responds orally or in writing to inquiries from managers, employees and the general public to provide information and advice, to solicit participation from non-respondents and to resolve complaints.

Prepares schedules, work plans and summaries outlining approaches, time-frames and resources involved in the operation of statistical collection systems and processes. The information is used by senior management to prepare program plans and has an impact on the nature, scope and cost of divisional statistical activities.

Knowledge and understanding of Statistics Canada’s mandate, programs, objectives, policies and procedures in areas such as survey methodology, operations integration, data confidentiality and security, dissemination and marketing to coordinate and ensure the development and operation of divisional programs consistent with departmental requirements.

Knowledge of the Statistical Survey Operations organization, its collective agreements, grievance procedures, policies and directives to ensure equitable treatment of all staff.

Clients are often uncertain of their data needs and are unfamiliar with statistical options, methods and techniques available.

implicated_work_descriptions.justification: Set up collection is the second strongest relationship because the role develops 'operational plans,' manages recruitment and readiness of a 'large temporary workforce,' supports hub opening and space readiness, develops collection strategies and contingency plans, and ensures financial, human, material, and systems readiness before and during operations. The work description explicitly includes preparing people, processes, facilities and systems for collection. It ranks below 4.3 because the main job is not only preparation but also ongoing operational control during collection. It is stronger than evaluation because readiness, staffing, training and contingency planning are recurring operational responsibilities. Drivers related to Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access, Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity, and Modern Statistical Methods will likely increase the complexity of collection setup through secure devices, credentials, digital tools, workforce training, and scalable readiness for online and hybrid collection models.

key_activities: As part of the area management team, contributes to the development of operational plans for census data collection activities and organizes, oversees and controls census field collection activities within the assigned geographic area; and manages census field operations for a 7-day collection operation.

Develops collection strategies and contingency plans; establishes and defines priorities; monitors and evaluates the cost, quality, efficiency, productivity and security of data collection systems and processes in their assigned geographic area; analyzes and produces reports on the progress of the activities in their assigned geographic area; and resolves problems including but not limited to the need for development, modification and adaptation of operational processes.

Represents the agency in consultations with the general public to solicit participation from non-respondents, responds to and resolves complaints; and contributes to public relations activities to promote census communications and respondent cooperation.

Disseminates and collects evaluation reports for the assigned geographic area; summarizes findings; and makes recommendations for program improvements.

Provides support to regional administration with the opening of the administrative hub in their geographic area such as visits during fit-up, ensures space readiness for the beginning of field activities as well as closing down activities at the hub once operations have been completed.

Decision making: Effort is required to make decisions/recommendations on: the determination and definition of objectives, content and approaches for census collection activities in the assigned geographic area and the operational framework and conditions within which the statistical program will occur; development and implementation of collection applications, alternate work methods and models to achieve desired outcomes; the development of strategies and business solutions to improve respondent relations, data collection and transmission processes; the resolution of complaints and problems related to survey participation and non-respondents; the development and distribution of guidelines, instructions and procedures for use by staff in their assigned geographic area; approval of appointments of all Statistics Act staff in the assigned geographic region; the assurance that financial expenditures and resources are within allocated budgets; and the day-to-day management of financial, human and material resources in their assigned geographic area.

Decisions/recommendations taken affect the efficient and effective operations of the assigned geographic area, as well as the area’s compliance to the Statistics Act and agency policies and procedures.
Leadership and operational management: Manages the recruitment, development and retention of a fully trained and professional data collection workforce in the assigned geographic area. Establishes, coordinates and leads multidisciplinary project teams and work groups comprising professional, technical, and administrative and field staff engaged in initiating, developing and implementing programs. Approves work plans and priorities. Assigns responsibilities to team or group members, monitors progress and evaluates employee performance, provides training and guidance. Supervision and guidance of human resources is significant and made complex by the size and scope of a temporary workforce, and the nature of a 7-day collection operation.

Monitors expenditures for staffing and material resources to ensure funds are spent appropriately and the budget in the assigned geographic area is respected. Exercises influence and decision making latitude in allocating funds and approving expenditures in line with the financial delegation bestowed.

Plans and budgets for the management and operation of the assigned geographic area in accordance with agency policy and procedures, identifies content and cost of development and operational requirements, estimates salary, equipment and travel costs, as well as professional fees.

Oversees some of the aspects related to fit-ups in the assigned geographic area with local contractors to ensure readiness at time of opening and coordinate the dismantlement of the facility at the end of census collection operation.
Communication: Communications skills are required to respond orally and in writing to inquiries from managers, employees to provide information and advice on the operation and use of systems and processes, and briefings on program results in the assigned geographic area.
Communications skills are required to respond orally and in writing to inquiries from the general public on the requirements for response, purpose of the census or issues with employees.

Communications skills are also required to intervene and deal with uncooperative and sometimes hostile respondents. There is a requirement to 'take control' over these emotionally-charged situations, and persuade the respondent to take a more rational approach to a situation. Strategic communication skills are required when negotiating problems of non-response or addressing problems and complaints raised by external bodies.

Negotiation skills are required to convince stakeholders when resolving problems including but not limited to the need for development, modification and adaptation of operational processes. Judgment, tact and flexibility are exercised in finding solutions that meet a range of business needs.
Knowledge of specialized fields: Advanced knowledge of socioeconomic concepts, methods and techniques applied in the development and operation of statistical programs to manage field operations in the assigned geographic area, analyze program outputs, anticipate and understand the need for new data and to assess the impact on collection activities and programs.

In-depth knowledge of statistical data collection methods, concepts and practices and survey operations to manage the activities in the assigned geographic area and to provide expert advice on data collection issues.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies (e.g., confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations and data quality), practices and classifications systems is required to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of census activities.

Knowledge of financial and human resources management and of project management methods, techniques and practices to manage the work, as well as organize, plan, schedule and control the operational activities in the assigned geographic area.
Contextual knowledge: Knowledge and understanding of Statistics Canada’s mandate, programs, objectives, policies and procedures in areas such as survey methodology, operations integration, data confidentiality and security, dissemination and marketing to manage staff in the delivery of the program within an assigned geographic area and ensure that work undertaken is standardized and consistent with departmental requirements.

Knowledge of the regional and local operation’s mandate, activities, priorities, standards and procedures to incorporate them into the management of the assigned geographic area and to recommend changes to management.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies (e.g., confidentiality of data, security, and respondent relations and data quality), practices and classification systems is required to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of census activities.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act, Financial Administration Act, the Public Service Employment Act, collective agreements and related policies and directives and supporting financial and human resources management methods, techniques and practices in order to manage the financial, human resource and material resources of assigned geographic areas.
Knowledge of the Canada Labor Code to ensure safe working conditions exist for all employees.

Knowledge of external business lines including those of Shared Services Canada and municipal entities are required when negotiating space requirements to facilitate the delivery of collection operations.
Research and analysis: Reviews and interprets the methods, concepts, techniques and practices applied in the operation of existing systems and processes and proposes modifications and enhancements or develops alternative approaches.
Identifies and evaluates variations in survey responses and contributes to promotional activities to increase respondent participation rates.

Analyzes and produces reports on the progress of activities in the assigned geographic area and resolves problems including but not limited to the need for development, modification and adaptation of operational processes.

Conducts comprehensive evaluations to determine the effectiveness and efficiency of collection operations. Identifies trends, gaps and inconsistencies, and makes recommendations for consideration by Head Office on areas requiring improvements or approaches to be adopted.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: Set up collection is the second strongest relationship because the role prepares and distributes procedures, operational specifications and training for manual and automated collection, provides input to training materials, assists in training delivery, and supports operational systems used for collection. These are direct indicators of readiness activities involving people, processes and collection technology. This is stronger than Run collection because the evidence is more about preparing systems, procedures, testing and training than live operational execution. Future drivers such as AI-enabled tools, enterprise infrastructure, cyber/privacy requirements, and workforce skills transition will likely shift this work toward provisioning digital collection tools, configuring secure channels, supporting online-first operations, and preparing staff for more automated and mixed-source environments.

key_activities: Participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data.
Evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives.
Provides assistance and advice to users on methods and practices of collection and coding.
Participates on data collection and operations teams.
Provides input to training materials concerning data collection operations and assists in training delivery.

1. Decision making: Evaluates methods, procedures and results of statistical collection, coding and processing operations and recommends alternatives. The surveys worked on can vary in size, complexity and methods.
Prepares and distributes procedures, operational specifications and training for the manual and automated collection, coding and processing of statistical data.
Develops and outlines system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems.
Evaluates and recommends appropriate procedures, software and hardware for the collection, coding and processing of data.
Develops test cases and data from functional specifications and specifies testing approaches for own use and use by other program staff to ensure that computer applications meet requirements.
2. Leadership and operational management: Participates in project teams, work groups, meetings and conferences in order to develop and improve work methods and practices, share knowledge and contribute to skill development.

Monitors and tracks time spent on activities for the purposes of recording and recovering such costs from the client. Incurs and accounts for petty cash, credit card, taxi voucher, bus pass, and other expenditures.
3. Communication: Responds orally and in writing to enquiries from managers, employees and the general public to provide information on the operation of divisional systems and processes and the use of program results.
Writes survey information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports.
Designs and prepares statistical tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text for use in regular and ad-hoc publications.
Prepares reports and recommendations outlining options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection and processing systems.

Meets with subject matter and systems specialists, clients, service providers and others, in order to comprehend and elaborate on the conditions within which statistical operations will occur. There is a requirement to understand the issues and resolve differences that can affect the efficiency of the division's operations and quality of outputs.

Contacts data suppliers or respondents to obtain their collaboration in responding to surveys, to clarify problems or irregularities. This may necessitate having to explain technical procedures for obtaining the data in the appropriate format, or to clarify and explain statistical concepts.
Participates in departmental meetings and working groups in order to share knowledge within an area of operational expertise.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of the underlying statistical and economic principles and concepts required for the collection, coding and processing of data.
Knowledge of the concepts, methods and techniques used in the management and control of statistical collection, coding and processing activities.
Knowledge of methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications.

Knowledge of methods and practices of operating personal computers in a network environment and of using databases and software packages (word processing, statistical analysis, graphics, spreadsheets, etc.) to prepare correspondence, reports and presentations.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows, general software packages and computer languages, for designing the specifications for testing of applications, the application and conversion of databases, and the maintenance and use of databases both for regular production of statistical data and for ad hoc manipulations and retrievals.

Knowledge of developments and changes in the subject area that may affect the efficiency and validity of data collection, coding and processing in order to devise and modify operational systems and processes.

Knowledge of divisional mandates, objectives, programs, policies and activities to adhere to the various statistical and administrative practices and procedures involved in the collection, coding and processing of statistical data.

Knowledge of data sources and contacts within Statistics Canada in order to locate, analyze and compare statistical output to ensure consistency and reliability; and external to Statistics Canada to obtain collaboration in the provision of statistical information and to verify the accuracy of data.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to ensure understanding and application in the collection, coding and processing of data. The position must have a particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data to ensure their own actions are in compliance.
6. Research and analysis: Analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results.
Assesses and reviews system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems.

Analyses reported data and work results and prepares reports for program managers or subject matter specialists, presenting findings on how the survey was conducted, problems encountered in implementing concepts, definitions, classifications and other instructions, and recommending alternatives.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Chief- Training and Strategic Development
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: Set up collection is the second strongest relationship because the role develops and adapts training materials and tools, coaches course participants, and ensures learning products reflect current survey and statistical business practices. This aligns with the subprocess's strong emphasis on training collection staff and preparing people and processes for operational use. It is stronger than generic evaluation or design subprocesses because the evidence points to operational readiness and staff preparation. Future drivers such as digital collection tools, mixed-source operations and skills transition will likely require more practical training on collection systems, methods and live operational procedures.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: District Manager, Regional Operations (Data Collection)
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This subprocess is also central because the role ensures operational readiness of people, systems and procedures before and during collection cycles. gsbpm_description: This sub-process is where the collection is implemented. The different collection instruments are used to collect or gather the information, which may include raw microdata or aggregates produced at the source, as well as any associated metadata. For survey or census data, it can include: Initial contact with respondents to request data and any subsequent follow-up or reminder actions, recording when and how they were contacted, and whether they have reacted; Management of the relationship between the statistical organisation and respondents, so that it remains positive, and recording and responding to comments, queries and complaints. (Minimisation of the number of non-respondents contributes significantly to higher quality of the collected data.); Manual data entry at the point of contact, or fieldwork management, depending on the source and collection approach; Georeferencing[12] at the same time as collection of the data (using inputs from location-enabled systems such as GPS), or recording location by putting a mark on a map, etc., depending on the geographical frame and the technology used. Automated logical checks on data at the point of collection (i.e. validation-on-entry for survey response data) are considered to take place in 5.3 (Review and validate). For administrative, geospatial, or other non-statistical data, the data supplier either sends it as scheduled or is contacted to send the information, which might require follow-ups. Broader technical-level engagement with data suppliers falls under the Data Supplier Management overarching activity. In the case where the data are published under an Open Data license and exist in machine-readable form, they may be freely accessed and used. This sub-process may also include the monitoring of data collection and making any necessary changes to improve data quality. This includes generating reports, visualising and adjusting the process for obtaining data to ensure the data are fit for use. When the collection meets its targets, it is closed and a report on the collection is produced. Some basic checks of the structure and integrity of the information received may take place within this sub-process, (e.g. checking that files are in the right format and contain the expected fields).

Evaluates the effectiveness of existing and new statistical systems and processes and the quality and completeness of data. Senior management uses the studies to assess the attainment of program objectives and the cost, efficiency and utilization of regional resources.
Plans and coordinates concurrent projects or production operations involving multi-disciplinary resources in order to meet program objectives.
2. Leadership and operational management: Manages the recruitment, development and retention, of a fully trained and professional data collection workforce in the regional district office. Establishes, coordinates and leads multi-disciplinary project teams and work groups comprising professional, technical, administrative and interviewers engaged in initiating, developing and implementing programs. Approves work plans and priorities. Establishes organizational structures, recommends classification levels, assigns responsibilities to team or group members, monitors progress and evaluates employee performance, provides guidance and direction on career development, and approves training plans.
Establishes and monitors district budgets, including main estimate and cost recovery funding, to ensure that funds are spent appropriately, with authority to reallocate funds among line objects.

Plans and budgets for the management and operation of the district office in accordance with departmental policy and procedures, identifies content and cost of development and operational requirements, estimates salary, equipment and travel costs, as well as professional fees.
3. Communication: Discusses and negotiates with subject matter and systems specialists to come to an agreement on the conditions within which statistical programs will occur. There is a requirement to understand the issues and to resolve differences that can affect the efficiency and quality of program operations and outputs.

Responds orally or in writing to inquiries from managers, employees and the general public to provide information and advice on the operation and use of systems and processes and the use of program results.

Prepares work plans and summaries outlining approaches, time-frames and resources involved in the operation of statistical collection systems and processes. The information is used by senior management of the region/branch and/or client divisions to prepare program plans, priorities, responsibilities, schedules and budget submissions and will influence the nature, scope and cost of divisional statistical activities.

Develops proposals and provides advice regarding changes and improvements on questionnaire design; enhancements or modifications to survey content and coverage; revisions to collection systems and processes, and the implementation of new hardware and software to be used in data collection activities. The information is used by program managers to define and modify operational procedures.

Negotiates agreements with program managers, subject matter or service divisions, departments/agencies and other outside organizations for the acquisition and dissemination of data and/or the procurement and use of services and equipment.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Advanced knowledge of socio-economic concepts, methods and techniques applied in the development and operation of statistical programs to analyze program outputs, to anticipate and understand the need for new data and to assess the impact on collection activities and programs.

In-depth knowledge of statistical data collection methods, concepts and practices and survey operations to manage the activities of a district office and to provide expert advice on data collection issues.

Extensive knowledge of current and emerging socio-economic issues in Canada and internationally, such as the changing social context and the globalization of markets, particularly as they relate to all aspects of a statistical program. This knowledge is required to understand the issues and to resolve differences that can affect the efficiency and quality of program operations and outputs.

Knowledge of financial and human resources management and of project management methods, techniques and practices to manage the work of a district office and the organization, planning, scheduling and control of statistical data collection activities.

Knowledge of questionnaire development to provide advice to subject matter experts and to recommend changes and improvements to questionnaire design as well as enhancements or modifications to survey content and coverage.
Knowledge of communication principles and techniques to negotiate agreements with subject matter and systems specialists and to defend the validity of collection methods and approaches.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of the departmental and regional operations branch mandate, activities, priorities, practices, standards and procedures applicable to the work to incorporate them into the management of a district office and to recommend changes to management.

Knowledge of broad subject matter areas and their interrelationship to other statistical programs in order to select and integrate new computer hardware and software technology and applications in mass statistical data capture and conversion systems and processes.
Knowledge of other departments and their business lines and legislative frameworks in order to seek cooperation in the conduct of surveys conducted on a cost recovery basis.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies (e.g. confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations and data quality), practices and classification systems is required to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of data collection activities.
Knowledge of the structure and operation of internal client organizations to establish and maintain a framework for the collection, exchange and dissemination of information.
Knowledge of the trends and developments in data collection concepts, methods and techniques to evaluate response patterns and respondent behavior and to provide feedback to subject matter experts.

Knowledge of the content and operation of the Agency’s household and business survey programs and their impact upon systems and processes to determine and devise procedures and standards to be applied in operational activities.
Knowledge of the Statistical Survey Operations organization, its collective agreements, grievance procedures, policies and directives to ensure equitable treatment of all staff.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act pertaining to data security and confidentiality to ensure adherence in all development and operational activities. Knowledge of the Canada Labor Code to ensure safe working conditions exist for all employees. Knowledge of the Financial Administration Act, the Public Service Employment Act and related policies and directives.
6. Research and analysis: Determines and evaluates changes in the statistical needs of clients and provides advice regarding questionnaire design, concepts, changes in technology, respondent reaction and understanding.
Extracts and interprets information from analytical reports to assess the content and operation of collection activities and programs.

Identifies trends and developments in data processing concepts, methods and processes in order to select and integrate new computer hardware and software technology and applications in mass statistical data capture, conversion and dissemination systems and processes.

Analyses the relative quality of data, researches gaps and inconsistencies in the collection methods and procedures used, determines reasons for variances, reviews the comparability of data over time and its relevance in light of trends, developments, changing requirements, policy issues and socio-economic conditions.

Reviews and interprets the methods, concepts, techniques and practices applied in the operation of existing systems and processes; proposes modifications and enhancements or develops alternative approaches.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Area Manager
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This is the strongest match because the position directly 'organizes, oversees and controls census field collection activities' and 'manages census field operations for a 7-day collection operation' in an assigned geographic area. The work includes developing collection strategies and contingency plans, monitoring cost, quality, efficiency, productivity and security of collection systems, responding to non-response and complaints, and resolving operational problems. This is stronger than 4.2 because the role is centered on directing live field collection, not only preparing for it. Future drivers such as online-first collection, adaptive collection, automation, integrated monitoring and operational efficiency will likely reshape the job toward more digitally coordinated collection, real-time performance intervention, supplier/platform dependence, and more targeted management of respondent follow-up and field effort.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Area Manager
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This is the strongest match because the job directly 'manages the organization, planning, scheduling and control of Census data collection activities' for multiple Census Field Offices and 'directs statistical data collection activities' across a large regional area. It monitors response patterns and respondent behaviour, resolves operational problems, and provides expert guidance on collection methodologies and techniques. This is stronger than setup or evaluation subprocesses because the central accountability is operational control of active field collection. Future drivers such as adaptive collection, online-first operations, automation, integrated monitoring and execution discipline will likely reshape the role toward more real-time operational steering, digital collection oversight, targeted intervention on response problems, and tighter management of quality, security and timeliness across CFOs.

key_activities: As part of the Regional Census Center Management team, contributes to the development of regional strategies and operational plans, and manages the organization, planning, scheduling and control of Census data collection activities (7-day, collection operation) for a large regional area comprised of a number of Census Field Offices (CFOs).

Manages the financial, human and material resources for the assigned area; and monitors, analyzes and resolves problems associated with resource allocations/expenditures and human resource recruitment strategies for the CFOs.
Directs statistical data collection activities for the assigned CFOs, and contributes to the planning and implementation of collection methodologies and techniques related to the Census Program.

Monitors response patterns and respondent behaviour, variances in response rates, assesses their impact on field collection operations within the area and provides advice and guidance on options to resolve problems identified.

As a subject matter expert, provides expert direction and guidance to CFO Managers and staff on the interpretation of departmental legislation and the application of Statistics Canada policies and procedures; and leads the preparation and delivery of training to CFO Managers.
Represents the department at area public relations venues intended to promote Census participation.

Represents the Region or Regional Census Center area in regional and/or departmental committees or departmental multidisciplinary project teams as a Census collection expert and provides advice on proposed modifications to operational procedures.

Oversees the dissemination and collection of evaluation reports for the assigned Region or Regional Census Center; and contributes, through briefings to discussions on enhancements to the overall Census Program.

Decision making: Effort is required to make decisions/recommendations on strategies and operational plans for multiple Census Field Offices; the organization, planning and scheduling of Census data collection activities (7-day, collection operation) for a large regional area; the resolution of problems associated with resource allocations/expenditures and human resource recruitment strategies for the CFOs; the provision of advice and expert guidance on collection methodologies and techniques related to the Census Program; action required to resolve unacceptable response patterns and strategies to promote Census participation; the analysis of evaluation reports for the assigned Region or Regional Census Center and recommendations for enhancements to the overall Census Program; the management of financial expenditures resources and ongoing analysis of CFO operations to ensure that they are within allocated budgets; and the day-to-day management of financial, human and material resources of the CFOs.
Decisions/recommendations made affect the efficient and effective operations of the CFOs and their compliance to the Statistics Act and departmental policies and procedures.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Regional Geographer and Management Information Systems Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: The role materially relates to run collection because it performs daily analysis of management information reports to monitor costs and field collection progress, makes recommendations to resolve anomalies, applies targeted strategies in difficult areas, and supports collective dwelling enumeration strategies during live operations. These are direct live operational monitoring and intervention activities. This is stronger than general evaluation because the analysis is used immediately to steer active collection. Future-state drivers such as adaptive collection, integrated monitoring, digital field-management tools, and real-time operational dashboards will increase the emphasis on dynamic intervention and anomaly management.

gsbpm_description: This sub-process integrates data from one or more sources. It is where the results of subprocesses in the Collect phase are combined. The input data can be from a mixture of external or internal sources, and a variety of collection instruments, including extracts of administrative and other non-statistical data sources. Administrative data or other non-statistical sources of data can substitute for all or some of the variables directly collected from a survey. This sub-process also includes harmonising or creating new figures that agree between sources of data. The result is a consolidated set of data. Data integration can include: Combining data from multiple sources, as part of the creation of integrated statistics such as national accounts; Combining geospatial data and statistical data or other non-statistical data; Data pooling, with the aim of increasing the effective number of observations of some phenomena; Matching or record linkage routines, with the aim of linking micro or macro data from different sources; Data fusion - integration followed by reduction or replacement; Prioritising, when two or more sources contain data for the same variable, with potentially different values. Data integration may take place at any point in this phase, before or after any of the other subprocesses. There may also be several instances of data integration in any statistical business process. Following integration, depending on data protection requirements, data may be deidentified, that is stripped of identifiers such as name and address, to help to protect confidentiality.

drivers.driver: AI and Automation in Statistical Production
workforce_implications: agency staff will integrate AI assistants into their daily work to increase efficiency
clarify handoffs across programs
developing skills to support the adoption of modern, open-source technologies and AI
enhancing executives' skills in all areas, from AI upskilling and strengthening leadership competencies, to promoting their change leadership capacity
extensive coordination across the agency's collection, communications, analysis and dissemination teams
involve the recruitment of thousands of employees—including enumerators who conduct in-person data collection
reduce manual effort
requires extensive preparation to ensure that Statistics Canada's infrastructure, systems and workforce ready to deliver Canada's largest statistical undertaking
work embedded directly into production workflows
drivers.impact: AI and automation materially affect data integration by enabling more automated ingestion and harmonisation of diverse structured and unstructured sources, while increasing the need for governed, secure, and monitored integration pipelines.
impact_mechanisms: automation supports repeatable ingestion and harmonisation across multiple sources
data extraction from unstructured sources broadens the types of inputs being integrated
enterprise platforms and shared solutions support common integration services across programs
monitoring improves oversight of integration quality and pipeline performance
data security, cyber security, and governance shape deidentification and controlled linkage practices
reducing duplication and sustainability of production encourage reusable integration patterns

drivers.driver: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion
workforce_implications: collection, analysis and dissemination workload
parallel census operations across the agency
provide employees with the tools and training they need
support a skilled and adaptable workforce
drivers.impact: This is one of the most directly affected subprocesses. The driver explicitly expands the use of administrative, alternative, linked and geospatial data, making integration, harmonisation, prioritisation and record linkage central production activities. SDLE-enabled linkage and multi-source consolidation become core to replacing or supplementing survey inputs and improving timeliness and relevance.
impact_mechanisms: SDLE directly supports linkage-ready integration across datasets
data linkages make record linkage and matching routines central to production
administrative data and alternative data increase the number and heterogeneity of sources to integrate
gridded data requires integration of geospatial and statistical data

Represents the division as an analytical research and modeling specialist in the area of expertise on development projects, task forces and committees.

1. Decision making: Investigates client requirements for statistical information, determines data sources, modifies existing methods and approaches for analytical research and modeling studies or develops new ones to meet specific needs.

Defines project objectives and priorities, prepares work plans and summaries outlining approaches, time-frames and resources. Each project is unique in nature and decisions impact on other ongoing studies.
Develops guidelines, proposals and recommendations for divisional management to improve existing surveys or to initiate new surveys / projects.

Selects and evaluates analytical techniques and quantitative analytical methods to be used to integrate and interpret mass volumes of data. Projects may involve a combination of statistical techniques and methods and the integration of data from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses) collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts and efforts must be made to translate them into common concepts.
2. Leadership and operational management: Manages a unit involved in statistical activities and/or leads multi-disciplinary project teams for special projects. Determines goals, priorities and milestones, sets objectives, and plans and schedules the work, resolves conflicting priorities; identifies human resources needs, determines the appropriate selection methods (internal and external resources / contractors) to meet program or project objectives, recruits staff, evaluates employee performance, develops training plans, motivates and maintains morale of employees.

Plans and budgets for on-going analytical projects and/or special projects, including estimates for salaries, professional fees and implementation costs, with authority to allocate/reallocate funds within the budget. Provides input to budgets based on operational needs and by obtaining/providing cost estimates for personnel, supplies, equipment purchases and travel for use in developing section or division budgets. Establishes and negotiates contracts for projects. Procures goods and services according to approved budget allocations.
3. Communication: Writes and presents analytical material to be disseminated to a target audience ranging from the general public to a specialized audience (e.g. academics). When addressing the general public, explains in clear terms the interpretation of complex data, reasons for variances in the results and the trends derived. When addressing a specialized public, it is also necessary to provide more detailed explanations of statistical and analytical methods and approaches used. When media representatives challenge or misinterpret the results of surveys or projects, it is necessary to further explain the results and statistical methods and approaches used in order to maintain the department’s reputation for producing high quality data.

Provides expertise, advice and interpretation to decision-makers at all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academics, on the practical application and interpretation of statistical data and information. This often requires the adaptation and presentation of complex information in basic, understandable formats. This information is used as input to decision making for a vast array of economic and social policies, programs and other activities.

Presents arguments and options and negotiates resources, timeframes and costs with service providers (e.g. system specialists, regional office staff, survey methodologists, contractors, etc.) and clients within and outside the department.
Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and workgroups to develop consensus or share knowledge within the area of expertise.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of advanced statistical theories, methods (including data gathering and analysis techniques), concepts and practices in order to plan and implement analytical research and modeling studies and to recommend and implement improvements to statistical programs.

Knowledge of economic or sociology principles and theory especially as they relate to a specialized area (e.g. System of National Accounts, Health, Justice, Education, Labor, Prices, Demography, International Trade, Balance of Payments, Environment, etc.). This is necessary to conduct analytical research and modeling studies and to assess the content of articles and reports that will be distributed widely or published.
Knowledge of the theories and principles of management to lead a multi-disciplinary unit or project teams.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of the divisional mandate, activities, priorities, practices, standards and procedures applicable to the work to incorporate them into the conduct and management of analytical projects.

Knowledge of the mandate, objectives and organization of Statistics Canada to manage analytical projects. Knowledge of other statistical programs (concepts, methods, and databases) related to the area of expertise to plan and implement statistical activities, to integrate conceptually different data from other programs, to explain variances and to recommend changes to other statistical programs.

Knowledge of departmental publication, marketing and dissemination policies and practices in order to establish common divisional policies and practices in the preparation of statistical tables, charts, explanatory notes etc. for dissemination to user and/or clients.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies (confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations, data quality), practices and classification systems to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of statistical projects and activities.
Knowledge of the policies and programs, of key client departments, to determine their information requirements and identify analysis opportunities.

Knowledge of data users and suppliers from all levels of government, and the private sector to discuss data reporting agreements; to understand their needs for statistical data or studies, to negotiate contracts and to provide them with expert advice on study or survey results.

Knowledge of current and emerging socio-economic issues in Canada and internationally such as the changing social context and the globalization of markets, particularly as they relate to the area of expertise in a statistical program (e.g. System of National Accounts, Education, Health, Labor, Prices, Demography, International Trade, Balance of Payments, Environment, etc.). This knowledge is required to analyze and interpret the data and assess their impact on the area of specialization. International public and private organizations involved in the area of statistics or in the area of expertise. This is necessary to share information.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements to other departments, agencies, industry, members of the public and the media. Knowledge of the Statitstics and Privacy Acts is particulary important with respect to the security and confidentiality of information and data provided and to ensure that they and their subordinates do not release any information which may identify an individual or group without prior consent.
6. Research and analysis: Analysis is required to understand and interpret user requirements for statistical information and to translate them into a concrete, timely and affordable information request. Determines data requirements and sources, and recommends modifications to the content and coverage of studies, procedures, concepts, methods and definitions.

Writes analytical papers and articles on the interpretation of surveys, statistical applications or project findings, their application to the area of specialization and the methodology used. This information is published and used by specialized groups of interest (e.g. academics, private sector industries , etc.) and Federal and provincial departments for decision / policy making purposes.

Researches gaps and inconsistencies in the collection, processing, analysis and dissemination methods and procedures; reviews the conceptual framework used and the compatibility with other statistical programs; conceptualizes enhancements or proposes modifications to study and/or program content and coverage and operational procedures, such as new or modified data sources, concepts, methods and definitions to be applied. Each project is unique in nature and may involve a combination of statistical techniques and methods and the integration of data from a variety of sources.

Selects and evaluates analytical techniques and methods to be used to integrate and interpret massive volumes of data. Reviews and modifies existing techniques, methods and approaches or develops new ones to meet specific needs. Often, these data come from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses) and have been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts. There is a requirement to integrate data from diverse sources and concepts into a common conceptual framework and to identify and measure complex and subtle relationships among variables to produce statistical information.

Interprets the relative quality of data produced, determines reasons for variances, its comparability over time and its relevancy in light of changing requirements, trends, developments, policy issues and socio-economic conditions.

Develops data bases for the provision of time-series information, interprets preliminary results, reviews and modifies approaches and techniques as necessary.
Reviews and approves detailed processing parameters, devises criteria and methods to rectify inconsistencies and recommends modifications to ensure the continuity and compatibility of data.
2. Leadership and operational management: Plans, organizes and coordinates the work of a unit or project team involved in the conduct of special studies, surveys and projects. Determines goals, priorities and milestones, sets objectives, plans and schedules the work, resolves conflicting priorities; identifies human resources needs, determines the appropriate selection methods (internal and external resources / contractors) to meet program or project objectives, participates in the recruitment of staff, provides input to employee performance, develops training plans, motivates and maintains morale of employees.

Plans and budgets for on-going studies and/or special projects, including estimates for salaries, professional fees and implementation costs, with authority to allocate/reallocate funds within the budget. Provides input to budgets based on operational needs and by obtaining/providing cost estimates for personnel, supplies, equipment purchases and travel for use in developing section or division budgets. Establishes and negotiates contracts for projects. Responsible for the acquisition of goods and services, according to the budget allocated.
3. Communication: Provides expert advice and guidance to all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academics, on statistical program results, methods, concepts and techniques applied and on trends and developments in economic, sociological or related data programs. This often requires the adaptation and presentation of complex information in basic, understandable formats. This information is used as input to decision making for a vast array of economic and social policies, programs and other activities.

Presents arguments and options and negotiates resources, timeframes and costs with service providers (e.g. system specialists, regional office staff, survey methodologists, contractors, etc.) and clients within and outside the department.

Writes and presents subject matter concepts and technical definitions in common terminology in order to explain and clarify current developments, to explain the results of studies and to resolve differences that can affect the efficiency of the manipulation, storage and retrieval of data and the quality of outputs.
Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and groups to develop consensus or share knowledge within the area of expertise.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of economic/sociologic principles and practices as they relate to a specialized area as well as specific knowledge of the area to initiate and conduct projects to improve existing concepts or develop new approaches to extend the application of divisional statistics, and to analyze, review and present survey findings. This knowledge is also required to provide subject-matter expertise, advice and consultative services to users, within and outside STC, as well as to provide related advice to other professionals.
Knowledge of statistical theories, methods, concepts and practices used in the manipulation, storage and retrieval of statistical data.
Knowledge of the principles and practices of human and financial resource management to plan and budget for on-going studies, surveys and/or special projects carried out by project teams.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of the divisional mandate, activities, priorities, practices, standards and procedures applicable to the work to incorporate them into the conduct and management of studies, surveys and projects.

Knowledge of the mandate, objectives and organization of Statistics Canada to manage subject matter studies, surveys and projects. Knowledge of other statistical programs (concepts, methods, and databases) related to the area of expertise to plan and implement statistical activities, to integrate conceptually different data from other programs, to explain variances and to recommend changes to other statistical programs.

Knowledge of departmental publication, marketing and dissemination policies and practices in order to establish common divisional policies and practices in the preparation of statistical tables, charts, explanatory notes etc. for dissemination to user and/or subject matter clients.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies (confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations, data quality), practices and classification systems to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of statistical projects and activities.

Knowledge of data suppliers to discuss data reporting agreements. Knowledge of data users from governments and from the private sector to identify potential new markets, to understand client needs for complex statistical data or studies, to negotiate contracts and to provide advice on program results.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements to other departments, agencies, industry, members of the public and the media. Knowledge of the Statitstics and Privacy Acts is particulary important with respect to the security and confidentiality of information and data provided and to ensure that they and their subordinates do not release any information which may identify an individual or group without prior consent.
6. Research and analysis: Interprets the results of tests, procedural investigations and feasibility studies to produce data bases and data retrieval packages used for the production of integrated statistical information.

Reviews and approves detailed processing parameters, classification, coding systems and report formats or develops new ones to meet specific needs. Some studies may involve a combination of statistical techniques and methods and the integration of data from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses). Often, the data have been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts and must be translated into common concepts.

Reviews new and revised processing systems and procedures to ensure compatibility with other statistical programs, assesses technical and conceptual problems and inconsistencies in the manipulation, storage and retrieval of statistical data and develops specifications for new and existing data compilation programs.
Evaluates the impact of technological developments on respondent operation and production procedures and prepares reports recommending appropriate approaches and guidelines.

Research and analysis are required to evaluate the effectiveness of processing systems, to formulate computer systems specifications, to design and create test procedures and acceptance criteria to ensure that processing systems yield the desired outputs.

Knowledge of the concepts, methods and techniques used in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical data in order to advise on subject-matter development and resolve subject-matter concept and definition issues.

Knowledge of system analysis and design, computer processing, generalized survey software packages to design, develop, test, maintain and implement processing systems; to design specifications for the testing of data, and to maintain and use databases.

Knowledge of contacts within key client departments to establish a liaison; to understand need for statistical data, and to provide advice and guidance on subject-matter concepts, methods, techniques and results.
Knowledge of the divisional mandate, objectives, priorities, practices, standards, processes and procedures in order to coordinate on-going operational activities and/or special projects.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to ensure understanding and application in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of data. The position must have a particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data to ensure their own actions are in compliance.
6. RESEARCH AND ANALYSIS: Reviews current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.

Researches and compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output. Adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats, depending on the complexity of the subject matter or the number of different sources.
Assesses and determines the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored.

Examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems.

Management skills and knowledge of the theories and principles of general and project management to lead a multi-disciplinary project team.
