implicated_work_descriptions.title: Principal Consumer Prices Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: Integrate data is the third strongest relationship because the role manages studies that 'select and evaluate analytical techniques and methods to be used to integrate and interpret massive volumes of data' and evaluates multiple data sources for integration into CPI production. This is stronger than downstream analysis-only subprocesses because the description explicitly includes integration of distinct sources and assessing their relevance, accuracy and impact. Future drivers such as alternative data, gridded and web data, integrated pipelines, and next-generation production will increase the complexity of harmonisation, source prioritisation and repeatable enterprise integration for consumer price indexes.

key_activities: Plans and implements long term strategies for the development, enhancement and operation of the highly specialized temporal and spatial consumer price index program. Develops new methods and techniques based on leading edge international developments, to meet the needs of the highly specialized temporal and spatial consumer price index program. Assesses the implications of new approaches and makes recommendations for their adoption.

Performs detailed analysis, evaluation and review of statistical methods and concepts to improve existing data and determines changes in the statistical needs of clients, assessing the impact on the critical programs and developing options and strategies to manage complex issues and multi-stakeholder relations.

Provides expert recommendations, analysis and advice to senior managers in government (from various divisions within Statistics Canada and in key client departments such as Finance Canada and the Bank of Canada) and officials in industry (data providers and users), academia, other national and international statistical institutions and special interest groups.

Oversees and coordinates the review of established statistical methods and processes within the highly specialized realm of temporal and spatial consumer prices indexes. Determines departmental and government-wide impacts and implications and makes recommendations for change.
Implements new systems or methodologies and processes to meet client demands, identifies new statistical methods, techniques and practices and evaluates their cost, efficiency and productivity
Supervision of project teams responsible for statistical outputs, research projects or studies and management of the financial resources attached to each project.

Work is done within the context of temporal and spatial indexes which are used throughout Statistics Canada (i.e., Producer Prices program and the Canadian System of Macroeconomic Accounts), throughout government and industry to index payments worth billions of dollars, and by the Bank of Canada, as the basis for the country’s inflation targeting and monetary policy. Impact of errors is extremely high and cuts across Statistics Canada, other departments and throughout the economy. These factors add to the priority, complexity and scrutiny of the work of this position.

Decision Making: Reviews and evaluates statistical program methods and concepts to improve existing data, to develop new techniques and methods of producing, evaluating and analyzing data and to extend the use and application of departmental statistical programs. Recommendations based on this work have the ability to influence the direction of major corporate initiatives, programs and policies, including those related to big data (e.g., scanner data, web-scraped data).

Initiates changes and implements new systems or methodologies and processes, identifies and assesses new statistical methods, techniques and practices and the associated costs and limitations, identifies the availability and reliability of new data sources, evaluates the suitability of new hardware and software, and identifies and determines the short and long term program impact and benefits. Recommendations lead to changes in approach for the program and take into consideration risks and impacts related to the changes and the use of the resulting program data for indexing and monetary policy purposes.

Manages complex studies related to the temporal and spatial consumer prices program, determines the objectives, content and methodology of such work, defines and sets priorities and milestones, selects and evaluates analytical techniques and methods to be used to integrate and interpret massive volumes of data and organizes the review and presentation of findings. Problems to be resolved usually impact other statistical programs such as Producer Prices and the Canadian System of Macroeconomic Accounts.

Determines objectives and priorities for specific studies and provides expert advice and innovative solutions and recommendations to senior management on course of action and outcomes, or on significant issues affecting temporal and spatial price index programs.
Leadership And Operational Management: Provides advanced subject matter expertise within a multi-disciplinary departmental and interdepartmental project team environment to facilitate big data or temporal and spatial consumer price index research and development activities and establishes objectives and priorities to achieve long term program goals.

Assesses and recommends human and financial resource needs to achieve research and project objectives. Monitors the scope, schedule and cost of the work against approved baselines. Provides input into ongoing and strategic financial planning exercises.

Manages multi-disciplinary intradepartmental and/or interdepartmental project teams involved in research and development activities and establishes objectives and priorities to achieve long term project goals.
For project team members, establishes work objectives and training related to project requirements, monitors achievements and provides input into performance evaluations.
Communication: Provides expert advice and consultative services to senior officials and policy makers at all levels of government, business and national agencies and academics on the results of research and analytical studies, economic and socio-economic theories and principles and statistical concepts and methods as they relate to temporal and spatial consumer price indices.

Attends divisional and intradepartmental meetings and represents the division in interdepartmental and international meetings, conferences and groups to develop consensus or share knowledge in the field of temporal and spatial consumer price indices or big data. Represents, expresses and defends the viewpoint, priorities, conceptual integrity and the validity of methods of the program in venues where decisions are made in order to promote the organization’s interests and influence conceptual directions.

When addressing the general public, explains in clear terms the interpretation of complex data and conceptual frameworks, reasons for variances in the results and the trends derived. When addressing a specialized public, it is also necessary to provide more detailed explanations of the concepts, statistical and analytical approaches used. When media representatives challenge or misinterpret the results of surveys or projects, it is necessary to further explain the results and statistical methods and approaches used in layman’s terms in order to maintain the department's reputation for producing high quality data.
Knowledge of specialized fields: Expert knowledge of economic and sociological principles, concepts and theories, especially as they relate to price index number theory, and specific knowledge of temporal and spatial consumer price indexes. This knowledge is required to provide expert advice on the results of surveys and studies to data users, to STC senior management and to other professionals within and outside STC. It is also required to provide expert evaluation of impacts and risks associated with proposed program changes on the use of the resulting program data for other Statistics Canada programs such as the Producer Prices program and the Canadian System of Macroeconomic Accounts, as well as for government-wide and economy-wide uses such as indexation and monetary policy uses.

Expert knowledge of systems, systems design and practices relevant for the maintenance and development of the temporal and spatial price index statistical programs. *related to the development environment only

Expert knowledge of statistical theories, methods, concepts and practices used in the development, collection, compilation, analysis and interpretation of temporal and spatial price index data in order to develop new methods and techniques and provide expert advice to internal and external stakeholders.
Advanced knowledge of resource and project management practices and principles in order to manage project teams and deliver on high priority projects related to temporal and spatial price indexes.

Advanced knowledge of the methodologies related to the highly specialized fields, such as big data in order to performed detailed analysis and assess new methods relevant to temporal and spatial price indexes.

Knowledge of quantitative analytical methods is required to integrate and interpret massive volumes of data within the context of temporal and spatial price index programs and to provide technical advice to other professionals.
Writing and editing skills to write papers, articles and reports and to determine and assess the design and content of studies, articles and reports that will be disseminated widely or published.
Contextual knowledge: Advanced knowledge of international frameworks (Canadian System of Macroeconomic Accounts, Prices, etc.), their conceptual building blocks and their interdependencies to contribute in a meaningful way to the evaluation and impact assessment of concepts and compilation methods within the realm of temporal and spatial price indexes.

Knowledge of divisional mandate, policies, priorities, practices, standards and procedures as well as existing databases and conceptual frameworks applicable to the work to incorporate them into the conduct and management of analytical and development projects and to determine or recommend changes.

Knowledge of STC mandate, policies, priorities, practices and classification systems as well as existing data bases, conceptual frameworks, and the statistical methods and procedures applicable to the work, to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of statistical projects and activities, and in the elaboration of recommendations for change to the program.

Knowledge of current and emerging economic issues in Canada and internationally as they relate to temporal and spatial price indexes, to understand needs for new data, analyze the data and assess their impact on the work of Consumer Prices Division and share expertise internally and/or with international organizations.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent legislation such as the Foreign Service Directives, and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements to other departments (e.g., Bank of Canada, Finance Canada, Treasury Board Secretariat), agencies, industry, members of the public and the media. Knowledge of the Statistics Act and Privacy Acts is particularly important with respect to the security and confidentiality of information and data provided and to ensure that they and their subordinates do not release any information which may identify an individual or group without prior consent, and to apply within the context of establishing big data applications for use in the temporal and spatial price index programs.

Knowledge of the uses of temporal and spatial indexes within the mandates and legislation of other federal organizations such as the Bank of Canada, Finance Canada and Treasury Board Secretariat. This knowledge is important so that proposed changes to the temporal and spatial index programs can be assessed to ensure that outputs continue to meet the legislated requirements and mandates of stakeholders without negative impacts on those uses.
Research and analysis: Investigates and assesses changes in the statistical needs of clients, determines the extent and approaches of surveys or studies such as the sources of information, statistical techniques, methods and approaches to be used for the collection, processing, analysis and dissemination of price index data. Modifies existing techniques, methods and approaches or develops new ones to meet specific needs.

Investigates and challenges existing conceptual frameworks from multiple disciplines and examines multiple variables from distinct sources within the realm of temporal and spatial price indexes to reach new conclusions or generate new solutions. Researches cutting-edge applications of new data sources, including those related to big data to make recommendations on changes to the program. Recommendations made result from work which is evaluated through the lenses of conceptual integrity, operational viability and a deep understanding of the needs of key users for applying the data for indexing and monetary policy purposes.

Evaluates various data sources for relevance and accuracy when integrating them into the statistical program data. Continuously researches and evaluates new data sources in order to maintain the program's relevance and accuracy.

Interprets the relative quality of data produced, determines reasons for variances, its comparability over time and its relevance in light of changing requirements, trends, developments, policy issues and economic conditions. It is necessary to understand and interpret present policy issues and the economic conditions of Canadians.

key_activities: Plans and directs economic, financial and/or socio-economic studies and research and develops new methods and models to produce, evaluate, analyse, present and extend the application of divisional statistics and prepares, edits and evaluates analytical material for publication purposes.

Performs detailed analysis, evaluation and review of statistical methods and concepts to improve existing data and determines changes in the statistical needs of clients, assessing the impact on divisional programs and developing options and strategies to manage complex issues and multi-stakeholder relations.
Supervises a unit or multi-disciplinary project teams responsible for statistical research projects and studies; manages the financial resources attached to each project.
Represents departmental interests when presenting analytical research and modelling studies to a variety of stakeholders.

1. Decision making: Plans and directs economic, financial and/or socio-economic studies and research covering multiple areas, industrial sectors, population segments or geographical areas.

Assesses client requirements for statistical information; recommends the conduct of special studies; defines project objectives and scope; selects and evaluates research standards and techniques to be used in the conduct of studies and in the reporting of findings as well as the analytical techniques and quantitative analytical methods to be used to integrate and interpret massive volumes of data.
Determines priorities for specific studies and provides expert advice and recommendations to senior management on the significant issues affecting the sector’s policies and programs.
Develops modifications to program content and coverage and devises new methods and models to produce, evaluate, analyze, present and extend the application of divisional statistics.
Conducts comprehensive research and analysis into socio-economic policy issues and recommends the development of policies, strategies and program proposals of concern to the Sector.

Communication: Chairs meetings with professionals from research groups, other departments or levels of government to discuss current trends and developments, to acquire up-to-date knowledge of results, regulations and policies relating to socio-economic programs, and to develop consensus on the significant issues and priorities affecting the sector’s policies and programs.

Provides expert advice and recommendations to senior management on the significant issues affecting the sector’s policies and programs and submits program proposals and initiatives addressing the areas of concern to the Sector.

Interprets and adapts complex statistical data and information to provide decision-makers at all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academics with expertise leading to decision making regarding a vast array of economic and social policies, programs and initiatives
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: In-depth knowledge of economic or sociology principles and theories as they relate to a specialized area to plan the conduct of comprehensive research and analysis into socio-economic policy issues and to recommend the development of policies, strategies and program proposals of concern to the Sector.

Knowledge of advanced statistical theories, methods, concepts and practices which are used in the development, collection, processing, analysis, marketing and dissemination of statistical data, in order to plan, develop, direct and undertake a research program.
Knowledge of quantitative analytical methods to integrate and interpret massive volumes of data and to provide technical advice to other professionals.
Writing and editing skills to write papers, articles and reports and to determine and assess the design and content of studies, articles and reports that will be disseminated widely or published.

Knowledge of methods, techniques and practices related to project management, human resources and financial management in order to plan projects/studies, manage staff, (either directly or within a matrix management environment) and administer a budget.

implicated_work_descriptions.justification: A third meaningful relationship is integrating data. Evidence includes managing studies that 'select and evaluate analytical techniques and methods to be used to integrate and interpret massive volumes of data', evaluating multiple data sources for integration into the statistical program, and developing approaches for big data use within consumer price indexes. This is weaker than 2.5 because the role appears to design and govern integration methods more than execute routine operational integration, but integration remains materially embedded in the work. Future drivers such as integrated data pipelines, enterprise data platforms, linked and alternative data, and efficiency pressures will likely push the role toward more standardized, automated and reusable multi-source integration methods for price index production.

gsbpm_description: This sub-process examines data to identify potential problems, errors and discrepancies such as outliers, item non-response, miscoding and duplicate records. It can also be referred to as input data validation. It may be run iteratively, validating data against pre-defined edit rules, usually in a set order. It may flag data for automatic or manual inspection or editing. Reviewing and validating can apply to data from any type of source, before and after integration, as well as imputed data from sub-process 5.4 (Edit and impute). Whilst validation is treated as part of the Process phase, in practice, some elements of validation may occur alongside collection activities, particularly for approaches such as computer assisted collection. Whilst this sub-process is concerned with detection and localisation of actual or potential errors, any correction activities that actually change the data is done in sub-process 5.4 (Edit and impute).

Responds to requests from subject matter specialists and clients for custom tabulations and liaises with survey officers, respondents and data users to understand and obtain clarifications on concepts, data collection and processing requirements.
Explains requirements and procedures for obtaining the information in the appropriate format.
Responds to inquiries from managers, employees and the general public on the availability, consistency and application of statistical data and on the methods and techniques used.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of the methods, techniques and practices required for the collection, capture, processing, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data.
Knowledge of statistical survey concepts and quantitative analytical techniques involved in the development, conduct and monitoring of statistical programs.

Knowledge of methods and practices of operating personal computers in a network environment and of using databases and software packages (word processing, statistical analysis, graphics, spreadsheets, etc.) to prepare correspondence, reports and presentations.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of a variety of commercial software tools and of customized production applications to regularly process data and/or to produce specified statistical outputs.
Knowledge of automated collection software and data capture applications to test applications and prepare reference material and training for the applications.

Knowledge of divisional mandates, objectives, programs, policies and activities to adhere to the various statistical and administrative practices and procedures involved in the collection, capture, processing, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of statistical data.
Knowledge of program context, program sponsors and participants to identify and resolve specific data production and dissemination issues.

Knowledge of data sources and contacts within STC in order to locate, analyze and compare statistical output to ensure consistency and reliability; and external to STC to obtain collaboration in the provision of statistical information and verify the accuracy of data.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to ensure understanding and application in the collection, capture, processing, editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data. The position must have a particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data to ensure their own actions are in compliance.
6. Research and analysis: Reviews reported data and prepares reports outlining data quality and any problems encountered in the implementation of established guidelines and results.
Compiles data from a number of different but easily identifiable sources to produce statistical tables and charts.

Analyses outputs with other related data sources or by making calculations to ensure no errors exist due to programming and classification of the original data, that it is in an acceptable format, and that the data is reasonable in relation to similar data for other periods.
Reviews user requests to determine the nature, feasibility, and options for providing the information required.
Adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats, depending on the complexity of the subject matter or the number of different sources.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Economist/Sociologist 2
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: Strongest fit because the role directly assesses data quality and validity. Evidence includes 'assesses the timeliness, completeness, accuracy and validity of data compiled for publication,' 'evaluates problems in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical information,' and knowledge of assessing 'the validity of collected and processed data.' This matches review and validation of input and processed data. It is stronger than method design because the role is more operational and supportive in examining quality problems than owning enterprise methodology. Future drivers such as automation, alternative data, and metadata-driven processing will shift the work toward validating more heterogeneous, automated, and linked inputs with stronger use of rules, indicators, and exception handling.

key_activities: Under guidance, participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes.
Identifies statistical trends and developments.

Under guidance, participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.
Provides data and assistance to users, within and outside Statistics Canada.
Under guidance, participates in subject matter studies and reviews to support the work of project teams or senior officers.

1. Decision making: Evaluates problems in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical information to provide solutions or recommendations to management and to resolve subject-matter, conceptual and technical problems.

Prepares special data releases, reviews and verifies data sources and methods of data compilation; develops and implements procedures for the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of data.
Develops and outlines new statistical methods, concepts and procedures or modifies existing techniques and approaches to incorporate changes in subject-matter content and definitions.
Reviews and designs questionnaires for the collection of data and assesses the timeliness, completeness, accuracy and validity of data compiled for publication.
Implements enhancements or modifications to processing systems and applications used to collect, process, edit, compile and present statistical data.
Develops or modifies statistical methods, concepts, definitions and approaches to improve existing surveys or to meet specific needs.
2. Leadership and operational management: Participates in project teams, work groups, meetings and conferences in order to develop and improve work methods and practices, share knowledge and contribute to skill development.

Monitors and tracks time spent on activities for the purposes of recording and recovering such costs from the client. Incurs and accounts for petty cash, credit card, taxi voucher, bus pass, and other expenditures.
3. Communiction: Writes and presents detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify divisional systems and applications.

Writes program information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports for use by colleagues, operational staff and management in the development, implementation and assessment of statistical programs.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of statistical or economic theory and principles and the relevance of their application in a computerized environment, and the methods and techniques of data gathering, statistical estimation and economic modeling.
Knowledge of current and emerging economic and social issues relating to the program area in order to identify and assess trends and issues represented by statistical data series.
Knowledge of methods, techniques, practices and procedures to conduct studies and to develop/assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs.

Knowledge of the socio-economic concepts and methods to assess the validity of collected and processed data, the output from computer applications, the validity of database contents and results from alternative manipulations of data.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of the subject and universe of the survey is required in order to propose suitable changes to statistical or reporting methods and techniques.
Knowledge of program context, program sponsors, participants and respondents to plan and organize the retrieval and processing of data for research or development projects.

Knowledge of the divisional mandate, objectives, programs, policies and activities to adhere to the various statistical and administrative practices and procedures involved in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical data.
Knowledge of data sources within Statistics Canada in order to locate, analyze and compare related statistical output to ensure consistency and reliability

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to ensure understanding and application in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of data. The position must have a particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data to ensure their own actions are in compliance.
6. Research and analysis: Analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services.
Assesses and determines the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored.
Analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Data Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: Review and validate is the second strongest relationship because the role explicitly edits and validates data, reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases, and compiles data from diverse sources to analyze consistency, reliability and appropriateness. This is stronger than more downstream analytical validation because the work focuses directly on data-level quality review and validation in production. Future drivers such as alternative and linked data expansion, AI-assisted validation, and integrated pipelines will change this work toward validating more heterogeneous multi-source inputs and monitoring automated quality checks, increasing needs in exception analysis and source-quality assessment.

key_activities: Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data.
Interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations.
Reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases.
Provides statistical data and consultative services to users.
Participates on data production and dissemination teams.
Provides input to training material and assists in the delivery.

1. Decision making: Assesses trends and developments in the subject area; reviews the potential impact on program subject-matter content and determines the implications for statistical methods and procedures.

Evaluates problems related to the editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of statistical information to provide solutions or recommendations to management and to resolve subject-matter, conceptual and technical problems.
Implements enhancements or modifications to computer systems and applications used to edit, validate, market and disseminate statistical data.
Modifies statistical methods, concepts, definitions and approaches to improve existing surveys or to meet specific new needs and incorporates changes in subject matter content and definitions.
2. Leadership and operational management: Participates in project teams, work groups, meetings and conferences in order to develop and improve work methods and practices, share knowledge and contribute to skill development.

4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of current economic and social issues relating to the program area in order to identify and assess trends and issues represented by statistical data series.
Knowledge of methods, techniques, practices and procedures to prepare information for studies and to review the feasibility and potential impact of new or modified statistical programs.

Knowledge of the socio-economic concepts and methods to assess the validity of collected and processed data, the output from computer applications, the validity of database contents and results from alternative manipulations of data.
Knowledge of quantitative analytical techniques.
Knowledge of analytical software for micro-computers.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of program context, program sponsors, participants and respondents to plan and organize the retrieval and processing of data for research or development projects.

Knowledge of the divisional mandate, objectives, programs, policies and activities to adhere to the various statistical and administrative practices and procedures involved in the editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of statistical data.
Knowledge of data sources within Statistics Canada in order to locate, analyze and compare related statistical output to ensure consistency and reliability.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to ensure understanding and application in the editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data. The position must have a particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data to ensure their own actions are in compliance.
6. Research and analysis: Compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output. Summarizes and describes meaning of data. Analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability and appropriateness.
Analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services.

Examines operational system concepts and methods and new or revised processing specifications, to determine their effect on the integration and co-ordination of the data capture and processing functions with other divisional systems.
Interprets user requests to determine the nature, feasibility, and options for providing the information required.
Adapts data to new definitions or presentation formats, depending on the complexity of the subject matter or the number of different sources.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Supervisor
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: A strong second fit is review and validate. Evidence includes integrating and analyzing outputs, 'reviews/certifies the quality and completeness of the individual program results,' and evaluating the effectiveness of systems and the quality and completeness of outputs. This is stronger than finalising outputs because the emphasis is quality review of program results rather than dissemination readiness. Future drivers will increase the use of automated validation, mixed-source quality checks, metadata validation and exception-based review.

key_activities: Integrates and analyzes statistical outputs and reviews/certifies the quality and completeness of the individual program results.
Develops statistical systems and processes, evaluates the quality of collections’ outputs and prepares analytical reviews.
Evaluates changes in the statistical needs of clients and develops new methods of collecting, coding and processing data.
Provides advice and guidance to users on the development, operation and use of collection systems and processes.
Acts as a divisional data collection and operations representative on projects, task forces or committees in various roles.
Supervises a unit or project team involved in the development of collection procedures and the capture, coding and processing of statistical data.

1. Decision making: Investigates client requirements for statistical information, determines the sources of information, methods and approaches to be used for the collection, capture, coding and processing of data. Modifies existing techniques, methods and approaches or develops new ones to meet specific needs. Each statistical project is unique in nature and decisions impact on other statistical programs.

Defines project objectives and priorities and assesses the requirements to conduct developmental projects; prepares work plans and summaries outlining approaches, time-frames and resources involved in the operation of statistical systems and processes.
Proposes modifications to program content and coverage and operational procedures, such as new or modified data sources, concepts, methods and definitions.

Evaluates the effectiveness of existing and new statistical systems and processes, the quality and completeness of outputs and pepares studies and reports for use by senior management of the division in assessing the attainment of divisional program objectives and the cost, efficiency and utilization of divisional resources.

Develops and distributes guidelines, instructions and procedures for the development, use and evaluation of statistical systems and processes for use by operational and systems staff when planning and performing their work.
Establishes and implements specifications, guidelines and procedures for the maintenance and safeguarding of computer systems, equipment, databases and files.

Develops proposals and recommends changes and improvements on questionnaire design, enhancements or modifications to survey content and coverage, revisions to collection or production systems and processes, and the implementation of new hardware and software to be used in data collection or statistical production activities.
2. Leadership and operational management: Supervises a unit involved in statistical operations and/or leads project teams for special projects. Determines goals, priorities and milestones, sets objectives, and plans and schedules the work, resolves conflicting priorities; identifies human resources needs, determines the appropriate selection methods (internal and external resources / contractors) to meet program or project objectives, recruits staff, evaluates employee performance, develops training plans, motivates and maintains morale of employees.

Plans and budgets for on-going operations and/or special projects, including estimates for salaries, professional fees and implementation costs, with authority to allocate/reallocate funds within the budget. Provides input to budgets based on operational needs and by obtaining/providing cost estimates for personnel, supplies, equipment purchases and travel for use in developing section or division budgets. Establishes and negotiates contracts for projects. Responsible for the acquisition of goods and services, according to the budget allocated.
3. Communication: Provides advice and interpretation to various data users at all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academics, on the practical use and application of statistical data and information. This often requires the adaptation and presentation of complex information in basic, understandable formats. When media representatives and others challenge or misinterpret findings, it is necessary to further explain the results and statistical methods and approaches used in order to maintain the department’s reputation for producing high quality data.
Writes and presents subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify operational systems and processes or explain program results.
Prepares and explains specifications and guidelines to be used by others in developing and operating systems and processes.
Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and groups to develop consensus or share knowledge within the area of operational expertise.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of economic/sociology principles and practices as they relate to a specialized area as well as specific knowledge of the area to initiate and conduct projects to improve existing concepts or to develop new approaches to extend processing systems applications for the collection, capture, coding and processing of statistical data. This knowledge is also required to provide expert advice and guidance to users within and outside Statistics Canada.
Knowledge of statistical theories, methods (including data gathering and analysis techniques), concepts and practices used in the collection, capture, coding and processing of statistical data.
Knowledge of the principles and practices of human and financial resource management is required to manage the work of a multi-disciplinary unit and/or a project team.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of the departmental and divisional mandate, objectives and organization is required in the management of statistical operations.
Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies, practices and classification systems is needed to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of statistical projects and activities.
Knowledge of other statistical programs related to the area of expertise within the department, especially the concepts, methods, and databases used in other divisions.

Knowledge of departmental publication, marketing and dissemination policies and practices in order to establish common divisional policies and practices in the preparation of statistical tables, charts, explanatory notes etc. for dissemination to user and/or subject matter clients.

Knowledge of data suppliers is required to discuss data reporting agreements, as well as knowledge of data users from governments and the private sector to identify potential new markets, to understand client needs for complex statistical data or studies, to negotiate contracts and to provide advice on survey results.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements to data suppliers, users and others with respect to the collection, capture, coding and processing of data. Knowledge of the Statitstics and Privacy Acts is particulary important with respect to the security and confidentiality of information and data provided and to ensure that they and their subordinates do not release any information which may identify an individual or group without prior consent.
6. Research and analysis: Interprets the relative quality of data produced, determines reasons for variances, its comparability over time and its relevancy in light of changing requirements, trends, developments, policy issues and socio-economic conditions.

Reviews and modifies existing operational techniques, methods and approaches or develops new ones to meet specific needs. Operational programs may involve a combination of statistical techniques and methods and the integration of data from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses). Often, the data have often been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts and must be translated into common concepts.

Reviews and resolves gaps and inconsistencies in the collection, capture, coding and processing methods and procedures used, reviews the conceptual framework used and the compatibility with other statistical programs, reviews and resolves technical and conceptual problems referred by staff or project teams.

Analysis is required to understand and interpret user requirements for statistical information and translate them into a concrete, timely and affordable information request. Clients are often uncertain of their data needs and are unfamiliar with statistical options, methods and techniques available.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Production and Database Expert
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: Review and validate is the third strongest relationship because validation and quality assurance are a recurring operational responsibility in the work description. Evidence includes 'coordinates activities ... to process, validate, and disseminate statistical data', 'develops and implements quality-assurance processes for high-impact statistical outputs', 'devises criteria and methods to rectify inconsistencies', and 'research and validation is required to evaluate the effectiveness of the processing systems'. This is stronger than adjacent subprocesses such as edit/impute or finalise data files because the description emphasizes validation rules, inconsistency detection, acceptance criteria and output quality more directly than data correction. Future-state drivers such as AI and automation, alternative and integrated data, metadata-driven processing, and reduced staffing will likely shift this work toward more automated validation, exception-based review, and stronger quality governance for complex multi-source outputs.

key_activities: Innovates and implements the design, evaluation, and applications for the manipulation, storage, and retrieval of high-impact statistical data.

Develops and maintains production and dissemination processes and outputs for analytical databases and provides support for tools and systems for the delivery of high-impact statistical programs, new products, special studies, and ad hoc requests.
Coordinates activities of multiple Statistic Canada divisional partners and other external partners to process, validate, and disseminate statistical data.
Provides specialized expertise and consultative services regarding production systems and processes for ongoing statistical program delivery.
Represents economic subject matter divisions on statistical development projects.
Occasionally leads project teams and undertakes complex technical projects in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems.

Decision Making: Integrates input from multiple economic subject matter areas to develop and maintain complex systems and frameworks for the ongoing production, validation and dissemination of a range of specialized, high-impact statistical outputs.
Operationalizes specialized conceptual and measurement frameworks in the development of production, validation and dissemination systems, processes and databases.

Evaluates alternatives and develops and applies new strategies to maintain and improve operational systems, processes and databases in the production and dissemination of official statistics. Decisions and recommendations regarding data production and dissemination practices impact multiple projects and high-impact statistical programs.
Develops and implements quality-assurance processes for high-impact statistical outputs.

Investigates requirements for statistical information and analysis, defines the nature and scope of special studies, data requirements, and decides the methods and approaches to be used to satisfy complex data requirements. Modifies existing techniques or develops new approaches to meet specific needs.

Defines project objectives and priorities, prepares work plans and summaries outlining approaches, time-frames and resources. Each project is unique in nature and decisions impact on other ongoing studies.
Develops guidelines for the design, evaluation, and testing of processing systems and applications and recommends and implements modifications and improvements to existing procedures.
Recommends and executes solutions to resolve complex technical issues pertaining to data production and dissemination that may lack precedents.
Develops data bases for the provision of time-series information, interprets preliminary results, reviews, and modifies approaches and techniques as necessary.
Reviews and approves detailed processing parameters, devises criteria and methods to rectify inconsistencies, and recommends modifications to ensure the continuity and compatibility of data.
Leadership And Operational Management: Occasionally plans, organizes and functionally coordinates the work of multiple partners within Statistic Canada divisions and units, as well as clients from other federal government departments involved in the conduct of statistical processing, validation and dissemination of specialized statistical outputs. Determines goals, priorities and milestones, sets objectives, plans and schedules the work and resolves conflicting priorities.
Establishes and coordinates schedules for the production, validation and dissemination of regular statistical outputs across multiple production teams.
Coordinates input and specifications from multiple partners to implement specialized solutions according to established production schedules in the context of complex statistical frameworks.
Communication: Provides expert advice and guidance to internal partners on statistical program results, dissemination methods, concepts, and techniques applied and on trends and developments in economic or related data programs. This information is used as input to decision making for a vast array of economic programs and other activities.
Interprets specialized information pertaining to a range of specialized subject matter areas to present arguments and options to clients within and outside the department.

Communicates subject matter concepts and technical definitions to internal contacts and other subject matter experts to explain and clarify current developments, to explain the results of studies, and to resolve differences that can affect the efficiency of the manipulation, storage, and retrieval of data and the quality of outputs.
Specialized knowledge: Advanced knowledge of economic statistical frameworks, principles, and practices as they relate to a specialized subject matter area.

Advanced knowledge of theories, concepts, and principles in statistical measurement, and how they interrelate with at least one specialized economic subject matter area or discipline, is required to design, evaluate, and innovate systems and applications for the production, validation, and dissemination of high-impact statistical outputs. This knowledge is also required to provide subject-matter expertise, advice, and consultative services to Statistic Canada partners, as well as to work with other professionals, in the ongoing production and validation of high-impact statistical data.
In-depth knowledge and mastery in the application of specialized software, such as SAS, for the compilation, validation, and quality assurance of key statistical outputs.
Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of the divisional mandate, activities, priorities, practices, standards and procedures applicable to the work is required to incorporate them into the conduct and management of surveys and complex and technical studies and projects.

Knowledge of the mandate, objectives and organization of Statistics Canada is required to manage subject matter studies, surveys and projects across economic-based divisions. Knowledge of other statistical programs (concepts, methods, and databases) related to the area of expertise is also required to plan and implement statistical activities, to integrate conceptually different data from other programs, to explain variances, and to recommend changes to other statistical programs if necessary.

In-depth knowledge of economics-related subject matter area(s) is required to understand complex data needs from internal and external data users and to deliver expert technical solutions in response to analytical requirements for statistical projects and programs.

Knowledge of departmental publication, marketing and dissemination policies and practices in order to establish common divisional policies and practices in the preparation of statistical tables, charts, explanatory notes etc. for dissemination to user and/or subject matter clients.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies (confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations, data quality), practices and classification systems to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of complex and technical statistical projects and activities.

Knowledge of data suppliers to discuss data reporting agreements. Knowledge of data users from governments and from the private sector is required to identify potential new markets and to understand client needs for complex statistical data or studies.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements to others. Knowledge of the Statistic and Privacy Acts is particularly important with respect to the security and confidentiality of information and data provided and to ensure that they do not release any information which may identify an individual or group without prior consent.
Research and analysis: Interprets the results of tests, procedural investigations, and feasibility studies to produce data bases and data retrieval packages used for the production of integrated statistical information.

Reviews and approves detailed processing parameters, classification, coding systems and report formats or develops new ones to meet specific needs. Some studies may involve a combination of statistical techniques and methods and the integration of data from a wide variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses). Often, the data has been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts and must be translated into common concepts.

Reviews new and revised processing systems and procedures to ensure compatibility with other statistical programs. Assesses technical and conceptual problems and inconsistencies in the manipulation, storage and retrieval of statistical data and develops specifications for new and existing data compilation programs.
Evaluates the impact of technological developments on operation and production procedures and prepares reports recommending appropriate approaches and guidelines.

Research and validation is required to evaluate the effectiveness of the processing systems, to formulate computer systems specifications, to design and create test procedures and acceptance criteria, and to ensure that processing systems yield desired statistical outputs.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Operations Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: The position materially connects to review and validate through stated knowledge of methods and techniques used to verify statistical data and ensure reliability and consistency to specifications, plus analysis of reported data and work results, and contact with respondents or data suppliers to clarify problems or irregularities. The role also evaluates collection and coding methods and results and recommends alternatives, which supports data validation and issue identification. This is stronger than edit/impute or output-focused subprocesses because the description emphasizes detecting and assessing quality issues rather than correcting data or approving releases. Future drivers such as administrative and alternative data expansion, AI-assisted validation, and integrated pipelines will likely increase the need for exception analysis, multi-source validation, and monitoring skills.

key_activities: Participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data.
Evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives.
Provides assistance and advice to users on methods and practices of collection and coding.
Participates on data collection and operations teams.
Provides input to training materials concerning data collection operations and assists in training delivery.

1. Decision making: Evaluates methods, procedures and results of statistical collection, coding and processing operations and recommends alternatives. The surveys worked on can vary in size, complexity and methods.
Prepares and distributes procedures, operational specifications and training for the manual and automated collection, coding and processing of statistical data.
Develops and outlines system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems.
Evaluates and recommends appropriate procedures, software and hardware for the collection, coding and processing of data.
Develops test cases and data from functional specifications and specifies testing approaches for own use and use by other program staff to ensure that computer applications meet requirements.

Prepares reports and recommendations outlining options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection and processing systems.

Contacts data suppliers or respondents to obtain their collaboration in responding to surveys, to clarify problems or irregularities. This may necessitate having to explain technical procedures for obtaining the data in the appropriate format, or to clarify and explain statistical concepts.
Participates in departmental meetings and working groups in order to share knowledge within an area of operational expertise.

Knowledge of the concepts, methods and techniques used in the management and control of statistical collection, coding and processing activities.
Knowledge of methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications.

Knowledge of methods and practices of operating personal computers in a network environment and of using databases and software packages (word processing, statistical analysis, graphics, spreadsheets, etc.) to prepare correspondence, reports and presentations.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows, general software packages and computer languages, for designing the specifications for testing of applications, the application and conversion of databases, and the maintenance and use of databases both for regular production of statistical data and for ad hoc manipulations and retrievals.

Knowledge of developments and changes in the subject area that may affect the efficiency and validity of data collection, coding and processing in order to devise and modify operational systems and processes.

Knowledge of divisional mandates, objectives, programs, policies and activities to adhere to the various statistical and administrative practices and procedures involved in the collection, coding and processing of statistical data.

Knowledge of data sources and contacts within Statistics Canada in order to locate, analyze and compare statistical output to ensure consistency and reliability; and external to Statistics Canada to obtain collaboration in the provision of statistical information and to verify the accuracy of data.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to ensure understanding and application in the collection, coding and processing of data. The position must have a particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data to ensure their own actions are in compliance.
6. Research and analysis: Analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results.
Assesses and reviews system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems.

Analyses reported data and work results and prepares reports for program managers or subject matter specialists, presenting findings on how the survey was conducted, problems encountered in implementing concepts, definitions, classifications and other instructions, and recommending alternatives.

implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This subprocess is relevant because the position works with processing, editing and validation of data, "analyses outputs with other related data sources... to ensure no errors exist," and drafts reports on "data quality and reliability." These are strong indicators of review and validation work on statistical data and outputs. It ranks below 3.5 and 3.2 because the role appears to support validation operationally rather than lead validation methodology design. Future drivers such as automation, metadata-driven processing, and modernized multi-source production will likely increase reliance on automated checks, exception handling, and validation across more complex datasets, changing the role's validation skills requirements.

Creates test data, sets up testing processes, identifies and corrects errors and problems, documents the inputs and presents the results for review.

Applies existing techniques and approaches to incorporate changes in subject-matter content and definitions and selects the appropriate software to be used for the preparation of reports, tables and charts.

Drafts reference and training material for data collection operations.

Responds to requests from subject matter specialists and clients for custom tabulations and liaises with survey officers, respondents and data users to understand and obtain clarifications on concepts, data collection and processing requirements.
Explains requirements and procedures for obtaining the information in the appropriate format.

gsbpm_description: This sub-process derives data for variables and units that are not explicitly provided in the collection, but are needed to deliver the required outputs. It derives new variables by applying arithmetic formulae to one or more of the variables that are already present in the dataset, or applying different model assumptions. This activity may need to be iterative, as some derived variables may themselves be based on other derived variables. It is therefore important to ensure that variables are derived in the correct order. New units may be derived by aggregating or splitting data for collection units, or by various other estimation methods. Examples include deriving households where the collection units are persons or enterprises where the collection units are legal units.

implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This subprocess is relevant because the role writes and presents analytical material to be disseminated, prepares papers and articles on interpretation and methodology, and turns research findings into publishable analytical products. That aligns with preparing draft outputs and accompanying methodological explanation. It ranks below 6.3 because the description emphasizes interpretive and consultative analysis slightly more than draft-output assembly. Future drivers such as timelier outputs, AI-assisted drafting, and metadata-rich dissemination will likely change how quickly and in what formats these draft analytical products must be prepared.

key_activities: Develops and conducts research and modeling studies and writes/edits analytical material for publication purposes.
Provides advice and consultative services to data suppliers and users, and directs staff on the uses and preparation of estimates.
Provides feedback and recommendations for improvement on established statistical programs.
Leads project teams involved in the conduct of analytical research and modeling studies.
Represents the division as an analytical research and modeling specialist in the area of expertise on development projects, task forces and committees.

1. Decision making: Investigates client requirements for statistical information, determines data sources, modifies existing methods and approaches for analytical research and modeling studies or develops new ones to meet specific needs.

Defines project objectives and priorities, prepares work plans and summaries outlining approaches, time-frames and resources. Each project is unique in nature and decisions impact on other ongoing studies.
Develops guidelines, proposals and recommendations for divisional management to improve existing surveys or to initiate new surveys / projects.

Selects and evaluates analytical techniques and quantitative analytical methods to be used to integrate and interpret mass volumes of data. Projects may involve a combination of statistical techniques and methods and the integration of data from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses) collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts and efforts must be made to translate them into common concepts.
2. Leadership and operational management: Manages a unit involved in statistical activities and/or leads multi-disciplinary project teams for special projects. Determines goals, priorities and milestones, sets objectives, and plans and schedules the work, resolves conflicting priorities; identifies human resources needs, determines the appropriate selection methods (internal and external resources / contractors) to meet program or project objectives, recruits staff, evaluates employee performance, develops training plans, motivates and maintains morale of employees.

Plans and budgets for on-going analytical projects and/or special projects, including estimates for salaries, professional fees and implementation costs, with authority to allocate/reallocate funds within the budget. Provides input to budgets based on operational needs and by obtaining/providing cost estimates for personnel, supplies, equipment purchases and travel for use in developing section or division budgets. Establishes and negotiates contracts for projects. Procures goods and services according to approved budget allocations.
3. Communication: Writes and presents analytical material to be disseminated to a target audience ranging from the general public to a specialized audience (e.g. academics). When addressing the general public, explains in clear terms the interpretation of complex data, reasons for variances in the results and the trends derived. When addressing a specialized public, it is also necessary to provide more detailed explanations of statistical and analytical methods and approaches used. When media representatives challenge or misinterpret the results of surveys or projects, it is necessary to further explain the results and statistical methods and approaches used in order to maintain the department’s reputation for producing high quality data.

Provides expertise, advice and interpretation to decision-makers at all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academics, on the practical application and interpretation of statistical data and information. This often requires the adaptation and presentation of complex information in basic, understandable formats. This information is used as input to decision making for a vast array of economic and social policies, programs and other activities.

Presents arguments and options and negotiates resources, timeframes and costs with service providers (e.g. system specialists, regional office staff, survey methodologists, contractors, etc.) and clients within and outside the department.
Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and workgroups to develop consensus or share knowledge within the area of expertise.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of advanced statistical theories, methods (including data gathering and analysis techniques), concepts and practices in order to plan and implement analytical research and modeling studies and to recommend and implement improvements to statistical programs.

Knowledge of economic or sociology principles and theory especially as they relate to a specialized area (e.g. System of National Accounts, Health, Justice, Education, Labor, Prices, Demography, International Trade, Balance of Payments, Environment, etc.). This is necessary to conduct analytical research and modeling studies and to assess the content of articles and reports that will be distributed widely or published.
Knowledge of the theories and principles of management to lead a multi-disciplinary unit or project teams.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of the divisional mandate, activities, priorities, practices, standards and procedures applicable to the work to incorporate them into the conduct and management of analytical projects.

Knowledge of the mandate, objectives and organization of Statistics Canada to manage analytical projects. Knowledge of other statistical programs (concepts, methods, and databases) related to the area of expertise to plan and implement statistical activities, to integrate conceptually different data from other programs, to explain variances and to recommend changes to other statistical programs.

Knowledge of departmental publication, marketing and dissemination policies and practices in order to establish common divisional policies and practices in the preparation of statistical tables, charts, explanatory notes etc. for dissemination to user and/or clients.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies (confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations, data quality), practices and classification systems to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of statistical projects and activities.
Knowledge of the policies and programs, of key client departments, to determine their information requirements and identify analysis opportunities.

Knowledge of data users and suppliers from all levels of government, and the private sector to discuss data reporting agreements; to understand their needs for statistical data or studies, to negotiate contracts and to provide them with expert advice on study or survey results.

Knowledge of current and emerging socio-economic issues in Canada and internationally such as the changing social context and the globalization of markets, particularly as they relate to the area of expertise in a statistical program (e.g. System of National Accounts, Education, Health, Labor, Prices, Demography, International Trade, Balance of Payments, Environment, etc.). This knowledge is required to analyze and interpret the data and assess their impact on the area of specialization. International public and private organizations involved in the area of statistics or in the area of expertise. This is necessary to share information.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements to other departments, agencies, industry, members of the public and the media. Knowledge of the Statitstics and Privacy Acts is particulary important with respect to the security and confidentiality of information and data provided and to ensure that they and their subordinates do not release any information which may identify an individual or group without prior consent.
6. Research and analysis: Analysis is required to understand and interpret user requirements for statistical information and to translate them into a concrete, timely and affordable information request. Determines data requirements and sources, and recommends modifications to the content and coverage of studies, procedures, concepts, methods and definitions.

Writes analytical papers and articles on the interpretation of surveys, statistical applications or project findings, their application to the area of specialization and the methodology used. This information is published and used by specialized groups of interest (e.g. academics, private sector industries , etc.) and Federal and provincial departments for decision / policy making purposes.

Researches gaps and inconsistencies in the collection, processing, analysis and dissemination methods and procedures; reviews the conceptual framework used and the compatibility with other statistical programs; conceptualizes enhancements or proposes modifications to study and/or program content and coverage and operational procedures, such as new or modified data sources, concepts, methods and definitions to be applied. Each project is unique in nature and may involve a combination of statistical techniques and methods and the integration of data from a variety of sources.

Selects and evaluates analytical techniques and methods to be used to integrate and interpret massive volumes of data. Reviews and modifies existing techniques, methods and approaches or develops new ones to meet specific needs. Often, these data come from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses) and have been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts. There is a requirement to integrate data from diverse sources and concepts into a common conceptual framework and to identify and measure complex and subtle relationships among variables to produce statistical information.

Interprets the relative quality of data produced, determines reasons for variances, its comparability over time and its relevancy in light of changing requirements, trends, developments, policy issues and socio-economic conditions.

gsbpm_description: This sub-process is where statisticians validate the outputs produced, in accordance with a general quality framework and with expectations and also comparing with auxiliary information available (e.g. from previous cycles or from other sources). This sub-process may include activities involved with the gathering of intelligence, with the cumulative effect of building up a body of knowledge about a specific statistical domain, in order to check for errors and validate the data as objectively as possible. This knowledge is then applied to the current collection, in the current environment, to identify any divergence from expectations and to allow informed analyses. Validation activities can include: Comparing the statistics with previous cycles (if applicable); Checking that the associated metadata, paradata and quality indicators are present and in line with expectations; Checking geospatial consistency of the data; Confronting the statistics against other relevant data (both internal and external); Investigating inconsistencies in the statistics; Performing macro editing; Checking aggregates as a validation for a microdata set; Validating the statistics against expectations and domain intelligence.

Recommends new research priorities and initiatives to senior management; reviews strategic directions for the management of significant research studies, recommends innovative solutions to address departmental goals and objectives and approves analytical material and research papers for publication.
2. Leadership and operational management: Directs the work of multi-disciplinary, departmental and interdepartmental project teams, working groups and committees involved in significant research and analytical activities.

Develops plans and objectives and allocates human and financial resources to ensure that these goals are met. Directs recruitment activities, identifies experience and knowledge requirements and selects project staff. Prepares performance appraisals for subordinate staff and resolves performance and disciplinary matters.
Negotiates and approves contracts with consulting firms. Selects contractors for specific projects. Assigns, directs, manages and evaluates the work according to contract specifications.
3. Communication: As a departmental expert, provides advice and recommendations to senior officials within and outside Statistics Canada on the results of unique economic and socio-economic studies and their impact on major program or regulatory issues.

Defends proposals for the development of new research initiatives to address current socio-economic trends and developments at the national and international levels, and negotiates the allocation of funding for the conduct of such studies and projects.

Represents the department in discussions where consensus must be achieved on major issues which impact the programs and/or policies of other government departments, industries and special interest groups. Writing skills to prepare and review research papers, articles and reports and to determine and assess the design and content of studies, articles and reports that will be disseminated widely or published.
Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and groups to develop consensus or share knowledge in a particular field.
Represents the federal government and broad Canadian interests while presenting options and strategies to develop research studies on complex policy issues of interest to a variety of stakeholders.

Knowledge of specialized fields: Expert knowledge of advanced economic or sociologic theories and principles relating to a specialized subject area to provide authoritative and expert advice to senior officials and policy advisors within and outside Statistics Canada on the results of unique economic and socio-economic studies and their impact on major program, policy or regulatory issues.

A deep understanding of the underlying theoretical concepts of economics, sociology and statistics as they relate to a group of specialized areas to develop and implement programs to produce statistics covering a wide range of issues.

Knowledge of writing and editing skills and techniques to write and review research papers, articles and reports and to determine and assess the design and content of studies, articles and reports that will be disseminated widely or published.

Knowledge of the principles and practices of management with regards to human and financial resources in order to direct the work multi-disciplinary departmental and interdepartmental project teams, working groups and committees.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of current and emerging socio-economic and political issues in Canada in relation to that of other industrialized countries such as the changed social context and the globalization of markets, as they relate to all the aspects of a variety of statistical programs.
