Knowledge of governmental policies, programs and regulatory issues in order to provide expert advice to senior officials and policy advisors, within and outside Statistics Canada, on the results and impact of unique economic and socio-economic studies.
Knowledge of the Department’s strategic direction, goals and objectives, is required in order to contribute to their development.

Knowledge of the division mandate and priorities as well as subject-matter expertise in order to review strategic directions in the management of significant research studies, and to recommend innovative solutions to address departmental goals and objectives.

Knowledge of the policies and programs of key client departments in order to mediate with their representatives to reach a consensus on the major issues affecting departments, industries and special interest groups, and to recommend priorities for new research initiatives.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements to other departments, agencies, industry, members of the public and the media. Knowledge of the Statitstics and Privacy Acts is particulary important with respect to the security and confidentiality of information and data provided and to ensure that they and their subordinates do not release any information which may identify an individual or group without prior consent.
Knowledge of a variety of Acts related to the area of expertise such as the Income Tax Act, the Excise Sales Tax Act, the Employment Insurance Act, and the Corporate Returns Act.

Research and analysis: Directs the conduct of high-profile research studies on policy issues impacting on major departmental entities across government, determines the extent of such studies, establishes the overall parameters and objectives, provides expert analysis and interpretation of results, and presents authoritative recommendations to senior executives.

Analyses current socio-economic trends and developments at the national and international levels, determines the implications of proposed areas of study, defends proposals for the development of new research initiatives and negotiates the allocation of funding for the conduct of studies and projects.

Reviews strategic directions for the management of significant research studies, recommends innovative solutions to address departmental goals and objectives and approves analytical material and research papers for publication.
Develops new methods, concepts and definitions to meet the needs of the most unique studies, assesses the implications of new approaches and develops solutions to complex methodology issues.

Analyses the impact of study results on major program, policy and regulatory issues and provides authoritative and expert advice to senior officials and policy advisors within and outside of Statistics Canada.

Provides assistance and subject matter advice to data users within and outside STC.
Undertakes subject matter studies/reviews in support of project teams or senior officers.
Leads project teams involved in special studies.

1. DECISION MAKING: Identifies and assesses changes and developments in the subject area, determines the impact on program subject-matter content and recommends alternative statistical methods and approaches.

Modifies existing techniques and approaches to improve program coverage or to meet specific needs and develops subject-matter concepts and definitions. Develops operational plans and project priorities and identifies areas necessitating study at the local, regional or national levels.

Reviews data collection and information systems to determine the usefulness of the existing data sources, to propose changes to the system and to assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs.

Identifies and evaluates problems in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical information to provide solutions or recommendations to management and to resolve subject-matter, conceptual and technical problems referred by staff.
2. LEADERSHIP AND OPERATIONAL MANAGEMENT: Leads project teams, determines goals, priorities and milestones, sets objectives, and plans and schedules the work, resolves conflicting priorities; assesses human resources needs, recommends the appropriate selection methods (internal and external resources / contractors) to meet program objectives, recruits staff, provides feedback on employee performance, develops training plans, motivates and maintains morale of employees.

Plans and budgets for special projects, including estimates for salaries, professional fees and implementation costs, with authority to allocate funds within budget. Procures goods and services according to approved budget allocations.
3. COMMUNICATION: Provides information and advice to managers, data users and clients on matters relating to subject-matter concepts used in the development and operation of a statistical database and to the data processing environment in general.

Discusses program subject-matter content requirements with operations managers, other subject matter and systems specialists, clients, service providers and others to comprehend and elaborate the framework and conditions within which statistical development and operations will occur. There is a requirement to understand the issues and resolve differences that can affect the efficiency of the division's operations and quality of outputs.

Liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development, to suggest improvements to ongoing programs, to negotiate procedural modifications and to establish project plans, priorities and target dates.
Writes and presents detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify divisional program content and applications.

Writes program information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports for use by colleagues, operational staff and management in the development, implementation and assessment of statistical programs.
4. KNOWLEDGE OF SPECIALIZED FIELDS: A thorough knowledge of the theories and principles of economics, econometric methods and techniques and of sampling theory are required, along with a working knowledge of survey design, time series and special analysis and forecasting.
Knowledge of current or emerging economic and social issues relating to the program area in order to identify and resolve existing and potential subject-matter conflicts, duplication and gaps.

Knowledge of the concepts, methods and techniques used in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical data in order to coordinate and advise on subject-matter development and resolve subject-matter concept and definition issues.

Knowledge of system analysis and design, computer processing, generalized survey software packages to manage the design, development, testing, maintenance and implementation of processing systems; to design specifications for the testing of data, and to maintain and develop databases.
Knowledge of high level programming languages, utility programs or statistical packages to retrieve and manipulate data.
Knowledge of management techniques and principles to manage financial and human resources, either directly or within a matrix management environment.
5. CONTEXTUAL KNOWLEDGE: Knowledge of statistical programs within Statistics Canada related to the area of expertise in order to identify and select sources of information for development and operations and/or special studies and to identify and evaluate data conflicts.

Knowledge of contacts within key client departments to establish a liaison; to understand need for statistical data, and to provide advice and guidance on subject-matter concepts, methods, techniques and results.
Knowledge of the divisional mandate, objectives, priorities, practices, standards, processes and procedures in order to coordinate and manage on-going operational activities and/or special projects.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements to data suppliers, users and others with respect to the manipulation, storage and retrieval of data. Reviews the development of new subject-matter methods, concepts and definitions and conducts studies and analytical projects to improve existing surveys and data.

Analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to determine the need for modification or replacement with alternative systems, methods and procedures.
Interprets program and user needs for statistical information, assesses the suitability of existing data products and services and translates them into a concrete, timely and affordable product.
Reviews the results of projects and surveys in order to provide interpretation and analysis on subject-matter concepts and definitions, survey methods, statistical applications and techniques used.

There may be an occasional requirement to carry equipment, presentation material and document cases to meetings or during travel.

9. WORKING CONDITIONS: The work is performed in an open office environment with constant exposure to glare from a computer screen, noise from conversations, telephones, traffic and equipment in the immediate area.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: International Relations Analyst
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This subprocess is materially related because the position coordinates the preparation and review of briefing notes for the Chief Statistician, ensures quality, seeks revisions where needed, prepares analytical reports and work plans for internal and international stakeholders, and supports the final information products used in international meetings and cooperation activities. The work includes ensuring all necessary approvals are secured before delivery and producing final briefings and reports that are fit for use by senior management and external stakeholders. This is stronger than dissemination-release subprocesses because the emphasis is on finalizing statistical content, supporting information and briefings rather than public release logistics. Future drivers such as Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity may increase pressure for faster finalization of high-quality briefing products, tighter approval cycles, and stronger communication capability to explain emerging international statistical issues and methods.

position_information.branch_division: International Cooperation and Corporate Statistical Methods Division
key_activities: HR A to Z index

1. Decision Making: Analyzes the user requirements for data users of other national statistical offices (NSOs) in order to determine the most appropriate research and comparative analysis studies to do, as well as which sources of information, methods and approaches should be used. Modifies existing techniques or develops new methods such as for the dissemination and communication of statistical information.

As the focal point or project leader, defines project objectives and priorities, prepares work plans and summaries outlining approaches, time-frames and resources. Each project is unique in nature and decisions impact on the timing and scope of product and service delivery to multinational organizations and other national statistical offices. Decisions also affect capacity of Statistics Canada expert communities to continue to perform their regular duties. Recommendations lead to effective and efficient distribution of effort towards international cooperation objectives.

In order to provide advice and consultative services to internal subject matter experts participating in international cooperation projects in statistics, gathers relevant information from various sources (for example different NSOs, multilateral organizations, different ministries participating in the national statistical system of a particular country), performs appropriate analysis and interpretation, considers all possible options, impacts and outcomes, and makes decisions about recommending strategic improvements, involvement of subject matter experts, or impacts on planning and scheduling.

In order to effectively coordinate the preparation of briefing notes for the Chief Statistician attending international meetings, decisions need to be made about which expert community is doing work that best corresponds to each topic on the agenda, which in turn requires up-to-date knowledge of the research and development work going on at Statistics Canada, as well as its regular statistical programs. The position is also responsible for reviewing the briefing notes and seeking clarifications or revisions from the authors if they are deemed to be of insufficient quality.
Scope of decisions relates to coordination with multinational organizations, other National Statistical Offices, and departmental senior management.
2. Leadership And Operational Management: Plans and coordinates the work in support of technical assistance projects for national statistical offices and multilateral (international) organizations. Human resources responsibilities include selecting, coaching and training personnel; planning and assigning work; monitoring and follow-up; developing and implementing work plans and priorities; conducting performance reviews and taking disciplinary action when appropriate; managing through subordinate staff.

Operational management includes recommending resource needs; preparing cost estimates and projections; keeping projects on schedule and within budget; managing an operating budget; monitoring material and financial resources; reallocating resources within a set budget; providing input into financial planning exercises; supervision of staff.

Assists in the allocation of human and financial resources and monitors their usage relative to forecasts. This has a direct positive impact on the statistical processes of the NSO receiving the technical assistance, and ultimately a positive impact on the quality of official statistics globally.
Leads project teams involved in the conduct of technical assistance projects with other National Statistical offices or Statistical Agencies.
3. Communication: Gathers, compiles, analyzes and interprets information and data requests from multilateral (international) organizations, assesses the relevance and impact for Statistics Canada, and determines which expert community or communities should respond. Coordinates the delivery of data and information. Negotiates for deadline extensions or staggered delivery where appropriate. Ensures that all necessary approvals are secured prior to delivery. All correspondence both internal and external is professional, polite, grammatically and factually correct, timely and archived using information management current best practices.

Prepares analytical reports and work plans in the context of international cooperation, to be shared with international stakeholders. Interacts with participating countries and regional stakeholders, providing mutually acceptable solutions to the challenge of simultaneously meeting the needs of multiple stakeholders.

Prepare written reports or supervise staff in the preparation of written reports for internal and international stakeholders, to ensure that they are informed of the progress of statistical capacity building activities being conducted in the course of a large technical assistance project with foreign countries (where capacity building means showing senior managers at other NSOs better ways of planning, managing and executing their statistical programs so that they will bring positive changes to their own organizations).
Makes formal presentations of recommendations, supported by original research, to senior management at Statistics Canada and senior management of other NSOs and international organizations.

Meets with senior management upon their return from multinational events, to gather feedback, status and direction on topics and issues in which Statistics Canada expert communities are involved. Analyzes and interprets this information, and presents it to the expert communities, soliciting their continued contribution and involvement. Researches and provides more background and supporting information for new or emerging topics. Answers questions from the expert communities and ensures that they are in contact with the appropriate parties from other NSOs or multilateral (international) organizations.

The Chief Statistician of Canada attends several international meetings per year at which he actively participates in discussions about emerging issues of global concern (for example global warming or population censuses based solely on administrative data) or international partnerships on the development of new technology (for example how to exploit Big Data). In order to actively participate in these discussions, the Chief Statistician needs detailed and accurate briefing notes from Statistics Canada’s expert communities. Each meeting has approximately 20 different discussion topics. These topics are very briefly described on the meeting agenda, which is made available typically a couple of weeks prior to the meeting. The position analyses the agenda items and recruits the appropriate expert communities to prepare briefing notes. The position supports the expert communities by searching the internet (sites of multilateral organizations such as the UNECE, UNSD, OECD, IMF) for background documentation, coordinating correspondence between Statistics Canada and experts from other NSOs working on similar topics, and providing other relevant information to the experts such as the governance structure of multilateral organizations or briefing notes from other meetings attended by senior managers.

Communicates orally with senior managers of other NSOs and multilateral organizations in a professional manner. Gathers and shares information relevant to the successful participation of Statistics Canada experts in capacity building activities, international working groups or senior manager level steering meetings. Provides written documentation to both Statistics Canada and external stakeholders of recommendations or results of studies or analysis, and progress on on-going activities.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of economic/sociologic principles and practices as they relate to a specialized area as well as specific knowledge of other regions (for example the Caribbean or South America) to initiate and conduct projects to improve existing concepts in other countries or develop new approaches to extend the application of official statistics internationally.
Knowledge of project management concepts, methods and techniques to determine the scope and depth of research and analysis projects for international clients.

Knowledge is required of computer software applications to conduct analysis and document project results, including specialized software such as statistical sampling, computer assisted techniques, automated working papers, and flowcharting.

Knowledge of social science research methods, techniques and practices, including multi-disciplinary analysis methods, to carry out analysis on a variety of approaches regarding the coordination of a national statistical system or improving relations between an NSO and other federal ministries.

Skill in synthesizing information from diverse disciplines (management science, economics, and public policy administration, etc.) to propose solutions that are feasible, reflect current best practices, and are multifaceted, addressing several challenges simultaneously.

Knowledge of theories, principles and techniques of consultation, management, small group process, interviewing and counselling to lead project teams, to negotiate contracts for services and agreements with other institutions.
Operational management requires management skills and knowledge of the theories and principles of general and project management to lead a multi-disciplinary project team.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge is required of the strategic direction, culture, structure and organization, mandate, objectives and relevant policies, procedures and practices of the International Cooperation programs and initiatives. This knowledge is required to achieve operational objectives and results in an effective and efficient manner, and to incorporate them into the conduct and management of studies and projects.

Knowledge of the mandate, objectives and organization of Statistics Canada to manage subject matter studies and projects. Knowledge of other statistical programs (concepts, methods, and databases) related to the area of expertise to plan and implement statistical activities, to integrate conceptually different data from other programs, to explain variances and to recommend improvements to other statistical programs.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements to other departments, agencies and international organizations.

Knowledge of current and emerging socio-economic issues in Canada and internationally such as the changing social context and the globalization of markets, particularly as they relate to the area of expertise in a statistical program (e.g. System of National Accounts, Education, Health, Labour, Prices, Demography, International Trade, Balance of Payments, Environment, etc.). This knowledge is required to provide subject-matter advice, consultative services and to analyze and interpret data requests and assess their impact on the area of specialization.

Knowledge of other countries’ national statistical offices, multilateral (international) organizations (International Statistical Agencies) and non-government organizations in order to effectively communicate on approaches, methods, data and analysis for the purpose of strengthening statistical reporting.
6. Research and analysis: Analysis is required to understand and interpret requests for statistical information and to translate them into a concrete, timely and affordable information request.
Research gaps and overlaps in Statistics Canada’s involvement in international activities, and propose to senior management a strategic approach to achieving effective and efficient collaboration.
Conducts research and comparative analysis on statistical products of different national statistical offices in order to recommend areas of improvement.

Conducts research and comparative analysis of international contexts and statistical processes in order to recommend how Statistics Canada will respond and prepares and edits analytical reports, including recommendations for improving efficiency or effectiveness.

Analysis is required to understand and interpret user requirements for statistical information and to translate them into concrete and timely research studies. Conducts research and comparative analysis on topics such as but not limited to: statistical products of different national statistical offices; data and information requests from multilateral (international) organizations; the scope and depth of involvement of internal subject matter experts in international activities. From this research and comparative analysis, prepares and edits analytical reports, including recommendations for improving efficiency or effectiveness, and shares these reports with both internal and international stakeholders. At the outset clients are often uncertain of their data needs and are unfamiliar with options, methods and techniques available.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Unit Head, Subject Matter
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: The role also materially fits finalise outputs because it 'prepares, edits and evaluates analytical material for publication purposes,' comments on written material to be published, and writes analytical material for dissemination to general and specialized audiences. This is stronger than dissemination production because the focus is on content quality and readiness rather than assembling products. Future drivers will increase the need for caveats, technical notes, uncertainty communication and metadata around modernized methods and source integration.

key_activities: Plans, develops and directs the analysis, review and presentation of program results; coordinates and reviews the development, processing, analysis, marketing and dissemination of statistical data; prepares, edits and evaluates analytical material for publication purposes.
Plans, manages and coordinates economic, financial and/or socio-economic studies and develops new methods to produce, evaluate, analyze, present and extend the application of divisional statistics.
Determines changes in the statistical needs of clients; assesses the impact on divisional programs; develops options and strategies to manage complex issues and multi-stakeholder relations.

Provides expert advisory and consultative services to data users (e.g. academics, policy makers, international bodies, etc.) on the results of surveys and studies, survey concepts and methods, and economic / social science theories and principles.
Represents subject-matter divisions on development projects, task forces or committees in various roles such as Project Manager, Task Manager and Task Force Leader.

Supervises a unit and multi-disciplinary project teams responsible for significant multi-sectoral and inter-departmental files/issues; manages the financial resources attached to each statistical program.

1. DECISION MAKING: Assesses the policies and programs of key client departments to determine their requirements for statistical information and recommends, for approval, those studies that should be conducted.
Recommends plans to improve and expand the content and direction of existing studies as well as the development of policies, strategies and program proposals of concern to the sector.

Defines the objectives and content of the studies and the overall approach to be followed; determines the standards, data concepts, definitions and techniques to be applied in the development and conduct of studies and in the reporting, analysis and presentation of findings.

Interprets study findings and conclusions and prepares recommendations and advice to senior management on current trends affecting the Sector policies and programs and on the significant factors related to the changing environment.

Develops enhancements and recommends modifications to be made to the program content, coverage and operational procedures, such as new or modified data sources, concepts, methods and definitions to be applied.
Investigates client requirements for statistical information and determines the capacity and ability of existing or modified program activities to meet these requirements.

Provides input to management decisions and recommendations designed to develop or improve departmental policies and develops new program initiatives covering areas such as recruitment, official languages, employment equity, dissemination and confidentiality of information.
2. LEADERSHIP AND OPERATIONAL MANAGEMENT: Manages a unit involved in the conduct of economic, financial and/or socio-economic studies and research and leads project teams for special projects. Determines program objectives and priorities and assesses the requirements of the program. Plans and schedules the work, resolves conflicting priorities, ascertains human resource needs, determines the appropriate selection methods (internal and external resources / contractors) to meet program and project objectives, recruits staff, evaluates employee performance or reviews performance evaluations prepared by subordinates and approves training plans.

Plans, develops and manages a budget for the unit in accordance with departmental policy and procedures. Exercises direct authority and accountability for allocated funds to meet planned objectives. Authorises, commits and approves expenditures in accordance with approved budgets with the authority to reallocate funds among line objects.

Negotiates and arranges contracts with consulting firms and for the acquisition of services. Selects contractors for specific projects, assigns, directs, manages and evaluates the work according to contract specifications. Negotiates with suppliers for cost reductions/discounts.
3. COMMUNICATION: Provides expert advisory and consultative services to policy makers at all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academics and presents rationale on the practical application and interpretation of statistical data and information. This information is used as input to decision making for a vast array of economic and social policies, programs and other activities.

Writes and presents analytical material to be disseminated to a target audience ranging from the general public to a specialized audience (e.g. academics). When media representatives and others challenge or misinterpret findings, it is necessary to present logical arguments to justify the results and to defend the validity of statistical methods and approaches used in order to maintain the department’s reputation for producing high quality data.
Provides expert advice to STC and other professionals from the private sector or from other statistical agencies on statistical program findings and their application to the area of specialization.

Provides guidance to subordinate staff, other professionals and management on study results, on methods of socio-economic analysis, dissemination, or on statistical techniques and systems; comments on written material to be published by STC.
Negotiates agreements and arranges contracts with consulting firms and suppliers for the acquisition of services.
Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and groups to develop understanding, consensus and share knowledge of the program area.
4. KNOWLEDGE OF SPECIALIZED FIELDS: Knowledge of economic or sociology principles and theory to provide expert advisory and consultative services to clients on program results and on the concepts and methods used in the collection, compilation, analysis, presentation and interpretation of findings.

Extensive knowledge of current and emerging socio-economic issues in Canada and internationally such as the changing social context and the globalization of markets, particularly as they relate to all aspects of a statistical program. This knowledge is required to analyze program outputs, anticipate and understand needs for new data, and assess the impact on the area of specialization.

Knowledge of advanced statistical theories, methods (including data gathering and analysis techniques), concepts and practices used in the development, collection, compilation, analysis and interpretation of statistical data.

Management and coordination skills and knowledge of general and project management methods, techniques and practices to manage and coordinate the activities of a multi-disciplinary sub-division/operational area and supporting project teams.
5. CONTEXTUAL KNOWLEDGE: Knowledge of the divisional mandate, activities, priorities, practices, standards and procedures applicable to the work to incorporate them into the management of a statistical program to recommend changes to management.
Knowledge of the mandate, objectives, organization, practices, policies, culture and priorities of Statistics Canada to define the objectives and content of studies.
Knowledge of other statistical programs related to the area of expertise within the department, especially the concepts, methods, and databases used in other divisions.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies (e.g. confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations, data quality), practices and classification systems to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of studies.
Knowledge of the policies and programs of key client departments in order to determine their information requirements.

Knowledge of data users from governments and from the private sector to identify potential new markets, to understand client needs for statistical data or studies, to negotiate contracts and to provide expert advice on study results.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to explain legislative and policy requirements to other departments, agencies, industry, members of the public and the media. Knowledge of the Statitstics and Privacy Acts is particulary important with respect to the security and confidentiality of information and data provided and to ensure that they and their subordinates do not release any information which may identify an individual or group without prior consent.
6. RESEARCH AND ANALYSIS: Reviews the conceptual framework of existing statistical programs and determines the need for development, modification and adaption. Programs involve a combination of statistical techniques and methods and the integration of data from a variety of sources (e.g. financial statements, tax files, other administrative sources, surveys, censuses). Source data have often been collected for other purposes using different definitions or concepts and must be translated into common concepts, taking into consideration the impact of the results on other statistical programs as well as departmental priorities.

Assesses and reviews statistical techniques, methods and approaches used in the collection, processing, analysis and dissemination of data within a program area (e.g. System of National Accounts, Demography, Health, Justice, Education, Labour, Prices, International Trade, Balance of Payments, Environment, etc.). Program areas are often unique in nature and involve different collection, processing, analysis and dissemination activities conducted concurrently.
Analyzes the results and findings of studies conducted by in-house analysts and consultants and provides senior management with interpretation and recommendations affecting social policy issues.

Researches gaps and inconsistencies in the collection, processing, analysis and dissemination methods and procedures used; reviews the conceptual framework used and the compatibility with other statistical programs. Problems to be resolved usually impact on other statistical programs.

Analysis is required to understand and interpret user needs for statistical information and to translate them into a timely and affordable information request. Clients are often uncertain of their data needs and are unfamiliar with statistical options, methods and techniques available.

gsbpm_description: This sub-process manages the update of systems (e.g. databases) where data and metadata are stored ready for dissemination purposes, including: Formatting data and metadata ready to be put into output systems; Loading data and metadata into output systems; Ensuring data are linked to the relevant metadata. Formatting, loading and linking of metadata should preferably mostly take place in earlier phases, but this sub-process includes a final check that all of the necessary metadata are in place ready for dissemination.

drivers.driver: AI and Automation in Statistical Production
workforce_implications: agency staff will integrate AI assistants into their daily work to increase efficiency
clarify handoffs across programs
developing skills to support the adoption of modern, open-source technologies and AI
enhancing executives' skills in all areas, from AI upskilling and strengthening leadership competencies, to promoting their change leadership capacity
extensive coordination across the agency's collection, communications, analysis and dissemination teams
involve the recruitment of thousands of employees—including enumerators who conduct in-person data collection
reduce manual effort
requires extensive preparation to ensure that Statistics Canada's infrastructure, systems and workforce ready to deliver Canada's largest statistical undertaking
work embedded directly into production workflows
drivers.impact: Updating output systems is materially affected because automated dissemination pipelines and enterprise platforms increase the importance of standardized loading, metadata linkage, and controlled system updates for scalable release operations.
impact_mechanisms: automation supports routine loading and updating of dissemination systems
enterprise platforms and shared solutions standardize output system operations across programs
documentation and transparency increase the importance of complete metadata linkage
data security and governance shape controlled updates to dissemination environments

drivers.driver: Administrative, Alternative and Linked Data Expansion
workforce_implications: collection, analysis and dissemination workload
parallel census operations across the agency
provide employees with the tools and training they need
support a skilled and adaptable workforce
drivers.impact: Output systems are materially affected because dissemination databases must store and expose richer metadata about source composition, linkage, quality and geospatial content. The driver also increases the need to maintain explicit links between outputs and methodological metadata for mixed-source products.
impact_mechanisms: administrative data and alternative data require richer source metadata in dissemination systems
data linkages require metadata linking outputs to linkage methods and quality information
gridded data increases geospatial metadata requirements
collection, analysis and dissemination workload shifts increase metadata management demands

drivers.driver: Cyber Security, Privacy and Secure Access
drivers.impact: Output systems are materially affected because dissemination-ready stores must be securely updated and managed, with metadata and data linked in ways that preserve confidentiality and support controlled access. This is especially important for modern digital dissemination platforms.
impact_mechanisms: platforms affect how dissemination databases and services are secured and updated
cyber security requirements shape protected loading and storage of dissemination-ready data and metadata
privacy requirements influence what metadata and data can be exposed together
secure access and authorizations affect controls on who can update and access output systems

drivers.driver: Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure
technology_themes: scalable, secure and sustainable digital infrastructure
workforce_implications: empower employees to access the IT systems and resources they need, when they need them
extensive coordination across the agency's collection, communications, analysis and dissemination teams
involve the recruitment of thousands of employees—including enumerators who conduct in-person data collection
make it easier for employees to locate, analyze and use the data and tools they need
make it easier for employees to locate, analyze and use the data and tools they need to deliver results efficiently
providing robust information technology (IT) infrastructure, advanced IT tools and strengthened cyber security
requires extensive preparation to ensure that Statistics Canada's infrastructure, systems and workforce ready to deliver Canada's largest statistical undertaking
self-serve platforms will also empower employees to access the IT systems and resources they need, when they need them
supports digital readiness and modern infrastructure for employees
drivers.impact: Updating output systems is materially affected because dissemination repositories are increasingly enterprise platforms or cloud-hosted systems that require standardized loading, metadata linkage, access controls and scalable storage patterns.
impact_mechanisms: Cloud, platforms and data platforms change the target systems used for dissemination-ready storage
Centralized data repository supports standardized metadata linkage and loading processes
Secure access, authorizations, privacy and data security affect how dissemination systems are updated and controlled
Capability themes of data accessibility and usability and faster delivery support more streamlined output-system updates

drivers.driver: Integrated Data Pipelines and Process Orchestration
capability_themes: Automated monitoring and control of production flow
Coordinated execution across collection, processing, analysis and dissemination
workforce_implications: Shift from manual step execution to pipeline supervision
Greater need for workflow configuration and orchestration skills
Greater emphasis on exception handling rather than routine processing
Need for cross-functional coordination across production stages
Increased operational responsibility for monitoring automated end-to-end runs
drivers.impact: This subprocess is strongly affected because dissemination systems become downstream nodes in integrated pipelines, receiving automated data and metadata loads from prior stages with minimal manual intervention.
impact_mechanisms: Integrated data pipelines connect analysis outputs directly to dissemination storage and delivery systems
Automated handoffs across production stages reduce manual loading and linking activities
Event-driven workflows can trigger dissemination system updates once outputs are approved
Staff roles shift toward monitoring automated publication readiness and resolving metadata or load exceptions

drivers.driver: Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability
drivers.impact: This subprocess is directly and strongly affected because the driver is fundamentally about metadata-rich, searchable, standardized assets. Updating output systems must ensure metadata are formatted, loaded, linked and ready to support discovery and reuse.
impact_mechanisms: Metadata-rich repositories require robust loading and linking of data to relevant metadata in dissemination systems.
Searchable access depends on metadata being formatted and stored in ways that support indexing and retrieval.
Standardized assets require consistent metadata structures across output systems.
The driver makes the final metadata readiness check a critical dissemination control.

drivers.driver: Modular Architecture, Reusable Components and Self-Service Development
capability_themes: capacity required to support solutions over time
workforce_implications: Teams will be supported as they continue to adopt open‑source tools while meeting ongoing production responsibilities
greater emphasis on validation, upskilling and governance
including through training and collaborative development practices
drivers.impact: Output system updates are materially affected because modular dissemination architectures rely on interoperable services, shared metadata components, and standard loading patterns. This shifts work toward governed configuration and integration of reusable output services.
impact_mechanisms: interoperability affects how data and metadata are loaded into modular output systems
shared components and reusable solutions support standard metadata linking and loading services
enterprise architecture constrains output system patterns and interfaces
validation increases final checks that metadata and outputs are correctly linked
secure and stable production environments require controlled updates to dissemination stores and services

drivers.driver: Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment
workforce_implications: decrease of approximately 900 full-time equivalents by 2028-29
flatten management structures
prioritize services and programs, while also finding new efficiencies
drivers.impact: This subprocess is affected through increased emphasis on automated loading and standardized metadata handling to reduce recurring operational effort.
impact_mechanisms: Automation and new tools and methods support lower-touch updating of dissemination systems
Decrease of approximately 900 full-time equivalents by 2028-29 encourages minimizing manual publication system updates

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Library Technician 3
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: The strongest relationship is to updating output systems because the work is centered on maintaining and administering the Library's information systems and associated metadata environment. Evidence includes 'conducts system administration / problem analysis of the integrated library system; manages the Library intranet site and Library wiki,' 'provides problem resolution in the integrated library system which includes adding patches, system upgrades and configuration,' and use of databases to 'create and modify records, to manipulate and extract data and to produce reports.' This aligns directly with managing systems where data and metadata are stored, linked and made ready for access. It is stronger than other subprocesses because the role is not producing statistics or validating outputs; it is operating and improving the information system infrastructure that supports storage, formatting, linking and access to information products. Future drivers such as Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and AI/automation would likely change the work through more platform administration, metadata linkage, system integration, secure updates, and support for searchable, reusable assets.

position_information.branch_division: Communications and Information Services/ Communications and Library Services
key_activities: Acquires the full range of print, non-print and electronic information resources for the Library and the department and maintains all related files.
Participates in collection development activities, including planning, information audits, product evaluation and usage reports.
Conducts system administration / problem analysis of the integrated library system; manages the Library intranet site and Library wiki.
Provides problem resolution in the integrated library system which includes adding patches, system upgrades and configuration.
Leads project teams involved in the provision of library services and products.
Trains Library staff on integrated library system functionalities.

1. DECISION MAKING: Recommends and implements changes to procedures, guidelines and other administrative and technical material for use by departmental staff or clients.
Recommends the development or modification of operational area working tools.
Resolves current issues requiring the application of procedures and precedents.
Determines the appropriate course of action when troubleshooting problems with the integrated library system.
Recommends improvements to library services to the supervisor or section head in his/her working role or as a member of a library committee and/or project team.
2. LEADERSHIP AND OPERATIONAL MANAGEMENT: Assists the unit head and/or section chief in the planning and establishment of goals, priorities and training plans; and in staffing activities and employee performance reviews.
Provides guidance, coaching and orientation to co-workers and new staff and reviews the work of staff and colleagues.
Conducts training for staff and clients on standards, policies, workplace procedures and practices and the integrated library system.

Chairs and participates in working groups and project teams for special projects both internal and external to the Library. Assists in the establishment of goals, priorities and schedules; monitors and reports on progress.
3. COMMUNICATION: Responds to requests from federal government employees, clients or colleagues, using language that is easily understood, whether orally or in writing.

Requests input, information or approval of existing information from internal clients, vendors and employees in other federal government departments, using language that is clearly understood, whether orally or in writing.
Prepares reports (including financial and usage) for a range of clients both internal and external to the Library in response to requests for information.
Prepares and delivers reports to library management for analysis and decision making.
Writes information products, draft procedures, correspondence, reports, training material and memoranda for clients, colleagues and management.
4. KNOWLEDGE OF SPECIALIZED FIELDS: Knowledge of the practices, techniques and standards (e.g., Anglo-American Cataloguing Rules, 2nd edition, MAchine Readable Cataloguing) related to a specialized area within the Library in order to provide services and/or products.

Knowledge of accounting techniques and financial procedures (e.g., commitment of funds, pre‑payment, deposit accounts, group orders, discounts) to manage an acquisitions budget (e.g., track expenditures, compare estimated and actual prices, estimate budget surpluses and deficits) and to choose vendors and process orders.

Knowledge of basic UNIX, Perl scripting language, API programming and HTML coding to correct problems that occur with the integrated library system and to develop/make improvements/enhancements to the system.
Knowledge of automated library systems to evaluate, test, implement, assess system requirements, to provide input for Requests for Proposals and maintain the integrated library system.
Writing and presentation skills are required to deliver training or instruction to clients and staff.
5. CONTEXTUAL KNOWLEDGE: Knowledge of the divisional mandate, activities, priorities, policies, standards, practices, procedures, integrated library system and Statistics Canada’s online catalogue to effectively deliver library services to the library’s clientele, both internal and external to the department.
Knowledge of the role, responsibilities and long term objectives of the department, its organization, programs, and regional activities to understand and fulfill information requirements.
Knowledge of departmentally supported software (e.g., word processing, spreadsheets, communication, Internet) to locate, assess and disseminate information.
Knowledge of the use of databases used within the Library to create and modify records, to manipulate and extract data and to produce reports for departmental clients.

Knowledge of the acts and regulations related to the services of the Library and the department, including but not limited to the Statistics Act, Library and Archives of Canada Act, Copyright Act and Financial Administration Act to provide information to internal and external clients and to comply with audit requirements.

Knowledge of administrative principles, contract management and project management. This knowledge is required to process / manage internal transactions such as journal vouchers and contract renewals.

Knowledge of the information industry and technological trends to improve library services and reduce costs by adapting new technologies, developing new services and/or recommending changes to current practices/policies.
6. RESEARCH AND ANALYSIS: Investigates and resolves problems with the integrated library system (e.g., configuration changes, content management of the Online Public Access Catalogue) by analyzing system information with departmental informatics staff, contractors and vendors.
Analyzes client requests and assesses the resource options, choice of information sources and retrieval result to develop and deliver responses.
Analyzes and organizes data from the integrated library system to develop and deliver reports for library management and departmental clients.
Analyses and provides the appropriate service delivery relative to operational and client needs.
Reviews and provides feedback on the terms of contracts; participates in the selection process; and monitors progress of the work. Reports back to unit head and / or section chief.

Interprets and applies divisional policies and procedures; analyzes them in order to revise or recommend changes. These policies may or may not be clearly defined, but contribute to the audit function and/or affect the delivery of service and access to information of departmental employees, other government employees and the general public.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Development and Evaluation Specialist
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: The strongest relationship is with Update output systems because the role directly plans, coordinates and undertakes the 'production, storage and dissemination of statistical metadata', including preparing metadata for storage and dissemination, and ensuring quality and consistency of metadata disseminated by Statistics Canada. Evidence includes 'plans, prioritizes, coordinates, directs, monitors and undertakes the development and preparation of statistical metadata for storage and dissemination' and repeated references to production, storage and dissemination of metadata. This is stronger than general metadata-related subprocesses because this subprocess explicitly covers formatting, loading and linking metadata into dissemination systems. Future drivers such as metadata-driven data management and discoverability, enterprise digital platforms, and integrated pipelines will most directly change this work through greater emphasis on standardized metadata loading, system interoperability, searchable repositories and automated metadata linkage.

1. Decision Making: Plans, prioritizes, coordinates, directs, monitors and undertakes the development and preparation of statistical metadata for storage and dissemination, reviewing, editing and validating statistical metadata.

Reviews trends and developments in the area of statistical metadata management, liaising with internal and external clients within Canada, in order to determine the need for short-term projects and strategies relevant to the development, enhancement and implementation of methods and procedures used at Statistics Canada for managing statistical metadata; recommending plans to improve methods and procedures; developing specifications for, implementing and testing modifications in methods and procedures; and identifying the impacts and results of new or modified approaches to metadata management.

Directs the development of, evaluates, and approves reports, documentation, procedures manuals and training materials which are related to the production, storage dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata and which are distributed internally and externally within Canada.

Plans, directs and undertakes quality evaluations in accordance with documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines, reviews and certifies the results of quality evaluations undertaken by subordinates and colleagues, compiles results and writes reports for clients and management; and presents results to management.

Provides input to management decisions and recommendations designed to develop or improve departmental, divisional and program initiatives covering areas such as recruitment, training, official languages, wellness, employment equity and information management.

Leadership And Operational Management: Manages a unit involved in activities related to the development and evaluation of statistical metadata and/or leads multi-disciplinary project teams for special metadata projects. Determines goals, priorities and milestones, sets objectives, and plans and schedules the work, resolves conflicting priorities; identifies human resources needs, determines the appropriate selection methods (internal and external resources) to meet program or project objectives, recruits staff, evaluates employee performance, develops training plans, motivates and maintains morale of employees.

Plans and budgets for on-going and/or special projects, including estimates for salaries, professional fees and implementation costs, with authority to allocate/reallocate funds within the budget and in accordance with Statistics Canada’s policies and procedures. Provides input to budgets based on operational needs and by obtaining/providing cost estimates for personnel, supplies, equipment purchases and travel for use in developing section or division budgets. Establishes and negotiates contracts for projects. Responsible for the acquisition of goods and services, according to the budget allocated.

Communication: Provides expert advice and training with respect to the policies, directives, guidelines, methods, procedures and systems used in the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata to subordinates, other statistical metadata specialists, systems specialists, clients and managers who use the information as input to on-going operations and to decisions concerning the management of statistical metadata at Statistics Canada and within other national organizations and agencies.

Liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, systems specialists, clients and managers at Statistics Canada to plan statistical metadata projects and implement short-term strategies for the development and enhancement of policies, procedures and methods used in the management of statistical metadata; to develop and translate strategies and requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata; to establish project plans, priorities and target dates; to negotiate modifications to methods, procedures and timelines; to coordinate and deliver training, and to suggest improvements to methods, procedures and systems.

Writes detailed reports and prepares and delivers presentations which explain rationale, requirements and results relating to policies, directives, guidelines, methods and procedures used in the production, storage and dissemination of statistical metadata and which are used by other statistical metadata specialists, systems specialists, clients, and management in the operation and enhancement of statistical metadata management programs.

Writes reports which describe policy requirements related to the development, production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of high quality metadata, which describe the results of metadata quality evaluations and which make recommendations for procedures and tools that could be developed to evaluate the quality of statistical metadata. These reports are used by clients and management to ensure the quality and consistency of statistical metadata disseminated by Statistics Canada.
Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and workgroups to develop consensus or share knowledge within the area of expertise.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Advanced knowledge of statistical metadata concepts and frameworks used within Canada and internationally and knowledge of how those concepts and frameworks are used and reflected in policies, methods and procedures relating to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata in order to plan, prioritize, coordinate, direct, monitor and undertake the preparation, editing, validation and quality evaluation of statistical metadata and short-term strategies for the enhancement of statistical metadata management processes

Advanced knowledge of methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata and the potential impacts of new or modified methods, procedures and systems on project teams and clients in order to plan, prioritize, coordinate, direct, monitor and undertake statistical metadata projects and short-term strategies for the development, operation and enhancement of statistical metadata management processes; to recommend improvements to methods, procedures and training; to develop procedures and tools for evaluating the quality of statistical metadata; and to explain the results of metadata quality evaluations.

Knowledge of survey and statistical program subject matter concepts, methods and techniques relevant to the collection, processing, certification and dissemination of data in order to evaluate client requirements for metadata production, storage and dissemination; to determine when changes in the needs of clients will impact statistical metadata programs and projects; and to more accurately and efficiently evaluate the quality of statistical metadata across surveys and statistical programs.

Knowledge of management principles, techniques and practices in order to lead a multi-disciplinary project team and manage financial and human resources, either directly or within a matrix management environment. Knowledge of the principles and practices of project management used at Statistics Canada.
Knowledge of software, statistical packages and programming languages used in the production, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata
5. Contextual knowledge: Advanced knowledge of Statistics Canada and Government of Canada policies, directives and guidelines directly and specifically related to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata, as well as other Statistics Canada policies, in order to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of all program activities and in order to explain policy requirements to clients and partners within Canada.

Knowledge of other statistical metadata management programs within Statistics Canada in order to integrate conceptually and structurally the statistical metadata required for various activities and programs.

Advanced knowledge of contacts within key client Divisions in order to establish a liaison; to evaluate and understand program statistical metadata requirements; and to provide expert assistance, advice and direction with respect to policy requirements, methods, procedures, systems, training, priorities and timelines relevant to the production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation of statistical metadata.

Knowledge of surveys and statistical programs within Statistics Canada in order to establish short-term priorities for the processing, storage, dissemination and evaluation of metadata across program areas and to effectively and efficiently direct metadata quality assessment projects, certifying and reporting to management on the overall quality, completeness, coherence and consistency of statistical metadata.

Knowledge of the mandate, objectives, organization, practices, policies, culture and priorities of Statistics Canada in order to ensure that these are reflected in the objectives and management of all statistical metadata projects and short-term strategies for the development and enhancement of statistical metadata management processes and systems, and to explain the context of statistical metadata management at Statistics Canada to clients and partners across Canada.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and Privacy Act is required in order to ensure understanding and application of these Acts in the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata, particularly with respect to the security and confidentiality of statistical metadata and other information; to explain legislative requirements to other departments, agencies, industry, members of the public and the media; and to ensure that Statistics Canada meets its commitment to ensuring confidentiality and does not release any information that identifies an individual or group without prior consent.
6. Research and analysis: Analyses and synthesizes diverse sources of statistical metadata in order to ensure that the quantity and quality of statistical metadata disseminated is optimal for Statistics Canada’s surveys and statistical programs.

Provides expert assistance, advice and direction to internal clients and external clients within Canada with respect to statistical metadata, documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines, determining changes in the needs of clients, assessing the impacts of these changes on statistical metadata programs and projects, and establishing short-term plans and priorities.

Analyses client requirements in order to determine the feasibility, procedural options, priorities, and target dates relevant to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata in order to ensure that approaches and results are consistent within, and across, surveys and statistical programs, and in order to direct and monitor statistical metadata projects and short-term strategies for the development, operation and enhancement of statistical metadata management processes.

Analyzes current production, storage, dissemination and evaluation methods, procedures and systems in comparison to those used elsewhere at Statistics Canada and elsewhere in Canada in order to ascertain their relevancy and to determine the need for modifications or the use of alternative methods, procedures and systems which would result in operational efficiencies and/or improvements in the quality of statistical metadata at Statistics Canada.

Analyzes changes in methods, procedures and systems used to produce, store, disseminate and evaluate the quality of statistical metadata in order to determine the need to update statistical metadata or adapt it to new formats; to determine where updates are required to existing documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals and to prioritize those updates; and to determine and mitigate potential short-term and long-term impacts on clients.

Analyses the quality of statistical metadata produced by surveys and statistical programs at Statistics Canada; evaluates current and proposed methods, procedures and tools for evaluating the quality of statistical metadata in order to develop enhancements; analyses gaps and inconsistencies in metadata quality and suggests possible reasons for variances among program areas; reviews the comparability of metadata over time in light of changing policy requirements, systems functionality and changing methodologies used by statistical programs; provides management with reports of findings.

Knowledge of survey and statistical program subject matter concepts, methods and techniques relevant to the collection, processing, certification and dissemination of data in order to evaluate client requirements for metadata production, storage and dissemination; to implement plans for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata; and to more accurately and efficiently assess the quality of statistical metadata.
Knowledge of management techniques and principles to manage financial and human resources, either directly or within a matrix management environment.
Knowledge of software, statistical packages and programming languages used in the production, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata.

Knowledge of surveys and statistical programs within Statistics Canada in order to locate, analyze and compare related statistical metadata and to identify, evaluate and ensure consistency in the methods of processing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of metadata across programs, identifying and evaluating any conflicts, gaps or duplication of effort.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and of Statistics Canada policies, directives and guidelines in order to ensure understanding and application of the Act and these policies, directives and guidelines in the production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation of statistical metadata.

Analyzes current production, storage, dissemination and evaluation methods, procedures and systems to ascertain their relevancy and to determine the need for changes or alternative methods, procedures and systems which would result in operational efficiencies and/or improvements in the quality of statistical metadata.

Analyzes changes in methods, procedures and systems used to produce, store, disseminate and evaluate the quality of statistical metadata in order to determine the need to update statistical metadata or adapt it to new formats; to determine where updates are required to existing documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals; and to determine potential short-term and long-term impacts on clients.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Development and Evaluation Specialist
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This is the strongest relationship because the role is fundamentally about preparing, validating, storing, linking and disseminating statistical metadata. Future drivers around metadata-driven discoverability, enterprise platforms and reusable dissemination systems will likely increase demand for standardized metadata structures, stronger linkage to dissemination repositories, and platform-based metadata governance skills.

Prepares reports (including financial and usage) for a range of clients both internal and external to the Library in response to requests for information.

Analyzes and organizes data from the integrated library system to develop and deliver reports for library management and departmental clients.
Analyses and provides the appropriate service delivery relative to operational and client needs.
Reviews and provides feedback on the terms of contracts; participates in the selection process; and monitors progress of the work. Reports back to unit head and / or section chief.

Interprets and applies divisional policies and procedures; analyzes them in order to revise or recommend changes. These policies may or may not be clearly defined, but contribute to the audit function and/or affect the delivery of service and access to information of departmental employees, other government employees and the general public.

gsbpm_description: This sub-process produces the dissemination products[14], as previously designed in sub-process 2.1 (Design outputs and dissemination), to meet user needs. They could include publications, press releases and websites. The products can take many forms including interactive graphics, tables, maps, public-use microdata sets, linked open data and downloadable files. Typical steps include: Preparing the product components (explanatory texts, tables, charts, maps, quality statements etc.); Assembling the components into products; Editing the products and checking that they meet publication standards.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Development, Dissemination and Evaluation Coordinator
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This subprocess is materially related because the role is not only about storing metadata but also about dissemination-ready metadata content, including reviewing, editing, validating and ensuring consistency of metadata that support disseminated products. The description emphasizes preparing and approving reports, procedures, manuals and training materials related to metadata dissemination and writing reports used by clients and management to ensure the quality and consistency of metadata disseminated by Statistics Canada. While the role does not appear to own full product release operations, it materially influences the production of dissemination products through the preparation of explanatory, quality-related and metadata content that supports those products. This is weaker than 7.1 because the main responsibility is metadata system and content management rather than assembling end-user products themselves, and weaker than 8.2 because evaluation is explicitly central to the job. Future drivers such as Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, and Workforce Skills Transition and Leadership Capacity will likely increase demand for richer metadata packaging, standardized product support content, and training/documentation for reusable digital dissemination products.

1. Decision Making: Plans, prioritizes, coordinates and undertakes the development and preparation of statistical metadata for storage and dissemination, reviewing, editing and validating statistical metadata.

Evaluates corporate and client metadata requirements, estimates the time required to complete tasks and assesses issues related to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata in order to provide direction to clients and management with respect to possible approaches, priorities, target dates and training needs and to resolve conceptual and technical problems.

Evaluates the methods, procedures and systems used in the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata, determining the need for, recommending, implementing and testing modifications; participates in the development of new specifications; advises clients of changes to methods and procedures; and advises clients and management of potential impacts and results.

Compiles, writes, edits and approves reports, documentation, procedures manuals and training materials which are related to the production, storage dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata and which are distributed internally.

Assesses human resources needs, recommends appropriate selection methods (internal and external resources), recruits staff, determines training requirements and recommends and approves training plans. Monitors and tracks time spent on activities for the purposes of reporting to management and informing planning activities.

Plans and budgets for special projects. Provides input to budgets based on operational needs and by obtaining/providing cost estimates for personnel, supplies, equipment purchases and travel for use in developing section or division budgets.
3. Communication: Provides advice and training with respect to the policies, directives, guidelines, methods, procedures and systems used in the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata to subordinates, other statistical metadata specialists, clients and managers who use the information as input to on-going operations and to decisions concerning the management of statistical metadata at Statistics Canada.

Liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, subject matter specialists, survey managers and management in order to develop and translate requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata; to establish project plans, priorities and target dates; to negotiate modifications to methods, procedures and timelines; to provide training, and to suggest improvements to methods, procedures and systems.

Writes and presents detailed documents, procedures manuals and training manuals which explain, clarify and make recommendations with respect to the methods, procedures and systems used to produce, store and disseminate statistical metadata and which are used by other statistical metadata specialists, systems specialists, clients, and management in the operation and enhancement of statistical metadata management programs.

Writes reports which describe policy requirements related to the development, production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of high quality metadata, which describe the results of metadata quality evaluations and which make recommendations for procedures and tools that could be developed to evaluate the quality of statistical metadata. These reports are used by clients and management to ensure the quality and consistency of statistical metadata disseminated by Statistics Canada.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of statistical metadata concepts and frameworks used within Statistics Canada, the Government of Canada and internationally, and knowledge of how those concepts and frameworks are used and reflected in policies, methods and procedures relating to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata in order to plan, prioritize, coordinate and undertake the preparation, editing, validation and quality evaluation of statistical metadata, to ensure that colleagues and clients understand the importance of adhering to policies, methods and procedures in the preparation, storage and dissemination of metadata and to assess the need for modifications to methods and procedures.

Knowledge of methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata and the potential impacts of new or modified methods, procedures and systems on workloads, outputs and clients in order to establish project plans, priorities, timelines and training plans; to recommend improvements to methods, procedures and training; to participate in the development of procedures and tools for evaluating the quality of statistical metadata and to explain the results of metadata quality evaluations.

Knowledge of survey and statistical program subject matter concepts, methods and techniques relevant to the collection, processing, certification and dissemination of data in order to evaluate client requirements for metadata production, storage and dissemination; to implement plans for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata; and to more accurately and efficiently assess the quality of statistical metadata.
Knowledge of management techniques and principles to manage financial and human resources, either directly or within a matrix management environment.
Knowledge of software, statistical packages and programming languages used in the production, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of policies, directives and guidelines directly and specifically related to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata in order to plan and prioritize the preparation, editing and validation of statistical metadata; to provide assistance, advice, direction, project plans and training to clients; to assist in the development of procedures and tools for evaluating metadata quality; and to effectively undertake evaluations of the quality of statistical metadata.

Knowledge of contacts within key client Divisions in order to establish a liaison, to evaluate and understand program statistical metadata requirements, provide assistance, advice and direction with respect to policy requirements, methods, procedures, systems, training, priorities and timelines relevant to the production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation of statistical metadata.

Knowledge of surveys and statistical programs within Statistics Canada in order to locate, analyze and compare related statistical metadata and to identify, evaluate and ensure consistency in the methods of processing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of metadata across programs, identifying and evaluating any conflicts, gaps or duplication of effort.
