Provides assistance, advice and direction to internal clients with respect to statistical metadata, documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines, negotiating procedural modifications and establishing target dates, project plans and priorities.

Analyzes current production, storage, dissemination and evaluation methods, procedures and systems to ascertain their relevancy and to determine the need for changes or alternative methods, procedures and systems which would result in operational efficiencies and/or improvements in the quality of statistical metadata.

Analyzes changes in methods, procedures and systems used to produce, store, disseminate and evaluate the quality of statistical metadata in order to determine the need to update statistical metadata or adapt it to new formats; to determine where updates are required to existing documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals; and to determine potential short-term and long-term impacts on clients.

Analyzes and evaluates statistical metadata with respect to policy and procedural requirements and consistency across survey and statistical programs. Future-state drivers around metadata-rich assets and reusable digital dissemination will likely increase the need for standardized metadata product components, stronger quality statements and more reusable supporting documentation.

Knowledge of survey and statistical program subject matter concepts, methods and techniques relevant to the collection, processing, certification and dissemination of data in order to evaluate client requirements for metadata production, storage and dissemination; to implement plans for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata; and to more accurately and efficiently assess the quality of statistical metadata.
Knowledge of management techniques and principles to manage financial and human resources, either directly or within a matrix management environment.
Knowledge of software, statistical packages and programming languages used in the production, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of policies, directives and guidelines directly and specifically related to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata in order to plan and prioritize the preparation, editing and validation of statistical metadata; to provide assistance, advice, direction, project plans and training to clients; to assist in the development of procedures and tools for evaluating metadata quality; and to effectively undertake evaluations of the quality of statistical metadata.

Knowledge of contacts within key client Divisions in order to establish a liaison, to evaluate and understand program statistical metadata requirements, provide assistance, advice and direction with respect to policy requirements, methods, procedures, systems, training, priorities and timelines relevant to the production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation of statistical metadata.

Knowledge of surveys and statistical programs within Statistics Canada in order to locate, analyze and compare related statistical metadata and to identify, evaluate and ensure consistency in the methods of processing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of metadata across programs, identifying and evaluating any conflicts, gaps or duplication of effort.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and of Statistics Canada policies, directives and guidelines in order to ensure understanding and application of the Act and these policies, directives and guidelines in the production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation of statistical metadata.
The position must have an awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of statistical information to ensure that actions are in compliance.
6. Research and analysis: Analyses client requirements in order to determine the feasibility, procedural options, priorities, and target dates relevant to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata, ensuring that approaches and results are consistent within and across surveys and statistical programs.

Provides assistance, advice and direction to internal clients with respect to statistical metadata, documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines, negotiating procedural modifications and establishing target dates, project plans and priorities.

Analyzes current production, storage, dissemination and evaluation methods, procedures and systems to ascertain their relevancy and to determine the need for changes or alternative methods, procedures and systems which would result in operational efficiencies and/or improvements in the quality of statistical metadata.

Analyzes changes in methods, procedures and systems used to produce, store, disseminate and evaluate the quality of statistical metadata in order to determine the need to update statistical metadata or adapt it to new formats; to determine where updates are required to existing documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals; and to determine potential short-term and long-term impacts on clients.

Analyzes and evaluates statistical metadata with respect to policy and procedural requirements and consistency across survey and statistical programs. Evaluates current and proposed methods, procedures and tools for evaluating the quality of statistical metadata in order to suggest potential improvements.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Unit Head, Metadata Development, Dissemination and Evaluation
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: The role is also materially tied to producing dissemination-ready metadata products because it provides methods, procedures and systems for the 'production, storage, dissemination' of metadata and advises clients on metadata 'development, production, storage, dissemination and evaluation needs'. This aligns with 7.2, where dissemination products are assembled with explanatory and quality components. It is weaker than 7.1 because the evidence points more to the metadata systems and infrastructure behind dissemination than to direct product-release assembly. Drivers such as metadata-rich dissemination, reusable enterprise components, and digital platforms will likely change the role through more standardized metadata packaging, stronger interoperability requirements, and increased demand for quality statements and structured metadata products across programs.

position_information.position_title: Unit Head, Metadata Development, Dissemination and Evaluation
key_activities: HR A to Z index
HR service standards
Wellness at Statistics Canada
HR committees
HR contact list
Corporate service providers

1. Decision Making: Determines the need for short-term and long-term projects and strategies relevant to the development, enhancement and implementation of methods, procedures and systems used at Statistics Canada for managing statistical metadata, recommending plans to improve and expand the scope, quality and level of integration of existing statistical metadata management programs.

Investigates client metadata requirements, determining the capacity and ability of existing methods, procedures and systems to fulfill these requirements effectively and efficiently; directs clients to the most appropriate options for their metadata development, production, storage, dissemination and evaluation needs; and identifies possible solutions when existing methods, procedures and systems appear not to be feasible, effective or efficient for the client.

Reviews trends and developments in the area of statistical metadata management in order to prepare program proposals, options and recommendations to management on the use and application of new methods, procedures and systems, identifying resource implications and impacts of new or modified approaches to metadata management.

Defines new methodological, procedural and systems specifications for the development, production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata, presenting this information in a logical and comprehensible manner to subordinates, colleagues, systems specialists, clients and management and ensuring that appropriate training and communications programs are in place.

Reviews and interprets policies, directives and guidelines relevant to the evaluation of statistical metadata quality, translating requirements into concrete plans for implementing, directing and monitoring statistical metadata quality assessment projects; determining the overall approach to be used in the reporting, analysis and presentation of results; and providing feedback to senior management with respect to where policies, directives and guidelines could be updated or enhanced.

Reviews and certifies the results of statistical metadata quality evaluations prepared by subordinates and makes recommendations to senior management with respect to how the quality of statistical metadata stored in, and disseminated from, corporate metadatabases may be enhanced by making changes to methods, procedures, guidelines, training plans or systems.

Provides input to management decisions and recommendations designed to develop or improve departmental policies and develops new divisional and program initiatives covering areas such as recruitment, training, official languages, wellness, employment equity, and information management.
2. Leadership And Operational Management: Manages a unit responsible for the development, production, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata and leads project teams for special projects. Assesses program requirements; determines objectives and priorities; plans and schedules work; resolves conflicting priorities. Ascertains human resource needs, determines appropriate selection methods (internal and external), recruits staff, determines training requirements and recommends and approves training plans. Evaluates employee performance and reviews performance evaluations prepared by subordinates.

Plans, develops and manages a budget for the unit in accordance with policy and procedures. Exercises direct authority and accountability for allocated funds to meet planned objectives. Authorises, commits and approves expenditures in accordance with approved budgets, with the authority to reallocate funds among line objects.
Negotiates and prepares service-level agreements related to the interoperability of statistical metadata across the Agency.
3. Communication: Provides expert advice and specialized training with respect to the policies, directives, guidelines, methods, procedures and systems used in the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata to subordinates, other statistical metadata specialists, systems specialists, clients and managers who use the information as input to on-going operations and to decisions concerning the management of statistical metadata at Statistics Canada and within other national and international organizations and agencies.

Liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, systems specialists, clients and managers to plan statistical metadata projects and implement short-term and long-term strategies for the development and enhancement of policies, procedures, methods and systems used in the management of statistical metadata. Provides direction with respect to establishing project plans, priorities and target dates; to negotiating modifications to methods, procedures and timelines; and to suggesting improvements to methods, procedures and systems.

Provides clear and comprehensible guidance, direction and specialized training to subordinate staff, colleagues, clients, systems specialists and management with respect to translating requirements for the management of statistical metadata into methods, procedures and systems specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata.

Writes detailed reports and prepares and delivers presentations which explain the rationale, requirements and results relating to policies, directives, guidelines, methods, procedures and systems used in the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata and which are used by other statistical metadata specialists, systems specialists, clients, and management in the operation and enhancement of statistical metadata management programs. When recommendations are challenged or misinterpreted, logical arguments are presented to defend the validity of the approaches used in order to maintain the division’s and Statistics Canada’s reputation for producing, storing and disseminating high quality metadata.
Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and groups to develop understanding, consensus and share knowledge on metadata management.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Extensive knowledge of statistical metadata concepts and frameworks used within Canada and internationally and knowledge of how those concepts and frameworks are used and reflected in policies, methods and procedures relating to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata in order to plan, develop, implement, direct, monitor and explain statistical metadata projects and short-term and long-term strategies for the development, operation and enhancement of statistical metadata management processes and systems.

Extensive knowledge of methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata and the potential impacts of new or modified methods, procedures and systems on project teams and clients in order to plan, develop, implement, direct, monitor and explain statistical metadata projects and short-term and long-term strategies for the development, operation and enhancement of statistical metadata management processes and systems; to manage and monitor the development, implementation and operation of new or enhanced metadata management processes and systems, and to lead metadata quality evaluations for surveys and statistical programs.

Knowledge of current and emerging trends and developments in the area of statistical metadata management in Canada and internationally, in order to evaluate Statistics Canada’s statistical metadata management program in a broader context; to anticipate, understand needs for, plan, manage and monitor the development, implementation and operation of new or enhanced metadata management methods, procedures and systems.

Knowledge of survey and statistical program subject matter concepts, methods and techniques relevant to the collection, processing, certification and dissemination of data in order to interpret client requirements for metadata production, storage and dissemination; to determine when changes in the needs of clients will impact statistical metadata programs and projects; to more accurately and efficiently evaluate the quality of statistical metadata across surveys and statistical programs; and to make recommendations to clients and managers with respect to possible enhanced approaches that could result in improved metadata quality.

Knowledge of management principles, techniques and practices in order to effectively manage financial resources, coordinate the activities of multi-disciplinary teams, manage performance, develop the skills, and competencies of team members. Knowledge of the principles and practices of project management used at Statistics Canada.

Knowledge of software, statistical packages and programming languages used in the production, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata and knowledge of new and emerging computer technology and applications in order to inform the planning of resource allocation and long-term strategies for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata.
5. Contextual knowledge: Extensive knowledge of Statistics Canada and Government of Canada policies, directives and guidelines directly and specifically related to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata, as well as other Statistics Canada policies, in order to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of all program activities and in order to explain policy requirements to clients and partners within Canada and internationally.

Extensive knowledge of the mandate, objectives, organization, practices, policies, culture and priorities of Statistics Canada in order to ensure that these are reflected in the objectives and management of all statistical metadata projects and short-term and long-term strategies for the development and enhancement of statistical metadata management processes and systems and to explain the context of statistical metadata management at Statistics Canada to clients and partners across Canada and internationally.

Knowledge of other statistical metadata management programs within Statistics Canada in order to integrate conceptually and structurally the statistical metadata required for various activities and programs into a broader corporate metadata management system and to ensure the overall relevance, completeness, coherence and consistency of statistical metadata contained within corporate metadata systems at Statistics Canada.

Extensive knowledge of surveys and statistical programs within Statistics Canada in order to establish short-term and long-term priorities for the processing, storing and dissemination of metadata across program areas and to effectively and efficiently plan and direct metadata quality assessment projects, certifying and reporting to senior management on the overall quality, completeness, coherence and consistency of statistical metadata.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and Privacy Act is required in order to ensure understanding and application of these Acts in the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata, particularly with respect to the security and confidentiality of statistical metadata and other information; to explain legislative requirements to other departments, agencies, industry, members of the public and the media; and to ensure that Statistics Canada meets its commitment to ensuring confidentiality and does not release any information that identifies an individual or group without prior consent.
6. Research and analysis: Analysis is required to understand and interpret client requirements with respect to the production, storage and dissemination of metadata, to determine the capacity and ability of existing or modified systems to meet the requirements of these clients and to translate client requirements into timely and affordable services. Clients are often uncertain of policy, procedural and systems restrictions and are unfamiliar with the options, methods and timelines required to produce and disseminate high quality metadata.

Reviews polices, guidelines, directives, methods, procedures and systems used for managing statistical metadata within Canada and internationally in order to determine the need for development, modification and adaptation of corporate metadata systems at Statistics Canada. Statistical metadata management programs are often very complex and have been designed for specific purposes which must be evaluated when taking into consideration the feasibility of the various features of such programs and the potential impacts and results in terms of Statistics Canada’s priorities for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata.

Analyses new methods, techniques and practices of managing statistical metadata and the associated costs and limitations. Identifies the availability of alternate means of producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata in order to evaluate the suitability of methods, procedures and systems with respect to the short-term and long-term program impacts and benefits.

Analyses the quality of statistical metadata produced by surveys and statistical programs at Statistics Canada; analyses gaps and inconsistencies in metadata quality and determines reasons for variances among program areas; reviews the comparability of metadata over time in light of changing policy requirements, systems functionality and changing methodologies used by statistical programs; provides senior management with interpretations and recommendations affecting policies, directives, guidelines, methods, procedures and systems used for the production, storage and dissemination of statistical metadata.

gsbpm_description: This sub-process ensures that all elements for the release are in place including managing the timing of the release. It includes briefings for specific groups such as the press or ministers, as well as the arrangements for any pre-release embargoes. It also includes the provision of products to subscribers, and managing access to confidential data by authorised user groups, such as researchers. Sometimes an organisation may need to retract a product, for example, if an error is discovered. This is also included in this sub-process.

safer innovation enables new release models only where secure and privacy-preserving controls are in place

drivers.impact: Release is materially affected because metadata completeness and linkage are now part of what must be in place for a successful release. Access to products, especially reusable data assets and confidential products, depends on accurate metadata and discoverability controls.
impact_mechanisms: Release readiness increasingly includes ensuring metadata are complete and correctly linked to products.
Searchable and reusable products depend on metadata being available at the point of release.
Access management for confidential and researcher products relies on clear metadata about content, conditions and use.
Retractions and corrections require metadata updates to preserve trust and discoverability.

implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This subprocess is strongly relevant because the role coordinates delivery of data and information to international organizations and ensures approvals before release. Evidence includes: 'Coordinates the delivery of data and information,' 'negotiates for deadline extensions or staggered delivery where appropriate,' and 'ensures that all necessary approvals are secured prior to delivery.' This directly matches managing release timing, approvals and controlled provision to external users. It is ranked below 1.5 because delivery/release follows from the prior assessment and coordination of requests, but it is still materially part of the work. Future drivers around execution discipline, secure access and digital platforms will likely increase emphasis on release governance, deadline control, secure external delivery and possible controlled access arrangements for international stakeholders.

gsbpm_description: This sub-process ensures that user queries and requests for services such as microdata access are recorded, and that responses are provided within agreed deadlines. These queries and requests should be regularly reviewed to provide an input to the overarching Quality Management activity, as they can indicate new or changing user needs. Replies to user requests can also be used to populate a knowledge database or a “Frequently Asked Questions” page, that is made publicly available, thus reducing the burden of replying to repeated and/or similar requests from external users. This sub-process also includes managing support to any partner organisations involved in disseminating the products.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Library Technician 3
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This is the strongest relationship because the role directly supports users and staff through library services: it acquires resources, analyzes client requests, develops and delivers responses, prepares reports for clients, writes procedures and training materials, and trains staff on integrated library system functionalities. Those duties align most closely with Provide user support, which includes responding to requests, maintaining knowledge resources and supporting partner/internal users. This is stronger than dissemination-system subprocesses because the clearest operational evidence is service provision to users and staff rather than formal statistical product release. Future drivers such as AI and Automation in Statistical Production, Enterprise Digital Platforms and Cloud Infrastructure, Metadata-Driven Data Management and Discoverability, and Operational Efficiency are likely to shift this work toward self-service support, knowledge-base maintenance, chatbot-enabled assistance, and support for more metadata-rich discovery environments.

position_information.branch_division: Communications and Information Services/ Communications and Library Services
key_activities: Acquires the full range of print, non-print and electronic information resources for the Library and the department and maintains all related files.
Participates in collection development activities, including planning, information audits, product evaluation and usage reports.
Conducts system administration / problem analysis of the integrated library system; manages the Library intranet site and Library wiki.
Provides problem resolution in the integrated library system which includes adding patches, system upgrades and configuration.
Leads project teams involved in the provision of library services and products.
Trains Library staff on integrated library system functionalities.

1. DECISION MAKING: Recommends and implements changes to procedures, guidelines and other administrative and technical material for use by departmental staff or clients.
Recommends the development or modification of operational area working tools.
Resolves current issues requiring the application of procedures and precedents.
Determines the appropriate course of action when troubleshooting problems with the integrated library system.
Recommends improvements to library services to the supervisor or section head in his/her working role or as a member of a library committee and/or project team.
2. LEADERSHIP AND OPERATIONAL MANAGEMENT: Assists the unit head and/or section chief in the planning and establishment of goals, priorities and training plans; and in staffing activities and employee performance reviews.
Provides guidance, coaching and orientation to co-workers and new staff and reviews the work of staff and colleagues.
Conducts training for staff and clients on standards, policies, workplace procedures and practices and the integrated library system.

Chairs and participates in working groups and project teams for special projects both internal and external to the Library. Assists in the establishment of goals, priorities and schedules; monitors and reports on progress.
3. COMMUNICATION: Responds to requests from federal government employees, clients or colleagues, using language that is easily understood, whether orally or in writing.

Requests input, information or approval of existing information from internal clients, vendors and employees in other federal government departments, using language that is clearly understood, whether orally or in writing.
Prepares reports (including financial and usage) for a range of clients both internal and external to the Library in response to requests for information.
Prepares and delivers reports to library management for analysis and decision making.
Writes information products, draft procedures, correspondence, reports, training material and memoranda for clients, colleagues and management.
4. KNOWLEDGE OF SPECIALIZED FIELDS: Knowledge of the practices, techniques and standards (e.g., Anglo-American Cataloguing Rules, 2nd edition, MAchine Readable Cataloguing) related to a specialized area within the Library in order to provide services and/or products.

Knowledge of accounting techniques and financial procedures (e.g., commitment of funds, pre‑payment, deposit accounts, group orders, discounts) to manage an acquisitions budget (e.g., track expenditures, compare estimated and actual prices, estimate budget surpluses and deficits) and to choose vendors and process orders.

Knowledge of basic UNIX, Perl scripting language, API programming and HTML coding to correct problems that occur with the integrated library system and to develop/make improvements/enhancements to the system.
Knowledge of automated library systems to evaluate, test, implement, assess system requirements, to provide input for Requests for Proposals and maintain the integrated library system.
Writing and presentation skills are required to deliver training or instruction to clients and staff.
5. CONTEXTUAL KNOWLEDGE: Knowledge of the divisional mandate, activities, priorities, policies, standards, practices, procedures, integrated library system and Statistics Canada’s online catalogue to effectively deliver library services to the library’s clientele, both internal and external to the department.
Knowledge of the role, responsibilities and long term objectives of the department, its organization, programs, and regional activities to understand and fulfill information requirements.
Knowledge of departmentally supported software (e.g., word processing, spreadsheets, communication, Internet) to locate, assess and disseminate information.
Knowledge of the use of databases used within the Library to create and modify records, to manipulate and extract data and to produce reports for departmental clients.

Knowledge of the acts and regulations related to the services of the Library and the department, including but not limited to the Statistics Act, Library and Archives of Canada Act, Copyright Act and Financial Administration Act to provide information to internal and external clients and to comply with audit requirements.

Knowledge of administrative principles, contract management and project management. This knowledge is required to process / manage internal transactions such as journal vouchers and contract renewals.

gsbpm_description: Evaluation material can be produced in any other phase or sub-process. It may take many forms, including feedback from users, process metadata (paradata), system metrics, and staff suggestions. Reports of progress against an action plan agreed during a previous iteration may also form an input to evaluations of subsequent iterations. This sub-process gathers all of these inputs, compiles quality indicators and makes them available for the person or team producing the evaluation. The collection of some of these evaluation materials can be automated and take place in a continuous way throughout the whole process, as defined by the quality framework (see Quality Management in Section V). On the other hand, for the evaluation of certain processes it can be necessary to perform specific activities such as small surveys, (e.g. post-enumeration surveys, re-interview studies, survey on effectiveness of dissemination).

Responsibility: 1. Information for the Use of Others

Prepares program evaluation reports and documents on the economy, efficiency and effectiveness of existing programs, operations and initiatives; monitors and assesses management accountability for departmental programs; and recommends ways to improve departmental policies, programs and operations.

Collects and analyzes foundation data in order to create new information about programs and their effectiveness; selects data sources to be used; develops and gathers information which will be used by management to make informed decisions concerning the scope, structure, redefinition or termination of major programs, initiatives, operations or activities.

Develops methodologies, tools and techniques to support the evolution of and use of professional practices and government-wide standards for the conduct of evaluation and review activities. This information is shared with colleagues, Senior Management, Central Agencies, OGDs, and other professional and governmental organizations.

Provides the Planning and Evaluation Manager with critical information for the development, use and maintenance of various system applications such as the LTP database, Risk Profile and the Management Accountability Framework which will significantly influence all aspects of systems development, implementation, maintenance and use.

Reviews emerging issues, trends and developments impacting government operations (i.e., strategic planning processes, performance evaluations, program evaluations and program review ) in order to develop and recommend strategies to assist departmental managers to effectively integrate program evaluation methodologies into the design and implementation of programs, policies, and initiatives. 2. Well-Being of Individuals No specific requirement

3. Leadership of Human Resources Plans, organizes and coordinates the work of project teams involved in the conduct of special studies, surveys and projects. Determines goals, priorities and milestones, sets objectives, plans and schedules the work, resolves conflicting priorities; identifies human resources needs, determines the appropriate selection methods (internal and external resources / contractors) to meet program or project objectives, participates in the recruitment of staff, provides input to employee performance, develops training plans, motivates and maintains morale of employees.

4. Money A. PLANNING AND CONTROLLING: Plans and budgets for on-going studies and/or special projects, including estimates for salaries, professional fees and implementation costs, with authority to allocate/reallocate funds within the budget. Provides input to budgets based on operational needs and by obtaining/providing cost estimates for personnel, supplies, equipment purchases and travel for use in developing section or division budgets.

B. ACQUIRING FUNDS: No specific requirement C. SPENDING FUNDS: Establishes and negotiates contracts for projects. Responsible for the acquisition of goods and services, according to the budget allocated. 5. Physical Assets and Products Ensures custody of, and protect confidential, secret and top-secret documents as well as proprietary and commercially confidential documents. This information is used to undertake evaluations and reviews. Often these documents are highly sensitive and cannot be copied. These documents usually cannot be replaced without substantial effort.

Creates, maintains and has custody of active hard copy and electronic project working files and Senior Management performance reviews and evaluations. These contain evidence (specimens, analysis-documentation, project findings, conclusions and recommendations) gathered during the course of evaluations and reviews. In many instances they are the Department’s only official record and depository of project results. Project team members use the working paper files to perform their work in delivering the evaluation-review services to departmental Senior Management and stakeholders. If lost, some documentation could be replicated or reconstructed from other sources, while other documentation would extremely be difficult to replace.
6. Ensuring Compliance Liaises with the Industry Portfolio Office and the Treasury Board Secretariat on an ongoing basis to ensure compliance to established standards.
Skills: 7. Job Content Knowledge Application Knowledge of statistical methods and techniques to conduct research and analysis into economic trends, policy and initiative issues; to collect and analyze foundation data in order to create new information about programs and their effectiveness; to select data sources to be used; and to develop and gather information which will be used by management to make informed decisions concerning the scope, structure, redefinition or termination of major programs, initiatives, operations or activities.
Knowledge of concepts, methods and techniques to develop evaluation standards and performance indicators as well as procedures for monitoring and reporting purposes.

Knowledge is required of computer software applications to conduct analysis and document project results, including specialized software such as statistical sampling, computer assisted techniques, automated working papers, and flowcharting.

Knowledge of social science research methods, techniques and practices, including multi-disciplinary analysis methods, to carry out analysis on a variety of approaches regarding performance and accountability framework in other levels of government, other jurisdictions and in the private sector.

Skill in synthesising information from diverse disciplines (management science, economics, and public policy administration, etc.) to facilitate the development and the implementation of interdepartmental performance frameworks. Knowledge of theories, principles and techniques of consultation, management, conflict resolution, small group process, interviewing and counselling to lead project teams, to negotiate contracts for services and agreements with other institutions. 8. Contextual Knowledge A. OWN WORK UNIT: Knowledge is required of the organization and objectives of the evaluation division; the strategic direction, culture, structure and organization, mandate, objectives, policies, procedures and work tools of the Field, branch, division; and the structure and organization of project work teams, their mandates and objectives. This knowledge is required to achieve operational objectives and results in an effective and efficient manner, and to recommend new or improved business services, policies, systems and procedures. Knowledge of the policies, procedures, guidelines, mandate and personnel of the Branch to provide consultative services related to strategic, annual and long-term evaluation plans, priority setting, strategic planning, policy development, performance measurement, monitoring and reporting; and to develop and recommend strategies to assist departmental managers to effectively integrate program evaluation methodologies into the design and implementation of programs, policies, and initiatives. B. OWN DEPARTMENT OR AGENCY: Knowledge of the policies, procedures, guidelines, mandate and personnel of the department to prepare program evaluation reports and documents on the economy, efficiency and effectiveness of existing programs, operations and initiatives; to monitor and assess management accountability for departmental programs; and to recommend ways to improve departmental policies, programs and operations. C. OTHER FEDERAL DEPARTMENTS AND AGENCIES: Knowledge of the personnel, organization, priorities, policies, mandate, objectives, goals and programs of a wide range of client departments and organizations to provide advice and guidance regarding the development and implementation of reporting and performance review frameworks, processes and tools.

Knowledge is required of the Parliamentary system and machinery of government, and its expectations for the Department, policy making and legislative processes, government priorities, and current and emerging management issues; the mandate, policies, programs, operations and reporting processes of Parliamentary committees, central agencies, and other federal government departments; and the role of Treasury Board and the Privy Council Office.

D. CANADIAN PRIVATE SECTOR AND OTHER PUBLIC SECTORS: Knowledge of personnel and organisation of different orders of government (provincial, territorial, municipal), the academic community, and non-government organisations in order to effectively communicate on performance and accountability approaches, methods, theories, studies, and analysis for the purpose of strengthening performance reporting to Parliament and the public. Knowledge of think tanks that are working in the area of citizen engagement, societal indicators and quality of life modelling, to carry out analysis regarding alternative performance and accountability frameworks and approaches (e.g. National Statistical Council). E. INTERNATIONAL PRIVATE AND PUBLIC SECTOR: Knowledge of personnel and organisation of different national governments, international organisations (International Statistical Agencies), the international academic community, and non-government organisations in order to effectively communicate on performance and accountability approaches, methods, theories, studies, and analysis for the purpose of strengthening performance reporting to Parliament and the public. F. LEGISLATION AND REGULATIONS: Knowledge of certain sections of legislation related to client departments and to STC reporting and reviews regulations and requirements. This knowledge is required to handle and process sensitive information and documentation related to client departments and reporting processes.

9. Communication A. COMMUNICATION IN: Listening and evaluation skills to interpret verbal and non-verbal communication when receiving information and feedback from colleagues, managers and departments to determine what their concerns are, to retain salient points and synthesize information on a variety of issues of differing complexity, and to understand opinion and points of view. Reading and listening skills, to maintain knowledge of key developments, research and innovations related to reporting and accountability processes and techniques, to attend conferences and meetings of professional associations related to auditing, financial analysis, and accountability reporting, to analyse and assess a wide range of alternative accountability approaches, strategies and processes, to liase and consult with academics, researchers and related specialists regarding a wide range of issues and innovations. B. COMMUNICATION OUT: Oral and written skills to make presentations and to consult with managers from client departments and organizations regarding strategic, annual and long-term evaluation plans, priority setting, strategic planning, policy development, performance measurement, monitoring and reporting.
Writing skills to prepare program evaluation reports and documents on the economy, efficiency and effectiveness of existing programs, operations and initiatives.

Speaking and writing skills are required to explain and clarify issues, to present arguments, report findings and recommendations to senior officials and stakeholders, and to adapt large volumes of information and specialized terminology in order to improve departmental policies, programs and operations.

10. Motor and Sensory Skills Dexterity and co-ordination skills are required on a daily basis to operate a computer keyboard and mouse to search, retrieve, and manipulate and transform information and data from information bases, the Internet and Intranet as well as to type briefing notes, memoranda, notes, reports, and analytical documents. Any requirement for proficiency, precision and speed in the conduct of this activity is under the control of the incumbent.
Effort: 11. Intellectual Effort Researches and analyzes complex, multi-dimensional and interrelated variables and issues; assesses the range of socio-economic and/or environmental impacts; and presents options and recommendations based on conclusions.

Develops new tools for statistical analysis in response to unique problems. The areas under evaluation are highly sensitive and require solid proof of findings. Views of stakeholders with differing or conflicting views must be integrated into the analyses, adding to the level of effort required. Additional constraints that hamper the analysis include information gaps that require the development and use of proxy measures.

Develops and carries out analytical reviews; develops strategic recommendations and proposals; and writes reports, working papers, background and briefing material for the direct use of analysts and senior officials in the directorate. Defends the results of analysis of complex issues and of information drawn from a wide variety of sources with varying degrees of technical complexity. The challenge lies in the lack of data and information or lack of existing tools or frameworks of analysis, which address the multiple objectives that departments and the government have in terms of accountability and reporting to Parliament. 12. Sustained Attention Attention is required to analyse complex issues and interpret and understand them in order to develop papers, briefings and recommendations. Participating in meetings with colleagues, senior management, or officials from other departments over periods of one to three hours requires sustained auditory and visual attention to focus in order to understand policy discussions and to be able to make effective contributions. 13. Psychological/Emotional Effort Psychological/emotional efforts are required on an ongoing basis to maintain professionalism when dealing with politically sensitive issues, adapting to shifting priorities and imposed short deadlines to meet the multiple, competing and sometimes conflicting demands of management. There is little or no control over the occurrence, frequency and duration of such situations. Psychological and emotional effort is required to maintain composure and professionalism in working with teams, meeting tight project deadlines, negotiating and consulting with TBS and IPO and providing constructive feedback to processes and methodologies. There is limited control over the occurrence, frequency and duration of these situations.
Urgent high profile evaluations requested by the Minister, Deputy Minister, or Senior Managers can cause immediate changes to existing assignments and priorities.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Chief- Training and Strategic Development
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: There is a meaningful relationship to gathering evaluation inputs because the role 'tracks and evaluates problems encountered,' 'monitors and identifies performance gaps,' conducts quality assurance exercises, and records deficiencies in training materials and participant performance. These activities generate structured feedback and operational evidence for improvement. This is stronger than formal evaluation reporting because the role mainly gathers and observes inputs rather than synthesizing enterprise evaluation reports. Future drivers around workforce transition and modernization will increase the amount and importance of readiness, adoption, and training-effectiveness evidence collected through this work.

1. Decision making: Judgment and initiative are required to provide technical subject matter expertise and coaching support to course participants. This involves continually studying changes to business practices of Statistics Canada survey, subject matter, and statistical learning programs to provide up-to-date and accurate information to staff. Judgment is required to identify and analyze coaching and training needs of course participants, to track and evaluate problems encountered, to ensure compliance to methodologies and to recommend solutions to resolve these issues. Each course participant has different levels of knowledge, and each learning session must be adapted to meet the individual performance requirements.

Apply judgment on the interpretation of various methodologies applied in “live” case scenarios undertaken by course participants; and conduct research and offer guidance to atypical issues that arise. This involves seeking out information from a variety of sources and providing advice and guidance based on the application of knowledge and a solid understanding of the Stats Can business practices.
2. Leadership and operational management: Contributes to new skill development by providing day-to-day technical guidance and direction to course participants; monitors and identifies performance gaps and develops and recommends coaching and training plans.

Ensures that training text, handouts, simulation exercises and testing tools reflect current business policies and practices. The incumbent is responsible for recording and following up on deficiencies, and in complex situations, working with subject matter resources in the design of new products to reflect changes to business practices.
3. Communication: Communication skills are required to mentor and coach course participants in the day-to-day classroom and group training activities and to provide technical guidance. Communication skills are required to adapt the style, tone and terminology to the course participant’s level of knowledge, which can vary considerably.

Communication skills are also required to participate in case studies; conduct interviews with external sources of information as part of the data gathering exercise; and respond to questions on methodologies accordingly.

Writing skills are required to develop, adapt and draft training materials and tools and to respond to concerns and information request from course participants. Writing skills are also required to prepare reports and correspondence.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of the theories and principles of Business and Economic development, Survey development is required in order to provide subject matter expertise to course participants on the interpretation and application of these business practices; mentor and coach throughout the duration of the course, and to provide subject matter expertise in the development and delivery training materials and tools to enhance competencies.

Knowledge of training delivery methods and practices in order to determine training needs of course participants and provide day-to-day coaching; assess the content of training case study materials and tools and recommend and initiate changes to deal with performance concerns.

Analytical and problem-solving methods, interviewing/information-gathering techniques and problem escalation practices, is required to provide support and troubleshooting services to course participants, to research, analyze and resolve interpretation problems, respond to questions and to provide coaching, training and ongoing technical guidance.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of Stats Can’s mandate, and business practices in order to ensure that the training programs accurately reflects Stats Can business practices; to provide advice subject matter expertise and guidance to course participants on the application of those practices; and to assess individual trainees knowledge and contribute to their training performance assessment.

Knowledge of TDL’s mandate, strategic objectives, business plans, organization, and accountability framework to work in close cooperation with Learning Specialist and transpose technical subject matter knowledge into adult learning methodologies.
6. Research and analysis: Conducts research and analysis of changes to Survey, Subject Matter and Statistical learning programs-related business practices in order to provide subject matter expertise to course participants, conduct monitoring and quality assurance exercises to ensure compliance and to case study methodologies.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Production and Dissemination Officer
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: A strong secondary relationship is to gathering evaluation inputs because the position explicitly undertakes quality evaluations of statistical metadata, evaluates selected indicators of metadata quality across surveys and programs, compiles information from diverse sources, and contributes to reports describing the results of metadata quality evaluations. This maps well to collecting and compiling quality indicators and evaluation material. It is stronger than later evaluation decision subprocesses because the role generates and compiles quality evidence rather than owning enterprise evaluation conclusions or action plans. Future drivers such as AI and automation, metadata-driven management, and operational efficiency will likely increase automated capture of metadata quality indicators, process metrics and cross-program comparability evidence, requiring stronger skills in continuous monitoring and metadata quality assessment.

Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of policies, directives and guidelines directly and specifically related to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata in order to prepare, edit and validate statistical metadata; to provide assistance, advice and training to clients; and to assist in reporting on metadata quality.

Analyzes changes in methods, procedures and systems used to produce, store, disseminate and evaluate the quality of statistical metadata in order to determine the need to update statistical metadata or adapt it to new formats and to determine where updates are required to existing documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals.
Evaluates selected indicators of statistical metadata quality across survey and statistical programs in accordance with pre-defined quality guidelines.

Analyzes and evaluates statistical metadata with respect to policy and procedural requirements, consistency across survey and statistical programs and other pre-defined quality measures.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Development, Dissemination and Evaluation Coordinator
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: The second strongest relationship is to gathering evaluation inputs because the role undertakes quality evaluations, reviews and verifies results of quality evaluations by others, compiles results, writes reports for clients and management, and analyzes metadata against policy, procedural and consistency requirements across programs. These are direct activities in compiling evaluation evidence and quality indicators. This is stronger than 8.2 because the role is producing and consolidating evaluation evidence rather than primarily synthesizing organization-level evaluation conclusions or determining follow-up action plans. Under future drivers, especially AI and automation, metadata management, and operational efficiency, this work will likely shift toward more continuous quality telemetry, reusable evaluation tools, and broader cross-program metadata quality benchmarking.

1. Decision Making: Plans, prioritizes, coordinates and undertakes the development and preparation of statistical metadata for storage and dissemination, reviewing, editing and validating statistical metadata.

Evaluates corporate and client metadata requirements, estimates the time required to complete tasks and assesses issues related to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata in order to provide direction to clients and management with respect to possible approaches, priorities, target dates and training needs and to resolve conceptual and technical problems.

Evaluates the methods, procedures and systems used in the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata, determining the need for, recommending, implementing and testing modifications; participates in the development of new specifications; advises clients of changes to methods and procedures; and advises clients and management of potential impacts and results.

Compiles, writes, edits and approves reports, documentation, procedures manuals and training materials which are related to the production, storage dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata and which are distributed internally.

Undertakes quality evaluations in accordance with documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines, reviews and verifies the results of quality evaluations undertaken by subordinates and colleagues, compiles results and writes reports for clients and management.

Provides input to management decisions and recommendations designed to develop or improve divisional and program initiatives covering areas such as recruitment, training, official languages, wellness and information management.
2. Leadership And Operational Management: Leads project teams or work units. Determines goals, priorities and milestones, sets objectives, plans and schedules work, resolves conflicting priorities. Assesses human resources needs, recommends appropriate selection methods (internal and external resources), recruits staff, determines training requirements and recommends and approves training plans. Evaluates employee performance and motivates and maintains morale of employees.
Monitors and tracks time spent on activities for the purposes of reporting to management and informing planning activities.

Plans and budgets for special projects. Provides input to budgets based on operational needs and by obtaining/providing cost estimates for personnel, supplies, equipment purchases and travel for use in developing section or division budgets.
3. Communication: Provides advice and training with respect to the policies, directives, guidelines, methods, procedures and systems used in the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata to subordinates, other statistical metadata specialists, clients and managers who use the information as input to on-going operations and to decisions concerning the management of statistical metadata at Statistics Canada.

Liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, subject matter specialists, survey managers and management in order to develop and translate requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata; to establish project plans, priorities and target dates; to negotiate modifications to methods, procedures and timelines; to provide training, and to suggest improvements to methods, procedures and systems.

Writes and presents detailed documents, procedures manuals and training manuals which explain, clarify and make recommendations with respect to the methods, procedures and systems used to produce, store and disseminate statistical metadata and which are used by other statistical metadata specialists, systems specialists, clients, and management in the operation and enhancement of statistical metadata management programs.

Writes reports which describe policy requirements related to the development, production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of high quality metadata, which describe the results of metadata quality evaluations and which make recommendations for procedures and tools that could be developed to evaluate the quality of statistical metadata. These reports are used by clients and management to ensure the quality and consistency of statistical metadata disseminated by Statistics Canada.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of statistical metadata concepts and frameworks used within Statistics Canada, the Government of Canada and internationally, and knowledge of how those concepts and frameworks are used and reflected in policies, methods and procedures relating to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata in order to plan, prioritize, coordinate and undertake the preparation, editing, validation and quality evaluation of statistical metadata, to ensure that colleagues and clients understand the importance of adhering to policies, methods and procedures in the preparation, storage and dissemination of metadata and to assess the need for modifications to methods and procedures.

Knowledge of methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata and the potential impacts of new or modified methods, procedures and systems on workloads, outputs and clients in order to establish project plans, priorities, timelines and training plans; to recommend improvements to methods, procedures and training; to participate in the development of procedures and tools for evaluating the quality of statistical metadata and to explain the results of metadata quality evaluations.

Knowledge of survey and statistical program subject matter concepts, methods and techniques relevant to the collection, processing, certification and dissemination of data in order to evaluate client requirements for metadata production, storage and dissemination; to implement plans for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata; and to more accurately and efficiently assess the quality of statistical metadata.
Knowledge of management techniques and principles to manage financial and human resources, either directly or within a matrix management environment.
Knowledge of software, statistical packages and programming languages used in the production, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of policies, directives and guidelines directly and specifically related to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata in order to plan and prioritize the preparation, editing and validation of statistical metadata; to provide assistance, advice, direction, project plans and training to clients; to assist in the development of procedures and tools for evaluating metadata quality; and to effectively undertake evaluations of the quality of statistical metadata.

Knowledge of contacts within key client Divisions in order to establish a liaison, to evaluate and understand program statistical metadata requirements, provide assistance, advice and direction with respect to policy requirements, methods, procedures, systems, training, priorities and timelines relevant to the production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation of statistical metadata.

Knowledge of surveys and statistical programs within Statistics Canada in order to locate, analyze and compare related statistical metadata and to identify, evaluate and ensure consistency in the methods of processing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of metadata across programs, identifying and evaluating any conflicts, gaps or duplication of effort.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and of Statistics Canada policies, directives and guidelines in order to ensure understanding and application of the Act and these policies, directives and guidelines in the production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation of statistical metadata.
The position must have an awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of statistical information to ensure that actions are in compliance.
6. Research and analysis: Analyses client requirements in order to determine the feasibility, procedural options, priorities, and target dates relevant to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata, ensuring that approaches and results are consistent within and across surveys and statistical programs.

Provides assistance, advice and direction to internal clients with respect to statistical metadata, documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines, negotiating procedural modifications and establishing target dates, project plans and priorities.

Analyzes current production, storage, dissemination and evaluation methods, procedures and systems to ascertain their relevancy and to determine the need for changes or alternative methods, procedures and systems which would result in operational efficiencies and/or improvements in the quality of statistical metadata.

Analyzes changes in methods, procedures and systems used to produce, store, disseminate and evaluate the quality of statistical metadata in order to determine the need to update statistical metadata or adapt it to new formats; to determine where updates are required to existing documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals; and to determine potential short-term and long-term impacts on clients.

Analyzes and evaluates statistical metadata with respect to policy and procedural requirements and consistency across survey and statistical programs. Evaluates current and proposed methods, procedures and tools for evaluating the quality of statistical metadata in order to suggest potential improvements.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Planning and Evaluation Manager
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: A third meaningful relationship is to gather evaluation inputs because the role authorizes and guides evidence collection, determines sources, and oversees methodologies and project teams that generate evaluation inputs. Evidence includes 'full latitude to scope, plan, authorize, and guide the collection and analysis of the foundation data,' deciding 'what data, from which sources will be used,' and managing multidisciplinary teams and tools to support evaluation and review activities. The role also oversees performance measurement criteria, monitoring processes, quality control, and system applications that support reporting and accountability structures. This is weaker than 8.2 and 8.3 because input gathering is an enabling activity within a broader evaluative and governance role, rather than the role's main differentiator. Future drivers such as AI/automation, enterprise platforms, integrated pipelines, metadata-driven management and modern statistical production will likely increase the volume and complexity of evaluation inputs, requiring stronger capacity in telemetry, standardized metrics, system-generated evidence, interoperability and ongoing monitoring of modernization performance.
