Responsibility: 1. Information for the Use of Others

Prepares program evaluation reports and documents on the economy, efficiency and effectiveness of existing programs, operations and initiatives; monitors and assesses management accountability for departmental programs; and recommends ways to improve departmental policies, programs and operations.

Collects and analyzes foundation data in order to create new information about programs and their effectiveness; selects data sources to be used; develops and gathers information which will be used by management to make informed decisions concerning the scope, structure, redefinition or termination of major programs, initiatives, operations or activities.

Develops methodologies, tools and techniques to support the evolution of and use of professional practices and government-wide standards for the conduct of evaluation and review activities. This information is shared with colleagues, Senior Management, Central Agencies, OGDs, and other professional and governmental organizations.

Provides the Planning and Evaluation Manager with critical information for the development, use and maintenance of various system applications such as the LTP database, Risk Profile and the Management Accountability Framework which will significantly influence all aspects of systems development, implementation, maintenance and use.

Reviews emerging issues, trends and developments impacting government operations (i.e., strategic planning processes, performance evaluations, program evaluations and program review ) in order to develop and recommend strategies to assist departmental managers to effectively integrate program evaluation methodologies into the design and implementation of programs, policies, and initiatives. 2. Well-Being of Individuals No specific requirement

3. Leadership of Human Resources Plans, organizes and coordinates the work of project teams involved in the conduct of special studies, surveys and projects. Determines goals, priorities and milestones, sets objectives, plans and schedules the work, resolves conflicting priorities; identifies human resources needs, determines the appropriate selection methods (internal and external resources / contractors) to meet program or project objectives, participates in the recruitment of staff, provides input to employee performance, develops training plans, motivates and maintains morale of employees.

4. Money A. PLANNING AND CONTROLLING: Plans and budgets for on-going studies and/or special projects, including estimates for salaries, professional fees and implementation costs, with authority to allocate/reallocate funds within the budget. Provides input to budgets based on operational needs and by obtaining/providing cost estimates for personnel, supplies, equipment purchases and travel for use in developing section or division budgets.

B. ACQUIRING FUNDS: No specific requirement C. SPENDING FUNDS: Establishes and negotiates contracts for projects. Responsible for the acquisition of goods and services, according to the budget allocated. 5. Physical Assets and Products Ensures custody of, and protect confidential, secret and top-secret documents as well as proprietary and commercially confidential documents. This information is used to undertake evaluations and reviews. Often these documents are highly sensitive and cannot be copied. These documents usually cannot be replaced without substantial effort.

Creates, maintains and has custody of active hard copy and electronic project working files and Senior Management performance reviews and evaluations. These contain evidence (specimens, analysis-documentation, project findings, conclusions and recommendations) gathered during the course of evaluations and reviews. In many instances they are the Department’s only official record and depository of project results. Project team members use the working paper files to perform their work in delivering the evaluation-review services to departmental Senior Management and stakeholders. If lost, some documentation could be replicated or reconstructed from other sources, while other documentation would extremely be difficult to replace.
6. Ensuring Compliance Liaises with the Industry Portfolio Office and the Treasury Board Secretariat on an ongoing basis to ensure compliance to established standards.
Skills: 7. Job Content Knowledge Application Knowledge of statistical methods and techniques to conduct research and analysis into economic trends, policy and initiative issues; to collect and analyze foundation data in order to create new information about programs and their effectiveness; to select data sources to be used; and to develop and gather information which will be used by management to make informed decisions concerning the scope, structure, redefinition or termination of major programs, initiatives, operations or activities.
Knowledge of concepts, methods and techniques to develop evaluation standards and performance indicators as well as procedures for monitoring and reporting purposes.

Knowledge is required of computer software applications to conduct analysis and document project results, including specialized software such as statistical sampling, computer assisted techniques, automated working papers, and flowcharting.

Knowledge of social science research methods, techniques and practices, including multi-disciplinary analysis methods, to carry out analysis on a variety of approaches regarding performance and accountability framework in other levels of government, other jurisdictions and in the private sector.

Skill in synthesising information from diverse disciplines (management science, economics, and public policy administration, etc.) to facilitate the development and the implementation of interdepartmental performance frameworks. Knowledge of theories, principles and techniques of consultation, management, conflict resolution, small group process, interviewing and counselling to lead project teams, to negotiate contracts for services and agreements with other institutions. 8. Contextual Knowledge A. OWN WORK UNIT: Knowledge is required of the organization and objectives of the evaluation division; the strategic direction, culture, structure and organization, mandate, objectives, policies, procedures and work tools of the Field, branch, division; and the structure and organization of project work teams, their mandates and objectives. This knowledge is required to achieve operational objectives and results in an effective and efficient manner, and to recommend new or improved business services, policies, systems and procedures. Knowledge of the policies, procedures, guidelines, mandate and personnel of the Branch to provide consultative services related to strategic, annual and long-term evaluation plans, priority setting, strategic planning, policy development, performance measurement, monitoring and reporting; and to develop and recommend strategies to assist departmental managers to effectively integrate program evaluation methodologies into the design and implementation of programs, policies, and initiatives. B. OWN DEPARTMENT OR AGENCY: Knowledge of the policies, procedures, guidelines, mandate and personnel of the department to prepare program evaluation reports and documents on the economy, efficiency and effectiveness of existing programs, operations and initiatives; to monitor and assess management accountability for departmental programs; and to recommend ways to improve departmental policies, programs and operations. C. OTHER FEDERAL DEPARTMENTS AND AGENCIES: Knowledge of the personnel, organization, priorities, policies, mandate, objectives, goals and programs of a wide range of client departments and organizations to provide advice and guidance regarding the development and implementation of reporting and performance review frameworks, processes and tools.

Knowledge is required of the Parliamentary system and machinery of government, and its expectations for the Department, policy making and legislative processes, government priorities, and current and emerging management issues; the mandate, policies, programs, operations and reporting processes of Parliamentary committees, central agencies, and other federal government departments; and the role of Treasury Board and the Privy Council Office.

D. CANADIAN PRIVATE SECTOR AND OTHER PUBLIC SECTORS: Knowledge of personnel and organisation of different orders of government (provincial, territorial, municipal), the academic community, and non-government organisations in order to effectively communicate on performance and accountability approaches, methods, theories, studies, and analysis for the purpose of strengthening performance reporting to Parliament and the public. Knowledge of think tanks that are working in the area of citizen engagement, societal indicators and quality of life modelling, to carry out analysis regarding alternative performance and accountability frameworks and approaches (e.g. National Statistical Council). E. INTERNATIONAL PRIVATE AND PUBLIC SECTOR: Knowledge of personnel and organisation of different national governments, international organisations (International Statistical Agencies), the international academic community, and non-government organisations in order to effectively communicate on performance and accountability approaches, methods, theories, studies, and analysis for the purpose of strengthening performance reporting to Parliament and the public. F. LEGISLATION AND REGULATIONS: Knowledge of certain sections of legislation related to client departments and to STC reporting and reviews regulations and requirements. This knowledge is required to handle and process sensitive information and documentation related to client departments and reporting processes.

9. Communication A. COMMUNICATION IN: Listening and evaluation skills to interpret verbal and non-verbal communication when receiving information and feedback from colleagues, managers and departments to determine what their concerns are, to retain salient points and synthesize information on a variety of issues of differing complexity, and to understand opinion and points of view. Reading and listening skills, to maintain knowledge of key developments, research and innovations related to reporting and accountability processes and techniques, to attend conferences and meetings of professional associations related to auditing, financial analysis, and accountability reporting, to analyse and assess a wide range of alternative accountability approaches, strategies and processes, to liase and consult with academics, researchers and related specialists regarding a wide range of issues and innovations. B. COMMUNICATION OUT: Oral and written skills to make presentations and to consult with managers from client departments and organizations regarding strategic, annual and long-term evaluation plans, priority setting, strategic planning, policy development, performance measurement, monitoring and reporting.
Writing skills to prepare program evaluation reports and documents on the economy, efficiency and effectiveness of existing programs, operations and initiatives.

Speaking and writing skills are required to explain and clarify issues, to present arguments, report findings and recommendations to senior officials and stakeholders, and to adapt large volumes of information and specialized terminology in order to improve departmental policies, programs and operations.

10. Motor and Sensory Skills Dexterity and co-ordination skills are required on a daily basis to operate a computer keyboard and mouse to search, retrieve, and manipulate and transform information and data from information bases, the Internet and Intranet as well as to type briefing notes, memoranda, notes, reports, and analytical documents. Any requirement for proficiency, precision and speed in the conduct of this activity is under the control of the incumbent.
Effort: 11. Intellectual Effort Researches and analyzes complex, multi-dimensional and interrelated variables and issues; assesses the range of socio-economic and/or environmental impacts; and presents options and recommendations based on conclusions.

Develops new tools for statistical analysis in response to unique problems. The areas under evaluation are highly sensitive and require solid proof of findings. Views of stakeholders with differing or conflicting views must be integrated into the analyses, adding to the level of effort required. Additional constraints that hamper the analysis include information gaps that require the development and use of proxy measures.

Develops and carries out analytical reviews; develops strategic recommendations and proposals; and writes reports, working papers, background and briefing material for the direct use of analysts and senior officials in the directorate. Defends the results of analysis of complex issues and of information drawn from a wide variety of sources with varying degrees of technical complexity. The challenge lies in the lack of data and information or lack of existing tools or frameworks of analysis, which address the multiple objectives that departments and the government have in terms of accountability and reporting to Parliament. 12. Sustained Attention Attention is required to analyse complex issues and interpret and understand them in order to develop papers, briefings and recommendations. Participating in meetings with colleagues, senior management, or officials from other departments over periods of one to three hours requires sustained auditory and visual attention to focus in order to understand policy discussions and to be able to make effective contributions. 13. Psychological/Emotional Effort Psychological/emotional efforts are required on an ongoing basis to maintain professionalism when dealing with politically sensitive issues, adapting to shifting priorities and imposed short deadlines to meet the multiple, competing and sometimes conflicting demands of management. There is little or no control over the occurrence, frequency and duration of such situations. Psychological and emotional effort is required to maintain composure and professionalism in working with teams, meeting tight project deadlines, negotiating and consulting with TBS and IPO and providing constructive feedback to processes and methodologies. There is limited control over the occurrence, frequency and duration of these situations.
Urgent high profile evaluations requested by the Minister, Deputy Minister, or Senior Managers can cause immediate changes to existing assignments and priorities.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Metadata Development and Evaluation Specialist
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: This subprocess is also materially supported because the role gathers, analyzes and compiles inputs used for metadata quality assessment. Evidence includes: 'evaluates and investigates... metadata requirements,' 'compiles results,' 'analyses client requirements,' and 'analyses current production, storage, dissemination and evaluation methods.' While the role goes beyond gathering inputs into full evaluation, there is clear responsibility for assembling evidence and quality information. It is ranked below 8.2 because the description more strongly emphasizes analysis, certification and reporting than collection of inputs alone. Future drivers will likely increase the continuous capture of metadata quality indicators, repository usage signals, standards compliance metrics and system-generated evidence to support enterprise metadata evaluation.

1. Decision Making: Plans, prioritizes, coordinates, directs, monitors and undertakes the development and preparation of statistical metadata for storage and dissemination, reviewing, editing and validating statistical metadata.

Evaluates and investigates corporate and client the metadata requirements, estimates the time required to complete tasks and assesses issues related to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata in order to provide direction to clients and management with respect to possible approaches, priorities, target dates and training plans; to resolve conceptual and technical problems; and to provide feedback on the capacity and ability of existing methods, procedures and systems to fulfill client requirements effectively and efficiently.

Reviews trends and developments in the area of statistical metadata management, liaising with internal and external clients within Canada, in order to determine the need for short-term projects and strategies relevant to the development, enhancement and implementation of methods and procedures used at Statistics Canada for managing statistical metadata; recommending plans to improve methods and procedures; developing specifications for, implementing and testing modifications in methods and procedures; and identifying the impacts and results of new or modified approaches to metadata management.

Directs the development of, evaluates, and approves reports, documentation, procedures manuals and training materials which are related to the production, storage dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata and which are distributed internally and externally within Canada.

Plans, directs and undertakes quality evaluations in accordance with documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines, reviews and certifies the results of quality evaluations undertaken by subordinates and colleagues, compiles results and writes reports for clients and management; and presents results to management.

Provides input to management decisions and recommendations designed to develop or improve departmental, divisional and program initiatives covering areas such as recruitment, training, official languages, wellness, employment equity and information management.
2. Leadership And Operational Management: Manages a unit involved in activities related to the development and evaluation of statistical metadata and/or leads multi-disciplinary project teams for special metadata projects. Determines goals, priorities and milestones, sets objectives, and plans and schedules the work, resolves conflicting priorities; identifies human resources needs, determines the appropriate selection methods (internal and external resources) to meet program or project objectives, recruits staff, evaluates employee performance, develops training plans, motivates and maintains morale of employees.

Plans and budgets for on-going and/or special projects, including estimates for salaries, professional fees and implementation costs, with authority to allocate/reallocate funds within the budget and in accordance with Statistics Canada’s policies and procedures. Provides input to budgets based on operational needs and by obtaining/providing cost estimates for personnel, supplies, equipment purchases and travel for use in developing section or division budgets. Establishes and negotiates contracts for projects. Responsible for the acquisition of goods and services, according to the budget allocated.
3. Communication: Provides expert advice and training with respect to the policies, directives, guidelines, methods, procedures and systems used in the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata to subordinates, other statistical metadata specialists, systems specialists, clients and managers who use the information as input to on-going operations and to decisions concerning the management of statistical metadata at Statistics Canada and within other national organizations and agencies.

Liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, systems specialists, clients and managers at Statistics Canada to plan statistical metadata projects and implement short-term strategies for the development and enhancement of policies, procedures and methods used in the management of statistical metadata; to develop and translate strategies and requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata; to establish project plans, priorities and target dates; to negotiate modifications to methods, procedures and timelines; to coordinate and deliver training, and to suggest improvements to methods, procedures and systems.

Writes detailed reports and prepares and delivers presentations which explain rationale, requirements and results relating to policies, directives, guidelines, methods and procedures used in the production, storage and dissemination of statistical metadata and which are used by other statistical metadata specialists, systems specialists, clients, and management in the operation and enhancement of statistical metadata management programs.

Writes reports which describe policy requirements related to the development, production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of high quality metadata, which describe the results of metadata quality evaluations and which make recommendations for procedures and tools that could be developed to evaluate the quality of statistical metadata. These reports are used by clients and management to ensure the quality and consistency of statistical metadata disseminated by Statistics Canada.
Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and workgroups to develop consensus or share knowledge within the area of expertise.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Advanced knowledge of statistical metadata concepts and frameworks used within Canada and internationally and knowledge of how those concepts and frameworks are used and reflected in policies, methods and procedures relating to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata in order to plan, prioritize, coordinate, direct, monitor and undertake the preparation, editing, validation and quality evaluation of statistical metadata and short-term strategies for the enhancement of statistical metadata management processes

Advanced knowledge of methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata and the potential impacts of new or modified methods, procedures and systems on project teams and clients in order to plan, prioritize, coordinate, direct, monitor and undertake statistical metadata projects and short-term strategies for the development, operation and enhancement of statistical metadata management processes; to recommend improvements to methods, procedures and training; to develop procedures and tools for evaluating the quality of statistical metadata; and to explain the results of metadata quality evaluations.

Knowledge of survey and statistical program subject matter concepts, methods and techniques relevant to the collection, processing, certification and dissemination of data in order to evaluate client requirements for metadata production, storage and dissemination; to determine when changes in the needs of clients will impact statistical metadata programs and projects; and to more accurately and efficiently evaluate the quality of statistical metadata across surveys and statistical programs.

Knowledge of management principles, techniques and practices in order to lead a multi-disciplinary project team and manage financial and human resources, either directly or within a matrix management environment. Knowledge of the principles and practices of project management used at Statistics Canada.
Knowledge of software, statistical packages and programming languages used in the production, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata
5. Contextual knowledge: Advanced knowledge of Statistics Canada and Government of Canada policies, directives and guidelines directly and specifically related to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata, as well as other Statistics Canada policies, in order to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of all program activities and in order to explain policy requirements to clients and partners within Canada.

Knowledge of other statistical metadata management programs within Statistics Canada in order to integrate conceptually and structurally the statistical metadata required for various activities and programs.

Advanced knowledge of contacts within key client Divisions in order to establish a liaison; to evaluate and understand program statistical metadata requirements; and to provide expert assistance, advice and direction with respect to policy requirements, methods, procedures, systems, training, priorities and timelines relevant to the production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation of statistical metadata.

Knowledge of surveys and statistical programs within Statistics Canada in order to establish short-term priorities for the processing, storage, dissemination and evaluation of metadata across program areas and to effectively and efficiently direct metadata quality assessment projects, certifying and reporting to management on the overall quality, completeness, coherence and consistency of statistical metadata.

Knowledge of the mandate, objectives, organization, practices, policies, culture and priorities of Statistics Canada in order to ensure that these are reflected in the objectives and management of all statistical metadata projects and short-term strategies for the development and enhancement of statistical metadata management processes and systems, and to explain the context of statistical metadata management at Statistics Canada to clients and partners across Canada.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and Privacy Act is required in order to ensure understanding and application of these Acts in the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata, particularly with respect to the security and confidentiality of statistical metadata and other information; to explain legislative requirements to other departments, agencies, industry, members of the public and the media; and to ensure that Statistics Canada meets its commitment to ensuring confidentiality and does not release any information that identifies an individual or group without prior consent.
6. Research and analysis: Analyses and synthesizes diverse sources of statistical metadata in order to ensure that the quantity and quality of statistical metadata disseminated is optimal for Statistics Canada’s surveys and statistical programs.

Provides expert assistance, advice and direction to internal clients and external clients within Canada with respect to statistical metadata, documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines, determining changes in the needs of clients, assessing the impacts of these changes on statistical metadata programs and projects, and establishing short-term plans and priorities.

Analyses client requirements in order to determine the feasibility, procedural options, priorities, and target dates relevant to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata in order to ensure that approaches and results are consistent within, and across, surveys and statistical programs, and in order to direct and monitor statistical metadata projects and short-term strategies for the development, operation and enhancement of statistical metadata management processes.

Analyzes current production, storage, dissemination and evaluation methods, procedures and systems in comparison to those used elsewhere at Statistics Canada and elsewhere in Canada in order to ascertain their relevancy and to determine the need for modifications or the use of alternative methods, procedures and systems which would result in operational efficiencies and/or improvements in the quality of statistical metadata at Statistics Canada.

Analyzes changes in methods, procedures and systems used to produce, store, disseminate and evaluate the quality of statistical metadata in order to determine the need to update statistical metadata or adapt it to new formats; to determine where updates are required to existing documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals and to prioritize those updates; and to determine and mitigate potential short-term and long-term impacts on clients.

Analyses the quality of statistical metadata produced by surveys and statistical programs at Statistics Canada; evaluates current and proposed methods, procedures and tools for evaluating the quality of statistical metadata in order to develop enhancements; analyses gaps and inconsistencies in metadata quality and suggests possible reasons for variances among program areas; reviews the comparability of metadata over time in light of changing policy requirements, systems functionality and changing methodologies used by statistical programs; provides management with reports of findings.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Local Census Office Manager
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: The role has a meaningful but secondary connection to gathering evaluation inputs. Evidence includes monitoring performance indicators, reporting on efficiency and effectiveness, disseminating and collecting evaluation reports for the LCO, summarizing findings, and making recommendations for improvements. This is more appropriate than 8.2 because the job gathers and compiles operational evidence and local findings, while broader evaluation synthesis appears to occur elsewhere. Future drivers such as integrated monitoring, operational dashboards, governance discipline, and efficiency pressures will likely increase the importance of continuous collection of performance metrics, security indicators, workforce feedback and operational lessons to support future census improvements.

key_activities: As part of the Area Management team, contributes to the development of operational plans for Census data collection activities; and manages census field and office operations for an LCO (7-day collection operation).

Manages the financial, human and material resources for the assigned LCO ; and manages the recruitment process for both Public Service Employment Act (PSEA) and Statistics Act employees required to meet the demands of a large temporary workforce.

Develops collections strategies and contingency plans; establishes and defines priorities; monitors and evaluates the cost, quality, efficiency, productivity and security of LCO data collection systems and processes; analyzes and produces reports on the progress of the LCO activities; and resolves problems including but not limited to the need for development, modification and adaptation of operational processes.

Monitors performance indicators; reports on the efficiency and effectiveness of LCO operations; and implements corrective action to resolve problems. Evaluates cost efficiencies, productivity and security of the Local Census Office.

Implements and provides expert interpretation of departmental legislation and the application of Statistics Canada policies and procedures; and leads the preparation and delivery of training to Assistant Manager, Field Operations, Assistant Manager Collection Unit, Assistant Manager Recruitment and Administration Officer.

Represents the department in consultations with the general public to solicit participation from non-respondents, responds to and resolves complaints; and contributes to public relations activities to promote Census Communications and respondent co-operation.
Represents the LCO in regional and/or department committees involved in the evaluation of the Census collection activities and provides advice on proposed modifications to operational procedures.
Disseminates and collects evaluation reports for the assigned LCO ; summarizes findings; and makes recommendations for program improvements.

Provides support to Regional administration with the opening of the office space such as visits during construction fit up, ensures office readiness for the beginning of field activities as well as closing down the LCO once operations have been completed.

Decision making: Effort is required to make decisions/recommendations on: the determination and definition of objectives, content and approaches for Census collection activities in the LCO and the operational framework and conditions within which the statistical program will occur; development and implementation of collection applications, alternate work methods and models to achieve desired outcomes; the development of strategies and business solutions to improve respondent relations, data collection and transmission processes; the resolution of complaints and problems related to survey participation and non-respondents; the development and distribution of guidelines, instructions and procedures for use by LCO Managers and staff; approval of appointments of all Statistics Act staff in the LCO region; the assurance that financial expenditures and resources are within allocated budgets; and the day-to-day management of financial, human and material resources of the LCO.
Decisions/recommendations taken affect the efficient and effective operations of the LCO and the LCO’s compliance to the Statistics Act and departmental policies and procedures.
Leadership and operational management: Manages the recruitment, development and retention of a fully trained and professional data collection workforce in the LCO. Establishes, coordinates and leads multi-disciplinary project teams and work groups comprising professional, technical, and administrative and Field Staff engaged in initiating, developing and implementing programs. Approves work plans and priorities. Establishes organizational structures, assigns responsibilities to team or group members, monitors progress and evaluates employee performance, provides training and guidance.
Monitors expenditures for staffing and material resources to ensure funds are spent appropriately and the LCO budget is respected.

Plans and budgets for the management and operation of the LCO in accordance with departmental policy and procedures, identifies content and cost of development and operational requirements, estimates salary, equipment and travel costs, as well as professional fees.

Oversees some of the aspects related to the LCO fit up with local contractors to ensure readiness at time of opening and coordinate the dismantlement of the facility at the end of Census collection operation
Communication: Communications skills are required to respond orally and in writing to inquiries from managers, employees to provide information and advice on the operation and use of systems and processes and briefings on LCO program results.
Communications skills are required to respond orally and in writing to inquiries from the general public on the requirements for response, purpose of the Census or issues with employees.

There is an occasional requirement to respond to inquiries from the media. These situations are difficult as dealing with the media requires "thinking on your feet", as well as ensuring that statements made are clear so as not to be misunderstood.

Communications skills are also required to intervene and deal with uncooperative and sometimes hostile respondents. There is a requirement to "take control" over these emotionally charged situations, and persuade the respondent to take a more rational approach to a situation.
Knowledge of specialized fields: Advanced knowledge of socio-economic concepts, methods and techniques applied in the development and operation of statistical programs to manage the LCO field operations, analyze program outputs, anticipate and understand the need for new data and to assess the impact on collection activities and programs.
In-depth knowledge of statistical data collection methods, concepts and practices and survey operations to manage the activities of the LCO and to provide expert advice on data collection issues.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies (e.g. confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations and data quality), practices and classifications systems is required to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of Census activities.

Knowledge of financial and human resources management and of project management methods, techniques and practices to manage the work of a Local Census Office and organize, plan, schedule and control the LCO operational activities.
Contextual knowledge: Knowledge and understanding of Statistics Canada’s mandate, programs, objectives, policies and procedures in areas such as survey methodology, operations integration, data confidentiality and security, dissemination and marketing to manage staff in the delivery of the program within a LCO and ensure that the work undertaken is standardized and consistent with departmental requirements.

Knowledge of the, regional and local operations’ mandate, activities, priorities, standards and procedures to the work to incorporate them into the management of the LCO and to recommend changes to management.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies (e.g. confidentiality of data, security, and respondent relations and data quality), practices and classification systems is required to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of Census activities.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act, Financial Administration Act, the Public Service Employment Act, Collective Agreementsand related policies and directives and supporting financial and human resources management methods, techniques and practices in order to manage the financial, human resource and material resources of assigned LCOs.
Research and analysis: Reviews and interprets the methods, concepts, techniques and practices applied in the operation of existing systems and processes and proposes modifications and enhancements or develops alternative approaches.
Analyses the relative quality of data, researches gaps and inconsistencies in the collection methods and procedures used, determines reasons for variances and initiates solutions.
Identifies and evaluates variations in survey responses and contributes to promotional activities to increase respondent participation rates.
Analyzes and produces reports on the progress of the LCO activites and resolves problems including but not limited to the need for development, modification and adaptation of operational processes.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Area Manager
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: A third meaningful relationship is gathering evaluation inputs. Evidence includes disseminating and collecting evaluation reports, summarizing findings, making recommendations for program improvements, and conducting comprehensive evaluations of collection effectiveness and efficiency. This is stronger than 8.2 because the role appears to produce and forward operational evidence and recommendations from the field rather than own the enterprise evaluation function. Future drivers such as execution discipline, performance dashboards, integrated pipelines and cost realignment will likely increase emphasis on continuous collection of performance metrics, issue logs, response-pattern evidence and workforce feedback to inform future census redesign.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Planning and Evaluation Manager
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: There is also a meaningful relationship to gathering evaluation inputs because the role has 'full latitude' to scope and authorize data collection, decide what data and sources will be used, and guide collection and analysis of foundation data for evaluation. Evidence includes selecting sources, creating information about programs and performance, establishing performance measurement criteria, and monitoring results. This is weaker than 8.2 because input gathering supports the evaluation function rather than being the primary end product of the job. Future drivers such as integrated telemetry, enterprise platforms, metadata-rich evidence, and AI-enabled monitoring will likely expand the role's need to pull together more automated operational metrics, cross-program indicators, and workforce adoption evidence.
