1. Decision Making: Determines the need for short-term and long-term projects and strategies relevant to the development, enhancement and implementation of methods, procedures and systems used at Statistics Canada for managing statistical metadata, recommending plans to improve and expand the scope, quality and level of integration of existing statistical metadata management programs.

Investigates client metadata requirements, determining the capacity and ability of existing methods, procedures and systems to fulfill these requirements effectively and efficiently; directs clients to the most appropriate options for their metadata development, production, storage, dissemination and evaluation needs; and identifies possible solutions when existing methods, procedures and systems appear not to be feasible, effective or efficient for the client.

Reviews trends and developments in the area of statistical metadata management in order to prepare program proposals, options and recommendations to management on the use and application of new methods, procedures and systems, identifying resource implications and impacts of new or modified approaches to metadata management.

Defines new methodological, procedural and systems specifications for the development, production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata, presenting this information in a logical and comprehensible manner to subordinates, colleagues, systems specialists, clients and management and ensuring that appropriate training and communications programs are in place.

Reviews and interprets policies, directives and guidelines relevant to the evaluation of statistical metadata quality, translating requirements into concrete plans for implementing, directing and monitoring statistical metadata quality assessment projects; determining the overall approach to be used in the reporting, analysis and presentation of results; and providing feedback to senior management with respect to where policies, directives and guidelines could be updated or enhanced.

Reviews and certifies the results of statistical metadata quality evaluations prepared by subordinates and makes recommendations to senior management with respect to how the quality of statistical metadata stored in, and disseminated from, corporate metadatabases may be enhanced by making changes to methods, procedures, guidelines, training plans or systems.

Provides input to management decisions and recommendations designed to develop or improve departmental policies and develops new divisional and program initiatives covering areas such as recruitment, training, official languages, wellness, employment equity, and information management.
2. Leadership And Operational Management: Manages a unit responsible for the development, production, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata and leads project teams for special projects. Assesses program requirements; determines objectives and priorities; plans and schedules work; resolves conflicting priorities. Ascertains human resource needs, determines appropriate selection methods (internal and external), recruits staff, determines training requirements and recommends and approves training plans. Evaluates employee performance and reviews performance evaluations prepared by subordinates.

Plans, develops and manages a budget for the unit in accordance with policy and procedures. Exercises direct authority and accountability for allocated funds to meet planned objectives. Authorises, commits and approves expenditures in accordance with approved budgets, with the authority to reallocate funds among line objects.
Negotiates and prepares service-level agreements related to the interoperability of statistical metadata across the Agency.
3. Communication: Provides expert advice and specialized training with respect to the policies, directives, guidelines, methods, procedures and systems used in the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata to subordinates, other statistical metadata specialists, systems specialists, clients and managers who use the information as input to on-going operations and to decisions concerning the management of statistical metadata at Statistics Canada and within other national and international organizations and agencies.

Liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, systems specialists, clients and managers to plan statistical metadata projects and implement short-term and long-term strategies for the development and enhancement of policies, procedures, methods and systems used in the management of statistical metadata. Provides direction with respect to establishing project plans, priorities and target dates; to negotiating modifications to methods, procedures and timelines; and to suggesting improvements to methods, procedures and systems.

Provides clear and comprehensible guidance, direction and specialized training to subordinate staff, colleagues, clients, systems specialists and management with respect to translating requirements for the management of statistical metadata into methods, procedures and systems specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata.

Writes detailed reports and prepares and delivers presentations which explain the rationale, requirements and results relating to policies, directives, guidelines, methods, procedures and systems used in the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata and which are used by other statistical metadata specialists, systems specialists, clients, and management in the operation and enhancement of statistical metadata management programs. When recommendations are challenged or misinterpreted, logical arguments are presented to defend the validity of the approaches used in order to maintain the division’s and Statistics Canada’s reputation for producing, storing and disseminating high quality metadata.
Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and groups to develop understanding, consensus and share knowledge on metadata management.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Extensive knowledge of statistical metadata concepts and frameworks used within Canada and internationally and knowledge of how those concepts and frameworks are used and reflected in policies, methods and procedures relating to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata in order to plan, develop, implement, direct, monitor and explain statistical metadata projects and short-term and long-term strategies for the development, operation and enhancement of statistical metadata management processes and systems.

Extensive knowledge of methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata and the potential impacts of new or modified methods, procedures and systems on project teams and clients in order to plan, develop, implement, direct, monitor and explain statistical metadata projects and short-term and long-term strategies for the development, operation and enhancement of statistical metadata management processes and systems; to manage and monitor the development, implementation and operation of new or enhanced metadata management processes and systems, and to lead metadata quality evaluations for surveys and statistical programs.

Knowledge of current and emerging trends and developments in the area of statistical metadata management in Canada and internationally, in order to evaluate Statistics Canada’s statistical metadata management program in a broader context; to anticipate, understand needs for, plan, manage and monitor the development, implementation and operation of new or enhanced metadata management methods, procedures and systems.

Knowledge of survey and statistical program subject matter concepts, methods and techniques relevant to the collection, processing, certification and dissemination of data in order to interpret client requirements for metadata production, storage and dissemination; to determine when changes in the needs of clients will impact statistical metadata programs and projects; to more accurately and efficiently evaluate the quality of statistical metadata across surveys and statistical programs; and to make recommendations to clients and managers with respect to possible enhanced approaches that could result in improved metadata quality.

Knowledge of management principles, techniques and practices in order to effectively manage financial resources, coordinate the activities of multi-disciplinary teams, manage performance, develop the skills, and competencies of team members. Knowledge of the principles and practices of project management used at Statistics Canada.

Knowledge of software, statistical packages and programming languages used in the production, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata and knowledge of new and emerging computer technology and applications in order to inform the planning of resource allocation and long-term strategies for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata.
5. Contextual knowledge: Extensive knowledge of Statistics Canada and Government of Canada policies, directives and guidelines directly and specifically related to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata, as well as other Statistics Canada policies, in order to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of all program activities and in order to explain policy requirements to clients and partners within Canada and internationally.

Extensive knowledge of the mandate, objectives, organization, practices, policies, culture and priorities of Statistics Canada in order to ensure that these are reflected in the objectives and management of all statistical metadata projects and short-term and long-term strategies for the development and enhancement of statistical metadata management processes and systems and to explain the context of statistical metadata management at Statistics Canada to clients and partners across Canada and internationally.

Knowledge of other statistical metadata management programs within Statistics Canada in order to integrate conceptually and structurally the statistical metadata required for various activities and programs into a broader corporate metadata management system and to ensure the overall relevance, completeness, coherence and consistency of statistical metadata contained within corporate metadata systems at Statistics Canada.

Extensive knowledge of surveys and statistical programs within Statistics Canada in order to establish short-term and long-term priorities for the processing, storing and dissemination of metadata across program areas and to effectively and efficiently plan and direct metadata quality assessment projects, certifying and reporting to senior management on the overall quality, completeness, coherence and consistency of statistical metadata.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and Privacy Act is required in order to ensure understanding and application of these Acts in the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata, particularly with respect to the security and confidentiality of statistical metadata and other information; to explain legislative requirements to other departments, agencies, industry, members of the public and the media; and to ensure that Statistics Canada meets its commitment to ensuring confidentiality and does not release any information that identifies an individual or group without prior consent.
6. Research and analysis: Analysis is required to understand and interpret client requirements with respect to the production, storage and dissemination of metadata, to determine the capacity and ability of existing or modified systems to meet the requirements of these clients and to translate client requirements into timely and affordable services. Clients are often uncertain of policy, procedural and systems restrictions and are unfamiliar with the options, methods and timelines required to produce and disseminate high quality metadata.

Reviews polices, guidelines, directives, methods, procedures and systems used for managing statistical metadata within Canada and internationally in order to determine the need for development, modification and adaptation of corporate metadata systems at Statistics Canada. Statistical metadata management programs are often very complex and have been designed for specific purposes which must be evaluated when taking into consideration the feasibility of the various features of such programs and the potential impacts and results in terms of Statistics Canada’s priorities for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata.

Analyses new methods, techniques and practices of managing statistical metadata and the associated costs and limitations. Identifies the availability of alternate means of producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata in order to evaluate the suitability of methods, procedures and systems with respect to the short-term and long-term program impacts and benefits.

Analyses the quality of statistical metadata produced by surveys and statistical programs at Statistics Canada; analyses gaps and inconsistencies in metadata quality and determines reasons for variances among program areas; reviews the comparability of metadata over time in light of changing policy requirements, systems functionality and changing methodologies used by statistical programs; provides senior management with interpretations and recommendations affecting policies, directives, guidelines, methods, procedures and systems used for the production, storage and dissemination of statistical metadata.

implicated_work_descriptions.justification: Conduct evaluation is the third strongest relationship because the role leads and certifies metadata quality assessments across surveys and statistical programs, analyzes gaps and inconsistencies, and provides senior management with interpretations and recommendations. Evidence includes 'reviews and certifies the results of statistical metadata quality evaluations', 'analyses the quality of statistical metadata produced by surveys and statistical programs', and reporting on 'overall quality, completeness, coherence and consistency'. This is stronger than 8.1 Gather evaluation inputs because the job synthesizes, interprets and reports findings at management level rather than merely collecting evidence. Future drivers such as metadata-driven management, enterprise-scale modernization, digital platforms and efficiency pressures will likely expand the use of quality dashboards, interoperability benchmarks, and evaluative evidence for metadata governance and continuous improvement.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: District Manager, Regional Operations (Data Collection)
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: There is a meaningful relationship to conduct evaluation because the role monitors and evaluates cost, quality, efficiency, productivity and security of regional collection systems and processes, evaluates effectiveness of existing and new systems, and produces studies used by senior management to assess program objectives and resource utilization. That is direct evaluative work, not merely ad hoc monitoring. This is stronger than gather-evaluation-inputs because the description includes interpretation and assessment for management use. Future drivers such as operational efficiency, execution discipline, digital telemetry from collection systems, and workforce pressures will likely increase dashboard-based evaluation and evidence-driven recommendations for collection modernization.

key_activities: Manages the work of the district office and the organization, planning, scheduling and control of statistical data collection activities in the regional district office (7-day collection operation), including the management of the Statistical Survey Operations (SSO) Office Interviewers and Senior Interviewers.
Monitors and evaluates the cost, quality, efficiency, productivity and security of regional data collection systems and processes and determines the need for development, modification and adaptation.

Identifies and reviews trends and developments in data collection concepts, methods and techniques, including response patterns and respondent behaviour, to determine variances in response rates and to assess their impact on statistical programs and operations within the department.

Develops and implements long term strategies and business solutions to improve respondent relations, data collection and transmission processes, and the development, enhancement and operation of Statistics Canada’s data collection programs.
Leads or participates in task forces, committees or departmental multidisciplinary project teams as a data collection expert and provides advice on proposed modifications to operational procedures.

1. Decision making: Defines the objectives, content and approaches for data collection activities in the regional district office and the framework and conditions within which statistical programs will occur.

Assesses the impact of changes in both technology and the subject area, develops and implements collection applications, alternate work methods and models, and establishes a framework for the on-going operation of statistical systems and processes.

Develops strategies and business solutions to improve respondent relations, data collection and transmission processes and resolves complaints and problems related to survey participation and non-respondents. A poor response rate can impact statistical programs and operations within the department.

Identifies and assesses new statistical methods, techniques and practices and the associated costs and limitations to identify the availability of respondents and to ensure quality control of data, to evaluate the suitability of new hardware and software, and to identify and determine the short and long term program impact and benefits.

Develops and distributes guidelines, instructions and procedures for the use and evaluation of statistical systems and processes. The information is used and applied by program, operational and system staff, when planning and performing their work, and contributes to the overall efficiency operations and quality of the outputs.

Identifies trends and developments in data processing concepts, methods and processes in order to select and integrate new computer hardware and software technology and applications in mass statistical data capture, conversion and dissemination systems and processes.

Establishes and implements specifications, guidelines and procedures for the maintenance and safeguarding of computer systems, equipment, databases and files. The information is used by staff for the collection, compilation, distribution and analysis of a broad range of statistical and administrative information.

Evaluates the effectiveness of existing and new statistical systems and processes and the quality and completeness of data. Senior management uses the studies to assess the attainment of program objectives and the cost, efficiency and utilization of regional resources.
Plans and coordinates concurrent projects or production operations involving multi-disciplinary resources in order to meet program objectives.
2. Leadership and operational management: Manages the recruitment, development and retention, of a fully trained and professional data collection workforce in the regional district office. Establishes, coordinates and leads multi-disciplinary project teams and work groups comprising professional, technical, administrative and interviewers engaged in initiating, developing and implementing programs. Approves work plans and priorities. Establishes organizational structures, recommends classification levels, assigns responsibilities to team or group members, monitors progress and evaluates employee performance, provides guidance and direction on career development, and approves training plans.
Establishes and monitors district budgets, including main estimate and cost recovery funding, to ensure that funds are spent appropriately, with authority to reallocate funds among line objects.

Plans and budgets for the management and operation of the district office in accordance with departmental policy and procedures, identifies content and cost of development and operational requirements, estimates salary, equipment and travel costs, as well as professional fees.
3. Communication: Discusses and negotiates with subject matter and systems specialists to come to an agreement on the conditions within which statistical programs will occur. There is a requirement to understand the issues and to resolve differences that can affect the efficiency and quality of program operations and outputs.

Responds orally or in writing to inquiries from managers, employees and the general public to provide information and advice on the operation and use of systems and processes and the use of program results.

Prepares work plans and summaries outlining approaches, time-frames and resources involved in the operation of statistical collection systems and processes. The information is used by senior management of the region/branch and/or client divisions to prepare program plans, priorities, responsibilities, schedules and budget submissions and will influence the nature, scope and cost of divisional statistical activities.

Develops proposals and provides advice regarding changes and improvements on questionnaire design; enhancements or modifications to survey content and coverage; revisions to collection systems and processes, and the implementation of new hardware and software to be used in data collection activities. The information is used by program managers to define and modify operational procedures.

Negotiates agreements with program managers, subject matter or service divisions, departments/agencies and other outside organizations for the acquisition and dissemination of data and/or the procurement and use of services and equipment.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Advanced knowledge of socio-economic concepts, methods and techniques applied in the development and operation of statistical programs to analyze program outputs, to anticipate and understand the need for new data and to assess the impact on collection activities and programs.

In-depth knowledge of statistical data collection methods, concepts and practices and survey operations to manage the activities of a district office and to provide expert advice on data collection issues.

Extensive knowledge of current and emerging socio-economic issues in Canada and internationally, such as the changing social context and the globalization of markets, particularly as they relate to all aspects of a statistical program. This knowledge is required to understand the issues and to resolve differences that can affect the efficiency and quality of program operations and outputs.

Knowledge of financial and human resources management and of project management methods, techniques and practices to manage the work of a district office and the organization, planning, scheduling and control of statistical data collection activities.

Knowledge of questionnaire development to provide advice to subject matter experts and to recommend changes and improvements to questionnaire design as well as enhancements or modifications to survey content and coverage.
Knowledge of communication principles and techniques to negotiate agreements with subject matter and systems specialists and to defend the validity of collection methods and approaches.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of the departmental and regional operations branch mandate, activities, priorities, practices, standards and procedures applicable to the work to incorporate them into the management of a district office and to recommend changes to management.

Knowledge of broad subject matter areas and their interrelationship to other statistical programs in order to select and integrate new computer hardware and software technology and applications in mass statistical data capture and conversion systems and processes.
Knowledge of other departments and their business lines and legislative frameworks in order to seek cooperation in the conduct of surveys conducted on a cost recovery basis.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies (e.g. confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations and data quality), practices and classification systems is required to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of data collection activities.
Knowledge of the structure and operation of internal client organizations to establish and maintain a framework for the collection, exchange and dissemination of information.
Knowledge of the trends and developments in data collection concepts, methods and techniques to evaluate response patterns and respondent behavior and to provide feedback to subject matter experts.

Knowledge of the content and operation of the Agency’s household and business survey programs and their impact upon systems and processes to determine and devise procedures and standards to be applied in operational activities.
Knowledge of the Statistical Survey Operations organization, its collective agreements, grievance procedures, policies and directives to ensure equitable treatment of all staff.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act pertaining to data security and confidentiality to ensure adherence in all development and operational activities. Knowledge of the Canada Labor Code to ensure safe working conditions exist for all employees. Knowledge of the Financial Administration Act, the Public Service Employment Act and related policies and directives.
6. Research and analysis: Determines and evaluates changes in the statistical needs of clients and provides advice regarding questionnaire design, concepts, changes in technology, respondent reaction and understanding.
Extracts and interprets information from analytical reports to assess the content and operation of collection activities and programs.

Identifies trends and developments in data processing concepts, methods and processes in order to select and integrate new computer hardware and software technology and applications in mass statistical data capture, conversion and dissemination systems and processes.

Analyses the relative quality of data, researches gaps and inconsistencies in the collection methods and procedures used, determines reasons for variances, reviews the comparability of data over time and its relevance in light of trends, developments, changing requirements, policy issues and socio-economic conditions.

Reviews and interprets the methods, concepts, techniques and practices applied in the operation of existing systems and processes; proposes modifications and enhancements or develops alternative approaches.

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Chief
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: There is meaningful evidence for conduct evaluation because the role 'undertakes analytical studies evaluating the effectiveness of divisional statistical programs and the resulting products and services' and evaluates 'cost, efficiency and productivity of divisional statistical systems and processes.' This is direct performance evaluation tied to recommendations and program improvement. It is stronger than generic quality review subprocesses because the focus is on assessing overall program effectiveness and resource utilization. Future drivers such as operational efficiency and cost realignment, governance discipline, and modernization will make this work more dashboard-driven and focused on evidence about productivity, sustainability, and continuation decisions.

key_activities: Manages a section and/or multidisciplinary project teams involved in statistical program operations, analysis, interpretation, marketing and dissemination.
Plans and implements long term strategies for the development, enhancement and operation of statistical programs.

Plans, develops and manages a comprehensive program of detailed analysis and evaluation across sectors and departments to improve existing data, develop new methods of producing, evaluating and analyzing data and to extend the application of divisional statistics.

Implements new systems and processes to meet client demands, identifies new statistical methods, techniques and practices and evaluates the cost, efficiency and productivity of divisional statistical systems and processes.

1. Decision making: Establishes and maintains a framework for the development and on-going operation of statistical systems and processes and evaluates and incorporates all the functions and activities associated with the data collection, processing, editing, compilation, analysis and dissemination of the division's statistical outputs and assesses the impact of changes in both technology and the subject area.

Establishes strategic directions for the management of significant studies, proposes innovative solutions and recommends to senior officials of Statistics Canada new or modified statistical programs to address departmental goals and objectives.

Manages complex studies covering a range of departmental statistical programs, determines the objectives, content and methodology of the research and development work, defines and sets priorities and milestones, selects and evaluates analytical techniques and methods to be used to integrate and interpret massive volumes of data and organizes the review and presentation of findings. Problems to be resolved usually impact on other statistical programs.

Initiates changes and implements new systems and processes to meet client demands, identifies and assesses new statistical methods, techniques and practices and the associated costs and limitations, identifies the availability and reliability of new data sources, evaluates the suitability of new hardware and software and identifies and determines the short and long term program impact and benefits.

Plans and manages the review and evaluation of statistical program methods and concepts to certify the overall quality and completeness of program results, to improve existing data, to develop new techniques and methods of producing, evaluating and analyzing data, to ensure the continued relevancy of data in light of changing requirements, trends, developments, policy issues and socio-economic conditions and to extend the use of statistical programs

Establishes policies and procedures for the security and confidentiality of data and the maintenance and protection of divisional computer systems, equipment, databases and files. The data, systems and equipment are used by staff for the collection, compilation, distribution and analysis of a broad range of statistical and administrative information.
2. Leadership and operational management: Manages, through subordinates, the work of a section and/or multidisciplinary project teams involved in statistical program operations, analysis, interpretation, marketing and dissemination. Establishes objectives and priorities to achieve long term program goals. Participates in the recruitment of staff and approves training and development plans. Allocates human and financial resource needs to achieve objectives. Prepares performance appraisals for subordinate staff, reviews performance appraisals prepared by subordinate supervisors.

Evaluates the cost, efficiency and productivity of statistical systems and processes. Manages budgets including estimates for salaries, professional fees and implementation costs, with authority to allocate/reallocate funds as needed. Submits cost estimates and projections to senior management and authorises expenditures in accordance with approved budgets.

Negotiates and arranges contracts with consulting firms and for the acquisition of services. Selects contractors for specific projects, assigns, directs, manages and evaluates the work according to contract specifications.
3. Communication: Provides expert advisory and consultative services to senior officials and policy makers at all levels of government, business and national social agencies and academics on the results of economic and socio-economic studies and their impact on complex policy issues, on the practical application and interpretation of statistical data, on advanced analytical methods, concepts and techniques, and on economic and social science theories and principles.
Writes reports outlining program results, developments and changes in the subject area in order to explain the nature, content and use of divisional statistical programs.

When addressing the general public, explains in clear terms the interpretation of complex data, reasons for variances in the results and the trends derived. When addressing a specialized public, it is also necessary to provide more detailed explanations of statistical and analytical methods and approaches used. When media representatives challenge or misinterpret the results of surveys or projects, it is necessary to further explain the results and statistical methods and approaches used in order to maintain the department’s reputation for producing high quality data.
Chairs intra-departmental meetings and participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences and groups to develop consensus or share knowledge in a particular field.

Negotiates significant resources and services, timeframes and costs for large scale projects with service providers(e.g. system specialists, regional office staff, survey methodologists, contractors, etc.) and clients within and outside the department.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of economic and sociological principles and theories, especially as they relate to a specialized area, and specific knowledge of the specialized area. This knowledge is required to provide expert advice on the results of surveys and studies to data users, to STC senior management and to other professionals within and outside STC.
Knowledge of advanced statistical theories, methods, concepts and practices used in the development, collection, compilation, analysis and interpretation of statistical data.

Knowledge of writing and editing skills and techniques to write papers, articles and reports and to determine and assess the design and content of studies, articles and reports that will be disseminated widely or published.
Knowledge of management practices and the theories and principles of project management in order to manage staff, either directly or within a matrix management environment.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge and understanding of current and emerging socio-economic trends and issues in Canada and internationally such as the changed social context and the globalization of markets, particularly as they relate to a broad area of expertise including all aspects of a statistical program.

Knowledge of STC policies, practices and classification systems as well as existing data bases, conceptual frameworks, and the statistical methods and procedures applicable to the work, to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of statistical projects and activities, and to recommend changes.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada mandate, objectives, organization, culture and priorities to define the objectives and content of analytical and research projects, as well as other statistical programs related to the area of expertise within the department, especially the concepts, methods, and databases used in other divisions.

Knowledge of the policies and programs of key client departments in order to determine their information requirements, analysis opportunities and to initiate the development of special projects to meet client needs.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act is needed to explain the legislative requirements to other departments, agencies, industry, members of the public and the media. This knowledge, along with knowledge of the Privacy Act is also required to ensure that the organization meets its commitment to ensuring the confidentiality of all information provided to them and does not release any information that identifies an individual or group without prior consent.
Knowledge of a variety of Acts related to the area of expertise such as the Income Tax Act, the Excise Sales Tax Act, the Employment Insurance Act, and the Corporate Returns Act.
6. Research and analysis: Undertakes analytical studies evaluating the effectiveness of divisional statistical programs and the resulting products and services in order to determine the attainment of divisional program objectives and the cost, efficiency and utilization of divisional resources. Prepares reports outlining program results, developments and changes in the subject area in order to explain the nature, content and use of divisional statistical programs.

Identifies gaps and inconsistencies in the collection, processing, analysis and dissemination methods and procedures used, reviews the conceptual framework used and the compatibility with other statistical programs. Conceptualizes enhancements and determines modifications to be made to the program content, coverage and operational procedures, such as new or modified data sources, concepts, methods and definitions to be applied.

Investigates and assesses changes in the statistical needs of clients, determines the extent and approaches of surveys or studies such as the sources of information, statistical techniques, methods and approaches to be used for the collection, processing, analysis and dissemination of the data in an area of specialty modifies existing techniques, methods and approaches or develops new ones to meet specific needs.

Researches and reports on trends and developments in data processing concepts, methods and techniques in order to present options and recommendations on the use and application of new computer hardware and software technology to mass data capture, conversion and dissemination applications; recommends strategies for the introduction or enhancement of statistical programs, the acquisition of new equipment and services and/or the adoption of new collection, production and dissemination strategies.
Writes and presents analytical material and research papers to be disseminated to a target audience ranging from the general public to a specialized audience (e.g. academics).

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Area Manager
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: Conduct evaluation is materially related because the position 'represents their assigned geographic area in ... committees involved in the evaluation of census collection activities,' 'disseminates and collects evaluation reports,' 'summarizes findings,' makes 'recommendations for program improvements,' and conducts evaluations of 'effectiveness and efficiency of collection operations.' This is direct evidence of analyzing evaluation inputs and recommending changes. It is ranked third because evaluation is an important but secondary responsibility relative to running and setting up collection. Future-state drivers such as Agility, Timelines and Execution Discipline, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and AI/automation-related monitoring will likely increase emphasis on dashboard-based performance assessment, productivity and quality metrics, and faster operational learning cycles, changing the role toward more evidence-based improvement and continuous performance management.

key_activities: As part of the area management team, contributes to the development of operational plans for census data collection activities and organizes, oversees and controls census field collection activities within the assigned geographic area; and manages census field operations for a 7-day collection operation.

Manages the financial, human and material resources for the assigned geographic area; manages employees hired under the Public Service Employment Act (PSEA); and works with recruitment teams to ensure Statistics Act employees required to meet the demands of a large temporary workforce are met for their respective areas

Develops collection strategies and contingency plans; establishes and defines priorities; monitors and evaluates the cost, quality, efficiency, productivity and security of data collection systems and processes in their assigned geographic area; analyzes and produces reports on the progress of the activities in their assigned geographic area; and resolves problems including but not limited to the need for development, modification and adaptation of operational processes.

Represents the agency in consultations with the general public to solicit participation from non-respondents, responds to and resolves complaints; and contributes to public relations activities to promote census communications and respondent cooperation.

Represents their assigned geographic area in regional and/or agency committees involved in the evaluation of census collection activities and provides advice on proposed modifications to operational procedures.
Disseminates and collects evaluation reports for the assigned geographic area; summarizes findings; and makes recommendations for program improvements.

Provides support to regional administration with the opening of the administrative hub in their geographic area such as visits during fit-up, ensures space readiness for the beginning of field activities as well as closing down activities at the hub once operations have been completed.

Decision making: Effort is required to make decisions/recommendations on: the determination and definition of objectives, content and approaches for census collection activities in the assigned geographic area and the operational framework and conditions within which the statistical program will occur; development and implementation of collection applications, alternate work methods and models to achieve desired outcomes; the development of strategies and business solutions to improve respondent relations, data collection and transmission processes; the resolution of complaints and problems related to survey participation and non-respondents; the development and distribution of guidelines, instructions and procedures for use by staff in their assigned geographic area; approval of appointments of all Statistics Act staff in the assigned geographic region; the assurance that financial expenditures and resources are within allocated budgets; and the day-to-day management of financial, human and material resources in their assigned geographic area.

Decisions/recommendations taken affect the efficient and effective operations of the assigned geographic area, as well as the area’s compliance to the Statistics Act and agency policies and procedures.
Leadership and operational management: Manages the recruitment, development and retention of a fully trained and professional data collection workforce in the assigned geographic area. Establishes, coordinates and leads multidisciplinary project teams and work groups comprising professional, technical, and administrative and field staff engaged in initiating, developing and implementing programs. Approves work plans and priorities. Assigns responsibilities to team or group members, monitors progress and evaluates employee performance, provides training and guidance. Supervision and guidance of human resources is significant and made complex by the size and scope of a temporary workforce, and the nature of a 7-day collection operation.

Monitors expenditures for staffing and material resources to ensure funds are spent appropriately and the budget in the assigned geographic area is respected. Exercises influence and decision making latitude in allocating funds and approving expenditures in line with the financial delegation bestowed.

Plans and budgets for the management and operation of the assigned geographic area in accordance with agency policy and procedures, identifies content and cost of development and operational requirements, estimates salary, equipment and travel costs, as well as professional fees.

Oversees some of the aspects related to fit-ups in the assigned geographic area with local contractors to ensure readiness at time of opening and coordinate the dismantlement of the facility at the end of census collection operation.
Communication: Communications skills are required to respond orally and in writing to inquiries from managers, employees to provide information and advice on the operation and use of systems and processes, and briefings on program results in the assigned geographic area.
Communications skills are required to respond orally and in writing to inquiries from the general public on the requirements for response, purpose of the census or issues with employees.

Communications skills are also required to intervene and deal with uncooperative and sometimes hostile respondents. There is a requirement to 'take control' over these emotionally-charged situations, and persuade the respondent to take a more rational approach to a situation. Strategic communication skills are required when negotiating problems of non-response or addressing problems and complaints raised by external bodies.

Negotiation skills are required to convince stakeholders when resolving problems including but not limited to the need for development, modification and adaptation of operational processes. Judgment, tact and flexibility are exercised in finding solutions that meet a range of business needs.
Knowledge of specialized fields: Advanced knowledge of socioeconomic concepts, methods and techniques applied in the development and operation of statistical programs to manage field operations in the assigned geographic area, analyze program outputs, anticipate and understand the need for new data and to assess the impact on collection activities and programs.

In-depth knowledge of statistical data collection methods, concepts and practices and survey operations to manage the activities in the assigned geographic area and to provide expert advice on data collection issues.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies (e.g., confidentiality of data, security, respondent relations and data quality), practices and classifications systems is required to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of census activities.

Knowledge of financial and human resources management and of project management methods, techniques and practices to manage the work, as well as organize, plan, schedule and control the operational activities in the assigned geographic area.
Contextual knowledge: Knowledge and understanding of Statistics Canada’s mandate, programs, objectives, policies and procedures in areas such as survey methodology, operations integration, data confidentiality and security, dissemination and marketing to manage staff in the delivery of the program within an assigned geographic area and ensure that work undertaken is standardized and consistent with departmental requirements.

Knowledge of the regional and local operation’s mandate, activities, priorities, standards and procedures to incorporate them into the management of the assigned geographic area and to recommend changes to management.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada policies (e.g., confidentiality of data, security, and respondent relations and data quality), practices and classification systems is required to ensure that they are applied in the conduct of census activities.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act, Financial Administration Act, the Public Service Employment Act, collective agreements and related policies and directives and supporting financial and human resources management methods, techniques and practices in order to manage the financial, human resource and material resources of assigned geographic areas.
Knowledge of the Canada Labor Code to ensure safe working conditions exist for all employees.

Knowledge of external business lines including those of Shared Services Canada and municipal entities are required when negotiating space requirements to facilitate the delivery of collection operations.
Research and analysis: Reviews and interprets the methods, concepts, techniques and practices applied in the operation of existing systems and processes and proposes modifications and enhancements or develops alternative approaches.
Identifies and evaluates variations in survey responses and contributes to promotional activities to increase respondent participation rates.

Analyzes and produces reports on the progress of activities in the assigned geographic area and resolves problems including but not limited to the need for development, modification and adaptation of operational processes.

Conducts comprehensive evaluations to determine the effectiveness and efficiency of collection operations. Identifies trends, gaps and inconsistencies, and makes recommendations for consideration by Head Office on areas requiring improvements or approaches to be adopted.

Knowledge of Statistics Canada mandate, objectives, organization, culture and priorities to define the objectives and content of analytical and research projects, as well as other statistical programs related to the area of expertise within the department, especially the concepts, methods, and databases used in other divisions.

Knowledge of the policies and programs of key client departments in order to determine their information requirements, analysis opportunities and to initiate the development of special projects to meet client needs.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act is needed to explain the legislative requirements to other departments, agencies, industry, members of the public and the media. This knowledge, along with knowledge of the Privacy Act is also required to ensure that the organization meets its commitment to ensuring the confidentiality of all information provided to them and does not release any information that identifies an individual or group without prior consent.
Knowledge of a variety of Acts related to the area of expertise such as the Income Tax Act, the Excise Sales Tax Act, the Employment Insurance Act, and the Corporate Returns Act.
6. Research and analysis: Undertakes analytical studies evaluating the effectiveness of divisional statistical programs and the resulting products and services in order to determine the attainment of divisional program objectives and the cost, efficiency and utilization of divisional resources. Prepares reports outlining program results, developments and changes in the subject area in order to explain the nature, content and use of divisional statistical programs.

Identifies gaps and inconsistencies in the collection, processing, analysis and dissemination methods and procedures used, reviews the conceptual framework used and the compatibility with other statistical programs. Conceptualizes enhancements and determines modifications to be made to the program content, coverage and operational procedures, such as new or modified data sources, concepts, methods and definitions to be applied.

Investigates and assesses changes in the statistical needs of clients, determines the extent and approaches of surveys or studies such as the sources of information, statistical techniques, methods and approaches to be used for the collection, processing, analysis and dissemination of the data in an area of specialty modifies existing techniques, methods and approaches or develops new ones to meet specific needs.

Researches and reports on trends and developments in data processing concepts, methods and techniques in order to present options and recommendations on the use and application of new computer hardware and software technology to mass data capture, conversion and dissemination applications; recommends strategies for the introduction or enhancement of statistical programs, the acquisition of new equipment and services and/or the adoption of new collection, production and dissemination strategies.
Writes and presents analytical material and research papers to be disseminated to a target audience ranging from the general public to a specialized audience (e.g. academics).

implicated_work_descriptions.title: Planning and Evaluation Manager
implicated_work_descriptions.justification: The strongest relationship is to agree an action plan because this role has clear decision-making authority, prioritization responsibility, and governance influence over what follows from evaluation findings. Evidence includes 'full latitude to analyze and elaborate,' 'prioritize proposed projects for the annual departmental Evaluation Plan,' 'provide input on issues and strategic considerations for use by the departmental Review Committee and Branch management in short and long term strategic planning,' 'develop and recommend strategies, plans, policies and procedures,' and 'recommendations are made to the Director ... to effect changes in Divisional plans and programs.' The role also leads consultations with senior management, develops briefings and recommendations, and is responsible for monitoring implementation and compliance improvements. This is stronger than 8.2 because the position goes beyond conducting evaluations to shaping prioritization, strategic response, and management action. Future drivers such as Governance, Prioritization and Decision Discipline, Agility/Timelines/Execution Discipline, Operational Efficiency and Cost Realignment, and Workforce Skills Transition are likely to increase emphasis on explicit trade-offs, action ownership, milestone-based follow-up, workforce adjustment measures, and enterprise modernization action plans.
